feat(gateway): opt-in Cloudflare Access JWT verification for trusted-proxy auth

* feat(gateway): opt-in Cloudflare Access JWT verification for trusted-proxy auth

With gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAccessJwt set, verify
cf-access-jwt-assertion (RS256) against <issuer>/cdn-cgi/access/certs,
check iss, aud and exp, and take the user from the signed email claim.
The user header must match the claim. Unset keeps today's behavior;
service-token requests keep their existing outcome.

* fix(gateway): bound Access certs reads and back off failed refreshes

Read /cdn-cgi/access/certs with a 64 KB limit, fetch it at most once per
30 s per issuer (including after a failure), document the lazy refresh
and 60 s clock skew, and cover delegation being refused with
verification on.

* refactor(gateway): guard the cached Access key set instead of asserting it

* refactor(gateway): narrow Access JWT segments and JWKs without type assertions

* fix(gateway): bound Cloudflare Access signing-key fallback

* fix(gateway): require 2048-bit RSA keys for Cloudflare Access

RFC 7518 §3.3 sets 2048 bits as the minimum RSA key size for RS256.
Cloudflare Access signing keys below that threshold are now treated as
unusable, so a weak-key certs response cannot replace the last good
cached set. The cache suite gains a weak-key case that fails on the
512-bit minimum.

fix(exec): keep OpenClaw's notes out of the output a script parses (#202852)

A foreground exec that left a process running, or whose process cleanup
could not be confirmed, had OpenClaw's note appended to the command
output. A Code Mode or cron trigger script that parsed `aggregated`
then failed on valid JSON followed by the note.

The note is now reported through the existing warning channel: ahead of
the output in the visible text and in `warningText` for scripts. A
command that was already backgrounded keeps the note in its process log
and approval follow-up, because it has no later tool result.

feat: only link file paths that open in chat (#202534)

* feat(control-ui): only link file paths the Gateway can open

Add sessions.files.stat, a batched metadata check that follows the same
session root, sandbox mapping, host-read policy, and bare-name fallback as
the file reader. Transcript file links whose path the Gateway reports as
missing render as plain text and no longer open the Files panel. Tell
agents to write absolute paths for files outside the working directory.

* perf(control-ui): batch file-link checks per session

Send one sessions.files.stat request per session with each reference's
message entry, instead of one request per message. The Gateway resolves the
session workspace once and only re-resolves per message when the session
carries a prior workspace. The check no longer folds the transcript's
touched files, and stats a repeated path once per workspace.

* perf(gateway): resolve bare file names in one workspace walk

The bare-name reader fallback ran one bounded workspace search per name,
about 90 ms each in a large checkout. sessions.files.stat now walks the
workspace once for every name in the request while stopping each name where
its own search would, and a parity test pins it to the search fallback.

* fix(gateway): keep file-link checks in step with the reader

Address review: a metadata check now opens the file so hard-linked or
unreadable files report missing like the reader; touched files are folded
when the session cwd differs from the workspace root, where they change
candidate resolution; and historical messages leave bare-name misses
unknown because the reader's fallback searches the current workspace.

* fix(gateway): admit bare-name matches and skip remote workspaces in file-link checks

Address follow-up review: a unique bare-name match is opened by its full path
under the reader's admission before it counts; remote workspace roots answer
unknown because only a full read decides them; and references with @, ~ or
file: syntax fold touched files, where touched membership changes resolution.

* fix(gateway): leave syntax-sensitive bare-name matches to the reader

A unique bare-name match whose path contains @, ~ or file: can resolve
differently without the transcript's touched files, so the check answers
unknown for it instead of admitting it without them.

* refactor(control-ui): check file links through the Markdown owner

Address review: the Markdown blocks owner hands settled file links to the
chat workspace, whose lazily loaded file runtime checks them and replaces
links the Gateway cannot open with text, so no new DOM scanner, stylesheet
rule or boot code is added. The bare-name check runs the same Files search as
the reader through one shared walker, the UI calls sessions.files.stat
without an older-Gateway branch, and the prompt rule cites its incident.

* fix(control-ui): keep focus and links when a file-link check cannot finish

Address review: a focused link that turns into text keeps focus outside the
tab order, and a failed lazy load of the check leaves links usable without an
unhandled rejection.

fix(daemon): Linux updates run out of space on a RAM-backed /tmp when TMPDIR was never set (#199689)

* fix(daemon): Linux updates stage on a RAM-backed /tmp when TMPDIR was never set

The Linux service installer froze the host default temporary directory into
the systemd unit as TMPDIR. Update staging treats TMPDIR as an operator
choice and ranks it ahead of the state volume, so on hosts where /tmp is a
small tmpfs the update ran out of space even with the state disk free.

Linux now writes TMPDIR into the unit only when the installer has one. An
explicit TMPDIR is kept as before, macOS keeps its state-directory TMPDIR,
and other platforms are unchanged. Precedence between an explicit TMPDIR
and the state volume is not changed.

Related: #199559

test(prompt-cache): extend the prefix journey with cron, steer, overflow and a concurrent chat on five transports (#201723)

## What was wrong

The prompt-cache journey is the CI check that each provider request in a chat extends the previous request byte for byte, except where a rebuild is expected. It skipped four triggers that real chats hit: a scheduled job that comes due in the chat, a user message steered into a running tool call, tool results that fill the context window, and an unrelated chat that compacts while this one runs. It also covered only three transports. A break in any of those paths could land without CI noticing.

**Example:** a scheduled job sent its reply to the model twice on every route. On Chat Completions and Gemini the copy merged into the next tool-call message, which rewrote history and lost the cache from that point on. Fixed in #201838. This journey would have caught it.

## Fix

- Adds the cron, steer, tool-result overflow and concurrent-compaction steps to the stability journey. It now runs on five transports: Anthropic, Responses, Chat Completions, Gemini and Bedrock.
- Adds a seeded randomized journey: 15 turn kinds on five transports, plus a variant with Tool Search turned off.
- Lists the breaks main still has, each with its owner. Entries expire: when a fix lands, the journey fails until its entry is removed. Each entry checks the whole request, so a known change cannot hide a second one.
- Rebuild steps are excused only when the rebuild actually happened. A compaction must put its new summary into the next request, and a model switch must make the next request come from the selected model.
- The steer step holds the tool open until the Gateway reports that the run has taken the steer. Before, it slept for a fixed 3 s.

## Numbers

| | main (before this PR) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Triggers covered | ordinary turns, tools, compaction | + cron, steer, tool-result overflow, concurrent compaction, cron-first chat, 15-kind randomized journey |
| Transports | 3 | 5 |
| Stability journey | n/a | 5/5 |
| Randomized journey (default seeds, 6 files) + negative controls | n/a | 12/12 + 5/5 |
| Anthropic and Tool Search off, seeds 1 and 6 | n/a | 2/2 and 2/2 |

<details><summary>Breaks still on main (accepted entries)</summary>

| Where | Change | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini, tool-result overflow (other chat) | the pre-request pressure check trims tool results that were already sent | #199530 |
| Bedrock, randomized | a dropped silent reply merges the user turns around it | accepted gap (#201654 closed) |
| Tool Search off, randomized | a provider switch adds `skills_read`/`skills_search` on turns started by a subagent completion or inter-session message | #201710 / documented exception of the opt-out surface |

Removed because their owners landed: the cron reply twice (#201838), the Chat Completions silent-turn merge (#201843), the cron-first `message` growth (#201710), and the skills rebuild after `config.patch` (issue #202150, which no longer reproduces on Anthropic seeds 1 and 6).
Bedrock refuses `cron.add` for AWS-SDK auth by design, and the journey expects that refusal.
</details>

<details><summary>Steer signal</summary>

- The steer is sent with `queueMode: "steer"`, as the chat composer sends it. The test waits for `sessions.changed` with reason `agent.input.steering`, which the Gateway emits when the active run accepts the steer into its queue. The tool is released only after that event.
- On all five transports the event arrives about 200-260 ms after the send is acknowledged, while the tool is still held.
- Negative control: releasing right after the acknowledgment lost the race on Gemini (1/5). The steered input became a separate turn.
- A default `chat.send` steer exposes nothing before release. Its pending input stays `queued` with no `steerNow`, and `agent.input.steering` only fires when the tool ends. So the step uses the composer's steer path.
</details>

<details><summary>Rebuild evidence checks</summary>

- Compaction: the fake numbers each compaction summary. The step needs a new summary, and the turn after it must contain that summary.
- Model switch: the alternate provider has its own model id. Every request after the switch must name exactly the selected model, read from the request body or the URL (Gemini, Bedrock), and at least one request must arrive.
- Teeth: with `sessions.compact` turned into a no-op, all 10 randomized seeds failed. With `sessions.patch` pinned to the first model, all 10 failed too.
</details>

<details><summary>Cron-first red on base</summary>

On the parent of #201710 with this PR's test files (no entry), the cron-first step fails on Anthropic and Responses at the owner turn's tool list (`at: 1, change: tools`). On main the step passes.
</details>

<details><summary>Harness fixes</summary>

- Each seed uses its own session keys. A retained subagent from the previous seed made every turn fail with `Retained subagent payload is unavailable`.
- After a silent reply, the fake acts only on the newest step marker, because main drops silent replies from replay.
- Every request is assigned to its session by its runtime line. A request from an unexpected session fails the journey.
- The Advisor fork check is dropped. Forks never arrived in earlier runs. When they did arrive, their requests differed from the parent's on all transports, which needs its own investigation.
</details>

<details><summary>Gates</summary>

- `ocx test` from source with an in-process Gateway and fake provider endpoints: 5 stability files, 6 randomized files and the known-breaks unit, 17/17. Anthropic and Tool Search off at seeds 1 and 6, 2/2 each. A second stability pass, 5/5.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files, and the test-lines ratchet all pass.
- Local review on this head: patch is correct, no findings.
</details>

fix: ACP clients get the whole reply when a prompt waits behind other work (#202658)

Root cause: src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-source-finalization.ts:276-281 strips model text from a queued follow-up's final payloads by design (#172810: the transcript, sent as `session.message`, is the only carrier of a queued answer, so WebChat does not show it twice), so the `chat` final for a queued prompt has no `message`; the ACP bridge (src/acp/translator.prompt-stream.ts, `chat` final branch) builds the reply only from `chat` frames, so it settles with whatever live text it already streamed.

Related: #202577, #202047

## What Problem This Solves

An ACP client (`openclaw acp`) can get only the start of a reply, for example `BRA` of `BRAVO`, followed by a normal `end_turn`. It happens when a prompt is queued behind other work on the session, such as the retry the Gateway runs after a `deliver: true` prompt whose reply was not sent with the message tool.

## User Impact

User impact: ACP clients get the whole reply for queued prompts. Prompts whose final already carries the reply are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A queued prompt's `chat` final leaves the reply text to the transcript on purpose (#172810). When a final arrives with no `message`, the bridge now reads the run's committed reply through the history recovery it already uses after a disconnect (`recoverTerminalReply`) and streams only the part it has not sent. If history has nothing for the run, or the reply does not extend what was sent, the prompt settles as before. The Gateway contract is unchanged.

Thanks @ElanHasson for finding this and capturing the frames in #202577.

## Evidence

Native Codex route: Gateway and `openclaw acp` from source, the real bundled Codex 0.169.0 app-server against a local ChatGPT-backend fixture (no real login), `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` on runtime `codex`, scripted replies streamed 8 ms apart (41 lines, or `BRA` then `VO`), a qa-channel route on the main session. Connection A: three rounds of a `deliver: true` prompt, a visible BRAVO prompt, a visible 41-line prompt. Connection B never uses deliver.

| | main 31ce94f0ad | this PR a9d1ef4f5e |
|---|---|---|
| A, BRAVO after a deliver prompt | `BRA` 2/3 (`BRA` 3/3 in each of 3 earlier runs on main 918d83996b) | `BRA` + `VO` 3/3, no repeated text |
| A, 41-line prompts | 41/41 lines | 41/41 lines |
| A, deliver prompts | streamed once, `end_turn` | same |
| B | complete | complete, same chunks |

Frames for each truncated run on main: `chat` delta `BRA` -> `session.message` `BRAVO` -> `chat` delta `replace: true` `""` -> `chat` final with no `message`. The same frames reach the candidate; it now recovers `VO` from history.

The deliver prompts' channel result is unchanged on both sides (the scripted model never calls the message tool, so `message_tool_only` sends its missing-reply notice).

Regression: `src/acp/translator.final-snapshots.test.ts` "streams the committed remainder when a queued final carries no message" fails on main (`expected [ 'BRA' ] to deeply equal [ 'BRA', 'VO' ]`) and passes here. `src/acp`: 92 files, 617 tests passed.

Observed proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202658#issuecomment-7047602270

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the truncation; no state, config or protocol changes. Blast radius: `openclaw acp` users. A `chat` final with no `message` now costs one `chat.history` read for the pending run.

fix: resume model catalog publishing when a release ships minified code (#202656)

## What Problem This Solves

The hosted model catalog has not published since 2026-11-19 12:29 UTC. Every scheduled `openclaw/catalog` publish since 16:26 UTC fails in the released-reader gate with `released reader entry point not found in .../2026.11.10-beta.1/node_modules/openclaw/dist: refreshRemoteModelCatalog`. Users keep seeing a catalog that is more than a day old.

## User Impact

The catalog publisher can check `openclaw@2026.11.10-beta.1` again, and publishing resumes. Future releases ship a fixed file for the gate, so a bundler change in a release can no longer stop catalog publishing. The gate stays strict: a release that reads the feed but has no runnable refresh still fails. No change for OpenClaw users.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gate runs each tagged release's own catalog refresh. It found that function by a source-name search that expected pretty-printed chunks: a declaration at the start of a line and `export {` with a space. 2026.11.10-beta.1 is the first release with whitespace-minified chunks (`}async function refreshRemoteModelCatalog(e){`, `export{…}`), so neither pattern matched. The function itself was not renamed, moved or inlined.

- Releases now build `dist/model-catalog/remote-refresh.js` as a named entry. The gate runs the refresh from it, and runs the config reader from the existing `dist/config/config.js`. If one of these files is present but does not export its function, the gate fails.
- Releases without the entry (2026.10.33, 2026.11.6, 2026.11.10-beta.1) are still searched by declaration, with whitespace-independent patterns. This search can be removed once every tagged release ships the entry.
- A `tsdown-config` test fails CI if either entry leaves the build or stops exporting its function under the name the gate uses.

## Evidence

- **Real gate, real releases (TMPDIR in scratch, live catalog files):** before the fix, `catalog-compare-released.mts --check` on the live v3 file fails with the exact publisher error for 2026.11.10-beta.1. With the fix:
  - v3: `2026.11.6`: no v3 reader, skipped; `2026.10.33`: no v3 reader, skipped; `2026.11.10-beta.1`: updated, 1414/1414 rows.
  - v2: `2026.11.6`, `2026.10.33` and `2026.11.10-beta.1`: updated, 1392/1392 rows each.
- **Regression tests** (`test/scripts/catalog-compare-released.test.ts`) run `--check` against fake releases. Minified chunks and the stable entry fail on the base with the production error and pass with the fix. A stable entry without the export fails. A v3 reader without a runnable refresh fails.

**Merge risk:** two-way door. A revert restores the old search. It writes no state and changes no package export; the only new artifact is one internal dist file. Blast radius if wrong: the catalog publish gate (publishing stays blocked, and the last good catalog stays live). OpenClaw runtime behavior does not change.

fix(gateway): keep a worker session's system prompt pinned across instruction changes (#202568)

Fixes #202523

## What was wrong

Turns that run on a worker node (cloud workers, or a required worker profile) rendered a fresh system prompt every turn. Embedded turns pin one system prompt per session and send later changes as an appended update. Worker turns did not, so any mid-session change to the prompt rewrote the very first item of the request, and the provider cache missed the whole conversation.

Example: the agent appends a rule to `AGENTS.md` on turn 2. Turn 3 on `main` sends a new system prompt: 12,668 tokens uncached, 0 cached.

## Fix

- The Gateway pins the worker session's system prompt with the same series owner embedded turns use (`prepareSessionSystemPrompt`). It reads the newest checkpoint in full (the worker's transcript view keeps only checkpoint navigation) and writes the checkpoint after the worker's rows commit; a failed turn writes none.
- A change goes out as a full-replacement "System prompt update" block appended to that turn's user message as model-only text. The Gateway stores it on the same user row (`modelPromptProjection`), so there is no new row, no parent or order change, and the chat shows the user's own text.
- A rebuild (compaction, model or route change) already contains every earlier delta. Both runtimes now retire the delta part of older user rows at a rebuild, keep any other model-only text, and the rebuilding request drops prompt-update rows.

## Numbers

Real Gateway with a real paired worker node and a real provider route (OpenAI Responses), same journey on both sides: ordinary chat, an `AGENTS.md` edit by the agent, two ordinary turns, `/compact`, two ordinary turns.

| Request | `main` uncached / cached | This PR uncached / cached |
|---|---|---|
| turn 3 (first turn after the edit) | **12,668 / 0** (system prompt rewritten) | **737 / 12,018** |
| turn 4 | 639 / 12,665 | 645 / 12,752 |
| first turn after `/compact` | 1,236 / 10,562 | 11,779 / 0 (planned re-pin) |
| next turn | 661 / 11,795 | 665 / 11,776 |

On `main` every prompt change costs a full miss; here only a rebuild point (compaction, model or route change) does, as on embedded turns. In this short journey the one `/compact` re-pin lands where `main` had already paid for the change.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/worker-turn-prompt-pin.e2e.test.ts`: real Gateway, paired worker node, fake Chat Completions provider. The agent edits `AGENTS.md` on turn 2. Asserts one system prompt across all requests, the update on turn 3's user message, and turn 4 replaying turn 3's request as an exact prefix. Fails on `main` (two different system prompts), passes here.
- `session-prompt-state.test.ts`: user-row deltas before the newest rebuild are retired, other model-only text on the same row survives, and a rebuilding request drops prompt-update rows.
- Worker tests that asserted "the leaf is the terminal reply" now assert the last message is the terminal reply: a settled turn appends its prompt checkpoint after its rows, as embedded turns do. The cancelled-during-hydration test checks the committed rows stay unchanged and only that checkpoint follows.
- `session-prompt-state`, `attempt-session-runtime-prepare`, `worker-turn-execution`, `-early-final`, `-launcher-media`, `-launcher-terminal-results`, `-launcher`, `-launcher-failure-recovery` and `worker-turn-rpc.transcript` pass; `tsgo:core`, `check:test-types` and the line-cap check pass.
- `skill-library-worker-wire` e2e: its fake provider read the skill catalog only from system/developer items. A pinned worker session now sends a newly attached skill as a prompt update on the user message, so the fixture reads the newest `<available_skills>` block from those items too (passes locally and in CI).
- `project-preparation-environment` (6) and `local-workspace-projection` (1) fail locally on `main` too (same files, same failures); this PR does not touch them.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Accepted edge case</summary>

If a worker turn stores its user row with a delta and then fails before it produces a reply, and the instructions are reverted before the next turn, that row still replays the reverted delta until the next rebuild. Visible, rare and recoverable (`/compact` or a model switch clears it); no extra state was added for it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Side effects and UI</summary>

- Ordinary chat turns before and after the change get their replies, and the turn-3 request carries the new `AGENTS.md` rule in the update block.
- `/compact` rebuilds the prompt once (expected), and the turn after it is cached again.
- Chat history shows only the user's own text; the update block is model-only.

fix(models): never list a model the provider's listing omits, including on the Gateway's first read (#202618)

## Problem

A model that the provider's account listing omits could appear in `models.list` on the Gateway's first read after start. Follow-up to #202490.

The approved rule: the provider's listing is the only source of which models exist. The hosted catalog and the manifest only describe models.

## Interleaving

1. The Gateway starts and publishes a quick `static` catalog (`publishConfiguredModelRuntimeSnapshots`, `src/gateway/server-startup-model-runtime.ts:59`).
2. That build seeds the registry for every signed-in provider with `loadManifestModelProviderConfigs` (`src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.facts.ts:556`, added in #167460). The manifest plan contains the hosted catalog rows, so the refreshable Together provider got `zz-lab/zz-day0-live` even though the saved listing (already loaded, `pluginCatalogs=1`) omits it.
3. `prepareCapturedRuntimeFacts` publishes the registry rows as list entries (`src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.configured-catalog.ts:124`).
4. `models.list` serves the published snapshot (`src/gateway/server-methods/models.ts:148`). The live full catalog, built from the account listing, publishes 5–24 s after `ready` and drops the row.

The leak depends on timing. It happens only when the first read arrives before step 4's live publication. A scratch build with logging showed this in 10 of 10 runs: all 5 runs where the first read came before the publication leaked, and none of the 5 where it came after. The suspect `includeProviderPluginAugmentation === false` branch in `model-catalog.ts` never ran during these reads.

The fix is in `loadManifestModelProviderConfigs`, the single source of manifest rows that claim a model exists. It no longer returns rows for providers that declare `runtime` or `refreshable` discovery. Those providers list only their saved or live account listing. While the first listing is pending they list nothing (`pendingProviders`), and they also list nothing after a failed first listing. Static providers and providers without a discovery declaration keep their manifest rows at once, as before. Description consumers (limits, price, thinking, typed-ref resolution) are unchanged: typed refs to an unlisted model still resolve, run and are priced.

Kept: the `includeProviderPluginAugmentation === false` branch in `buildPreparedModelCatalogSnapshot` (#143837) still passes dynamic manifest rows in no-augmentation builds. The first head removed it, and CI then showed that utility preparation uses those typed rows to refuse a Decisions model a credential has no grant for (`utility-completion.clawrouter.test.ts`). The scratch build showed that branch never runs on the Gateway or CLI list reads measured here. Moving that entitlement data onto a description-only path is a follow-up.

**Contract change (approved):** this reverses part of #167460. Right after sign-in, a refreshable or runtime provider shows as pending instead of showing its known manifest models, until its listing arrives. A failed first listing leaves it empty with `refreshFailed`. Docs updated (`docs/plugins/manifest/models.md`). No schema, protocol or config change.

fix(models): apply a changed catalog source at once without breaking turns (#202583)

## What Problem This Solves

Changing `models.catalogRefresh.url` (or `.enabled`) on a running Gateway waited up to six hours for the next scheduled catalog check, so a model the new catalog describes stayed unlisted and its turns were priced at $0.

The obvious fix, re-arming the catalog check from the config listener (part 3 of #202490, reverted), broke worse. The check ran inside the hot reload that published the config. The Gateway scheduler keeps the async context of whoever schedules a job, and the reload runs inside a plugin lifecycle operation with its own plugin cache, which retires when the reload ends. The catalog adoption then built its plugin generation from that short-lived inventory:

- inventory retired during the build: `PluginInventoryRetiredError` ("check failed") or a rejected candidate ("superseded"), then a 6-hour wait;
- inventory retired after the adoption committed: the published owner was retired with it, and every later turn failed with `UNAVAILABLE: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for main` until restart;
- every later scheduled check chained from the same retired context and failed again. In the reverted branch this showed up as the 10-second retry failing with an `AbortError`.

## Timeline of one wedged run

Probe build (main plus the naive re-check), one Gateway, URL change at t=10.49 s:

| 10.498 | The runtime config is set and `sessionChanges.emit` fires inside that context. The update owner's listener re-arms the catalog check. `GatewayScheduler` snapshots the registrant's context | `config/runtime-snapshot.ts:272`, `infra/update-startup-scheduler.ts:90`, `infra/gateway-scheduler.ts:190` |
| 10.499 / 10.504 | Reload commit marks prepared runtimes stale (R1), then its refresh supersedes R1 with R2 | `gateway/server-reload-hot.ts:280`, `:596` → `agents/prepared-model-runtime.ts:519` |
| 11.197 | The fetch is done; the adoption waits for R2 | `agents/prepared-model-runtime.configured-refresh.ts:97-101` |
| 11.271 | The reload commits R2 and reply dispatch publishes `main` (generation 5) | `agents/prepared-model-runtime.ts:580` |
| 11.272 | The adoption claims generation 5 and builds candidates. Their plugin metadata belongs to the reload's operation cache | `configured-refresh.ts:256-298`, `plugins/plugin-cache.ts:315` |
| 12.791 | The reload operation ends; its cache retires | `gateway/config-reload.ts:470`, `plugins/plugin-lifecycle-lease.ts:128` |
| 14.336 | The adoption commits generation 6: "remote model catalog applied" | `configured-refresh.ts:363-373` |
| after | Cache retirement retires the published owner (needs refresh, no plugin generation). No recovery runs, because it was not a Gateway loan | `agents/prepared-model-runtime.plugin-lifetime.ts:390`, `:407-425` |
| 41.858 | Turn: owner mismatch → `UNAVAILABLE ... runtime owner was not published for main` | `agents/prepared-reply-dispatch-runtime.ts:179-188` |

The stale mark and the pending replacement were not the cause. The adoption waited correctly for R2 and claimed fresh owners. What broke it was where the check ran, not when.

## Fix

One owner: the update-check scheduler.

- When `models.catalogRefresh` changes, the config listener re-arms the existing catalog check. It does not add a second scheduler.
- Re-arms from the listener run in the update owner's own context, taken from `AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot()` at `start()`, not in the publishing reload's context. The catalog check and every later re-arm use the Gateway's plugin inventory, the same one the startup check uses.

No change to the adoption, the stale mark or reply dispatch. The four symptom patches from #202490 (10-second superseded retry, `PluginInventoryRetiredError` → superseded, captured cancel signal, docs) stay reverted. None of them is needed, and none was added back.

Accepted edge case: an unrelated model-affecting reload that lands while an adoption is building still defers that adoption to the next scheduled check, as on `main` (#168981 removed adoption retries on purpose). A further `catalogRefresh` change re-arms at once.

fix(cli): refuse saved history only when another CLI account ran the session (#202428)

## Problem

A fresh Claude CLI session only received a chat's saved history when OpenClaw could prove that every stored row was written by an earlier `claude-cli` run under the same account. Any row it could not attribute, such as turns written by Gemini or Codex, turns from a native Claude login without the attestation opt-in, legacy rows or imports, made the whole chat `auth-unknown` and refused for good.

As a result, switching an existing chat from another model to Claude dropped all context. The Gateway logged `cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown`, and the new Claude session got only the current message. The rest of OpenClaw already replays the full conversation to Gemini, OpenAI and Codex on every switch without any such check.

The case #140294 actually guards against still matters: account A's history must not be replayed into a session for account B. Enforcing it took per-row coverage watermarks, a CLI history writer carried through every transcript write path, owner probes over `SharedArrayBuffer` in the SQLite workers, native-login rechecks at spawn, prompt send and prompt-hook time, refresh-due handling, a compaction coverage commit and a terminal write context. All of that existed only to keep the proof alive.

## Solution

The session now records the first identified CLI account that runs it. That is a fingerprint of a resolved API key or token, a named OAuth account, or an attested native login. The account is checked once, when a turn is prepared:

- **No account recorded yet:** history replays. This includes turns from other runtimes and from an unidentified login. The first identified account is recorded.
- **Same account as recorded:** history replays.
- **Different or unidentified account after one was recorded:** that turn runs without saved history and the session is marked `mixed`. Every later CLI turn in the session also runs without saved history, including a switch back to the original account. `/new` (a new session id) starts clean.

`admitCliHistoryAccount` is the single owner of this decision. Everything that existed only to keep the coverage proof alive is deleted: the writer async context, coverage advance in all worker and actor write paths, owner probes, the `cliHistory` patch guard, the compaction coverage commit, the native-login recheck hooks (`assertReadable`, `assertPrivateInputCurrent`, `bindExecutionEnv`, `settleNativeLogin`, the refresh-due handling), the node dispatch readable hook, and the CLI-only terminal write context (`bindAgentRunTerminalWriteContext`, `runInAgentRunWriteContext`, `clearAgentRunTerminalWriteContext`).

**Stored data:** no schema change. Existing `known` records keep their account fingerprint, which is derived the same way as before. Old `unknown` records mean "no proof", so they are treated as no account recorded. The new `mixed` state is never read as `known` by older binaries, so a downgrade fails closed.

**Accepted edge case:** if a chat runs on an unidentified login first and an identified account second, the unidentified turns replay to that account. These are the same session's own turns, and every other runtime already replays them.

## Impact

- Switching a chat from Gemini or Codex to `claude-cli` now carries its history into the fresh Claude session.
- Native Claude logins without the attestation opt-in now recover history in chats that no other identified account has run.
- An account change still keeps the earlier account's history out of the prompt. The transcript itself is untouched, and Claude can still read it through `sessions_history` when tool policy allows.
- Production code: **+455 −1,678 (net −1,223)**. Tests: net −2,102. Docs updated in `docs/gateway/cli-backends.md` and the anthropic plugin help text.

## Evidence

**Live E2E.** Each side ran on an isolated scratch Gateway with a real Gemini model and a real `claude-cli` (Claude Code 2.x) on an Anthropic API-key profile pinned with `sessions.patch` `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6@anthropic:manual`.

**Journey 1:** 10 Gemini turns that set `GOAL_TOKEN aurora-7` and `DEPLOY_REGION QUARTZ-ZETA-41`, then a switch to Claude asking for both values without using tools.

| | base `04d1dd10d05e` | head |
|---|---|---|
| Claude answer | `NOT_IN_CONTEXT` | `GOAL_TOKEN: aurora-7 \| DEPLOY_REGION: QUARTZ-ZETA-41` |
| first Claude prompt | current message only, refused (`auth-unknown`) | `<conversation_history>` envelope, 30,874 chars, both facts, no tool calls |

**Journey 2:** key A stores `SECRET_A`, then the session switches to a different key B, then back to A.

- **Base and head:** key B's fresh session received no history; head logged `refused ... auth-unknown`, and B's prompt was 95 characters with no `SECRET_A`.
- **Back on key A:** the run resumed A's own native Claude session, which already held the secret. Nothing was replayed.

**Tests:**
- New: `history-boundary.test.ts`, which covers other-runtime replay, the A→B→A no-laundering case, an unidentified login after a recorded account, `/new`, and named versus identity-less OAuth. Also `prepare-native-history.test.ts`, which covers an unidentified native login.

fix: show menus and tooltips in the Linux app (#202500)

Root cause: ui/src/components/solid/overlay.css:184 (base) Every anchored menu, popover, picker and tooltip entered through an `@starting-style` CSS transition while its `position-try-fallbacks` were active. WebKitGTK 2.50 restarts that transition on every rendering update, so it never leaves currentTime 0: the surface stays at opacity 0 and the renderer keeps re-rendering.

Fixes #202467

Thanks @Mezetix for the detailed report, render-path matrix and follow-up observations.

## What Problem This Solves

In the Linux app (WebKitGTK), opening the Sessions "Filter & sort" menu, the composer "+" menu or any tooltip showed nothing, or flashed and vanished. The reporter's renderer also spun one core at 100% and the UI stopped responding. The Inbox and the model picker kept working because they don't use this entry transition.

## User Impact

Menus, popovers, pickers and tooltips appear and close normally in the Linux app. Chromium, Firefox and Safari look the same as before: the same fade and scale, with the same durations and easing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared overlay styles now play the entry and exit as one-shot CSS animations, scoped to the lifecycle's `opening` and `closing` phases, instead of transitions. The lifecycle already waits for these animations before it settles, and placement fallbacks stay active, so menus still flip and fit near window edges. Surfaces that tuned the old transition (pickers, tooltips, the composer settings popovers, the agent picker) now set the same values through the shared keyframes' variables. No WebKit check.

## Evidence

- WebKitGTK 2.50.4 (Ubuntu 22.04, the AppImage's base), bare page with no OpenClaw code:
  - Anchored popover with fallbacks and an `@starting-style` transition: stuck at opacity 0, currentTime 0, renderer 301-342 ticks in 3 s (3/3).
  - Same popover with a keyframe entry and exit: opacity 1, renderer 0 ticks (3/3).
  - Playwright Chromium 156 and WebKit 27.2: both forms settle, 0-1 ticks (3/3).
- Real Gateway and Control UI on WebKitGTK 2.50.4, before (2026.11.6) and after (this branch): see the proof comment.

Observed proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202500#issuecomment-7041253140 · Screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202500#issuecomment-7041257608

### Test changes

- `tooltip.test.ts` pins both tooltip motion durations to 0 ms for the whole file. The file runs under fake timers, which cannot advance CSS animations. The tooltip lifecycle waits for the new entry and exit animations before it settles (it never waited on the old transitions this way), so under fake timers a closing tooltip stayed open. The assertions are unchanged: the same open and closed outcomes. The real-time motion contract is still covered in `tooltip.browser.test.ts`, which asserts completion after the real opening animation.
- `tooltip.browser.test.ts` looks for the running `CSSAnimation` instead of a `CSSTransition` and reads `animationDuration`. It asserts the same outcome: "opened" is published only after the real entry finishes.
- No other test changed. Settled menus and popovers keep `scale: 1`, so the existing geometry waits still hold.

fix: give parents the sub-agent's answer, not its model-switch notice (#202540)

Root cause: `src/sessions/transcript-visible-record.ts:29` treated a same-run `model-fallback` delivery mirror as the run's answer, so when the model notice is saved after the answer, the newest-first result read hands the notice to the parent.

Fixes #202482
Supersedes #202486. Thanks @Hidetsugu55 for the report and the fix; this PR keeps your commits.

## What Problem This Solves

When a sub-agent's run ends with a model notice saved after its answer (for example "Selected model … restored (was …)."), the parent agent gets that notice as the child's result instead of the answer, and cannot continue the delegated work.

## User Impact

The parent receives the child's answer. The model notice stays in the child's own history, unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exact-run result selection now skips only `model-fallback` delivery mirrors, next to the existing skip for non-final message-tool mirrors. Transcript writes, chat history and every other delivery mirror kind (`channel-final`, `channel-final-suppressed`, final `message-tool-source-reply`, `cron-direct-delivery-context`, `subagent-completion-direct`, `plugin-notice`) are unchanged.

The predicate is read only by "what did run X answer" consumers: the parent completion announcement, `agents.wait` full-answer recovery and cron descendant follow-up (all through `readSubagentRunFinalAnswerUsing`), via the live, cold-storage and archived transcript readers. Chat history and display paths do not use it, so the notice is still shown in the child session.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway (source tier, isolated state, scripted local provider): a parent spawns a worker whose primary returns `404 model_not_found` and falls back; follow-up turns to the child then fall back again and finally restore the primary, which saves the answer and then the "restored" notice in the same run. Base: the parent's completion event carries `Selected model mock-openai/childa restored (was mock-openai/childb).` This PR: it carries `CHILD-PRIMARY-ANSWER-3`, and the child history still shows the notice. Control without fallback: unchanged (`CHILD-PRIMARY-ANSWER-1` on both). Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202540#issuecomment-7043164834
- Regression on the real SQLite transcript reader (`session-transcript-match.worker.test.ts`): fails on base (returns the notice), passes here.
- Tests: one regression replaces the two overlapping additions from #202486 (production +6/-1, tests +27/-0 against the merge base).

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert restores the old selection, no state or config is written. Blast radius: sub-agent result text delivered to parents (announce, `agents.wait`, cron follow-up) when a run's last transcript row is a model notice.

fix: show hosted model details in `models list` without a Gateway (#202490)

## What Problem This Solves

When no Gateway is running, `openclaw models list` never loads the saved hosted model catalog. A model the provider lists shows guessed limits (128000 or 200000 context instead of the published 524288 or 400000), and a new hosted model for a provider without a list endpoint stays invisible until some Gateway has run once.

## User Impact

- `models list` without a Gateway describes listed models with the hosted catalog, the same as the Gateway does.
- The provider's listing still decides which models exist: a model the listing omits stays hidden, and a typed reference still runs.
- No config, schema, stored row or pricing change.

Known limit, not changed here: changing `models.catalogRefresh.url` on a running Gateway still waits for the next scheduled check, up to six hours, so turns in that window record $0. Checking at once races the config reload's model-runtime publication. A follow-up will handle that.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Local catalog reads:** the prepared catalog owner now loads the saved hosted catalog before it builds rows, as Gateway startup does. Every catalog read without a Gateway gets it, not just `models list`. A process that already has it stays synchronous, so callers still join the owner published at call time.
- **Unchanged:** hosted catalog adoption already relists every credentialed provider, because replacement owners start without inventory. A new test pins that behavior. Native harness listings still wait for demand, so adoption does not start Codex or ACP processes.
- **Why the URL-change fix was dropped:** an earlier revision checked the new catalog at once and ran adoption alongside the config reload. In the replay, adoption won that race and left reply dispatch unpublished, so turns failed with `UNAVAILABLE` until restart. That is worse than the scheduled wait, so the revision was reverted. The scheduler and adoption code are back to base exactly.

## Evidence

Day-zero replay, base `e4c17c5dd441` vs this branch. Each run used an isolated Gateway with fresh state per case, a loopback hosted catalog with three new rows, and TLS mocks for api.abliteration.ai, api.together.xyz and chatgpt.com. CLI = `models list` with no Gateway.

| Case | base | branch |
|---|---|---|
| Static provider, hosted-only row | CLI: not listed, with or without `--refresh`. Gateway: listed 262144, runs, $3.0e-5 | CLI: listed 262144. Gateway: same. Runs, $3.0e-5 |
| Together listing includes the new ID | CLI `--refresh`: 128000 (guessed). Gateway: 524288. Runs, $6.0e-5 | CLI `--refresh`: 524288. Gateway: 524288. Runs, $6.0e-5 |
| Together listing omits the ID | CLI and Gateway: hidden. Typed turn runs, $6.0e-5 | CLI: hidden. Gateway: hidden, except one first read right after start in one of three runs (see note). Typed turn runs, $6.0e-5 |
| ChatGPT subscription, `/codex/models` lists it | CLI `--refresh`: 200000 (guessed). Gateway: 400000. Runs, $9.0e-5 | CLI `--refresh`: 400000. Gateway: 400000. Runs, $9.0e-5 |
| Running Gateway adopts a new catalog on schedule | Applied; Together relisted in the same second; listed 524288; $6.0e-5 | Same |

The branch column comes from head `0c1cd5ae`. The current head differs only by restoring the scheduler and adoption files to base, so the catalog read path is the same code.

Note on the omitted-ID row: a Gateway's first `models.list` right after start can show an omitted ID before the saved listing applies. That was recorded on main before this PR, and this PR doesn't touch the Gateway path, which already had the hosted catalog at startup.

Tests:
- New tests, red on base and green here:
  - a local catalog read carries hosted metadata for a listed ID;
  - a local read lists a static provider's hosted-only row.
- New test that passes on base too: adoption relists an unchanged provider.
- Consumer suites are green: prepared catalog resources and outside-workspace, `models list`, model catalog, prepared model runtime, remote inference, update startup schedule, prefix stability.
- `tsgo:core` and `check:test-types` report one error, in `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts` (`revalidateOnCompletion`). It is inherited from base and in a file this PR doesn't touch.

Merge danger: a two-way door. It writes no state and changes no config, schema or published contract, so a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: model lists read without a Gateway (the CLI, TUI, cron and other standalone catalog readers). Gateway behavior is unchanged.

fix(ai): keep steering context where it was first sent on Responses routes (#198736)

## What was wrong

On custom (non-native) OpenAI Responses routes, a message sent while the agent was in the middle of a tool loop (a steer) rewrote input the provider had already seen. The steer's runtime-context note was moved back in front of tool calls that earlier requests in the same run had already sent, so the provider prompt cache missed from that point on.

Example (Control UI, one chat, a six-step tool loop, a steer after round two):

- request before the steer: `[user, context, call 1, result 1]`
- request after the steer on `main`: `[user, context, steer context, call 1, result 1, ...]`: item 3 changed from a tool call to a message, so everything after it was re-read uncached.

## Fix

The Responses replay converter still moves a turn's own context note back to its user (needed for async replay and for routes that keep the note at the tail). A later note that sits right before a user message is that steering user's note: it now stays where it was first sent. Production code: +6/-4 lines in one file.

## Numbers

Real Gateway, Control UI, custom Responses route to `api.openai.com` (`gpt-6.1-sol`), same journey on both sides. Each tool result is about 6k tokens.

| Request | `main` uncached / cached | This PR uncached / cached |
|---|---|---|
| tool round 2 | 6,047 / 31,494 | 6,047 / 31,500 |
| **first request after the steer** | **12,282 / 31,494** | **6,238 / 37,544** |
| tool rounds 4-6 (each) | 6,047 | 6,047 |
| follow-up chat turn | 750 | 750 |
| prefix rewritten | yes, at item 6 | never |

The extra ~6k uncached tokens on `main` are one tool round re-read after every steer; it grows with the size of the tool results already in the run.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

- A steer from the Control UI carries the requester context, so it gets its own runtime-context note, stored right before the steering user message, after the tool rounds that already ran (`materializeSteeringRuntimeContext`, retained by `agent-session-base.ts`).
- `openai-responses-replay-messages-internal.ts` anchored every note to the preceding user message (#138575). For the steering note that inserts a new `message` item in front of `function_call` items that earlier requests had already sent.
- The anchoring is still correct for a turn's own note (async replay, where the note was persisted after the response fragments it preceded on the wire; and routes that move the current note to the tail). The fix only skips it for a second note that directly precedes a user message.
- Single-person CLI `chat.send` steers carry no requester context and so no note; the bug needs a Control UI (or other requester-bound) steer.

</details>

refactor(gateway): delete in-run operator authority watchers (#202442)

## Problem

Retained runs (queued, child and system turns started for an operator) kept watching for role-assignment changes, OpenClaw ID changes and device revocation while they ran, and cancelled the run mid-flight when one fired. That is the in-flight re-check the authority rule removes: check once when work starts; a started request may finish; queued, retried and replayed work checks again when it starts.

## Fix

- `operator-run-cancellation.ts`: delete the role-assignment and OpenClaw ID subscriptions, the recheck callback, the revocation controller, the composed signal, wrapper reference counts and wrapper device binding. The retained-run helper now admits once when the work starts and releases on failure.
- `device-revocation.ts`: delete the unused in-run revocation-listener export, listener set and notifications. Live device indexing and invalidation stay.
- `followup-turn-execution.ts`: a next-start refusal ends the turn through the existing pre-model run lifecycle emitter (`createAgentLifecycleTerminalBackstop`), so an active Goal pauses with "Paused after an error. Resume to continue." exactly as before, without aborting authority shared with already-started siblings.

## Behavior

- A started run finishes after its requester is demoted or a device is revoked. The next turn checks again and is refused visibly.
- Unchanged: queued replay of an allowed sender runs once; a revoked sender's replay runs zero effects and zero model requests; Stop still cancels.

Production: -60 lines. Test: -29 lines.

## Evidence

Focused tests: started-run / next-start / Stop, Goal (paused after demotion, same as base), queued replay product test with effect counts (allowed 1, revoked 0/0), question flow. oxlint and oxfmt on touched files. Hosted CI for types and broad suites.

fix: open the recorded run from an automation's Inspect run link (#201899) Root cause: `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts:356` (at d902b29bce59) built the announcement's Inspect run link from the run's temporary session alias (`resolveControlUiSessionUrl(..., { sessionKey: params.runSessionKey, exactKey: true })`), and `removeCronRunContinuationSessionIfIdle` (`src/cron/run-continuation-cleanup.ts`) deletes that alias as soon as the run settles, so every isolated run's link opens an empty, missing session. Related: #155588 (fixes the channel announcement Inspect link; the "agent finished" web push path stays open) Thanks @vit-pavlenko for the report, @Oldrich333 and @dalsoop for the follow-up details (dalsoop's comment traced this exact channel-link path), and @omerough for the fix. ## What Problem This Solves When a scheduled automation that runs in its own session finishes, its chat announcement ends with an **Inspect run** link. That link points at a temporary chat session that is cleaned up as soon as the run settles, so opening it shows an empty "No messages yet" chat instead of the run. ## User Impact User impact: Inspect links on automation announcements now open that exact run in Automations history, for scheduled and manual runs, including after the temporary session is gone. ## Why This Change Was Made Completion and failure notifications for command and script automations, and failure alerts, already link to the recorded run through the existing Automation run URL, with the run id built from the scheduler's start time (`job.state.runningAtMs`). The isolated announcement now uses the same URL and the same start time. Run history records that same value: the claim sets `runningAtMs` and the run receipt's `startedAtMs` to the same `nowMs` in one transaction (`src/cron/store/run-queue.worker.ts`), and history stores the receipt's start as `runAtMs`; the Automations page selects the run by that value (`cronRunEntryMatchesLink`). Model-switch retries stay inside the same claim; a scheduled retry is a new claim with its own history row and its own link. Jobs the scheduler never claimed (synthetic hook, plugin and channel-join jobs) have no recorded run and keep the session link. Only URL generation changes; execution, retention and the session lifecycle are unchanged. Main-session automations are not affected. Not in this PR: the generic "OpenClaw agent finished" web push notification (`src/gateway/event-web-push.ts`) carries no destination at all, which is a separate owner. Run history's own transcript view already reads the recorded run (#148211). ## Evidence Real Gateway run (isolated state, scripted local model, fixture channel that records every announcement, recurring isolated automation plus one manual run, main-session automation as control), each Inspect link opened in the Control UI in Chromium: [proof comment with screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201899#issuecomment-7037243560), [re-run on the current head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201899#issuecomment-7037698942). | Before (base) | After (this PR) | |---|---| | | | - Base: both isolated links open `/chat/main/cron//run/` with "No messages yet"; the run alias is gone from the session list. - Head: scheduled and manual run links each open Automations with "Showing the linked run." and exactly that run highlighted; each link's start time equals the run's recorded `runAtMs`. - Control: the main-session automation's announcement is unchanged (no Inspect link on either side). - `src/cron/isolated-agent.delivery-awareness.test.ts`: the two link-target tests fail on the merge base and pass on this head; the dispatch suites that use loose job fixtures pass too. Merge danger: two-way door; a revert restores the old link. Only the text of the Inspect link in isolated automation announcements changes; no state, config or contract changes. fix: keep web_search via Tool Search working on chat-completions providers that reject assistant prefill (#202436)

Root cause: `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-params.ts:300` gave the Chat Completions history converter only the tools in the outgoing `tools` list, so a Tool Search directory tool that a direct call hydrates (kept out of that list so the tool block stays cache-stable) was treated as an unavailable historical tool, and `openai-completions-messages.ts:185`/`:287` replayed its call and result as assistant text, leaving the follow-up request ending with an assistant message.

Fixes #202415

Thanks @paulsimmondsplato for the detailed report, including the request shapes and the `exec` control.

## What Problem This Solves

With Tool Search in directory mode on an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions provider (for example LiteLLM in front of Anthropic), every turn that called `web_search` failed: the follow-up request carried the search as assistant text instead of a tool call and result, and ended with that assistant message. Anthropic rejects that as assistant prefill, so the turn errored. This started in 2026.11.6.

## User Impact

Turns that use a Tool Search directory tool such as `web_search` work again on chat-completions providers that require the conversation to end with a user or tool message. Tools that are truly no longer available in a conversation's history still replay as text, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

#174797 (8fc3509a66ad, first shipped in 2026.11.6) made the request builder replay calls to tools missing from the outgoing tool list as text, so strict providers stop rejecting hallucinated or removed tools. Hydrated directory tools are never in that list by design, so they were caught by the same check. The embedded runner now tells the request builder which directory tools are callable in this run, and the builder treats those as current. The tool list itself is unchanged, and the projection is the same on every request of the session, so prompt-cache prefixes stay append-only.

## Evidence

Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`), isolated state, openai-completions provider pointed at a loopback fixture that records request shapes and returns Anthropic's prefill 400 for an assistant tail, `tools.toolSearch.mode: "directory"`, bundled SearXNG `web_search` pointed at the fixture. Same session: a `read` turn, a `web_search` turn, then a restart with `tools.deny: ["read"]` and one more turn.

- Base `217bb899f09f`: the `web_search` follow-up ends `assistant text:"[tool call id=... name=web_search]" "[tool result ...]"`, fixture answers 400, turn fails with `LLM request rejected: This model does not support assistant message prefill`.
- Candidate: the same request ends `assistant tool_calls[web_search]`, `tool tool_call_id=...`; the turn answers. `web_search` is still absent from `tools` on every request.
- Controls: the `read` call (directly exposed) is `tool_calls[read]` + `tool` on both; after `read` is denied, its history replays as text on both (the #174797 behavior), and on the candidate the earlier `web_search` exchange stays native, matching the previous request.
- New regression in `openai-completions-replay.test.ts` fails on base and passes here; `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` passes.

Observed proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202436#issuecomment-7037801731

Merge danger: two-way door. No stored state, config or published contract changes; a revert restores the 2026.11.6 projection. Blast radius: embedded runs with Tool Search directory mode on chat-completions providers. A strict provider that rejects tool calls to tools absent from `tools` would now see those calls natively, which is how 2026.10.33 sent them.

fix(openai): send the numeric OpenClaw release as the ChatGPT version header (#202427)

Follow-up to #202380.

## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT gates subscription models in two places: the `/codex/models?client_version=` listing and the `version` header on `/responses` turns. Since #202380 the listing sends the numeric OpenClaw release (`YYYY.M.P`, falling back to `99.0.0`), but OpenClaw-harness turns still send the raw runtime version. Prerelease and dev builds therefore send values the backend has never been probed with (`2026.11.5-beta.1`) or that likely fail the model gate (`unknown`, `0.0.0-dev`). Then a model can be listed but its turn rejected. On 2026-11-18, a turn with `version: 0.164.0` returned HTTP 400 for `gpt-6.2-sol`.

## Solution

- Provider attribution now owns the ChatGPT gate value. For the `openai` provider, the `version` header is the numeric release (year 2026 or later), or `99.0.0`.
- `User-Agent` keeps the full build (`openclaw/2026.11.5-beta.1`), so OpenAI still sees the real version. It is not a gate input.
- `extensions/openai/base-url.ts` reads that header for `client_version` instead of repeating the rule, so the list and the turn send the same value by construction.
- Other providers keep their headers unchanged, including xAI, which shares the OpenAI header shape.
- Codex-harness turns are unchanged: the Codex binary sends its own version.

## User Impact

- Stable releases: no change. `2026.11.5` was already numeric.
- Beta builds: turns send `2026.11.5` instead of `2026.11.5-beta.1`.
- Dev and source builds without a calendar version: turns send `99.0.0` instead of a placeholder. Turns on newly launched models then pass the same gate as the listing.

## Evidence

- **Red on main, green on the fix:** `src/agents/provider-attribution.test.ts` › "sends ChatGPT the numeric OpenClaw release …". On main, 4 of 5 cases fail (`2026.11.5-beta.1`, `2026.11.5-1+build.abc`, `unknown`, `0.0.0-dev`); the plain `2026.11.5` case passes on both. Each case also checks that `User-Agent` keeps the full build.
- **Consumers green:** `provider-attribution`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `openai-transport-stream.base`, `stream-wrappers/openai`, `openai-codex-discovery`, `provider-live-listing.contract`, OpenAI TTS, realtime browser auth and device-code tests.
- **Gates:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `check:test-types` pass. `ocx build --dts` and the packed release smoke (`scripts/release-check.ts`) pass.
- **End to end** (isolated Gateway from source, fresh ChatGPT device-code login): `models.list` returned 11 subscription models with outcome `ready`, including `gpt-6.2-sol` and `gpt-6.2-astra`. A real turn on `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` returned `NVH_OK`.
- **Live values:** the 2026-11-18 probe with a real ChatGPT login returned HTTP 200 on `/responses` for `gpt-6.2-sol` with `version` set to `2026.11.5` and to `99.0.0`, the only two shapes this change sends.
- **Not proven live:** a beta or dev runtime version. The dev tooling strips `OPENCLAW_*` from the Gateway environment, so the source Gateway reported the stable `2026.11.5`. The attribution test covers those inputs.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: no state, config or contract changes, and a revert restores the raw header. Blast radius: the `version` header on OpenAI-provider requests (ChatGPT and platform routes) for prerelease and dev builds. Stable builds send identical headers.

fix: stop empty automation checklists from recording failed runs and "did not start" notices (#202390)

Root cause: src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts:220 (and its twin in src/cron/session-run.ts:224) returns `status: "skipped"` when `skipIfScratchEmpty` finds an explicitly empty checklist, and every skipped run is a failure downstream: `resolveCronCompletionStatus` maps skipped to `completionStatus: "failed"`, run storage records it as failed, it counts toward skipped-run alerts, and the Gateway posts "did not start" for any skipped run without an admission-deferral reason.

Fixes #202350. Thanks @herosuncy for the clear report and repro.

## What Problem This Solves

A heartbeat-style automation with "Skip empty scratch" on and the default comments-only checklist skips every interval, as intended. But each skip is recorded as a failed run, and the owner conversation gets `Automation "heartbeat-main" did not start: Automation scratch is explicitly empty. Check automation history, resolve the cause, then run it again.` every 30 minutes. An idle heartbeat looks broken, and the only workaround was disabling it.

## User Impact

An empty checklist now completes quietly: run history shows `status: "ok"`, `completionStatus: "succeeded"` and the same summary `Automation scratch is explicitly empty`, the model is still not called, no "did not start" notice is posted, and it no longer counts toward skipped-run alerts. Real start failures (for example a model that is not configured) still record a failed run and still post the notice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The skip is a deliberate "nothing to do" decision, not a failed start. The cron outcome model has no non-failure skipped state, but it already has one for a run that completes with nothing to deliver: `status: "ok"` with a delivery suppression reason (the same outcome a heartbeat turn with nothing to report records). Both empty-scratch producers now return that outcome with the existing `"empty"` suppression reason, so completion, storage, failure alerts and the conversation notice all treat it as a quiet completion through their existing rules. The primary webhook already ignored skips that never started (#200032); its guard now ignores any non-error run that never started, so the empty-checklist summary is still not POSTed as output. No new status, field, wording or stored shape.

Behavior notes: `lastRunStatus` for these ticks is `ok` instead of `skipped`, and `consecutiveSkipped` no longer grows. A one-shot (`at`) job with `deleteAfterRun` and an empty checklist is now deleted like any other succeeded one-shot instead of being kept disabled; it was already consumed and never replayed.

History: the skipped return came with the Doctor heartbeat migration (ec5d369a6f66, #179387). It predates the "did not start" notice, and #194276 only kept the empty-scratch notice as an untouched control while fixing active-hours/busy deferrals, so recording it as a failure was never a product decision.

## Evidence

Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`), isolated state, deterministic local Responses provider that logs every model request, and a process-local Gateway clock stepped past each due time (the system clock is untouched). Job from the issue: every 30 min, `sessionTarget: session:agent:main:main`, `skipIfScratchEmpty: true`, scratch = the issue's comments-only template.

| | main e99e8482f8a8 | this PR 0519148ecf96 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 scheduled ticks of heartbeat-main | `skipped` / `failed` x2 | `ok` / `succeeded` x2, same summary |
| job state | `consecutiveSkipped: 2` | `consecutiveSkipped: 0` |
| "did not start" notices in the session | 0 -> 2 | 0 -> 0 |
| model requests during the ticks | 1 -> 1 | 1 -> 1 |
| control: checklist with a real item | runs the turn (`ok`/`succeeded`, model called) | same |
| control: model override on an unconfigured provider | `error`/`failed` + "did not start" notice | same |

Observed output: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202390#issuecomment-7035458979

- `src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts`: the existing scratch-empty one-shot case now asserts `ok`/`succeeded` history and no skip counter; it fails on main and passes here.
- `src/cron/service.trigger-eval.test.ts`: the existing webhook case still proves no POST for the empty checklist.
- Production: +7/-4 lines in three files. Tests: +9/-4 (the one regression).

Merge danger: two-way door. Nothing is migrated; a revert restores skipped/failed recording for later ticks, and rows written meanwhile stay `ok`/`succeeded`. Blast radius: automations with `skipIfScratchEmpty` and an empty checklist (run history status, completion, notices, skip alerts, `deleteAfterRun` one-shots).

fix(openai): list ChatGPT models with the OpenClaw release version (#202380)

Supersedes #202284. Restores the approach of #201493. Related: #201130.

## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT subscription model discovery calls `/backend-api/codex/models?client_version=<X>`, and the backend hides every model whose `minimal_client_version` is above X. On main (#202284), X comes from a lookup of the latest `@openai/codex` on npm, cached in memory for six hours. That puts a registry request (1 s budget) on the model-listing path. A failed or slow lookup lists at the bundled 0.169.0 floor and can hide newly launched models. The in-memory cache also does not survive a restart or eviction.

## Solution

- List with the OpenClaw release that OpenClaw-harness Responses turns already send as the `version` header (provider attribution). The list and the turn use one value from one owner.
- Send only the numeric `YYYY.M.P` part (year 2026 or later). For example, `2026.11.5-beta.1` lists as `2026.11.5`. Anything else (`unknown`, `0.0.0-dev`, a bad `OPENCLAW_VERSION` override, or a proxy without attribution headers) lists as `99.0.0`.
- Treat an empty subscription list as a failed listing. A ChatGPT account always has models, so an empty 200 response keeps the last good rows instead of replacing them. API-key access-program discovery, where an empty list is valid, is unchanged.
- Delete the npm lookup, the six-hour cache, the 0.169.0 floor, the floor contract test, and the test mocks that existed only for them. Production: +19 / −74 lines.
- Keep the Responses `version` header unchanged. Keep Codex binary selection and update behavior unchanged.

Why this replaces the earlier designs:
- #201130 and #202284 needed a network request for a value the backend only compares numerically. Any version at or above a model's minimum shows the model.
- Peer clients hardcode a value for the same reason: Hermes `99.0.0`, Zed `0.999.0`, Crush `999.0.0`.
- #202284's concern was that an OpenClaw version goes into a Codex-version parameter. The same value already passes the same gate on every Responses turn, and an npm-latest value does not describe the binary that runs a turn either.
- A version starting with 2026 stays above every Codex 0.x release, so new models appear on launch day without a lookup.
- The version check is stricter than #201493's: suffixes are dropped instead of sent, because no live probe has tested a prerelease string.

Accepted edge cases (code comment in `base-url.ts`):
- A Codex-harness binary older than a listed model fails that turn with the existing update instructions and **Start a new session** (#201130). npm-latest had the same tradeoff.
- An old OpenClaw release can list a future model whose request shape it does not support yet. Every fixed-version and npm-latest approach has this.

I also considered an omp-style background npm refresh with persistence (oh-my-pi `codex-version.ts`). Plugin keyed state is unavailable in the catalog worker threads where discovery runs (`Shared-state admission requires the host broker`). An in-memory variant still needed a network request and reset to the floor on every restart.

## User Impact

- ChatGPT subscription users see newly launched models without an OpenClaw release, without a network lookup, and without depending on npm availability.
- Listing makes one request: the ChatGPT `/models` call.
- A transient empty model list from ChatGPT no longer clears the model picker.

## Evidence

- **Red on main, green on the fix** (`extensions/openai/openai-codex-discovery.test.ts`):
  - The version-table cases fail on main, which makes two requests (npm, then `/models`). The fix makes exactly one, to chatgpt.com, with the expected `client_version`.
  - The empty-list case fails on main (`expected ['ready'] to deeply equal ['unavailable']`) and passes on the fix.
  - Main result: 14 of 16 failed (the 2 GPT-6.1 Sol cases pass on both).
- **Focused suites green:** `openai-codex-discovery`, `openai-provider`, `openai-provider.codex-catalog`, `openai-api-key-catalog`, `platform-access-programs`, `base-url`, `src/plugins/contracts/provider-live-listing.contract.test.ts`, `test/openai-model-discovery-auth-order.test.ts`, `test/model-account-catalog-authority.integration.test.ts`.
- **Live, real ChatGPT Pro login (2026-11-18 probe):**
  - `client_version` 2026.11.5, 0.166.0, 0.169.0 and 99.0.0 return the same 13 models, including `gpt-6.2-sol` and `gpt-6.2-astra` (`minimal_client_version` 0.166.0).
  - 0.164.0 and 0.165.0 hide GPT-6.2. 0.0.0 returns a frozen legacy list of 7 models.
  - `/responses` with `version: 2026.11.5` on `gpt-6.2-sol` returns 200.
- **End to end on this branch** (isolated Gateway from source, fresh ChatGPT device-code login, nothing live touched):
  - `models.list` returned 11 subscription models with outcome `ready`, including `gpt-6.2-sol` (1.05M context) and `gpt-6.2-astra`.
  - The Gateway log shows no `registry.npmjs.org` request.
  - A real turn on `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` returned `CXV_OK2`.
  - The same account listed identical models at 0.169.0 and 0.171.0 earlier today. No live model is currently gated between the bundled pin and npm latest, so the "floor hides a model" case was proven in tests, not live.
- **Not proven live:** a Gateway with `OPENCLAW_VERSION=unknown` (the dev tooling strips `OPENCLAW_*`). The version table covers that fallback.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: no state, schema, config or published contract changes, and a revert fully restores the npm lookup. Blast radius: ChatGPT subscription model listing for OpenAI OAuth and token profiles. API-key listing, Responses headers and Codex binary selection are unchanged.

fix(msteams): deliver the rest of a reply when Teams rejects the stream end (#202368)

Root cause: extensions/msteams/src/messenger.ts:120 renders reply text through `getMSTeamsRuntime().channel.text.chunkMarkdownTextWithMode`, but a late Teams stream settlement (`reply-dispatcher.ts:455`, run from `onSettled`) renders its fallback outside the plugin instance runtime slot added in #144252, so the lookup throws `MSTeams runtime not initialized` (src/plugin-sdk/runtime-store.ts:84) and the fallback reply is dropped without a log line.

Related: #59731, #18636, #56040 (earlier lost Teams replies; none proves this exact regression)

## What Problem This Solves

When Teams rejects the end of a streamed reply (for example a partial-mode answer with a Markdown table, where the rendered table no longer matches the already-streamed raw text), OpenClaw is meant to send the rest of the answer as a normal message. Since v2026.10.1 that recovery message is silently dropped, so the user only sees a cut-off, never-finalized stream.

## User Impact

Teams users get the rest of the answer as a message when the stream cannot be completed, instead of a truncated reply with no error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Teams reply renderer now uses the pure SDK chunker (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-chunking`), which is the same function the runtime chunker re-exports, so rendering no longer depends on the plugin runtime being reachable. Output is unchanged. The test file no longer installs a runtime stub, so the render tests prove rendering works without one; the unused runtime chunker stubs are removed.

Other late msteams send paths checked: the dispatcher's failure system event uses the `core` captured at dispatcher creation, and `sendMSTeamsMessages` reads the runtime only through `user-agent.ts` (already caught). No other late path uses this lookup.

## Evidence

Isolated `ocx src` Gateway with the real msteams plugin, a Teams connector fixture that enforces Microsoft's documented streaming rule (403 ContentStreamNotAllowed when streamed content changes), and a scripted model (two tool calls, then a table answer) in a 1:1 chat, partial streaming mode.

- Before (main e72860564b): the stream shows "Tools found: | Tool | Scope | ... | whoami | Graph" and is never closed; no fallback message reaches the connector. A temporary log line in a scratch copy showed the fallback (the rest of the table, ending with the `list | MCP` row) was built and render threw `MSTeams runtime not initialized`.
- After: the same run sends the remainder of the table once as a normal message (HTTP 201 from the connector).
- Controls: a successful progress-mode stream sends no extra message; partial-mode plain text is identical before and after.
- Unit: `messenger.test.ts` fails on main with `MSTeams runtime not initialized` and passes with the fix.

Observed proof lines (connector request logs, base and candidate): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202368#issuecomment-7034785606

Merge danger: two-way door, a revert fully undoes it; no state, config or contract change. Blast radius: Microsoft Teams reply rendering only.
