refactor(agents): tighten the system prompt and render a compact skills catalog (#202326)

## Problem

OpenClaw's generated system prompt is several times larger than comparable harnesses before any user context is added (measured from source on 2026-11-20):

| Harness | Stock base prompt |
|---|---:|
| T3 Code (wrapper overlay) | ~1.4k chars |
| Pi | ~1.6k chars |
| OpenCode (Claude) | ~1.8k chars |
| Hermes | ~3.5–4k chars |
| Oh My Pi | ~10–13k chars |
| **OpenClaw, full toolset (main)** | **19,481 chars** |

Two causes:

1. **Restated rules.** The same policy appeared in two or three sections. Examples: subagent waiting (`sessions_yield`, never busy-poll), `isolated`/`fork` context, image/video `status`, ACP routing, approval flow, and `message(send)` repeats. Each restatement was patched in separately over time.
2. **The skills catalog kept Pi's XML shape after `skills_read` made it unnecessary.** Every skill rendered as a 6-line `<skill>` block with a full `<location>` path, plus path-loading prose. `skills_read(name)` resolves by name, so the paths and that prose only cost context. 150 skills came to about 40k chars.

## Solution

- Rewrote the generated sections tersely and folded each repeated rule into one owner:
  - execution bias and promised work
  - runtime context, care, and credential safety
  - OpenClaw control and documentation
  - messaging and UI presentation
  - Control UI embed and side chat
  - delegation/ACP, and media generation
- Every decision those sections encode is preserved (checked by the behavioral A/B below). Tests that only pinned prompt phrasing were removed rather than rewritten. Behavioral checks remain, for example: the prompt-advertised `gateway` update action still executes, and guidance still appears on every prompt surface.
- When `skills_read` is available, `buildSkillsSection` renders `<available_skills>` as one `- "name": description` line per skill (with a `location_note` if present). Names are JSON-quoted and byte-exact because `skills_read` matches them with `===` and a name may contain `: ` or ` (` and drops the path-loading prose.
  - Sessions without `skills_read` (path reads, CLI backends) keep the XML catalog with locations.
  - The stored snapshot format and every catalog parser are unchanged.
  - `system-prompt-report` counts both shapes.
- Production code is net negative.

**Design note.** The compact catalog is rendered by rewriting the canonical XML catalog in `buildSkillsSection`, not by a second catalog owner: the stored skills snapshot is built before tool policy is known, and only the prompt builder knows whether `skills_read` is available. The snapshot format and every snapshot parser (session snapshots, Code Mode, sandbox/worker resource transfer, Doctor) are unchanged. `system-prompt-report` accepts either the rendered or the stored catalog, so `/context`, CLI backends and embedded runs report the same entries.

## Impact

Rendered prompt size (full toolset, webchat):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| No skills | 19,481 chars | 14,031 chars (−28%) |
| 150 real installed skills | 60,581 chars | 31,925 chars (−47%) |

Prompt-cache layout is unchanged. `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, the cache-prefix tests and the prompt snapshots pass.

## Evidence

**Behavioral A/B through the real prompt builder** (base `da816e2190ca` vs head, 150 real skills, 12 cases: 4 skill-routing + 8 encoded decisions — `sessions_yield`, media `status`, `openclaw` for config, never self-`/approve`, no repeat after final `message(send)`, `portal_show`, `git worktree` over clone, no implicit `update.cleanup`):

| Model | base score | head score | base input tokens | head input tokens |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `openai/gpt-6-luna` | 12/12 | 12/12 | 15,085 | 7,301 (−52%) |
| `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` | 12/12 | 12/12 | 23,600 | 12,081 (−49%) |

**E2E: real embedded agent turns** (`openclaw agent exec --code-mode direct`, isolated state, `openai/gpt-6-luna`, 10 real skills in the workspace, 3 tasks × 3 trials per arm):

| | base (`main`) | head |
|---|---:|---:|
| Runs completed | 9/9 | 9/9 |
| Loaded the matching skill before acting | 7/9 (tmux skipped the skill 2/3) | 9/9 |
| First-request prompt tokens (median) | 15,919 | 13,594 (−15%) |
| System prompt chars (median) | 37,186 | 28,265 (−24%) |
| Skills catalog chars (27 skills) | 8,594 | 3,676 (−57%) |

Tasks: Hyderabad weather (`weather`), live tmux sessions (`tmux`), Node heap-snapshot procedure (`node-inspect-debugger`). fix(gateway): refuse a retained continuation at start when its operator's device was revoked (#202318)

Problem: a retained continuation restored from a tokenless (trusted-proxy) operator carried no device in its snapshot, so its own revocation capture never joined the device index; if the operator's device was revoked before the continuation started, the start check passed and the replayed send ran. On main a post-dispatch check then replaced the response with a refusal notice, so the requester was told "refused" while the target had received the send.

fix(discord): transcribe voice with live config and gpt-transcribe (#202362)

## Problem

Discord voice meeting transcripts collect junk lines for clips with no speech: coughs, wind, breathing, keyboard and low noise-gate hiss. In one real meeting, roughly 40% of stored utterances were junk ("咳咳", "Cough", "안녕하십니까?", "こんにちは", "deciembre", Hebrew, Arabic and Polish words), even though `tools.media.audio.language` was `en`. Switching `tools.media.models` to `gpt-transcribe` did not help: the junk continued until the Gateway restarted.

Two causes:

1. **The default OpenAI file-transcription model hallucinates on non-speech.** `gpt-4o-transcribe` (the current default) returned text for every one of 600 Opus-round-tripped noise clips (ESC-50 coughs, wind, breathing, keyboard, sneezes, laughter, clicks, knocks, footsteps, coloured hiss). Sending `language=en` did not change that. `gpt-transcribe` returned empty text (and `languages: []`) for 98–100% of the same clips while keeping 99–100% of speech. `gpt-4o-transcribe` is also scheduled for shutdown.
2. **Discord voice ignored hot-reloaded config.** `DiscordVoiceManager` received the Gateway's startup `cfg` and passed that object down to recording, STT, agent turns and TTS. A config hot reload published a new runtime snapshot, but voice transcription kept the old one, so the model change never reached Discord voice.

A third, smaller issue: `gpt-transcribe` takes a `languages` list instead of the single `language` field, and OpenAI's guide says not to send both. We sent `language`.

## Solution

- **Default model:** the OpenAI plugin's batch audio-transcription default is now `gpt-transcribe` (`default-models.ts` and manifest `mediaUnderstandingProviderMetadata`). Explicitly configured models, including `gpt-4o-transcribe` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, keep working unchanged.
- **Language hint:** the shared OpenAI-compatible transcription helper accepts a `languageField` (`"language"` by default). The OpenAI plugin, which owns the model behaviour, selects `languages[]` for `gpt-transcribe` models. Other OpenAI-compatible providers (Groq, DeepInfra, Mistral, SenseAudio, OpenRouter, ClawRouter) are unchanged.
- **Live config for voice:** `DiscordVoiceManager` now takes `readConfig` (the same runtime-config reader the Discord monitor already uses for live policy) instead of a `cfg` snapshot. Voice reads config at each use: per-clip STT, the audio budget at join, agent turns, TTS, realtime session start and text fallback. Hot-reloaded `tools.media.*` settings apply to the next clip.
- Docs: default model, `languages` behaviour, and a note that voice STT follows config changes without a restart.

No audio heuristics or transcript text filters were added. An audio-only voicing gate was measured first (2,860 clips) and could not separate voiced coughs/laughter from single words without dropping real words, so it was dropped in favour of the model fix.

## Impact

- New installs and configs without an explicit audio model transcribe with `gpt-transcribe`; noise-only Discord voice clips produce no utterance.
- Operators can change the transcription model or language for a running Discord voice session without restarting the Gateway.
- Explicit `gpt-4o-transcribe` configs keep their current behaviour (including its hallucinations) until changed.

## Evidence

**Tests (red on base, green on head)**
- `extensions/discord/src/voice/transcripts-recording.test.ts` › "transcribes with media config hot-reloaded after the voice session started": base sends the second clip with the startup model (`gpt-4o-transcribe`), head with the reloaded `gpt-transcribe`.
- `extensions/openai/media-understanding-provider.test.ts`: default `gpt-transcribe` with a `languages[]` field and no `language`; explicit `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` keeps `language`. 5 cases red on base.
- `ocx test extensions/discord/src/voice extensions/discord/src/monitor extensions/openai src/media-understanding`: green. `check:test-types`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files: green.

**Real STT through the Discord voice recording path, base vs head**

The QA Discord lease has no voice channel, so a real Discord voice session was not possible. Closest available path: the Discord voice manager harness with real recording, WAV writing and transcript capture; decoded PCM from real Opus round trips (libopus, 48 kHz stereo, VoIP, 64 kbit/s); and the OpenAI plugin's real `transcribeOpenAiAudio` request to the live API. The Discord gateway, voice transport and Opus decoder were simulated by the harness. 22 clips per phase, one speaker, `language: "en"`. Phase A starts with `gpt-4o-transcribe`; phase B hot-reloads to `gpt-transcribe`; phase C hot-reloads to no explicit model (provider default).

| Phase | Base: model sent | Base: noise clips with an utterance | Head: model sent | Head: noise clips with an utterance | Speech kept (both) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (`gpt-4o-transcribe`) | gpt-4o-transcribe, `language` | 13/13 | gpt-4o-transcribe, `language` | 13/13 | 9/9 |
| B (reload → `gpt-transcribe`) | **gpt-4o-transcribe** (reload ignored) | **13/13** | gpt-transcribe, `languages[]` | **0/13** | 9/9 |
| C (reload → default) | gpt-4o-transcribe | 6/6 | gpt-transcribe, `languages[]` | 0/6 | 4/4 |

Base phase B utterances for noise: "सकते हैं.", "咳咳", "咳咳", "そんなん。", "No.", "لا.", "Entscheidung.", "Hah.", "किसान.", "さて。", "떨림이나", "Hi.", "哈哈". Head phase B: none; speech was "And in sad, dreamy mood listened to the howling.", "An everlasting laugh.", "When I bring home my new program.", "Off.", "No.", "Stop.", "Yes.", "One.", and a sentence over wind at 10 dB SNR.

**Model sweep (direct API, 1,000 clips, Opus round trip)**

| Class (n) | `gpt-transcribe`, no hint | `gpt-transcribe`, `languages[]=en` | `gpt-transcribe`, `language=en` | `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `language=en` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Single words (200) | 96% kept, 10% non-English | 99% kept, 0% non-English | 99% kept, 0% non-English | 100% kept (100 words) |
| Sentences (100) | 100% | 100% | 100% | — |
| Speech over wind or keyboard (100) | 97% | 100% | 100% | — |
| Cough, wind, breathing, keyboard, clicks, knocks, footsteps, hiss (60 each) | 0% with text | 0% with text | 0% with text | ~100% with text |
| Sneezing / laughing (60 each) | 0% / 0% | 2% / 2% | 2% / 0% | 100% / 100% |

`languages: []` coincided exactly with empty text in all 3,000 `gpt-transcribe` responses, so the existing empty-transcript handling already covers it. Median latency was about 665 ms for both models.

## Follow-ups

- Realtime transcription defaults (`OPENAI_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_DEFAULT_MODEL`, voice-call streaming docs) still name `gpt-4o-transcribe`; moving them needs separate realtime proof.
- QA fixtures that explicitly pin `gpt-4o-transcribe` (WhatsApp live config, some QA scenarios) will need updating before the model shuts down.
- `resolveDiscordVoiceAccess` (owner/admission allowlists) is still resolved once at voice manager construction.

fix(msteams): streamed reply is sent again when Teams rejects the formatted final (#158429)

Root cause: `extensions/msteams/src/reply-stream-controller.ts:329` (current main) streams the raw Markdown progress final. Later, `finalize()` at `:396-401` clears the SDK buffer and emits the formatted text: tables become code blocks and headings become bold. That replaces content Teams already accepted, and Teams rejects it with 403 `Request streamed content should contain the previously streamed content`. The same block sets `replacementTextAwaitingAcknowledgement` (`:400`), so the late acknowledgement of the raw chunk is ignored (`:95-98`). The controller then believes nothing was delivered and returns the full answer as `fallbackPayload`, which goes out as a second message.

Fixes #158103

## What Problem This Solves

With `streaming.mode: "progress"` in a Teams 1:1 chat, a multi-tool answer whose Markdown is reformatted for Teams (for example a table) fails to finalize. Teams reports `Request streamed content should contain the previously streamed content`, and the answer is sent again as a fallback. Teams documents that each streaming request "represents a full message update" and that "Requests that attempt to change content provided in previous request will result in a 403 ContentStreamNotAllowed error" ([Stream bot messages](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/bots/streaming-ux)).

## Why This Change Was Made

The progress final is rendered before its first emission, through the existing `queueFinalReplacement` owner. The stream update and the close then carry the same rendered activity. Acknowledgements keep the logical Markdown for fallback accounting. Partial mode is unchanged.

The root-cause repair is by @rdbartram (commit author kept), adapted by @ericcaiwx-star. Thanks to @rdbartram for the report and the sanitized live sequence. On top of it: a merge of current main, and the added tests folded into one controller regression.

## User Impact

Progress-mode replies are streamed once in their Teams-formatted form and close cleanly: no 403, no duplicate answer. Plain-text answers and partial mode keep their current wire behavior.

## Evidence

[Gateway proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158429#issuecomment-7033619234), against base `477b611174`:

- Base: raw table streamed (201), then 403 `Request streamed content should contain the previously streamed content` on the formatted update and on the final message. The stream is never closed. The controller returns the full answer as fallback because it ignored the raw acknowledgement (diagnostic probe). On current main, that fallback is then dropped by a separate `MSTeams runtime not initialized` error in the late settlement path. The reporter's 2026.9.6 build delivered it as the duplicate.
- Candidate `14cc468efa`: rendered table streamed once (201), final message 201, one answer.
- Controls are identical on base and candidate: a plain-text progress answer and a partial-mode table.
- Unit: the new controller case fails on base and passes on the candidate. The controller, SDK loopback and dispatcher suites pass (59 tests).

Merge danger: two-way door. The change only alters what one msteams progress-mode stream emits and can be reverted cleanly; it writes no state and changes no config. Blast radius: Microsoft Teams personal chats using progress streaming.

fix(ui): keep Review visible when sending a message (#202255)

Root cause: ui/src/lib/sessions/session-row-reconcile.ts:579 deletes every null session-row field outside NULLABLE_SESSION_ROW_FIELDS. The Gateway sends `workspaceReadDisabledReason: null` to mean "workspace read allowed", so the row loses that decision. ## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made
The send event carries `workspaceReadDisabledReason: null` to explicitly allow reads. Session-row reconciliation interpreted that value as a tombstone and removed the field. Review then saw `undefined` (no known decision) and stopped rendering the diff. Preserve the explicit null for this field only. Denials and Gateway authorization checks are unchanged.

- **Real Gateway, compiled Control UI:** an isolated local Gateway handled browser sends against a deterministic loopback model provider, using a synthetic Git checkout. The browser showed the diff before sending in both runs. After the assistant reply, without reloading, the UI built with the base reconciler (`b4ddf4b30fc`) showed the empty Review placeholder; the UI built from the PR head (`fb668991137`) still showed all three changed files. fix: keep ACP replies alive while tools are still returning results (#202276)

Root cause: src/acp/control-plane/manager.turn-runner.ts:508 (on e62a1a37a) receives every backend text and tool event in `onOutputEvent` but never reports progress to the reply's watchdog (`progress()` in src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.ts:152), so the watchdog stops an active ACP reply 6 minutes after it started.

Related: #195520, #195584

## What Problem This Solves

A Codex reply in an ACP session can disappear after six minutes even while tools are returning results. On OpenClaw 2026.11.5, two interrupted replies had tool results just 14 and 17 seconds before cancellation.

This PR covers replies dispatched through the ACP session manager (`/acp` sessions and bound ACP chats). #195584 covers liveness in the ACPX harness attempt; the two change different files and code paths.

## User Impact

An active ACP reply can now run past six minutes and finish. A stalled reply still times out at the existing window when the backend only repeats a completed tool update or emits empty text, usage, or an in-progress status.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ACP manager already receives backend output before projecting it into chat. It now reports nonblank text and thought deltas, and the first terminal event for each tool call, as progress to the watchdog of the current reply. It reports nothing after the turn is cancelled. No timeout value changes.

## Evidence

- Gateway proof (real `gateway run`, isolated state, scripted local ACP agent through the acpx backend, only the Gateway's clock stepped): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202276#issuecomment-7033158382
  - Base e62a1a37a: the reply is cancelled at 6 min 13 s of Gateway time while a tool result arrived 15 s earlier; no reply in chat history.
  - This PR: the same 7-minute run finishes and the final answer is in chat history.
  - Control: a backend that only repeats one completed tool update is still cancelled 6 minutes after its last real progress.
- `dispatch-from-config.acp-controller.test.ts`: the three new cases fail on base (no progress recorded) and pass here.

Thanks @vsgik for the fix.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert restores the old behavior; nothing is persisted or migrated. Blast radius: ACP session replies only; if wrong, a stalled ACP backend that keeps emitting new text or new tool completions could run longer, bounded by the ACP turn timeout.

fix: keep paired desktop streams open during large screen updates (#202313)

Root cause: src/node-host/node-stream-transport.ts:194 sends each loopback read as one WebSocket message, but the Gateway node-stream attach server (src/gateway/desktop/node-stream-broker.ts:158) accepts at most 64 KiB per message; Bun-based node hosts read whole framebuffer bursts above that, so the Gateway closes the stream with 1009.

Fixes #202267

## What Problem This Solves

Opening the Control UI Desktop for a paired Mac (OpenClaw.app, whose node worker runs on Bun) disconnects a few seconds after login with "Desktop disconnected: desktop stream failed". The first large screen update closes the node's stream.

## User Impact

Paired-node desktops stay connected and render large screen updates. Portal streams use the same sender and get the same fix. Small traffic is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node now splits each read into ordered binary messages of at most 64 KiB before sending. The attach stream is a plain byte stream, so the Gateway reassembles it unchanged. The 64 KiB limit moves into one shared constant used by both the Gateway attach server and the node sender. The Gateway's receive limit does not change.

Thanks @honoyr for the precise report and root-cause analysis.

## Evidence

Real Gateway and real node host from source (pinned Bun 1.4.4), paired in isolated state. The node's desktop points at a loopback VNC fixture that sends 256x256 raw screen updates (262,160 bytes each) in one write. The driver uses the Control UI path: `desktop.observe` for the node, then the returned desktop WebSocket.

- Before (`da816e2190`): the viewer closes on the first update with `1011 desktop stream failed`; node log `closeCode: 1009`, Gateway `websocket-error`/1006. This matches the report.
- After: all 1,048,640 bytes of 4 updates arrive in order (SHA-256 matches what the fixture sent), and the viewer stays open until the driver closes it. The same holds when the fixture writes in 1 KiB pieces.
- Control: 16 KiB updates work before and after.
- New regression test: one 200 KiB read against a server with the Gateway's 64 KiB limit. It fails before the fix and passes after.

Observed proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202313#issuecomment-7032758415

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert fully undoes it. No state, config or protocol change. Blast radius: desktop and portal node streams from node hosts; the Gateway side only reuses the existing limit.

fix(agents): keep the prompt series when the bounded window drops an old compaction (#201655)

## What was wrong

OpenClaw ties a session's system prompt series to the newest compaction or reset in its hydrated transcript window. When a chat grew long after a compaction, that compaction fell out of the bounded window, causing the history ID to flip to `null`, restart the prompt series (`restarted:history`), and miss the entire provider cache. Compaction summaries were also re-reading every accumulated `System prompt update` message even though compaction starts a fresh prompt series.

## Example

You compact a chat, then edit `AGENTS.md` several times with follow-up turns until the compaction scrolls out of the bounded transcript window:

- **Before:** the next turn stopped seeing the compaction, triggered `restarted:history`, and missed the cache (OpenAI: **0 / 11096**; Claude: **1394 / 16782**).
- **Now:** the latest prompt checkpoint identifies the current history using its boundary count, so the series stays pinned and hits cache (OpenAI: **12336 / 484**; Claude: **18263 / 988**).

## The fix

- Use the newest `openclaw.system-prompt` checkpoint in the window to name the history when the compaction boundary has scrolled out of view (`session-prompt-history-id.ts`, `session-prompt-state.ts`, porting the first commit with its original author).
- Record `sessionManager.getBoundaryCount()` on each checkpoint so a stale checkpoint from before a later compaction or reset cannot spoof the current history. When neither a visible boundary nor a matching checkpoint is in view, use `unknown:<boundaryCount>` so the series restarts at most once.
- Exclude `System prompt update` messages from compaction summary input (`src/agents/compaction-planning.ts`), since compaction starts a new series with fresh rendered sections.
- Production diff vs main: +102 / -34 (compaction change: +33 / -14). Existing compacted sessions without a boundary count restart at most once after deploy if the compaction is already out of window.

## Proof

Isolated scratch Gateways on merge base `b4ddf4b30fc5` vs head `af7ee63f5b61` (final head `dfb4d5bce649` only reshapes a test fixture; OpenAI Responses `gpt-6.2-astra`, `contextTokens: 24000`, `maxTokens: 2048`, numbers are `cacheRead / cacheWrite`):

| Metric (long workspace rules, 2 runs per side) | Base (`b4ddf4b30fc5`) | Head (`af7ee63f5b61`) |
|---|---|---|
| Req 13/14 after window drops compaction | `restarted:history`, **0 / 11096** (run 2); **0 / 11459** at req 14 (run 1) | pinned, **12336 / 484** (run 2); **12332 / 484** (run 1) |
| History restarts without a compaction | 2 and 3 | **0** and **0** |
| Live prompt updates at compaction (peak) | 34 KB | 88 KB in history, none in summary input |

Earlier real-route run (`3df7c5332e81` / re-run `3677e9f`) on cliproxy Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`, `contextTokens: 30000`): req 15 went from `restarted:history` (**1394 / 16782**) on base to pinned (**18263 / 988**) on head (1 → 0 uncompacted restarts).

- **UI and side effects:** Control UI on the head scratch Gateway renders history across both compactions and answers every turn after Gateway restart (screenshots in PR comments). Concurrent chat (`gate-other`), short-rules control, cron/tool/session paths, and upgrade from legacy checkpoints all passed.
- **Tests and gates:** `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.history-boundary.test.ts`, `prepared-compaction-plan.test.ts`, `session-prompt-state.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint, oxfmt, and all baseline ratchets pass.

<details><summary>Full test details</summary>

### Boundary-count and upgrade details

- A checkpoint is evidence of the current history only when its recorded `sessionManager.getBoundaryCount()` matches the current count. A checkpoint whose count matches names the history even when the boundary is also in the window. Otherwise the visible boundary names it; with neither, the history is `unknown:<boundaryCount>`.
- `null` stays valid only for a session that never compacted or reset. A restored checkpoint without a count is rewritten with the count on the next persist.
- Existing checkpoints do not record a boundary count. In a session that has compacted, the first run after deploy whose window does not contain the compaction restarts the series once. A legacy checkpoint read while the compaction is in the window is rewritten with the count instead. Never-compacted sessions are not affected.
- Provider requests outside compaction are unchanged.

### E2E details (`af7ee63f5b61` vs merge base `b4ddf4b30fc5`; `dfb4d5bce649` only reshapes a test fixture)

Isolated scratch Gateways from source (`env -i`, own state, random ports), same driver on both sides, OpenAI Responses (`gpt-6.2-astra`, `contextTokens: 24000`, `maxTokens: 2048`). Journey `gate-h`: three story turns, `/compact` asking for a very long summary, then workspace `AGENTS.md` edits each followed by a follow-up turn (the history after the compaction outgrows the bounded window), then a **Gateway restart** on the same state and three more edit/follow-up pairs. An unrelated chat (`gate-other`) runs ordinary turns and `/compact` every second turn throughout.

- **Automatic compaction after the restart:** base run 2 had 1 failed attempt then succeeded, and one turn failed ("Couldn't finish this reply"). Head run 2 had 2 failed attempts then succeeded, and every turn answered; head run 1 answered every turn.
- Before the compaction change (head `dd58eb1`, two runs), the same journey failed automatic compaction three times in a row after the restart and the last turn failed in both runs. The remaining failed attempts on both sides are `summary truncated at the output token limit` and come from the journey itself: the `/compact` message asks for "at least 3000 words" and stays in the history the next automatic compaction summarizes. With a plain `/compact`, base and head match request for request and both compact twice without a failure.
- **Short workspace rules (control, 9 edits):** neither window loses the compaction, so both sides stay pinned and match (req 22: 14398 / 664 head, 14336 / 662 base); both compact automatically after the restart and every turn answers.
- **Side effects:**
  - Ordinary chat (`gate-other`): every turn and every `/compact` returned `ok` on both sides in all runs.
  - Cron, tool and session paths (run on head `dd58eb1`, unchanged by the compaction commit except the summary input): cron starting a chat, exec background wake, subagent completion, steer, `sessions_send`, cron surviving new/reset/edited chats, Stop and reset gave identical results on base and head, then a Gateway restart.

### Earlier real-route run (`3df7c5332e81` vs merge base; re-run on `3677e9f`)

On `3677e9f`: OpenAI requests 13/15 pinned at 9474/484 and 12048/484, 0 history restarts without a compaction; Claude request 15 pinned at 18150/988, only restart at a real compaction with `boundaryCount: 2`.

OpenAI Responses (`gpt-6.2-astra`, minimal tool profile, `contextTokens: 24000`):

| Request | Base series, cacheRead / cacheWrite | Head series, cacheRead / cacheWrite |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | `restarted:history` (historyId -> null), **2700 / 3876** | pinned, 9432 / 484 |
| 15 | pinned, 7061 / 484 | pinned, 12005 / 484 |
| 16 | `restarted:history` (flips back), 7545 / 485 | real automatic compaction (allowed rebuild) |
| History restarts without a compaction | 2 | 0 |

cliproxy Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`, `contextTokens: 30000`):

| Request | Base series, cacheRead / cacheWrite | Head series, cacheRead / cacheWrite |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | `restarted:history` (historyId -> null), **1394 / 16782** | pinned, 18263 / 988 |
| 20/21 | restart at a real automatic compaction | restart at a real automatic compaction (checkpoint `boundaryCount: 2`) |
| History restarts without a compaction | 1 | 0 |

### Upgrade test (one state dir: base then head, OpenAI route)

- Target chat: one `restarted:history` on the first turn after the upgrade, then pinned through 6 edit/follow-up pairs (cacheRead 2432 -> 10213); `/compact` on head restarts once and writes `boundaryCount: 2`; later checkpoints stay pinned at count 2.
- Never-compacted chat: pinned across the upgrade (legacy checkpoint `historyId: null`, then `boundaryCount: 0`).
- Unrelated chat: restarts only at its own compactions (counts 2-5 recorded).
- Cron created on base: still enabled on head and fired on schedule in the target chat; with the scratch model at `maxTokens: 2048`, that turn failed in automatic compaction (summary output budget exhausted); the merge base fails the same way on the same setup. With `maxTokens: 8192` the cron turn passes on head, the target chat restarts once after the upgrade and then stays pinned (cacheRead 2297 -> 10078), and `/compact` restarts once with `boundaryCount: 3`.

### Unit and integration tests (merge base vs head)

- `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.history-boundary.test.ts` (real SQLite hydration, one bounded view per run; every case pushes the boundary out of the window so it reaches the count rule):
  - three runs whose byte window includes, then drops, then includes an old compaction keep one series (base: `restarted:history` on run 2);
  - eviction: the newest checkpoint leaves the window with the compaction, the series restarts once as `unknown:1`, then stays pinned when the boundary returns beside that checkpoint (previous head `3df7c53`: second restart);
  - a legacy checkpoint that names the visible boundary is rewritten with the count and stays pinned when the boundary leaves (previous head: two restarts);
  - a legacy checkpoint with `historyId: null` restarts once, then stays pinned (base: pinned on the wrong history);
  - rewind to a checkpoint written at count 1 (stored as `unknown:1`, `boundaryCount: 1`) past a later compaction: the series stays pinned to that checkpoint (fails if the count were store-wide);
  - a counted reset restarts the series although the window holds a checkpoint of the earlier history (fails if resets were not counted);
  - a visible compaction after a counted checkpoint restarts the series (fails if any counted checkpoint outranked the visible boundary).
  - Each of the last three cases was checked with a local mutation of the behavior it guards (store-wide count, uncounted reset, checkpoint always outranking the boundary): each fails under its mutation and passes after revert.
- `prepared-compaction-plan.test.ts`: prompt updates between turns are left out of the summary selection, the turns stay (red on `7a698fb`: the updates were selected).
- The rewind case reads the same SQLite bounded context through `SessionManager.openBoundedAsync`; the separate SQLite reader case was dropped after main grew that file past the line cap.
- `session-prompt-state.test.ts`:

  - a never-compacted session stays pinned (passes on both);
  - the ported unit test for a window that starts after the compaction, now passing the boundary count as production does (base: restart).
- The earlier prefix-stability journey step was removed: it passed on the merge base, so it could not catch this defect.

### Follow-ups (not blockers) and gates

- A session fork loses its pinned prefix while the source series is `unknown:N` (the fork view carries no checkpoint data); this costs cache until the next compaction.
- `removeTrailingEntries` can delete a boundary through the plugin compatibility surface; core does not reach that path today.
- A legacy session gets one extra checkpoint append after the upgrade, when its count is first written.
- Gates on `af7ee63`, plus lint, format, the touched test and test-lines on `dfb4d5b`: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint and oxfmt on touched files, the baseline ratchets (mock-exports, test-lines +400 of 400, line-cap, max-lines, database-worker), the focused tests above, the prompt-cache prefix-stability suites, and the compaction, safeguard and memory-flush tests.

fix(openrouter): non-Gemini image models ignore the requested aspect ratio (#200041)

Root cause: extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.ts:180 `buildImageConfig` returns geometry only for `google/gemini-*` models, and the dedicated `/api/v1/images` body (line 247) took `aspect_ratio` from it, so every other model silently lost the requested aspect ratio.

Related: #199883 (fixes the aspect-ratio part; resolution forwarding for non-Gemini models stays open there)
Related: #199902 (same bug; this PR differs in how it treats resolution, see below)

Thanks @brettdaman for the report, the live OpenRouter checks and this fix, and @chelsealong for the first PR on this bug (#199902).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: images generated through OpenRouter with a non-Gemini model (for example Seedream 5.5) always come back in the model's default shape, because the requested aspect ratio is dropped before the request is sent.

## User Impact

User impact: `aspectRatio` now takes effect for every OpenRouter image model on the dedicated image endpoint.

One behavior change to be aware of: a ratio the selected model does not support now returns OpenRouter's error, which names the accepted values. Before, that ratio was silently ignored and an image in the default shape was returned. Resolution handling is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedicated `/images` request took its geometry from the Gemini-only chat `image_config`. It now reads the aspect ratio from the validated request for all models.

Resolution stays Gemini-only on purpose. For edits, `image_generate` infers a resolution from the reference image (`4K` at 3000 px or more, `2K` at 1500 px or more), and other models accept different sets: Seedream 5.5 rejects `4K` and accepts `1K`, `1.5K`, `2K`. Forwarding the inferred value for every model would turn a Seedream edit of an ordinary phone photo, which works today, into an HTTP 400. Doing that safely needs per-model `resolutionsByModel` data, which fits better in a follow-up.

#199902 forwards both fields. That is the one functional difference between the two PRs, and the live results below are meant to help either one land.

## Evidence

**Local fixture, shipped CLI, base vs this head** (request bodies recorded, Gemini control unchanged byte for byte): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200041#issuecomment-7032057689

**Live, shipped CLI entry point** (`openclaw infer image generate`, real OpenRouter key, paths shortened). The patched run is `node openclaw.mjs` from this branch after `pnpm build`, in an empty state directory with only `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set. It reports `OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (ff91bc0)`; the current head `e409aa844` has the same tree and differs only in the commit message (`Related` instead of `Closes`). The "before" run is the released npm package, not a build of the base commit.

fix(channels): record a refused queued request for the owner without replying in the channel (#202252)

Problem: a queued channel request refused at admission because the requester's channel access is gone (ChannelRunAuthorizationError "denied") gave the session owner no reason in the transcript or Control UI, and its "silent" reply was a bare NO_REPLY text without silentReply metadata, so it reached the reply dispatcher's deliver and could be sent to the revoked conversation. Reachable today only through channels that supply a public child-session publication renewal (the X plugin).

Fix: the denied branch's existing lifecycle error terminal carries a fixed host-authored errorNotice ("This request was not started because the requester no longer has access to this channel."), and the final payload is marked silent through setReplyPayloadMetadata. The unavailable branch, token, failure bookkeeping and log are unchanged. docs/channels/groups.md documents the owner-visible, channel-silent refusal.

Proof: source tier (ocx test). New regression through the real runner and reply dispatcher: one visible receipt with the run id and notice, projected history, replay dedupe, no nested secret in displayed/projected text, zero deliver/deliverPrepared calls; the notice assertion is red on unchanged main, where deliver received bare NO_REPLY. 159 tests across 13 files; typecheck, oxlint, format, ratchets, docs checks; clean exact-head local ClawSweeper review; ocx build --dts plus packed install smoke. A real Discord run on main and head confirmed Discord does not reach this branch (no publication renewal) and found a separate pre-existing queued-admission bug, fixed separately.

feat(plugins): composer tasks can send their result and resume in a returning chat (#202243)

## What Problem This Solves

Two gaps in composer tasks (#201695), found while using the Better plugin:

- **No send.** An action whose result the user wants sent right away ("rewrite and send") had to insert it and leave the user to press Enter.
- **Work is dropped on a chat switch.** Leaving the chat retires the action, so its card disappears while the work it started (a Gateway run) keeps going. Coming back shows nothing, the work is unreachable, and the plugin cannot even stop it because its UI handle has ended. In Better this surfaced as "already running; Cancel stops it" with no card and no Cancel.

## User Impact

- `task.propose(text, { title, send: true })` inserts the text and then sends it through the composer's own send, as Enter would: same admission, follow-up queueing, connection, dictation, goal and pending-attachment checks. When the composer cannot send yet, the inserted draft stays unsent with its Undo receipt; a locked editor keeps the proposal for Use, as with `insert`.
- A composer action can declare `attach`. The host calls it, with the same context as `run`, each time a built-in composer shows the chat (mount, chat switch, return from another page), so the action can start a task again and follow its earlier work. `startTask({ startedAt })` keeps the original elapsed clock. Leaving still aborts the action's `signal` and retires the card; the action keeps its work going and stops it only when the task's signal aborts while `signal` has not (the user's Cancel).

Both are optional and additive.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Send goes through the existing owner.** The mounted composer publishes its send beside its Escape stop policy (`state.sendDraft`, cleared on unmount), and `submitDraft` now reports whether it submitted. The task owner calls it after inserting; no second send path.
- **Attach is a presentation event, not a retained handle.** Composer handles still retire on chat switch, so a retained handle never touches another chat's draft. `attach` gets a fresh handle bound to the chat being shown, once per presentation lifetime, after the render settles. The work's own owner (the plugin's Gateway run) decides whether there is anything to show.

## Evidence

- New e2e in `native-plugin-composer.e2e.test.ts`: `send: true` produces exactly one `chat.send` with the rewritten text and clears the composer (red without the send: 0 sends); a running task leaves with its chat and returns with the original clock (`1m 0Xs`) when the chat is shown again, then inserts its result there.
- All composer-task and native plugin UI e2e (19) and unit tests pass; `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:core`, oxlint, controller guard, line-cap and test-lines ratchets.
- Chat boot JS +73 B gzip vs the merge base, within the limit.

**SDK impact.** Additive: optional `send` on `ControlUiDraftProposal`, optional `attach` on `ControlUiAction`, optional `startedAt` on `startTask`. The only consumer is the Better plugin.

fix(cron): a session cron's reply reaches the model once (#201838)

## Problem

A session-target cron (`sessionTarget: "session:<key>"`) or a main-session cron runs its turn in the target conversation. That turn's own assistant reply stays in model context (it is hidden from the chat view because cron execution prose is audit-only).

When the turn settles, `settleSessionEventTurn` publishes the settled reply into the same conversation through `commitCronConversationResult`, so the chat view can show it. The cron turn still holds the session at that moment, so `commitBackgroundResultToSession` writes the row as a pending background result (`excludeFromContext` + `openclawModelPlacement: "pending"`). The next request boundary then places it into model context as a normal assistant message.

Result: the model sees the cron reply twice. In a real run the model apologised for "answering twice". Isolated crons are not affected (0 copies in the chat).

## Solution

The settle step's commit is always into the conversation that the cron turn ran in, so the row is for display only. `settleSessionEventTurn` now passes `displayOnly: true`. The writer then stores `excludeFromContext: true` with no pending placement, so the row is shown in the chat and never placed into model context.

### Why a parameter (and not derivation or removal)

The brief asked for subtraction first. I checked both options:

1. **Derive at the write site.** `commitBackgroundResultToSession` only knows "this session has active work". It cannot tell whether that work is the producer (this cron turn) or a foreign turn (a user typing while an isolated cron result arrives from another session, a subagent completion). Both callers also pass the same `{ kind: "cron", jobId, runId }` provenance. The run registry entry that names the job (`cronRunsByJobId`) is consumed before the commit. Exact derivation needs new state; a heuristic (active cron turn in this session) would drop a foreign result from model context when two crons overlap.
2. **Drop the commit.** The cron turn's own reply is `display: false`, so this commit is the only persistent display path. Removing it removes the reply from the chat after a reload. Making the raw reply visible instead changes what the chat shows (no_change, silent replies, directive text, media).

So the only callers that know the fact ("my own turn already holds this text") state it. The flag is threaded through `commitCronConversationResult` → `commitBackgroundPayloadsToSession` → `commitBackgroundResultToSession`. Two callers set it:

- `settleSessionEventTurn` (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-automation.ts`): session-target and main-session cron turns.
- `commitExecutionResult` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts:112-136`, callers `:196` and `:421`): a persistent execution committing into its own conversation.

### Is the isolated runner reachable with a `session:` or `main` job?

- **From the cron timer: no.**
  - `script` payloads return early (`src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts:362`).
  - `runsCronMainSessionRoute` (`src/cron/service/timer-session-route.ts:20-30`) sends every non-plugin-command job with `sessionTarget: "main"`, or with `session:` and `agentTurn`, to `executeMainSessionCronJob` (`timer-execution.ts:379`).
  - Validation (`src/cron/service/jobs-validation.ts:106-127`) allows only `agentTurn` or `command` on `session:` targets, and only `systemEvent`, `agentTurn` or `script` on `main`.
  - In `executeDetachedCronJob`, `command` payloads go to the command runner (`timer-execution.ts:479`), and anything else that is not `agentTurn` is rejected (`:526`).
  - What remains for `runIsolatedAgentJob` (`:541`) with a `session:` target is a plugin-command job. `runPluginCommandScheduledTurn` claims those, because `readPluginCommandScheduledJob` either returns the schedule or throws (`src/gateway/plugin-command-scheduled-run.ts:70-92`). So they never reach `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` (`src/gateway/server-cron-agent-run.ts:39-60`).
- **From persistent webhooks: yes.** `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts:315` builds `sessionTarget: "session:<key>"` for `sessionMode: "persistent"` and calls `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` directly (`:548`). That path's `commitExecutionResult` committed into the execution's own conversation, so it had the same double copy. It now passes `displayOnly: true` too, and the persistent-session delivery tests assert the flag. This part is proven by reading the code and by those unit tests; no real-Gateway run covers webhooks.

### Behavior notes

- **Host-authored payloads in the same commit become display-only too.** For example, the `isError` payloads kept on `no_change`. They no longer reach the model through the placed row. This is intended: the model already saw its own turn, and the host text is for the reader.
- **Retries that straddle the deploy.** A retry over an old pending row with the same idempotency key stays pending, because the retry spreads `priorMessage` (`src/sessions/background-session-result.ts:164-169`). Only runs that straddle the deploy are affected.
- **Reset between turn end and commit.** The row lands display-only in the new transcript. This is defensible: the reset already dropped the turn that produced it.
- **CLI runtime.** By reading the code, CLI runtime sessions take the same settle path, and their history reader also skips `excludeFromContext` rows, so the fix holds. This is not tested end to end.

### Unchanged

- Isolated crons, source-conversation commits (an isolated cron created from a chat), run-outcome notices and subagent completions keep their placement.
- Readers: placement readers match only `openclawModelPlacement: "pending"`; the Control UI automation boundary reads `openclawAutomation`, which is kept. Existing pending rows from older versions are still placed once (accepted, transient).

## Evidence

### Tests (red on merge base `dbc1aa04e88f`, green on head)

`src/cron/session-cron-result-single-copy.gateway.integration.test.ts`: a real Gateway, cron service and session store; only the provider endpoint is synthetic. The last two are guards for unchanged behavior, so they pass on both sides.

 Consumer suites (background result, destination/current-session completion, double announce, cron notifications, session event handoff and automation result, CLI history boundary): 248 tests pass. `tsgo:core` passes. `check:test-types` reports only existing errors in `test/scripts/release-*` (unrelated).

fix(agents): freeze a prompt series' tool set at its first request (#201710)

> **Size:** production code vs `main` (base `3da2118`, excluding tests and docs) is +290 / -205 (net +85). Not net negative: the growth is the execution-gate conversion itself (build the session's full list, then gate by turn policy in assembly and the message policy), keeping refused tools out of delegation, capture, guidance and the preparer path, the run-policy mark that keeps the empty-allowlist error identical to `main`, and the opt-out admission path `toolSearch: false` still needs. 27 added lines are a move (`session-prompt-delta.ts`) forced by the line-cap ratchet.
>
> **Isolated crons keep main's narrowed list.** A session whose key is an isolated cron run (`agent:<id>:cron:<job>:run:<runId>`, one run per session, `isCronRunSessionKey`) has no series to share, so it keeps the listing narrowed to its allowlist, as on `main`. Every other session, including a cron that runs in a shared session, keeps the fixed listing. Call gates apply everywhere. First request of an isolated cron with `toolsAllow: ["read"]` (tools / input tokens; Claude input = uncached + cache read + cache write):
>
> | | main `3da2118` | `a5d2e08` (fixed listing everywhere) | this head |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | OpenAI | 4 / 6,128 | 14 / 12,368 | 4 / 6,114 |
> | Claude | 4 / 9,206 | 14 / 20,121 | 4 / 9,258 |
>
> A cron that runs in a named shared session (journey J2) still sends the fixed list (14 tools), which is what keeps that session's later turns on one cached prefix.
>
> **Scope:** this PR covers core and plugin tools. MCP and LSP keep `main`'s behavior exactly: their runtimes start only when the run's allowlist permits it, and sender/group denies still apply at MCP discovery. Because MCP tools sit in the deferred catalog, an MCP-only-allowlist cron after `/compact` (J12) no longer narrows the pinned tool list on this head; what remains (the deferred directory following the allowlist, sender denies dropping an MCP server, and starting MCP/LSP from the pin) is the follow-up: pin-owned MCP/LSP listing with a lazy runtime start.

## Problem

The session prompt owner pins the tool definitions of a prompt series. A turn that built a tool the pin lacked extended the pin, so the provider tool list changed. Tools sit at the front of the request, so the whole cached prefix missed.

The list changed with turn authority:

- A chat whose series starts on a cron turn has no `message` tool under the `coding` profile. The next user turn in `message_tool_only` delivery builds `message`, the pin grows, and that request reads 0 cached tokens.
- A run's `toolsAllow` (cron, queued follow-ups, cross-session events) narrows the list. A subagent child's spawn turn (`disableMessageTool`) lists no `message` while its follow-up turns do.
- Group `tools` / `toolsBySender` policy narrows the list per sender, so a guest and an owner in one group chat send different lists.
- The deferred MCP directory sat in the `tool_search` definition, so an MCP server that connected later changed a tool definition.

Freezing the pin alone made the first turn's omissions permanent (an owner turn after a narrowed turn silently lost tools). This PR makes the list independent of turn authority and gates calls at execution instead.

## Solution

1. **Freeze** (`session-prompt-state.ts`, `prepareSessionToolSurface`): on a fixed listing the series' first request pins the tool set and every definition. A pinned tool a turn did not build stays listed and refuses its call. The tool policy digest's inputs changed (it now includes `config.mcp`), so every session starts one new pin after upgrade.
2. **MCP directory out of `tool_search`**: `buildToolSchemaDirectoryPrompt` appends the bounded, sanitized MCP directory to the system prompt's `### Deferred Tool Schemas` section. An MCP server that connects, disconnects or changes its tools reaches the model as an appended prompt-update note, never as a definition change.
3. **`message` always listed, gated at execution**: on a fixed listing the assembly builds `message` regardless of reply mode; `resolveTurnToolSurface` refuses it on a turn that cannot send ("message cannot send on this turn: ... Do not retry message.").
4. **Every run allowlist and group/sender policy is an execution gate** (core and plugin tools): on a fixed listing, `toolsAllow` on any trigger and the group `tools` / `toolsBySender` policy no longer narrow construction. `resolveTurnToolSurface` refuses the tools the turn's policy omits ("`<tool>` is outside the tools this run allows. Do not retry `<tool>`."), marks them unavailable and as run-policy refusals, and never hands them the source's execution preparer, so direct calls, the agent loop's preparer path and a `dispatch_action` rewrap all refuse. Turn authority, child inheritance, cron-creator capture and the catalog restriction read the same policy, so the callable set is unchanged (table below). An allowlist that leaves nothing callable still fails with "No callable tools remain", as on `main`.
5. **Guidance follows callable tools** (m6): `applyPromptBuildToolsAllow` drops listed-but-refused tools from `callableToolNames`, so a turn that cannot send is not told to "use the message tool".
6. **Docs**: `docs/reference/prompt-caching.md`, `docs/tools/tool-search.md`, `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md`.

### Authority recheck at `390da1c` (fixed in this head)

- **A1** (allowlists narrowing the list): for core and plugin tools, the allowlist no longer narrows construction on a fixed listing. The attempt-level filter is skipped (the assembly's turn policy already refuses what the allowlist omits, so the old attempt-level gate was redundant and is deleted). The MCP part (J12) is out of scope; see Scope.
- **A2** (refused copies carried the source's execution preparer): `copyAgentToolMetadata` no longer copies the preparer onto a target that refuses execution (the turn-policy refusal in `resolveTurnToolSurface`, including the scoped-reads split). Ring-zero tools: a ring-zero harness run has no Tool Search controls, so it is never a fixed listing and the allowlist still removes them, as on `main` (test).
- **m-a**: a tool built after the session pin is logged (`tools built after the session pin wait for the next prompt series`).
- **m-b / 1b** (fixed for plugins): on a fixed listing, plugin construction keeps every grant plus the default plugin tools and uses a denylist without sender, group and run denies; those refuse at execution. Children still inherit the full denylist. The MCP part (a sender deny dropping a whole MCP server at discovery) is out of scope.

fix(agents): keep projected prompt updates out of later user turns (#201843)

## Problem

Some routes cannot send a system prompt update as a system message (`inHistorySystemUpdates` is false). Examples: custom OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions providers, and Claude through a non-native Responses proxy. On these routes, the boundary projects the update as a plain `{ role: "user" }` message. The update is the last message of its turn.

When that turn ends silent (a `NO_REPLY` turn after an `AGENTS.md` edit, or a silent exec wake that carries a `## Tooling` update), no assistant message follows the update. On the next turn, the stream boundary merges the new user message into the update (`mergeConsecutiveUserMessages`). `canMergeUser` refuses carriers, operator messages and synthetic messages, but not this projected update. The result: a message that the provider already received is rewritten, and the prompt cache misses from that point.

## Fix

- When `inHistorySystemUpdates` is false, the projection puts a symbol-keyed marker (`PROJECTED_PROMPT_UPDATE`) on the projected update message.
- `canMergeUser` refuses to merge across that marker.
- A symbol key is not in `JSON.stringify` or structured clone output, so the marker never reaches a provider request, the worker protocol or the transcript. Only `canMergeUser` reads it.
- Why not `synthetic`: at least one route has `inHistorySystemUpdates` false and also reads `synthetic` on user messages. The ChatGPT Codex backend (`provider: "openai"`, `api: "openai-chatgpt-responses"`, `chatgpt.com`) is not a native Responses endpoint (`packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-endpoint.ts:21-25` needs `api: "openai-responses"` on `api.openai.com`), so its prompt updates are projected as plain user messages. The same backend is the only one eligible for ChatGPT V2 compaction (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/chatgpt-v2-compaction.ts:35-55`, `usesNativeOpenAICodexResponsesBackend`). During V2 compaction it sets `retainUserProvenance` (`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts:221-223` → `openai-chatgpt-responses-request.ts:118-124`). Then `openai-responses-replay-messages-internal.ts:441-448` tags non-synthetic user input as retained, and `chatgpt-v2-compaction.ts:180-185` checks non-synthetic user input before persistence. A `synthetic` update would drop out of the V2 retained input on that route, which changes behavior. The symbol changes nothing there.
- Routes with `inHistorySystemUpdates` (native OpenAI Responses, direct Anthropic) are unchanged: they keep `operatorMessage` and never get the marker.

Production diff: 8 added, 2 removed lines in 2 files.

## Scope and limits

- Accepted gap: Bedrock Converse. It requires strict role alternation, so the stream boundary calls `mergeConsecutiveUserMessages` with `preserveContextBoundaries: false` for `bedrock-converse-stream` (`attempt-tool-call-replay-sanitization.ts:382`) and never consults `canMergeUser`. A silent turn rewrites the prefix there with or without an update. This PR does not change Bedrock.
- One-time cache miss on upgrade: the marker also stops an update from merging backward into a user message directly before it in the same turn. Where history was sent as `[user + update]`, the first request after the upgrade sends `[user, update]`. After that request, history is append-only again.
- Longer runs of consecutive user-role messages: after a silent turn a request can now contain, for example, user, carrier, update, user, carrier in a row (main merged the update with the next user). Carriers already produce consecutive user-role messages on every turn on these routes, so this is not a new failure class.
- Google Gemini routes do not merge user turns (`validateAnthropicTurns` is false), so this bug does not occur there.
- The OpenAI provider plugin's own Chat Completions policy does not merge user turns either. The bug occurs on custom and plugin-owned OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions routes that use the strict OpenAI-compatible replay policy.
- This supersedes the closed #201654 (silent replies in replay) for the routes above.

## Evidence

### Tests (`attempt.silent-prompt-update.test.ts`)

The test runs the real boundary projection, the real stream sanitization wrapper with the resolved transcript policy, and the real transport for each route (`streamOpenAICompletions` / `streamOpenAIResponses`). It captures the live payload object in `onPayload`, before serialization, so the key check sees symbol keys too.

The original capture and the gate below use the same config: provider id `oaic` (a custom provider, no owning plugin, plugins disabled), `api: "openai-completions"`, model `gpt-5.6-sol`, base URL pointing to a local logging proxy in front of the OpenAI API.

- With that flag, the stream wrapper merges consecutive user messages (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-tool-call-replay-sanitization.ts:378-383`, the same line 381 on `8a23d7c`). `canMergeUser` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/turns.ts:433`) decides which messages may merge.

fix(discord): agent presentation controls stop expiring (#201965)

## Problem

On Discord, a button or select that the agent sends through the `message` tool (`presentation` with `action: { type: "callback" }` or a legacy `value`) stops working 30 minutes after it is sent, and after any Gateway restart that loses the in-memory registry: the tap answers "This component has expired." The agent never sees it. Follow-up to #201764, which made these taps reach the agent on every channel while the Discord callback is still registered.

## Root cause

Discord presentation controls get a random `occomp:cid=<id>` custom id, and the meaning of the tap lives only in the component registry (`extensions/discord/src/components.builders.ts:55-84`, select at `:194-244`), which expires after `agentComponents.ttlMs` (default 30 minutes) and is lost when persistence is unavailable. The resolver then replies "This component has expired." (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/agent-components.ts`, `handleDiscordComponentEvent`). Core already marks agent-authored values (#201764), so the value alone is enough to route the tap; it was just not carried by the component.

## Solution

Agent-authored controls are stateless:

- **Send** (`shared-interactive.ts`, `components.builders.ts`): a core-marked callback button gets the custom id `agent:<index>:<marked value>`; a select whose options are all core-marked gets `agentsel:<index>` and keeps the marked values as option values. No registry entry is written. The index keeps ids unique per message (duplicate values, several selects). The send-action parser (`components.parse.ts`, `readDiscordComponentSpec`), which re-reads the generated spec on the `message` tool path, keeps `agent:`/`agentsel:` ids; other internal ids (approvals, questions) stay builder-only.
- **Tap** (`monitor/agent-components.system-controls.ts`): the existing `agent`/`agentsel` component handlers, which no code path produced anymore, now handle these ids:
  1. the normal sender checks for components (`resolveAuthorizedComponentInteraction`: DM policy, pairing, guild/channel allowlists, policy freshness);
  2. single use unless the button sets `reusable: true` (carried in the id as `agent:<index>r:`): the tap response disables the agent's buttons and selects (Discord renders them greyed out and rejects further taps) and keeps the text, media, URL buttons and other controls unchanged; the message can never become empty. This happens before any handler runs, so a plugin-handled tap is single use too; a handler that edits the source message replaces that update;
  3. plugin first on the value (the core dispatcher strips the mark); select handlers get the selected option labels in `values`, as registry selects did;
  4. the value reaches the conversation's session as `callback_data: <value>` through the same dispatch as registry-backed components.
- Native `components` and forms keep the registry and `agentComponents.ttlMs`.

## What was deleted

- The legacy `agent:`/`agentsel:` system-event handler body (`[Discord component: … clicked by …]`), `parseAgentComponentData`, `ensureAgentComponentInteractionAllowed`, and their tests. Nothing produced these ids.
- Registry writes for agent-authored presentation controls.

## Accepted edges

- If any agent button value in a presentation does not fit Discord's 100-character custom id (values over about 90 characters), all of that presentation's agent controls use the registry path, one consumption group as before, and expire as before. Not dropped, not silent.
- Buttons sent before this change keep their registry entries and expire as before.
- A tap goes to the conversation's session (the normal inbound route of the channel and sender), not to the session that sent the message. This matches Telegram, Mattermost and Feishu after #201764, and it is what the agent-controls design specifies ("stateless taps re-run normal inbound auth and resolve the conversation session"). Before, Discord routed to the sender's session through the registry entry, which is the state that expires. Controls sent into a channel from another session (for example, a cron run) now reach that channel's session.

## Local review

- `[P2]` reusable buttons, `[P2]` URL buttons kept, `[P2]` empty container, `[P2]` controls-only message stayed tappable: fixed, with tests (consumed controls are now disabled instead of removed).
- `[P2]` plugin-handled tap skipped consumption, `[P2]` mixed short and long values, `[P2]` stateless select lost `values` for plugin handlers: fixed, with tests (red on `71786b2`, green on head).
- `[P1]` send parser dropped the generated agent ids on the `message` tool path (the earlier tests bypassed the parser): fixed. The tests now render through `readDiscordComponentSpec`; without the parser fix 8 of 11 fail.
- `[P1]` sender session route: conversation-session routing approved by the maintainer, see accepted edges.

## Tests (red on base `cd2ae19272a3`, green on head)

`extensions/discord/src/monitor/monitor.agent-components.test.ts` renders a core-marked presentation through the real builders, clears the in-memory and persistent registry (restart or TTL expiry), and routes the tap to the registered control the way the Discord client resolves custom ids.

| Test | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| typed callback button after the registry is gone → `callback_data: pick:a`, controls removed, plugin offered `::pick:a` | ✗ "This component has expired." | ✓ |
| legacy value button after the registry is gone → `callback_data: /pick a` | ✗ "This component has expired." | ✓ |
| select choice after the registry is gone → `callback_data: size:m` | ✗ | ✓ |
| tapper outside the allowlist → "You are not authorized to use this button.", no dispatch | ✗ | ✓ |
| duplicate values and two selects in one message → distinct custom ids | ✓ (guard) | ✓ |

Gates: Discord extension suite, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files.

- `monitor.agent-components.test.ts`: tapping an agent button disables it and keeps a URL button in the same row; a `reusable` agent button leaves the message unchanged and still delivers `callback_data: refresh`; a controls-only message has its control disabled, so a second tap cannot fire ; a plugin-claimed tap disables the control and the handler runs once; a select handler gets `values: ["Medium"]`; a presentation with one value too long for an id renders every agent control through the registry, in either order (added after local review).

## E2E

Not run live. Discord component clicks need a real user client: bots cannot click components, and the Discord E2E skill treats component clicks as manual (`.agents/skills/discord-e2e/features.md`). No computer-control node was available for a manual click. A maintainer can verify by sending a presentation button with the `message` tool, restarting the Gateway (or waiting 30 minutes), and tapping it.

## Size

- Production: +115 / −126 (net **−11**).
- Tests/docs: −185 net (legacy handler tests removed).

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

fix(gateway): refresh native command channels when their registry is replaced (#199743)

Root cause: src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-channels.ts:88 `collectTargets` restarts channels only when command entries change identity or the channel's own plugin changed. A reload of an unrelated plugin keeps the other plugins' command entries by identity, so no channel restarts. The old registry is still retired, and Telegram, Discord and Slack keep dispatching through native command candidates captured from it at account start.

Fixes #199612

Thanks @eliavb43 for the report and diagnosis, @jupiterkatz1989-coder for confirming it, and @555aaditya for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a config hot reload of any plugin, every plugin slash command on Telegram answers "⚠️ This command is no longer available after the plugin registry changed. Please try again." until the Gateway restarts. Discord and Slack native commands bind the same way.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin slash commands on native-command channels keep working after a plugin hot reload, including when the reloaded plugin is unrelated to the command.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram (`bot-native-commands.ts:80`), Discord (`provider.commands.ts:34`) and Slack (`slash.ts:919`) take native command candidates from `createPluginCommandRuntime().listNativeCandidates()` when an account starts. Each candidate is bound to that registry generation, and a dispatch from a retired generation returns the refusal above (`plugin-command-runtime.ts:149`). A plugin reload publishes a new registry and retires the old one, but `collectTargets` did not refresh channels when the command list kept its identity.

`collectTargets` now also targets channels with `capabilities.nativeCommands` that had a plugin command for that channel in the replaced registry. It uses the same `pluginCommandSupportsChannel` filter as `listNativeCandidates`. Those channels go through the existing reload stop, start and route-handoff path that command-list changes already use. Channels without native commands, or without plugin commands for that channel, keep running.

Update behavior: Gateway runtime only. No persisted state, config or schema change. It takes effect when the updated Gateway starts; the installed updater is not involved.

## Evidence

Live Telegram Test Server run (real QA user DM, TDLib records), built merge base `6341f93c9c` against this branch, same scenario: [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199743#issuecomment-7028740443).

- Base: `/p199612ping` answers `P199612_PONG`. After `plugins.entries.p199612-other.config.rev` changes (hot reload, no Telegram restart), it answers `⚠️ This command is no longer available after the plugin registry changed. Please try again.`
- This branch: Telegram restarts with `reason: plugin-reload` during the same reload, and `/p199612ping` keeps answering `P199612_PONG`.
- Control, same on both: disabling the plugin that owns `/p199612gone` removes the command. Its handler never runs, and the message goes to a normal agent turn.

Regression in `server-plugin-reload.recovery.test.ts`: an unrelated plugin reloads while a sibling owns a native-command channel with a retained command and a channel without native commands. It fails on the merge base (`expected [ 'plain', 'native' ] to deeply equal [ 'plain', 'native', 'native' ]`). On this branch it passes: only the native channel restarts, and its new candidate runs the command.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert restores the old behavior, and nothing is persisted. Blast radius: on a plugin hot reload, channels with native commands and plugin commands (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Mattermost) now restart through the existing reload path. They already did this whenever the command list changed.

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>
