commits.message:
Use a shared `ToolCallId` for dispatched tool invocations (#62888)

## Why

Dispatched invocations, model-visible Responses calls, and Code Mode's
per-cell runtime calls use IDs with different roles. A dedicated Rust type
makes the dispatch identity explicit in APIs that carry it.

## What changed

Add `codex-tool-call-id` and use its `ToolCallId` across core tool dispatch,
nested Code Mode calls, and rollout tracing. The type wraps a string and
continues to serialize as a string.

GitOrigin-RevId: 119de57a9af840c4de72895adc9acdd0ed15b4fd

Track explicit web search modes and expose indexed in the SDK (#62884)

## What changed

Record whether an explicit `web_search` setting matches the effective
mode after applying configuration requirements. Mark the thread manager
sample's disabled mode as explicit.

Accept `indexed` in the TypeScript SDK's `WebSearchMode` type.

## Testing

Extend the SDK test to verify that both `cached` and `indexed` are passed
to `codex exec` as `web_search` config overrides.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0cf98c9a32f4da31fecc50da71acb601f6043b47

Tag user reports with the latest reasoning removal status (#62883)

## What changed

Set the `cot_removed` tag from the latest completed sampling
request on the live thread. Use `true` for reported reasoning removals
and `false` for an explicitly empty report. Omit the tag when no report
is available and discard any caller-supplied value.

Clear the stored result when thread history is replaced. A resumed
session starts without a stored result.

## Testing

Cover tag values in saved reports across tool calls, compaction, and
session resume. Verify that failed compaction preserves the last
sampling result.

GitOrigin-RevId: f1568567a6b4a62685569478fc7194f4357cb605

Compose managed domain rules across network config layers (#62882)

## Why

Managed requirements from different sources could not be combined when one
used `[permissions.network]` and another used `[network_proxy]` or
`[experimental_network]`.

## What changed

Allow these tables to compose across sources. The highest-priority list of
each kind replaces lower lists of that kind, while keyed `domains` entries
update individual selectors by source priority. A deny wins when a selector
appears in both surviving lists. A surviving `allowed_domains = []` clears
lower-priority grants, while an empty `domains` map contributes no updates.

Require mirrored domain declarations to agree on how they compose with other
domain sources. Unix socket path rules still require a single network table
spelling across sources.

Carry equivalent denied selector spellings into the effective proxy policy.
When local binding is disabled, an attached executor's explicit local grant
must also satisfy the controller's allowlist constraints. The standalone
proxy can still narrow a wildcard to an explicit local grant.

## Testing

Cover mixed table spellings, list replacement and clearing, conflicting
mirrors, equivalent IPv6 spellings, and local grants in standalone and
attached proxy modes.

GitOrigin-RevId: b3d550d9f462564c89663ea4b15e723f0ea76881

Allow new threads to opt out of Daybreak propagation (#62879)

## Why

App-server clients that prepare threads for later use need to be able
to skip Daybreak propagation for an individual thread when the server
configuration enables it.

## What changed

With `experimentalApi`, pass `daybreakProgramPropagationEnrolled: false`
to `thread/start` to opt a new root thread out. Managed requirements
take precedence. Omitting the field or passing `null` or `true` uses the
configured enrollment rule.

The same field on `Thread` reports actual enrollment for the live
session, including in the start response and `thread/started`
notification. Reusing a live session preserves its enrollment. A thread
returned from stored metadata alone reports `null`, and resuming it
from storage in a new session reports `false`.

## Testing

App-server tests cover enrollment under enabled, required, and disabled
configuration, as well as reporting across live reads and resumes,
unload, and resume from storage. A core test checks that opting out
prevents native helpers from inheriting the root's saved Daybreak choice.

GitOrigin-RevId: f9aae9ff76702b1e5a38d45120cd889a26f8ece5

Prewarm MCP servers during cloud catalog refresh (#62876)

## Why

A slow cloud skill lookup can delay MCP startup even after the plugin
catalog is ready. If the refresh is canceled while waiting for skills,
it can miss the chance to prewarm those servers before the first turn.

## What changed

Queue MCP prewarm as soon as plugin discovery changes or clears the
catalog. Skill discovery alone leaves the MCP server set unchanged.

At the end of the refresh, queue a retry for eligible MCP startup
failures. If discovery is canceled, check for those failures the next
time the catalog lock is acquired. Reuse pending handshakes and leave
authentication failures and Apps-managed reconnects to their existing
recovery paths.

## Testing

Add regression tests for first-turn tool availability after cancellation,
startup recovery with cloud plugins disabled, and a single retry for a
persistent startup failure.

GitOrigin-RevId: f92162d1629358953d8810d20244e55f07416a01

Preserve per-image metadata in app-server image generation items (#62871)

## Why

App-server clients lose metadata supplied by the image backend when
Codex turns the response into a completed image generation item.

## What changed

Expose the backend's `image_metadata` as optional `imageMetadata` in
app-server items and preserve nested values through thread persistence,
resume, and legacy history replay and migration. Keep this metadata out
of model tool output.

Omit empty metadata and discard non-object, oversized, or deeply nested
metadata without dropping the generated image.

## Testing

Extend coverage for per-image parsing, metadata limits, and round trips
through app-server completion, persisted history, and thread resume.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7211a9db1149cb05e6176b08b0462ca173ac72d5

Use runtime authentication for TUI WebRTC calls (#62870)

## Why

The TUI creates WebRTC calls locally, and that request path did not use
runtime agent authentication even when runtime agent instances were enabled.

## What changed

- Reuse local credential and runtime managers across calls while the login
  configuration stays the same. Reload first-party credentials before
  creating a call and keep network policy under the primary account owner's
  control.
- Use the shared provider request resolver for call authentication and HTTP
  transport. Apply the WebRTC base URL override before resolving credentials
  so runtime authentication is selected for the actual destination.

## Testing

Add mock-server coverage for concurrent calls sharing a runtime with fresh
assertions, credential changes, and both dual-header and assertion-only
modes. Cover the feature toggle, custom call destinations, network policy
permits, and provider credentials when the local login file is malformed.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6503b3375c79d3126911d1d7c1aea898face37b9

Enable configuration server OAuth during app-server startup (#62867)

## Why

When an organization's configuration server requires a new OAuth grant,
clients need a way to sign in before the app server starts so they can
load and validate the required settings.

## What changed

- Have `--print-startup-config` return the `configServerLogin` action
  when browser sign-in is required, and verify that the required server
  settings were applied before returning startup requirements.
- Add `codex app-server --startup-oauth`, a dedicated stdio mode that
  resolves the configuration server from local managed requirements,
  sends the client a browser authorization URL, and handles the callback,
  token exchange, and credential storage. Clients can cancel a pending
  sign-in or rerun `--print-startup-config` after it succeeds.

## Testing

Add a test that checks the browser handoff URL and verifies that
cancellation completes the pending login request with `LoginFailed`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 00f10d28befe33539882f4f3c0d2baf868ceb4a1

Defer Windows sandbox owner restoration until sign-in (#62865)

## Why

At boot, the recorded Windows session may no longer exist or may not
have a user token yet. The sandbox service can retry restoration when a
session change signals sign-in.

## What changed

Treat missing sessions, missing tokens, and sessions belonging to
another user as owner unavailability. Search the other sessions for the
recorded owner's SID. If no session restores the owner, report the first
restoration error if one occurred, or let the service retry on a later
session change.

GitOrigin-RevId: c40971e70c6eee46068aafe534c0f0147d16bb77

Keep agent concurrency guidance when native tools are disabled (#62864)

## Why

Disabling native multi-agent tools also dropped the default guidance about
how many agents can be active in a session. That limit still matters for
agents running on a host that handles turn admission.

## What changed

When `multi_agent_v2.disable_native_tools` is set, root agents and
subagents receive only the configured
`multi_agent_v2.max_concurrent_threads_per_session` in their default role
guidance. Explicit role overrides retain precedence, and empty role text
still suppresses the guidance.

## Testing

Cover both roles with bundled and catalog-provided role text. Update the
request snapshots for explicit and proactive delegation to show the
concurrency hint with native tools hidden.

GitOrigin-RevId: e940e7a7886b69888002307c021607b19bb87cd0

Ask the Responses API to omit the echoed tool catalog (#62863)

Set `x-codex-exclude: tools` in the shared Responses API request headers.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6d46bf95fd1b88a4e01e7d0d3b3d995b4a3f6545

Define the startup OAuth protocol for config servers (#62859)

## What changed

Add the optional `target` field to `account/gatewayOAuth/login`.
The startup protocol defines `{"kind":"configServer"}` as a target
for `--startup-oauth`, mutually exclusive with `modelProvider`.
The regular app-server login handler rejects explicit targets.

Define `StartupGatewayOAuthChangedNotification` with the target,
status, and authorization URL for the browser handoff. Export the
new types in the JSON schemas, TypeScript bindings, and Python SDK.

## Testing

Update the TUI device login regression test to expect `target: null`
when signing in to a resumed thread's saved gateway.

GitOrigin-RevId: fb3ce66a143cad9ad56c93f3ac37f8b6f1abdb0e

Keep Cloud threads current in the Agents overview (#62858)

## Why

The Agents overview can go stale when Cloud threads change from another
client, especially when the TUI has no conversation stream attached.

## What changed

- Use Cloud stream notifications to update thread status and refresh the
  thread list. Poll every 10 seconds while the overview is visible and
  no stream is attached.
- Refresh the history already shown while preserving the `Show more`
  cursor. Use fresh list metadata for thread names, recency, and unread
  state, and restore rows when a refresh catches a missed unarchive.

## Testing

Cover Cloud inventory notifications, polling while detached, pagination
across refreshes, and recovery from a missed unarchive.

GitOrigin-RevId: 63c98438b6ddd2e47dd2d1f419c2a676508c6d91

Defer built-in Default mode instructions until after Plan mode (#62857)

## Why

Threads that stay in Default mode carry a collaboration-mode prompt even
though they have no Plan mode instructions to supersede.

## What changed

Omit bundled and model-catalog Default mode instructions until a thread
uses Plan mode. Emit Plan mode instructions on entry and Default mode
instructions when switching back. Preserve eligible caller-provided
instructions and carry the active mode through compaction and resume.

## Testing

Cover prompt contents before, during, and after Plan mode in core and
app-server tests, including compaction and resume in the core tests.

GitOrigin-RevId: b734767da15be53c4eccae71994e46eba63a9ecc

Specialize OpenTelemetry providers for HTTP traces and metrics (#62854)

## Why

The code-mode host exports traces over OTLP/HTTP, and the elevated Windows
Filtering Platform setup helper exports Statsig metrics. Both used the
general-purpose provider, which made exporter builders for unused signals
and transports reachable from those binaries.

## What changed

Add `OtelProvider::try_new_http_traces` for the code-mode host and
`OtelProvider::try_new_http_metrics` for the Windows setup helper. Select
exporter builders at compile time so each constructor reaches only the
builders it needs. Both constructors reject unsupported signals and gRPC
configuration. The metrics constructor also accepts Statsig.

## Testing

Add unit tests for unsupported signals and gRPC configuration. Exercise
the specialized constructors in the HTTP loopback tests for trace delivery
on a current-thread Tokio runtime and cumulative metrics export.

GitOrigin-RevId: 875916791f0176839764c51b5ab289d5dc45a4d2

Limit guardian response resampling to one retry (#62852)

## Why

When the retried response also meets the guardian's resampling criteria,
it can trigger another model request and keep the turn from finishing.

## What changed

Consume the original prompt when scheduling the retry. The second
verdict stays buffered until completion and is replayed after usage
accounting, even if it also meets the resampling criteria. Usage from
the discarded first response still counts toward spending.

GitOrigin-RevId: f8ded8f31bd7d9e440c0c92a92a80480acec61d2

Reduce allocations when preparing tool schemas and catalogs (#62849)

## Why

Tool schema budget checks cloned the schema and allocated a JSON buffer
just to measure its size. Building a Responses Lite catalog also cloned
tool definitions before serializing them.

## What changed

- Deserialize schemas from borrowed JSON during compaction, count
  serialized bytes without allocating a buffer, and reuse the parsed
  schema when it fits the budget.
- Serialize borrowed tool specs and namespace members directly, and pass
  filtered specs as an iterator. Preserve the serialized namespace field
  order because the bytes contribute to the `additional_tools` item ID.

## Testing

- Compare the exact serialized Responses Lite catalog against the
  expected namespace layout.
- Add a `tool_catalog` benchmark for connector schema preparation and
  Responses Lite catalog encoding with 1 and 64 tool specs.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6bd03a12fcedd4abfa8c3a03f298243483e98c63

Return an assessment for explicit Guardian reviews (#62846)

## Why

An explicit `thread/guardianReview` request could return a null assessment when live execution would skip approval, leaving callers without a verdict on the recorded action.

## What changed

Require `assessment` on every successful `thread/guardianReview` response. Review eligible recorded calls even when a command is allowlisted, an MCP tool is configured for automatic approval or has a remembered approval, or the policy disables permission requests. The review runs without executing the call or granting permissions.

Include the MCP server's owning environment permissions in the review context, matching live review.

## Testing

Cover allowlisted commands, permission requests with prompting disabled, and automatically approved MCP tools. Compare live and recorded MCP review input for a server whose owning environment has denied paths.

GitOrigin-RevId: 54689dc043d77f940e10d29842308340f6937980

Tag all multi-agent role instructions consistently (#62842)

## Why

Only catalog role instructions carried the `<multi_agent_role>` tag,
so the same guidance appeared in different formats depending on its source.

## What changed

Render bundled, catalog, and configured root and subagent guidance as
`multi_agent.role_instructions` developer messages. Wrap the guidance in
`<multi_agent_role>` tags and preserve configured text that's already tagged.
Match untagged parent guidance by its body when filtering forked history.

## Testing

Update prompt and session assertions for tagged role instructions, and keep
the cold-resume test exercising a rollout with legacy untagged guidance.

GitOrigin-RevId: 60c55b5d7227811b92bd1bf125f1cd3a965720fd

Reuse one syntax highlighter when building TUI Markdown styles (#62840)

## Why

Building Markdown styles clones the active syntax theme and constructs a new
highlighter for each foreground lookup.

## What changed

Borrow the active theme and use one highlighter for all foreground lookups
in `MarkdownStyles`. Preserve the readability adjustment for text styles
and the accent-color fallback for inline code.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8ddfad7e61e2dc7968398ff3bdecd3b389c1bb07

Load managed cloud config for plugin add and list (#62837)

## Why

`codex plugin add` and `codex plugin list` loaded configuration without
the managed cloud configuration layer, so plugin discovery and
installation could miss settings supplied by that layer.

## What changed

Use the shared cloud-aware configuration builder for add and list,
passing through CLI overrides. Keep `codex plugin remove` on the local
configuration loader and use the loaded configuration's Codex home
for all three commands.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5ebe94de30e553c57ae6296a2ddb91792260a61f

Record MCP tool call outcomes in traces (#62833)

## Why

A successful JSON-RPC exchange can still return a failed tool result.
MCP error metrics count that failure, but the trace span can lack an
error status. Dropped calls can also leave spans without an outcome.

## What changed

Record `codex.mcp.call.outcome` on `mcp.tools.call` spans and mark
failures with OpenTelemetry error status using the same classification
as the metrics. Record `interrupted` when the call future is dropped
before completion, including before its first poll.

Capture the numeric JSON-RPC error code in `rpc.jsonrpc.error_code`
when available, leaving server error messages and data out of the span.

## Testing

Extend in-memory telemetry tests to check that spans and metrics agree
on error classification and that span attributes omit sensitive test
values. Cover success and cancellation before the first poll and while
the call is pending.

GitOrigin-RevId: 57fcdc36f19cfc2f227c1ec964a932f3cf7eaa04

Let required hooks block continuation on failure (#62831)

## Why

A required hook check can fail to run or return a usable result. Continuing
after that failure can let an action proceed without a completed check.

## What changed

Add per-handler `onFailure` for command and MCP tool hooks. The default
`continue` preserves existing behavior. On supported synchronous hooks,
`block` applies the event's blocking behavior and reports the reason while
preserving failure diagnostics. For example, a failed `PreToolUse` check
prevents the tool from running, while a failed `PostToolUse` check withholds
the result of a tool that already ran.

Expose the policy in the app-server's `configRequirements/read` response.

## Testing

Add tests for command and MCP failures under both policies, and scenario
coverage for blocked tool execution, withheld results, and completion after
a `Stop` hook recovers.

GitOrigin-RevId: 20d6ebda0094382fe052bbf34338edb994cc7bd3

Apply elastic Guardian budgets to retained user and sender evidence (#62829)

## Why

Fixed retention limits could discard long user instructions or leave
older sender messages out of Guardian review even when the configured
elastic budget had room for them.

## What changed

- Apply the configured retained-instruction entry limit when capturing
  and restoring user messages. Fixed-budget reviewers use the fixed
  retention window for both user and assistant messages.
- Build elastic sender snapshots at delivery using the receiver's sender
  evidence budget. Give recent user messages first claim on space, then
  include preceding assistant context where it fits. Mark omitted
  evidence and save the snapshot for review and rollback.

## Testing

Add coverage for cross-host delivery after compaction, large sender
snapshots through checkpoint restore and rollback, and how synchronous
and asynchronous reviewers read saved or empty sender snapshots.

GitOrigin-RevId: f0b01a2d558e3286335efac85a4f8645dd9b954b

Honor Guardian retention settings for assistant messages (#62828)

## Why

The fixed retention window can discard assistant messages before elastic
Guardian reviews can use them as context for a user's reply.

## What changed

Apply the thread's Guardian retention policy when recording assistant messages,
including confirmed messages sent through the user messaging tool. Keep full
text within the configured record limit and the overall assistant history byte
budget. Preserve an incomplete marker when a confirmed delivery exceeds the
record limit.

Recover the thread's retention settings from saved history and compaction
checkpoints. Fixed-budget reviews continue to use the fixed retention window.

## Testing

Add coverage for record limits during capture and restore, thread-owned
settings recovery, and replay of oversized confirmed deliveries.

GitOrigin-RevId: e828f06824ce6712910a9cc5ef42a438d1ddf27e

Persist Guardian retention limits in thread settings (#62827)

## What changed

At session startup, derive `assistant_record_bytes` from the Sync Elastic
per-entry token limit for retained user instructions. Use the default
section limit when the configuration omits that section.

Store the resolved byte limit in the optional `guardian_retention` field
of `ThreadSettingsSnapshot` and update the app-server schema. Fixed-mode
snapshots omit the field, and older snapshots can still be read.

GitOrigin-RevId: a8de88c5bd0e35c4a114577e70fb0c858acb13c9

Enable OAuth discovery by default for config servers (#62824)

## Why

Config servers that publish OAuth metadata still required administrators
to configure OAuth endpoints explicitly for Codex to use them.

## What changed

- Discover OAuth metadata when `config_server.oauth` is omitted. Use
  explicit settings when provided, and fetch managed configuration
  anonymously when discovery finds no metadata.
- Have the Git credential helper resolve the config server before
  fetching managed configuration. It refuses explicit or discovered
  OAuth so it can apply workspace policy without opening the OS keyring.
- Apply local network policy to discovery during `codex logout`.

## Testing

Cover app-server recovery after a discovery failure, Git credential
helper rejection of explicit OAuth without a network request, and
logout discovery blocked by local network policy.

GitOrigin-RevId: c7f50510531b456c0e547e8b7cb15d4bdbcca0bb

Include native USD in ChatGPT turn cost telemetry (#62810)

## Why

When a turn incurs usage priced directly in USD, reporting only the
credit-converted estimate understates its cost.

## What changed

Sum `estimated_usage_usd_micros` and `native_usage_usd_micros` for
settled turns. Default an omitted native USD field to zero for legacy
responses. Suppress the total when either component is unavailable
(including explicit null), either is negative, or their sum overflows.

## Testing

Cover omitted and null native USD values, zero costs, negative amounts,
and overflow in backend client tests. Verify that the combined amount
reaches the OTLP exporter in the app-server integration test.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8709e48329db813cd66baf270ee3f1bcfd87cb03

Remove model-selected Search MCP routing (#62808)

## What changed

Use the turn's effective `web_search` mode for standalone and hosted
web search. Remove model-selected Search MCP discovery, fallback, and
provider tracking across thread resumes.

Remove `web_search_provider` from model metadata, the
`tools.client_search_provider` hint from configuration, and the
`hosted_search_policy` feature flag. Update the app-server schemas and

GitOrigin-RevId: 59e3371f4a43d532a484db52d5998f6770292028

Reset TUI thread-switch state on reconnect (#62807)

## Why

Reconnect replaces the app event queue, so queued thread-switch events can be
discarded while their resets are still counted as pending.

## What changed

- Clear the pending thread-switch reset count when replacing the event queue
  and use a shared accessor for the displayed thread during reconnect.
- Box the app event dispatch future and extract helpers for choosing the side
  conversation target and rendering the composer pane.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6bb14443952262b6a0df7fdf05db053038c7ce2d

Read Responses WebSocket messages during blocked uploads (#62771)

## Why

When a server stops reading a request, the client's WebSocket write can
stall. If the server sends a Ping or rejects the request while the write
is blocked, the client can leave that message unread until the write
fails or times out.

## What changed

Poll for incoming messages before each outgoing frame and while a write
is pending. On subsequent polls, give the pending write first use of
Tokio's cooperative budget and cap read-ahead across the entire upload.

## Testing

Add regression tests for Pong delivery before upload completion, early
size-limit closes, and bounded read-ahead without write starvation.
Cover error precedence for buffered peer replies, local send failures,
and network policy revocation, plus token usage when a close arrives
before an interrupt can be sent.

GitOrigin-RevId: c018c25dcdc70b64835b07935caede5e34dfa8f2

Recover server replies after Responses WebSocket write failures (#62749)

## Why

A server can reject an oversized request after reading just the first
frame header. If the upload then fails with a broken pipe, the write
error can hide the server's message-too-large close.

## What changed

After a write fails partway through an upload, drain immediately
readable replies within the send deadline and a bounded read budget.
Use those replies to surface server errors, including
`WebsocketMessageTooLarge`. Treat a close seen before the first frame
as belonging to the idle connection, and retire the socket after a
failed send.

## Testing

Add regression tests for size-limit closes on an idle socket, just
before the first frame, and after a partial first-frame write fails
with pings and pongs ahead of the close.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2feeb1961992b425dbec06129015dbe4c44ff3f2

Flush idle Responses WebSocket pongs under backpressure (#62742)

## Why

An idle Responses WebSocket still needs to answer server pings when the
write buffer is full. The pong must finish flushing once the peer drains
the socket, even if no further messages or requests arrive.

## What changed

Have the WebSocket pump flush automatically queued pongs and retry pending
flushes as the socket becomes writable. Bound incoming polling and the
number of pongs tracked while a flush is pending.

## Testing

Add an in-memory WebSocket test that forces a partial pong write and
checks that the peer receives the full heartbeat reply without further
traffic.

GitOrigin-RevId: 12865842c80a8a25a5e107be690f9c3962ce9775

Link agent tool calls to delivered messages in rollout traces (#62709)

## Why

Matching messages by text can link a tool call to an earlier message
with the same content. A recipient can also accept a message without
ever including it in a model request.

## What changed

Record the originating tool call ID when the recipient adds a spawn,
task assignment, or message to its history. On replay, use that ID to
link the accepted message to its sender even if the recipient records
it before the sender tool finishes.

Keep the interaction edge pointed at the recipient thread until the
message appears in a model request. Track distinct conversation items
across history resets and count repeated prompt prefixes only once.

## Testing

Replay tests cover identical message text, receipt before tool
completion, and messages observed again after compaction.

GitOrigin-RevId: ccab7c33993ba5fce7fceb733dc90c9d428ec78f

Match TUI task mentions by displayed title (#62691)

## What changed

Use state database-backed `thread/list` requests for task mentions without
searching conversation contents. Merge title-filtered results with recent
threads by thread ID so a full filtered page cannot crowd out recent
candidates. Native Cloud uses the recent list because it lacks a title filter.

Fuzzy-match the displayed title in the picker. Keep the working directory
visible as a description and exclude it from matching.

## Testing

Cover remote listing, retention of recent candidates when the filtered page
is full, and fallback when the filtered request times out. Check that a
directory-only match stays out of the picker.

GitOrigin-RevId: ec2a5ae9f046e533104251fd82f6683343854ee0

Let administrators disable Codex daemon updates (#62690)

## Why

The daemon's automatic update preference still permits manual updates.
Administrators need a policy that covers both paths.

## What changed

Set `features.daemon_updates = false` in managed `requirements.toml` or
local MDM policy to block scheduled updates and manual daemon package
replacements. Updates are allowed by default. User configuration cannot
override the policy, and cloud-delivered requirements reject the setting.

When policy blocks updates, the TUI hides update actions in `/daemon`,
suppresses update offers in version notices, and directs users to their
administrator where a newer daemon is required.

## Testing

Add coverage for the default, disabled, and invalid policy cases,
rejection of the setting in cloud requirements, and the TUI with daemon
updates disabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: de9e50c4acc4dc8e83bbd2b9a5e902deb8c6f477

Copy pasted image files into temporary TUI attachments (#62687)

## Why

A pasted image path could become unreadable before submission if the
original file was moved or deleted.

## What changed

Copy the image into a private temporary file at paste time and use that
copy as the attachment. Apply a 1 GiB limit when saving image files and
clipboard PNGs. If copying a pasted image path fails, show an error and
preserve the draft.

## Testing

Cover attachment readability after deleting the original file and verify
that an oversized image paste reports an error and preserves the draft.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5f797979f36173fb3355345e0f124b81fcf86d01

Allow hosts to route selected analytics events (#62684)

## Why

The analytics client sends eligible events through HTTP. Hosts that
embed Codex need a way to deliver specific event types themselves while
keeping HTTP delivery for the rest of the batch.

## What changed

Add `AnalyticsEventsClient::new_with_event_transport` so hosts can opt
in and select eligible events by wire type. The transport receives the
complete wire payload and the event's product SKU, when available.
Events stay on the HTTP path unless the transport returns `Handled`,
which suppresses a duplicate HTTP send.

Disabled analytics and local file capture bypass the transport.
Rebinding the client to a new auth context restores HTTP delivery.

## Testing

Add tests for mixed batches that verify HTTP payloads and product
attribution, plus coverage for auth eligibility, local capture,
analytics opt-out, and auth rebinding.

GitOrigin-RevId: 27ba3fe54050754b5f844f00e7e761a4d7bcb8c0

Retry executor discovery V2 failures with backoff (#62679)

## Why

Discovery could retry transport failures on successive lookups while
caching server errors until invalidation. That could repeat requests
against an unhealthy executor or leave a session without an inventory
after the server recovered.

## What changed

Cache failed discovery loads per context and return the cached error
during cooldown. The first lookup after cooldown retries, with delays
doubling from 1 second up to 30 seconds on consecutive failures.
Successful inventories are reused, canceled loads add no cooldown, and
explicit refresh clears the cooldown for the next lookup without
interrupting in-flight readers.

Compare discovery snapshots to detect inventory changes so recovered
plugins and MCP capabilities can become available without an explicit
refresh.

## Testing

Cover backoff timing, shared results for concurrent callers,
cancellation, and refresh bypassing cooldown. Exercise recovery after
failed prewarming and verify that MCP inventory updates after recovery.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6de34bb8957a0b24ee874e2447157bd3af562430

Keep explicitly pinned history outside the carryover token budget (#62677)

## Why

An exhausted carryover budget could drop explicitly pinned items, and an
oversized pin could crowd out ordinary user messages during local compaction.

## What changed

Preserve eligible pins in full and in their original order for the current
thread, child threads, or both, according to their retention policy. Apply
the carryover budget to the remaining history, including items retained by
features without an explicit pin.

## Testing

Add regression tests for destination-specific pins at zero budget and for
keeping an ordinary user message alongside an oversized pin during local
compaction.

GitOrigin-RevId: fc8529bcc254d8e7a4a010337ce760e94daa4bef

Force executor capability rescans after V2 cache invalidation (#62675)

## Why

Invalidating Codex's discovery cache could still return stale inventory
if the executor reused its cached snapshot before its file watcher
reported a change.

## What changed

Add an optional `forceReload` flag to `capabilities/discoverV2` that
makes the executor rescan its files. Codex sends it on the next lookup
of each invalidated context. Explicit reloads also replace the matching
cache entry so subsequent ordinary requests can reuse the fresh result.

## Testing

Add coverage for discovering a newly added skill before the watcher
runs, forwarding the reload flag after invalidation, and reusing
refreshed results.

GitOrigin-RevId: c98f2b8d4772e10b74ff09dd382ad8386857158f

Prewarm executor capability discovery during remote startup (#62674)

## Why

Step-time discovery can make the first step that needs a remote executor
inventory wait for a discovery round trip. Starting discovery during
environment setup lets deferred turns begin sampling while the inventory
is being fetched.

## What changed

When executor capability discovery V2 is enabled, prewarm the thread's
discovery cache for supported remote executors before marking their
environments ready. Reserve cache capacity for all selected environments
so the first step can reuse their inventories.

Give each prewarm up to five seconds and let environment startup proceed
after discovery errors or a timeout. Step-time discovery reuses cached
successes and permanent errors and can retry transient failures and
timed-out loads.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for deferred readiness and cache reuse after
success, permanent errors, transient failures, and timeouts. Also cover
cache retention across multiple environments and session startup when
discovery receives no reply.

fix(gemini realtime): report barge-in as cancelled response.done (#52596)

* fix(gemini realtime): report barge-in as cancelled response.done

Gemini/Vertex Live interruptions now close the cut-off item as incomplete and
end with one response.done status=cancelled, reason=turn_detected, carrying
the usage from Gemini's trailing turnComplete. Previously the interruption
looked like a normal completion and a phantom second response.done held the
tokens. Resolves LIT-9749.

* fix(gemini realtime): close transcript-first items on barge-in

A response opened by outputTranscription before any audio left the delta
type unset, so a barge-in in that window never closed the item. Record the
audio delta type when the transcript opens the item, which also closes it
on generationComplete in a normal turn. Rewrite the test helper without
mutation.

* fix(gemini realtime): end the turn when generationComplete and turnComplete share a frame

A frame carrying both flags took the generationComplete path only, so the
item closed but response.done never fired. Route it to the turn end and
close the open item there. Type the test helper with the real event types.

* test(gemini realtime): type the interruption tests

Annotate the added tests' parameters and locals (Final, -> None).

* fix(gemini realtime): bill buffered interruption usage when the session closes

If Gemini reports usage on the interrupted frame, that usage waits for the
trailing turnComplete. A session that closes in between used to drop it, while
main billed it on the interrupted frame's own response.done. Add an
unbilled_response_on_session_close hook (None by default); Gemini returns the
cancelled response.done carrying the buffered usage, and the realtime stream logs
it at session close next to the transcription usage flush.

* fix(gemini realtime): flush close-time usage only for an interrupted response

Usage buffered from a tool call's trailing turnComplete or a standalone usage frame no longer becomes a never-created completed response.done at session close. Add an integration test: a real proxy and a scripted Vertex Live upstream, a session closed after the interrupted frame, and the spend row carrying that frame's usage.

feat(guardrails): hold streamed tool calls for the verdict and log prompts blocked with a reply (#51872)

* feat(guardrails): opt-in hold of streamed tool calls until the end-of-stream verdict

A guardrail that checks a live stream once, at its end (streaming_end_of_stream_only
without streaming_buffer_until_moderated), releases every chunk as it arrives and
holds back only the stream's final frames. A tool call in that stream reaches the
client before the verdict exists, so a client that runs tools has already run it
when the guardrail blocks.

streaming_hold_tool_calls is a new streaming flag, off by default and read the same
way as the other streaming flags. With it on, the shared streaming loop also holds
everything from the first item that starts a tool call the client would run. Text
before the tool call still streams live. The held items are released in order when
the check passes and dropped when it blocks, through the handling the final frames
already had.

The hold applies in every mode that releases a stream before its end-of-stream
verdict: scanned once at its end, scanned every few chunks in the foreground or in
the background, and the incremental text transform, which keeps back its raw
tool-call chunks until its end-of-stream block inspection. A stream buffered until
moderated already waits for a scan and is unchanged.

A held tool call is released only on a verdict that covered it. A stream that stops
without its terminal marker (an upstream error, a cut connection) is scanned closed
the way its endpoint ends a stream, as it already is after a client disconnect.

Each endpoint translation answers starts_client_tool_call for one stream item, so
nothing re-walks the stream: chat completions, messages, responses (every output
item the client runs) and the Bedrock pass-through frames, Converse and invoke.
The base answer is False: a guardrail that does not set the flag, and an endpoint
with no answer of its own, behave as before.

With the flag on, the loop reads the stream in whole frames. Native /v1/messages
relays raw transport reads, so an SSE event can arrive split across two of them,
which hides the start of a tool call, and the end of the stream, from a check that
reads one item at a time. split_whole_stream_frames cuts each read at the last
frame boundary and carries the rest into the next read. The client receives the
same bytes.

The Straiker guardrail sets the flag when stream_mode is "streaming". "buffered"
already holds the whole response and is unchanged.

* feat(guardrails): opt-in failure logging for a prompt blocked with a reply

A guardrail that blocks the prompt by raising ModifyResponseException is answered
with an HTTP 200 reply. The LLM is never called and the reply runs no success
logging, so the block reaches no logging callback on non-streamed chat completions,
messages, responses or text completions. Only a streamed chat completion logs it,
as a success event from the stream wrapper.

ModifyResponseException takes a new log_as_failure argument, off by default. When
a block sets it, post_call_failure_hook treats it like the other proxy-only errors
and sends one failure event to the logging callbacks.
The streamed chat completion path tells the hook its reply already logs a success
event, so that route still logs exactly one event.

A guardrail that does not set it behaves as before. Blocked answers and the spend
logs are unchanged.

The Straiker guardrail sets it on the reply it raises for a blocked prompt.

* fix(guardrails): always run the end-of-stream round while a tool call is held

The end-of-stream round was skipped as redundant when its scan key equalled the
key of the last sampled round. A scan key carries only what a translation
fingerprints, so with a held item it does not fingerprint (a Responses
shell_call, apply_patch_call or computer_call), the keys matched and the item was
released with no round after it arrived. The round now always runs while a tool
call is held, so a guardrail that reads the whole response judges the item.

The whole-frame split goes through a typed translation variable. The untyped
lookup it used left three later call sites partially unknown to the type checker.

Tests: the blocked-prompt logging test waits for the callback instead of a fixed
delay, and the new recording callback and its fixtures are typed.

* fix(guardrails): hold the whole stream on a route that cannot tell a tool call apart

With streaming_hold_tool_calls on, a translation with no tool-call detection, the
native Gemini generateContent one for example, answered that no stream item starts
a tool call, so a functionCall part reached the client before the end-of-stream
verdict.

The base answer of starts_client_tool_call is now True: a translation that cannot
tell a tool call apart holds its whole stream for the verdict. Text completions
answer False, since they carry no tool calls. A pass-through stream no translation
reads is not scanned at all, so it is still not held.

A guardrail that does not set the flag is unaffected.

* feat(straiker): hold_tool_calls option to turn the streamed tool-call hold off

In stream_mode `streaming` the guardrail holds a tool call the client would
run until the end-of-stream verdict. That was fixed on, with no way out for a
deployment that prefers tool calls to stream as they arrive.

`hold_tool_calls` (default true) is read only in `streaming` mode. False
releases tool calls as they arrive, as before the hold existed. A value the
initializer cannot read keeps the hold and logs a warning: raising there
would start the proxy without the guardrail.

* feat(guardrails): tell a function call apart on Gemini streams, so only it is held

With the tool-call hold on, the native Gemini generateContent route held its
whole stream for the verdict, because its translation could not tell a tool
call apart. Text that streamed live before arrived in one burst at the end.

The translation now recognises a functionCall part. Text streams live and
everything from the first function call waits for the verdict. An item it
cannot read for a function call (a cut event, a payload that is not a JSON
object) still waits.

A translation that never scans a stream gives no verdict to hold for, so the
base answer now holds a whole stream only for a translation that scans it.

* test(guardrails): type the new test helpers and drop a banned suppression

The hold_tool_calls tests in test_straiker.py left parameters and return
types unannotated, and the Gemini detection table used `# type: ignore`,
which the repository bans. The fixture now builds the second candidate with
a typed helper instead of indexing into a dict.

fix(anthropic)!: send extra_body fields at the top level of the Messages request (#48373)

* fix(anthropic): send extra_body fields at the top level of the Messages request

extra_body passed to litellm.completion for an Anthropic model reached the
Messages API as a literal nested "extra_body" key, and Anthropic rejected the
request with "extra_body: Extra inputs are not permitted". That blocked every
Anthropic request field litellm doesn't model yet, including server-side
fallbacks

AnthropicConfig.transform_request now pops extra_body from the request params
and merges its keys into the wire body. The direct Anthropic, Vertex AI and
Azure paths all go through this transform. Paths on llm_http_handler, like
Bedrock invoke, already pop extra_body before transform_request, so nothing
is merged twice. extra_body only adds fields the request doesn't already
have. It can't override anything litellm built, can't change the model
(EXTRA_BODY_ROUTING_KEYS), and can't set messages or system, so content
that pre-call guardrails checked or redacted is the content that is sent

fallbacks is registered in BETA_GATED_FIELDS under both betas that unlock it,
server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 and server-side-fallback-2026-06-01. Under
drop_params a request that doesn't end up sending either of them, like a
Vertex AI leg where the 07-01 beta is filtered out or a deployment without
the header, drops fallbacks with a warning instead of getting a 400

The proxy rejects fallbacks inside a client's extra_body with a 400. Anthropic
runs the fallback model itself, so those targets never reach the key's model
access checks. Server-side fallback is set in the deployment's litellm_params
instead, next to the beta header the admin already configures there

When Anthropic serves a turn from a fallback model, usage.iterations spans
models, so its entries are no longer summed. The top-level usage, which
Anthropic documents as the attempt that served the turn, is priced at the
response's model. Attempts that declined with a billed refusal category are
not priced yet

The regression tests drive litellm.completion end to end against a mock
transport and assert the request body

* fix(anthropic): never take tools from extra_body

The proxy checks a key's or team's allowed tools against the request's
top-level tools only. A tools list inside extra_body skipped that check
and still reached Anthropic when the request had no top-level tools, so
extra_body now never supplies tools, like messages and system.

* fix(anthropic): keep every fallback attempt in usage

Dropping usage.iterations for a server-side fallback chain left only the
serving attempt in spend, so billed refusals on earlier attempts escaped
key and team budgets. Usage is back to adding up every attempt, which can
overcount but never lets billed tokens escape. #50556 prices each attempt
at its own model's rate.

* fix(proxy): reject fallbacks inside a fallback target's extra_body

A litellm fallback target can carry its own extra_body, which the router
merges into the request when that target runs. The proxy only rejected
fallbacks in the request's own extra_body, so a target's extra_body could
still pick Anthropic server-side fallback models the key isn't allowed to
use. Every fallback target's extra_body now gets the same check.

* test(anthropic): type the extra_body request test

* fix(anthropic): let extra_body override defaults on every Claude route and admit client fallbacks through the admin opt-ins

extra_body now wins over fields litellm set, so its max_tokens takes effect, while model, messages,
system, tools, and stream stay litellm's on anthropic/, azure_ai, and Bedrock invoke. A non-object
extra_body answers 400 instead of a retried 500. Bedrock invoke drops extra_body fallbacks under
drop_params without a fallback beta, like anthropic/. Client extra_body fallbacks go through the
banned-param opt-ins (allow_client_side_credentials or configurable_clientside_auth_params)

* fix(anthropic): let extra_body lower max_tokens but never raise it past the request's cap

The rate limiter reserves output tokens from the top-level max_tokens, so an
extra_body max_tokens above it would spend tokens the limiter never reserved.

* fix(anthropic): answer 400 for extra_body keys litellm builds unless drop_params is on

Setting model, messages, system, tools or stream in extra_body now answers 400 naming them, or drops them under drop_params, on anthropic/, Vertex AI, Azure AI and Bedrock invoke Claude. Databricks keeps sending extra_body as it is, and a non-object extra_body error is returned as a value

* fix(vertex_ai): apply the batch row's drop_params to its extra_body

A Claude batch row's extra_body merge got an empty litellm_params, so drop_params set on the row or deployment never reached the extra_body rule and a field litellm builds answered 400 instead of being dropped

* fix(anthropic): add the beta headers a field sent in extra_body needs

A field like context_management sent in extra_body reached Anthropic at the top level without the anthropic-beta header that the same top-level field gets, so Anthropic answered 400. The extra_body fields litellm forwards now count toward the beta headers too

* fix(anthropic): answer 400 for a raised extra_body max_tokens and promote system on Azure AI and OpenCode Go

An extra_body max_tokens above the request's answers 400 unless drop_params
is on, which caps it, so the output tokens the limiters reserved still bound
the call. Keys litellm builds that extra_body tries to set are dropped with a
warning under drop_params. Azure AI and OpenCode Go send extra_body.system as
the system prompt, since litellm moves a top-level system kwarg there.
extra_body output_config now wins over the mapped one, and transform_request
no longer pops extra_body from the caller's optional_params.

* fix(bedrock): keep the extra_body guard on Bedrock Mantle without the invoke beta strip

Bedrock Mantle inherits the Bedrock invoke extra_body guard. feat(upgrade): add a per-tool bump option to exclude a tool from --bump (#15947)

`mise upgrade --bump` rewrites every tool's request past its configured
range. For some tools that is never wanted: `node = "lts"` bumps to a
non-LTS Current, Java vendor selectors bump to an unrelated version, and
deliberately pinned tools get rewritten. Until now the only control was
`-x` on every invocation, which tools that run `mise upgrade` for you
(such as topgrade) cannot pass.

A tool can now opt out with a `bump` option:

```toml
[tools]
node = { version = "lts", bump = false }
```

`mise upgrade --bump` and `mise outdated --bump` then treat that tool
like plain `mise upgrade`: it is upgraded within its request and
mise.toml is not rewritten. Plain `upgrade` is unaffected. Naming the
tool (`mise upgrade node --bump`, `mise outdated --bump node`) still
bumps it, so an explicit request wins over the config.

`bump` is not available in `.tool-versions`, which has no table to hold
it.

`mise outdated` now passes the tools it was asked about as a filter
rather than only narrowing the toolset, so it can tell a named tool from
a sweep. Output for existing configs is unchanged.

Discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15946

Verified with a new e2e test (`test_upgrade_bump_option`) and the
existing bump tests. `cargo clippy` reports one unrelated error in
`crates/mise-ui` that also fails on `origin/main`.

fix(java): resolve sdkman temurin hotfixes by their canonical version (#15928)

`.sdkmanrc` entries for recent Temurin hotfix releases fail to install.
With `idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools = ["java"]` and

```
java=25.0.5.1+2-tem
```

`mise install` reports `no metadata found for version
temurin-25.0.5+102`. The #15877 fix for #15872 computed the catalog
version as `hotfix * 100 + build`, but Adoptium changed how it encodes
those builds, so the formula no longer matches (reported in discussion
#14872).

The catalog (mise-java#647) now lists a Temurin hotfix under its
canonical Java version, the same name SDKMAN uses: `temurin-25.0.5.1+2`
and `temurin-25.0.4.1+1`, where it used to list `+100000002` and `+101`.
mise therefore no longer translates a hotfix: `java=25.0.5.1+2-tem`
resolves to `temurin-25.0.5.1`, which selects that release. Regular
releases written with a `.0` fourth component, such as `21.0.13.0+9`,
still map to `temurin-21.0.13+9`.

This needs the regenerated catalog, which is live now. Anyone pinning an
old hotfix string, such as `temurin-25.0.4+101`, has to switch to
`temurin-25.0.4.1+1`.

## Testing

Unit tests cover the hotfix and padded-version cases and the `.sdkmanrc`
parse. `cargo clippy -p mise --all-features --all-targets -- -D
warnings` passes on stable. I did not run an end-to-end install against
the live catalog.

fix(lock): skip platforms a tool has no build for in --check (#15941)

`mise lock --check` failed on a lockfile that `mise lock` had just
written whenever one tool had no build for a platform that another tool
in the same lockfile had. Running `mise lock` again changed nothing, so
the hint could not fix it.

```toml
[tools]
diffoci = "0.1.8" # no Windows build
gh = "2.103.3"
```

```sh
mise lock
mise lock --check   # before: "No lockfile URL found for diffoci@0.1.8 on platform windows-x64", exit 1
```

Without `--platform`, `--check` takes every platform any entry in the
lockfile has and checks each tool against all of them. `mise lock`
records nothing for a platform a tool has no build for, so `--check`
could not tell that apart from an entry that went missing.

Now, when no platform is named (`--platform` or `lockfile_platforms`),
`--check` skips a platform where a tool has entries on other platforms
but none on that one. This is the rule `mise lock` already uses to
decide when to warn about an unavailable platform. A tool with no
entries at all still fails, and a named platform is always checked:

```sh
mise lock --check                        # passes
mise lock --check --platform windows-x64 # still reports the missing entry
```

Limits: the check is offline, so it cannot prove a tool has no build for
a platform. An unnamed `--check` therefore also accepts an entry that is
missing for another reason (for example one deleted by hand, or a failed
cross-platform fetch) when the tool has entries elsewhere; naming the
platform catches it. The current platform is always checked, and a
platform whose lock options differ from the host's (per-platform
`asset_pattern`, Swift distro) is still checked strictly. Recording
skipped platforms in the lockfile would avoid this but changes the
format, so this PR doesn't do it.

Extended `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_check`, which passes. Clippy and
lint were not run.

Fixes https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15930

feat(audit): add `mise audit` and `mise upgrade --vulnerable` (#15942)

Closes https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15936, which asked for a
vulnerability checker like `brew vulns` and `brew upgrade --vulnerable`.

## `mise audit`

`mise audit` looks up each tool version the current config uses in the
[OSV.dev](https://osv.dev) database and lists the advisories that affect
it. It exits 1 when it finds any, so it can gate CI.

```toml
[tools]
"npm:lodash" = "4.17.15"
go = "1.22.0"
zig = "0.13.0"
```

```
$ mise audit
Tool        Version  ID                   Severity  Fixed    Summary
npm:lodash  4.17.15  GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm  high      4.17.21  Command Injection in lodash
npm:lodash  4.17.15  GHSA-p6mc-m468-83gw  high      4.17.19  Prototype Pollution in lodash
go          1.22.0   GO-2024-2887         -         1.21.11, 1.22.4  Unexpected behavior from Is methods for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses in net/netip
...
mise not checked, no known advisory source: zig@0.13.0
mise 88 known vulnerabilities in 2 tools. Run `mise upgrade --vulnerable` to upgrade them.
```

(Output trimmed.) `mise audit node python` checks only those tools, and
`--json` prints `{"vulnerabilities": [...], "unchecked": [...]}` with an
`osv.dev` link for each advisory.

Which tools are covered:

- Package registry tools (`npm:`, `pipx:`, `cargo:`, `gem:`, `go:`,
`dotnet:`) are looked up by package name. npm git and tarball sources
are not registry packages, so they are listed as not checked.
- Tools released from GitHub (`github:`, `aqua:`, `packslip:`,
`gitlab:`) are looked up by repository and version, which OSV matches
against the release tags (`1.7` finds jq's `jq-1.7`). aqua tools use the
repository their version resolves to, and packslip subprojects their
repository. Go programs are also looked up as Go modules, which carry
fixed versions. A `github:` or `gitlab:` tool with its own `api_url`
(GitHub Enterprise, a self-hosted GitLab) is listed as not checked.
- Of the core tools, go (as the Go standard library), node, python,
deno, bun and erlang are covered.
- Anything else (zig, `conda:`, `path:` and `ref:` versions…) is listed
as **not checked**, never reported as clean.
- A configured version that does not resolve (a registry outage, a
missing package) fails the audit rather than dropping out of it, and so
does naming a tool that has no configured version (`mise audit node`
asks for `node@VERSION`).

Severity is the advisory's own rating, or computed from its CVSS v3
vector; it is `-` when the record has neither. Duplicate advisories (a
GHSA and its CVE alias) are shown once. mise doesn't order versions
here: "Fixed" lists the fixed versions as the advisory gives them.

`mise audit` needs network access to `api.osv.dev` and fails in offline
mode. It sends only tool names and versions, with URLs and credentials
left out.

## `mise upgrade --vulnerable`

`--vulnerable` filters a normal `mise upgrade` down to the installed
tools that have a known vulnerability. It composes with the existing
flags:

With `"aqua:jqlang/jq" = "1"` in the config and jq 1.7 installed
(affected by CVE-2023-50246):

```
$ mise upgrade --vulnerable --dry-run
Would install aqua:jqlang/jq@1.8.2
```

- Upgrades stay within the configured range; add `--bump` to go past it.
- `--dry-run`, `--exclude`, tool arguments and the other flags work as
usual. With `--inactive` it also checks installed versions the config no
longer uses.
- It lists the tools it could not check, warns when an affected tool has
no newer version in range (pointing at `--bump`), and warns when the
version it would upgrade to is still affected.

Both are stable from the start, not behind `experimental`.

## Testing

- Unit tests for query building (PyPI name normalization, Go module
paths, GitHub/GitLab URLs, aqua tag prefixes, non-release versions),
severity and CVSS scoring, and fixed-version extraction.
- `e2e/cli/test_audit` checks npm and Go stdlib findings, JSON output,
the not-checked list, unresolved versions, offline mode, and `upgrade
--vulnerable` with and without `--bump`, `--exclude` and `--inactive`.
It queries the live OSV.dev API.
- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D
warnings` passes.

fix(lock): refuse version upgrades that drop a platform in generate mode (#15939)

`mise lock` now refuses a version upgrade that would drop a platform the
old version supported, in the default `generate` mode as well as in
`merge` mode.

Previously, if a tool's new release had no build for one platform (for
example Renovate bumping Temurin to a release Adoptium had only
published for some platforms), `mise lock` exited 0, pruned the old
version and wrote a lockfile without that platform:

```text
✓ Pruned 1 stale version entry from mise.lock: java@temurin-21.0.0+35.0.LTS
exit 0
```

It now fails and leaves the lockfile untouched:

```text
mise ERROR failed to resolve java@temurin-21.0.1+12.0.LTS for windows-x64; refusing to replace locked version(s) temurin-21.0.0+35.0.LTS that support this platform
```

The check from #11664 only ran in `merge` mode. In `generate` mode (the
default since #14893) no per-platform results exist and the stale
versions are already gone from the rebuilt lockfile, so it could never
fire. The new check compares the rebuilt lockfile against the previous
one, and keeps the same rules as before: tools with several current
versions, platforms excluded by `os`, and platforms the old version
never locked are not refused.

Covered by unit tests only; an e2e needs a tool whose new release lacks
a platform, which can't be reproduced offline.

Fixes discussion #15929.

`mise watch --restart a ::: b` starts one watchexec over the union of
both tasks' sources, so a change to `a`'s sources also restarts `b`.
That is how it works today, but the help never said so, and the wording

independently: a separate `mise watch` per task (for example from a

```

mise watch --restart a          # restarts only a
```

fix(deps): watch aube-workspace.yaml and workspace members' manifests (#15940)

`mise deps` with the `aube` provider now notices changes to
`aube-workspace.yaml` and to workspace packages' `package.json`. Before,
the provider only watched the root `package.json` and `aube-lock.yaml`,
so editing a catalog, an override, or a member's dependencies could
leave it "fresh" until the lockfile changed:

```
mise deps aube --explain   # Status: fresh
```

The provider now also lists the workspace file (`aube-workspace.yaml`,
and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when present, since aube falls back to it) and
each member's `package.json` as sources. An explicit `sources = [...]`
still replaces the defaults, and a missing or unreadable workspace keeps
the previous behavior.

This mirrors the pnpm change in #15926. Member discovery now accepts
either workspace file (`pnpm_member_manifests` became
`workspace_member_manifests`).

Fixes discussion #15935.

fix(secrets): let tasks, including global ones, list keys from your own fnox config (#15937)

A key you keep in your own fnox config (fnox's global config, or a
`fnox.toml` in or above your home directory) can now be listed by a
task, and tasks in your global mise config can list secrets.

Since jdx/mise#15133 and jdx/mise#13974, neither worked. A project task
that named one of your own keys failed with `X comes from your own fnox
config, so the project cannot grant it`, and a task in
`~/.config/mise/config.toml` that listed any secret failed with `which
is not project config`. The only way to use such a key was to type `mise
run --secrets KEY <task>` on every run.

Both refusals are removed:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[tasks.gh-release]
secrets = ["GH_TOKEN"]          # now allowed in a global task
run = 'gh release create "$@"'
```

```toml
# a project's mise.toml
[secrets.fnox]

[tasks.eval]
secrets = ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]    # each developer's own key, from ~/.config/fnox/config.toml
run = './run-evals.sh'
```

`mise run eval` now starts the task with `OPENAI_API_KEY` set. The same
applies to a `{{ secrets.NAME }}` reference in a task's `env`, and to
tasks defined in system config or in a config file in or above your home
directory.

## Why

The refusals did not protect a key from a project you do not trust. A
task is the project's code and runs as you, so it can run `fnox get KEY`
itself, or call `mise run --secrets KEY other-task`; only the
declarative `secrets = [...]` form was blocked. They did block ordinary
use: a team task that expects each developer's own API key, and personal
tasks in the global config. The docs now describe the handling of your
own keys as scoping, not protection.

## What stays the same

- `--secrets-all` still leaves your own keys out, so a run that asks for
everything gets the project's keys only and a signed-out provider behind
one of your keys cannot fail it. A task that names one of your own keys
itself still receives it under `--secrets-all`; other tasks in the same
run do not.
- Remote tasks (`git::`, `oci::`, URL includes) still cannot list
secrets, and tasks started by hooks, `watch_files`, daemons or `mise
bootstrap` are still refused.
- A task that lists secrets still needs a project that declares
`[secrets.fnox]`, so a global task that lists secrets works only when
run inside such a project.
- mise secrets is still experimental.

## Compatibility

`mise secrets ls --json` and `mise tasks validate` no longer report
problems of kind `personal` or `not_project_config`.

## Tests

The secrets unit tests and the 20 e2e tests under `e2e/secrets` pass
locally. `test_mise_secrets_personal_keys` and
`test_mise_secrets_cli_grants` now expect these grants to work, and a
new unit test covers a task that lists one of your own keys under
`--secrets-all`. The full unit and e2e suites were not run locally.

fix(config): name the config file in Tera deprecation warnings (#15927)

## Problem

`mise install` and `mise reshim` read every tracked config, including
ones from other folders. A deprecated Tera helper in such a file warned
with no hint of where it came from, and `mise config` and `mise doctor`
don't list the file, so the user couldn't find what to fix:

```
mise WARN  deprecated [tera-v1-slice]: Tera v1 template helper `slice` is deprecated in mise templates. Use Tera 2 slice syntax like `array[start:end]` instead. This will be removed in mise 2027.4.0.
```

## Fix

Deprecation warnings raised while rendering a config's templates now
name the file:

```
mise WARN  deprecated [tera-v1-slice]: Tera v1 template helper `slice` is deprecated in mise templates (in ~/src/adjacent/.mise.toml). Use ...
```

The warning is kept, since it is actionable. Rendering records the
config path in a thread-local for the duration of the render
(`mise_util::tera::template_source`).

Fixes discussion #15924.

fix(deps): watch pnpm-workspace.yaml and workspace members' manifests (#15926)

`mise deps` with the `pnpm` provider now notices changes to
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` and to workspace packages' `package.json`. Before,
the provider only watched the root `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`,
so editing a catalog, an override, or a member's dependencies could
leave it "fresh" until the lockfile changed:

```
mise deps pnpm --explain   # Status: fresh
```

The provider now also lists `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and each member's
`package.json` (from the `packages` globs, including `!` exclusions) as
sources. An explicit `sources = [...]` still replaces the defaults, and
a missing or unreadable workspace falls back to the previous behavior.
Members are found through the same discovery the Node workspace tasks
use, so `node_modules` is never walked.

This mirrors the uv change in #15918. The issue's second request,
pointing one uv provider at several independent projects, is not part of
this PR.

fix(spaces): Windows sets up WSL 2 in one step; Docker Desktop is never offered (#8246)

* fix(spaces): Windows sets up WSL 2 in one step; Docker Desktop is never offered

Local Linux Spaces on Windows run in a runtime Cua Spaces manages itself (a

engine picks it in Settings, Runtimes; New Space never pushes one.

fix(cua-driver): return app_unresponsive at once for a Linux app while its GetState probe is pending (#8380)

* fix(cua-driver): a Linux app that did not answer GetChildren stays app_unresponsive without a walk until it answers a GetState probe

A stopped or modal-grabbed app made every get_window_state walk spend its whole budget (1 s by default) in the application lookup before it came back app_unresponsive, because nothing remembered the miss. The pid is now remembered with its bus and root; later walks of that pid return the same app_unresponsive result at once, and one GetState to its root runs on the AT-SPI runtime at a time, bounded by the operation timeout. Any reply forgets the pid, so the next walk reads the app again.

(cherry picked from commit c8f294adeeca4bcf08be6f5d2fc55db4dfd00dbc)

* fix(cua-driver): clear a Linux app's unresponsive mark when its probe ends

A GetState probe that timed out left the pid marked, so the first walk
after a stop longer than OP_TIMEOUT returned a stale app_unresponsive.
The mark now lasts only while one probe is pending; a reply, an error or
the timeout each clears it, and the next walk reads the app again.

An optional constraint passes when its argument is absent, so the tool

every element of an array argument, so launch_app additional_arguments can

fix(cua-driver): release content-only UIA references after get_window_state (#8370)

The walker AddRefs every row it emits, but the snapshot hand-off kept only
indexed rows and dropped the rest as plain integers, so each Windows
get_window_state leaked one COM reference per content-only row. The
CoreWindow fallback also dropped whichever node set it discarded.

UiaSnapshot::from_nodes now takes every reference out of the nodes:
indexed rows move into the snapshot, the rest are released, and each
element_ptr is zeroed. The fallback releases the set it discards.

fix(relay): stop machines retrying a refused token every few seconds (#8302)

* fix(relay): stop retrying a refused machine token every few seconds

A computer whose machine token the relay no longer knows (removed from the
account, token rotated, account deleted) retried the join about every 15-30 s
forever. On a 401 the client now retries once, then waits 1 min doubling to
1 h with jitter, logs one 'sign in again' error, and retries at once when its
token file changes. The relay checks the credential before the join limiter,
so refused tokens take no join slot, and the 401 log line now carries the
client's version.

* test(relay): expect SessionEnd::Unauthorized for a refused machine token

The 401 handling in this PR gives a refused token its own SessionEnd
variant (Unauthorized) instead of SessionEnd::Refused("HTTP 401"), so the
relay_refuses_bad_machine_tokens_and_anonymous_clients e2e that matched
Refused(r) containing "401" encoded the old shape. It now asserts the new
intended behaviour: a wrong machine token ends the session as Unauthorized.

feat(cua-relay): drain connections on SIGTERM before closing tunnels (#8310)

On the stop signal the relay refuses new machine tunnels and mesh
connections (503 with Retry-After), keeps open tunnels up while client
streams finish (CUA_RELAY_DRAIN_SECS, default 0 = unchanged), then closes
every tunnel cleanly (yamux GoAway, mesh close code 4000) right before it
exits, so the next relay takes the state lock at once. The hard stop is
drain plus the shutdown grace. Logs a drain report.

/healthz now carries x-cua-relay-boot (random id per process start),
x-cua-relay-started (Unix seconds) and x-cua-relay-version. Tests,
canaries and dashboards can tell a rollout from an outage and wait for a
restart instead of inferring it from a dropped tunnel. No secret.

fix(cua-driver): fall back on what a run_steps step last sent (#8282)

* test(cua-driver): pin run_steps foreground fallback after a re-found target

A stale token found again and then refused in the background must fall
back on the re-found token, and must not report that it ran in the
foreground when the retry failed. Fails on main: the fallback re-sends
the stale original token.

* fix(cua-driver): keep omitted and explicit background apart in DeliveryMode

DeliveryMode now has BackgroundPreferred (delivery_mode omitted),
BackgroundStrict (explicit "background") and Foreground, so the opt-out
from escalation lives in the type instead of a second string check.
allows_escalation() replaces background_requested_explicitly for the
macOS brief foreground drag; adapters that only need background versus
foreground use is_background().

* fix(cua-driver): fall back on what a run_steps step last sent

The step's attempt is now an explicit StepAttempt (Original, MenuRoute,
Refound). The foreground fallback re-sends attempt.current_args() with
the attempt's tool, so a re-found token or the invoke_menu route is kept,
and the fallback is offered only when that tool takes delivery_mode. The
step is parsed once into DeliveryMode, and only an omitted mode falls
back. A failed foreground retry now says so instead of noting that the
step ran in the foreground.

* fix(cua-driver): say a re-found run_steps target was found, not acted on

The re-find note leads a failed step's message, so it must not claim the
action landed.

fix(cua-driver): match running Windows Store apps to their bundle_id grant (#8127)

* fix(cua-driver): match running Windows Store apps to their bundle_id grant

Windows list_apps matched running processes to installed apps only by
executable basename, so a running packaged (Store/MSIX) app surfaced with
bundle_id null and a capability-manifest bundle_id grant could never match
it. Read the package identity Windows attests for the process
(GetApplicationUserModelId / GetPackageFamilyName) and match the installed
uwp entry first: an exact AUMID wins, an AUMID-less packaged helper matches
only its family's single entry, and unpackaged processes keep the existing
basename match.

Refs #3330

* fix(cua-driver): describe packaged-app matching in list_apps and the grant check

Move the packaged-identity tests next to list_apps on main, give the new
test file its SPDX header, and update the list_apps description, its
generated reference, and the bundle_id grant comments now that a running
packaged app is paired by its OS-reported package identity.

* fix(cua-driver): read the Store app's manifest Application Id past the Applications wrapper

The AppxManifest scan matched `<Applications>` first, found no `Id`, and
fell back to `App`. A packaged app whose Id is anything else then got a
launch_path its AUMID never equals, so list_apps could not attach its
bundle_id.

* fix(cua-driver): read the Store manifest's Application Id in XML attribute syntax

The scan required the literal `Id="`, so a valid `Id = 'Editor'` fell
back to `App`, which the exact AUMID match then rejects.

* fix(cua-driver): skip comments and other non-tag markup in the Store manifest scan

A commented-out `<Application>` was taken as the first one, so the
installed entry got that Id and the exact AUMID match rejected the
running app.

* test(cua-spacesd): closing a session while its capture callback needs the lease (#5376)

* fix(cua-spacesd): stop a session's capture lease outside its lock (#5376)

* fix(cua-spacesd): deliver macOS capture callbacks without a lock stop waits on (#5376)

* test(cua-spacesd): a frame after a native close must not revive its target (#5376)

* fix(cua-spacesd): retire a hub capture sink when its target closes (#5376)

fix(cua-driver): refuse background type_text into the iOS Simulator (#8112)

* fix(cua-driver): refuse background type_text into the iOS Simulator

The Simulator forwards physical key codes to the guest and ignores the
Unicode string on a synthetic keycode-0 event, so background type_text
turned "abc" into "Aaa". Treat it like Screen Sharing: background text
input refuses with IOS_SIMULATOR_REQUIRES_FOREGROUND_HID before any
event is sent, and delivery_mode:"foreground" with a window_id types
physical HID key transitions.

* fix(cua-driver): focus the target field before Simulator HID typing

Foreground type_text to a key forwarder went straight to physical HID
transitions without focusing the field its element_token names, so keys
could land in whichever field already had focus. Share the AX focus step
from the CGEvent path and run it after activation in the HID branch too.

* fix(cua-driver): refuse key-forwarder HID typing into an unfocused field

Best-effort focus still let physical keys reach whichever field kept
focus when the AX focus write did not stick. Move press_key's
with_confirmed_key_focus guard into ax_actions and use it in the
type_text HID branch, so an element_token whose focus cannot be
confirmed is refused with target_focus_unconfirmed before any key.
This replaces the shared best-effort focus helper from the previous
commit; the CGEvent path is back to its original code.

fix(cua-driver): honor the permissions grant verification in the macOS capture consent gate (#8119)

* fix(cua-driver): honor the permissions grant verification in the macOS capture consent gate

The daemon skipped every implicit capture with direct_capture_consent_required
when replayd's approvals file had no entry for CuaDriver.app, even after
permissions grant had captured a probe frame and recorded that verification.
Treat the recorded verification for this bundle as consent.

Fixes #6831

* fix(cua-driver): trust the grant verification only for the driver daemon

An embedded or caller-launched driver inherits another app's capture
attribution, so a standalone grant record must not let its implicit
captures skip the consent gate.

* fix(cua-driver): require self-responsibility before trusting the grant record

A bundled driver reparented to launchd after its launcher exits still
answers to that launcher's host, so a parent pid of 1 does not prove the
capture alert would name the driver. Ask macOS which process is
responsible instead.

* fix(cua-driver): count only grant records whose probe raised the bundle's own alert

The grant now records whether its probe ran on macOS 15 or later as its
own responsible process. The capture gate trusts only such records, so a
grant made on macOS 14 or by a helper answering to its launcher no longer
stands for consent. Records written before the field stay visible in
permissions status but do not open the gate.

* fix(cua-driver): validate the grant record timestamp on the consent gate path

records_consent_alert and load now share one reader, so a record whose
timestamp is out of range opens neither permissions status nor the gate.

fix(cua-driver): never retype a batched macOS send into a terminal (#8128)

* fix(cua-driver): retype a batched macOS send only after a native field took the start of it, never in a terminal

A batched type_text whose read-back counted short was retyped from that count, about 500 ms later. A terminal's screen cannot count what it read: with echo off (read -s, sudo, ssh) the screen stays unchanged, the count was 0 and the whole text went in a second time; vim's dd shrinks the screen, which also counted as 0. The reply then said "delivered 0 of N", retryable from character 0, which invites a third copy. A native control that takes only the first character of each batched event ("aq" for "abcdefghijklmnopq") was also retyped from character 2.

The tail is now retyped only when a native field shows its old value followed by the text's first 1 to N-1 characters. A terminal key insert that the screen does not show in full reports no delivered count, on the background and foreground routes.

Fixes #7245.

* fix(cua-driver): keep retyping a native field that showed no change, and test the terminal count drop

Upstream retypes a batched send that a native field did not take at all (#6884), and appends_prefix with no characters reduces to an unchanged value, so that case stays as it was; only terminals and web content are never retyped. The terminal count drop is a function with its own test.

* fix(cua-driver): allow the eighth argument of cgevent_type_verified

The terminal flag made it eight; the alternative is a parameter struct for one private caller set.
