Pipeline lab: replay a recorded day through a ref's real pipeline, with an agent guide (#25862)

The pipeline lab replays one recorded day through a ref's real pipeline
code against local emulators. You can then compare, card by card, what
that ref would have built with what production built that day. It is how
the v3 sit-down work (#25794, #25829) was measured.

This PR lands the lab on main so every agent works from one copy instead
of a long-lived lane branch.

## Scope

- **What it touches.** Everything is under
`backend/testing/pipeline_lab/` and
`backend/tests/unit/test_pipeline_lab_*.py`, plus:
  - one `make pipeline-lab ARGS=...` target;
- a size budget for the new lab `AGENTS.md` in
`.github/scripts/check_agents_md_lean.py`, set to its size at creation;
- one `exempt` entry in `.github/firestore-collection-budgets.json` for
`parakeet_batch`. That is the lab's STT adapter name, not a collection:
the collection-budget scanner resolved unrelated `.collection(name)`
parameters in `backend/database` to it.
- five node ids in `backend/tests/fast_unit_duration_allowlist.txt`. The
first test of each of those lab files drives real product code and pays
its import chain in its call phase.
- one reviewed edge in
`backend/tests/unit/fixtures/sync_legacy_import_baseline.json`. The
lab's sync-lane replay imports `utils.sync.pipeline` as its subject, and
is deleted with that module in C11.
- **What it does not touch.** No product module imports the lab, no
service or deploy path runs it, and no workflow is added.
- **Contents.**
  - Run store and spend ledger.
  - LLM record/replay proxy with a hard cap.
  - Pinned per-ref worktrees.
  - Stage registry and CLI.
  - Seeder, chain and v3 drivers.
  - Inspector.
  - Ideal-day scoring.
  - Read-only v3 exporter.
- **Agent guide.** `backend/testing/pipeline_lab/AGENTS.md`, linked from
the lab README, records what earlier agents got wrong:
  - replay bistability at default timing (repeat runs, report ranges);
  - no text in reports;
  - one replay at a time on the shared emulator;
  - never killing `dev_harness` supervisors by pattern;
  - harness parity with `store.load` (tombstones);
  - mutation passes for custody tests;
  - cleanup.
- **`ideal/runs.py`.** It replaces the per-session scratch scripts: a
score table against the day's ideal and a per-card diff across runs. It
prints times, counts and flags only.
- **`ideal/score.py`.** A line two conversations share now goes to the
earlier-starting one. It used to go to whichever file the directory
listing returned first. With overlapping cards that made the score
depend on file order: Home precision on one 11-19 run came out 1.00 or
0.67.
- **Speaker labels.** No raw speaker interpolation:
  - stored `SPEAKER_NN` labels come from `contracts.wire_speaker_label`;
- the Home-judge prototype (`ideal/jevhome.py`) labels unnamed voices
with the display authority's `SpeakerLabeler`;
- the STT cassette's per-window diarization id comes from a named helper
and is never shown as text.
- **`v3/fake.py`.** It now accepts `max_events`. Without it, every
fake-engine v3 run exited 2 after the options gained that key.

## Privacy and production

- **The store refuses any root inside a git worktree.** Private data
lives under a 0700 root outside git. Tests use synthetic fixtures only.
- **Replays never touch production.** They write only to local emulators
under the synthetic uid `local-dev-user`.
- **`v3/prod_export.py` is the only production reader.** It is an
operator tool, run by hand under a read-only GCP agent tier for one
consenting owner and one day.
- It reads that owner's v3 recordings and derived conversations for the
day window.
- That is one day's rows, a few hundred to a few thousand reads per run.
  - It has no schedule and nothing calls it automatically.
- **No credential, uid, name, conversation id or transcript is in the
diff.** The owner uid and the gateway token are read from 0600 files by
path at the moment of use.

## Verification

Run on `m5-mbp`, at this branch rebased on `origin/main`:

- All 29 `tests/unit/test_pipeline_lab_*.py` files pass, each in its own

## Review

There were two panel rounds:

- Round 1 had 17 findings: 16 fixed, 1 rejected with a reason.
- Round 2 had 14: the blocker and 7 others fixed, 6 deferred. Under R28
only blockers block.

Main fixes:

- Exporter outputs are owner-only and never follow symlinks, and the git
probe fails closed.
- The write fence also refuses deletes and Redis pipelines.
- The owner uid is redacted from every log record during an export.
- The proxy allows plain HTTP only to loopback.
- Pinned arms are refused when they contain untracked Python.
- Lab roots and ids are validated before any write.
- The CodeQL ReDoS and header-injection alerts are fixed.

- **`corpus add-day --replace`.** It should clear optional v3 and audio

ci(ui-approval): carry an approval to a descendant head with no UI change (R29) (#25860)

## Summary
This implements David's R29 ruling (2026-11-20, omi-workspace
`2a41cff`). An `/approve-ui` approval now stays valid on a later head
when that head only adds commits on top of the approved one and none of
them touch UI. Today every new head clears the approval. On #25771 that
meant two hand re-approvals after backend-only fix rounds
(SCA-3062/SCA-3063).

An approval carries forward only when all three conditions hold:
- **Newest command is an approval:** the newest approver command on the
PR is `/approve-ui` for an earlier head, and no command names the
current head. Any later `/reject-ui` withdraws it.
- **Descendant head:** the approved head is an ancestor of the current
head (compare status `ahead` or `identical`). The compared range is then
exactly approved..current.
- **No UI change:** that range touches no UI path. This includes renamed
paths and Swift UI detected by file contents, using the same
`evidence()` reads as the main check.

Anything else still needs a fresh approval: a rebase, a force-push, a UI
change, a truncated or unreadable range, or a newer command on the
current head. The bot notice is now posted only while approval is
actually missing.

## Tests
- `node --test .github/scripts/tests/ui-author-approval.test.cjs`: 23
pass, 5 of them new. The new tests cover the carry candidate rules, how
`decision()` treats a carried approval, an end-to-end carry, refusals
(UI, renamed UI, rebase, behind, truncated range, later reject) and the
Swift content scan inside the range.
- `scripts/pr-preflight`: 14 checks pass.

## Risk and rollback
The gate is not loosened for UI changes. The workflow runs the script
from `github.workflow_sha` (main), so this takes effect for every PR
once merged. Rollback is reverting this commit.

Both reads must disagree with the manifest's SHA-256 of decoded PCM before recovery commits `failed_held` with `retained_digest_changed`. The successful CAS emits the bounded `omi_fallback_total` reason; the task receives 200 and duplicate deliveries and automatic redrive do not retry the source. A matching confirmation resumes ordinary recovery. Storage outages, missing inputs, invalid manifests, and switched-off target 409s keep their existing paths. The SHA-256 check, custody, expiry/deletion policy, and reviewed operator redrive are unchanged. Set `BATCH_PIPELINE_RETAINED_DIGEST_HOLD_ENABLED=false` to restore the legacy single-read 500 for new mismatches without altering existing held rows. Recovery, merge, projection, expiry, and metrics readers are listed in `backend/utils/batch_pipeline/CONTRACT.md`. State exit: retained_digest_changed is a refusal reason on the existing terminal failed_held state. Normal retained dead-letter expiry still applies, and only a reviewed operator redrive can requeue the row. ### Cause evidence An offline native-Opus probe reproduced the exact digest failure with identical object bytes and generation. Admission's `source_metadata=True` read used the frame table to skip a zero-sample diagnostic packet; recovery used the plain decoder, which decoded that packet. The asymmetric branch arrived in #25045, before #25675. A rewrite to a different generation cannot satisfy the pinned read. This proves a decoder path can cause the error without a rewrite; it does not identify the affected production cohort or establish the rollout trigger. No production reads, writes, merges, or deploys for this PR. ## Tests `backend/tests/unit/test_batch_pipeline_retained_digest_hold.py` exercises the real FastAPI handler, manifest materialization, and recovery transactions with synthetic pinned reads. It covers confirmed mismatch, delivery replay, transient mismatch, read outage, rollback, stale intent, changed URI, privacy revocation, and automatic versus reviewed redrive. ## UI evidence UI-Evidence: none -- backend recovery only ## Failure class (fixes) Failure-Class: FC-batch-fault-domain-head-of-line-poison

fix(batch): keep L4 nodes through worker rolls; GPU floor 4 -> 6 (#25842)

## Why

Incident SCA-3274 (2026-11-20). A preserve-live worker image roll under
`Recreate` stopped all ten batch workers at 04:14Z. Nine exited within
about a minute. One hung, logging nothing after 04:14:07Z, and was
killed at 04:39:02Z when its 1500 s grace ran out. `Recreate` creates no
replacement until every old pod is gone. The cluster autoscaler removed
the nine empty L4 nodes at 04:24:30–04:25:15Z (its 10-minute
unneeded-node timer), into a three-zone L4 stockout, and batch ran on
one GPU for about 40 minutes while the ready queue climbed past 20k.

The HPA floor did not help: it counts pods, and `Recreate` had removed
them. `batch-pipeline-pool` has no node minimum.

## What changes

- **Worker roll strategy:** every worker Deployment (primary, `-t4`,
`-borrow`, `-spot`) uses `RollingUpdate` with `maxSurge: 0` and
`maxUnavailable` from `rollout.maxUnavailable` (default `50%`,
percentages only; the render fails on anything else, including a null
map). 50% finishes a roll in two drain-plus-startup waves, which fits
the deploy workflow's existing rollout wait, while half the fleet keeps
serving.
- No surge GPU. Every pod still requests a whole `nvidia.com/gpu`, so
the chart's "never surge, never co-locate" invariant holds.
- Each replacement is created (Pending) as soon as its predecessor is
told to stop. It takes the freed node seconds after that pod exits, so
no node is idle long enough to be scaled down. A hung pod now delays
only its own replacement.
- Old and new images already run side by side today:
`record-seal-worker` shares the image, and preserve-live rolls
deliberately leave it on the old one.
- **`worker_image_only.py`:** admits `Recreate`, or `RollingUpdate` with
an explicit zero `maxSurge`. It refuses any strategy that could surge,
including an omitted `maxSurge`, which Kubernetes defaults to 25%.
- **Prod floor 4 → 6** (David, 2026-11-20, superseding D4 of
2026-11-06). Over the prior three days the HPA never asked for fewer
than 6 workers, so the floor adds about zero machine-hours at that
demand.
- **Runbooks:** floor 6, a `batch-pipeline-pool` total node minimum of 6
(operator-managed, applied by Release), the roll strategy, and
rollbacks.

## Tuning (before -> after)

Prod minReplicas 4 -> 6 and replicaCount 4 -> 6. Rolling strategy knobs,
new: maxSurge new: 0 and maxUnavailable new: 50 percent (Recreate
before, which behaves as maxSurge 0 with maxUnavailable 100 percent).
Node pool total minimum 0 -> 6 (operator change, not in this diff).
Deployment progress deadline 2400 -> 3000 seconds.

| Knob | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `autoscaling.minReplicas` (prod) | 4 | 6 |
| `replicaCount` (prod) | 4 | 6 |
| strategy | Recreate (all pods stopped, then all started) |
RollingUpdate |
| `maxSurge` | n/a under Recreate (effectively 0) | 0 |
| `maxUnavailable` | n/a under Recreate (effectively 100%) | 50% (new:
`rollout.maxUnavailable`) |
| `batch-pipeline-pool` total minimum (operator, not in this diff; live
since 06:00Z) | none (0) | 6 |
| `progressDeadlineSeconds` | 2400 | 3000 (1500 s drain + 1200 s
startupProbe + margin) |

Measured basis (Prometheus, ro-prod, 2026-11-20 05:22Z): over the prior
3 days the HPA's desired replicas were >= 6 100% of the time, >= 8 87%,
at the 16 cap 45%. Average extra workers a floor would add: floor 6 ->
0.00, floor 8 -> 0.17, floor 10 -> 0.62. Saturated throughput ~55
audio-s/s per worker (4-day average while ready > 2,000).

## Rollout

Ships on; there is no flag. Release applies it on SCA-3276:
1. HPA `minReplicas` 6 and pool `--total-min-nodes 6`. Applied by
Release at 06:00Z (prod-operator); readback HPA 6/16, pool 6/18, worker
revision 82 unchanged, 6/16 Ready before and after.
2. After merge: a live `kubectl patch` of the Deployment strategy. This
is spec-only: no new ReplicaSet, no restart. It changes the
preserve-live baseline hash, so re-run `worker_image_only.py inventory`
before the next image-only roll (runbook updated).
3. The next full worker Helm roll persists everything. That roll also
applies `pipelineDepth` 3 → 4, committed 11-17 but never live; that's
Release's separate call.

Rollback:
- `rollout.maxUnavailable: 100%` (values-only), or revert this PR.
- Floor 4 in both values.
- Pool `--total-min-nodes 0`.

## Verification

- `backend/tests/unit/test_batch_pipeline_chart.py`: 105 passed. New
test: every worker Deployment renders the no-surge strategy, `100%`
renders, and `0%`, `1`, `150%`, `25` and `all` fail.
- `.github/scripts/test_worker_image_only.py`: 88 passed. New test:
no-surge `RollingUpdate` is admitted and preserved; surge or
omitted-`maxSurge` strategies refuse.
- Every other test that reads the worker's prod values (cohort config,
HPA replays, config train, cross-service deploy contract, adapter/HPA
contract, record-seal, token lease): 216 passed, 3 skipped.
- Workflow contract tests: 143 passed.

Done means a production readback on SCA-3276: the next worker roll keeps
`batch-pipeline-pool` at or above the floor throughout, with no
replacement waiting on all old pods.

feat(backend): deployable, startup-isolated backend-projection-pump Cloud Run target (#25795)

## What

Adds a deploy target for a fifth backend Cloud Run service,
`backend-projection-pump`, so the batch projection pump can run on a
small fixed-size service instead of on every `backend-integration`
instance. No change under `backend/utils/batch_pipeline/` or
`backend/database/batch_pipeline*`. `backend/main.py` gains a startup
gate that is inert for every existing service (see Startup isolation).
The pump process code and its flag already exist (#24905 and earlier)
and stay default-off.

Tracking: Multica SCA-3120. The `.github/` change was approved by David
for this work on 2026-11-19.

## Why

Read-only production measurement on 2026-11-19: `backend-integration`
has sat at 35 of 35 instances for 7 days at any request rate. Revisions
with zero traffic still run at about half of their 2 vCPU, and Firestore
reads from the follow-up loop and serving tick scale with instance
count, not work. Raising the ceiling was tried on 11-13 and 11-17 and
projected no faster. The deploy headroom gate refuses the service for
this reason. Evidence: omi-knowledge-base
`projects/gcp-cost-efficiency/evidence/2026-11-19-backend-integration-saturation.md`.

## How

- **Selection.** `backend-projection-pump` is an explicit singleton for
manual production `cloud-run-only` deploys. `all` still expands to
exactly the four existing services, so no existing train, auto-dev train
or staging deploy changes. `deploy-backend-stack/action.yml` is
byte-identical.
- **Deploy path.** New composite
`.github/actions/deploy-projection-pump` and a `deploy-projection-pump`
job in `gcp_backend.yml` under the same prod-train concurrency group,
admission, readiness and break-glass jobs. It deploys the
already-published admitted backend image; it never builds one.
- **Shape.** 2 vCPU / 4Gi, CPU always allocated, min = max = 4, 3600 s
timeout, `--ingress=internal`, `--no-allow-unauthenticated`, no invoker.
`verify_projection_pump_shape.py` reads ingress, IAM members, size and
the dark env back before traffic moves.
- **Env.** `derive_from: backend-integration` in the prod overlay,
overriding only: `BATCH_PIPELINE_SERVING_ENABLED=false`,
`BATCH_PIPELINE_PROJECTION_PUMP_ENABLED=false`, pump pages 1 / tick 2 s
/ owner drains 8,
`FIRESTORE_READ_LEDGER_SERVICE=backend-projection-pump`, and independent
language recovery off.
- **Metrics.** Dedicated revision-aware RunMonitoring profile (sync
keep-list plus the two pump gauges; `targetLabels.metadata: [service,
revision]`). The shared profiles are not edited; a test keeps the pump
profile equal to the sync profile plus those additions.
- **Checks.** Source-admission, runtime-env workflow validation,
cross-service contract, CI budget and env-drift allowlist learn the new
job and service.

## Startup isolation

A review finding on the deploy-only version of this PR: with both batch
flags false the pump was not dark, because `main.startup_event` starts
every reconciler on every process. The pump is deployed only by its own
selection, so it can sit on an older SHA than the trains with no time
bound, and an old-code instance could win an account-deletion or purge
lease.

- New `OMI_PROCESS_ROLE` (`backend/config/process_role.py`): unset or
`all` is today's startup, unchanged for every existing service;
`projection_pump` is set only on `backend-projection-pump`; any other
value fails startup. Independent of `OMI_ROLE` and of the pump flag, so
turning the pump off does not bring the reconcilers back.
- Pump keeps: metrics sidecar, STT cap cohort refresh (read-only cache
the projector consults), `start_serving_from_env()`, both startup
validators, executor health, and `retry_settled_composes` (the projector
queues process-local episode transcript receipts that only this task
drains).
- Pump skips: Pinecone mutation lifecycle, messaging adapters, live-STT
health, held-content cohort, batch pressure, Soniox usage, every
`_run_fsr_loop` reconciler (deletion wipes, listen finalization, stale
processing and in-progress conversations, BYOK abandonment, conversation
batch purges), the queue-age publisher and the proactive dispatcher.
- `_run_fsr_loop` returns without touching a lease under the pump role;
the pump role with `BATCH_PIPELINE_SERVING_ENABLED=true` fails startup;
the pre-traffic shape check refuses a revision whose role is not
`projection_pump`.
- Not isolated here: import-time work (Stripe price validation, Firebase
init, rollout runtime binding), the pump's secret set, mounted routers.

Review asked of the account-deletion, purge and finalization owners and
lead2: confirm the four train services still cover each reconciler the
pump no longer competes for, and that the pump running
`retry_settled_composes` (paid episode composes) is acceptable.

## Ramp plan (default-off flag)

`backend/docs/listen_pusher_pipeline/changes/2026-11-19-projection-pump-deploy-target.md`.

fix(conversations): store meeting context on external-integration captures

`store_meeting_context` assigned `conversation.external_data` for every
conversation that was not a `CreateConversation`. An
`ExternalIntegrationCreateConversation` has no such field, so pydantic raised
`ValueError: "ExternalIntegrationCreateConversation" object has no field
"external_data"` out of `process_conversation` whenever a calendar meeting
context resolved for an external-integration capture. The conversation never
completed (Cloud Error Reporting group CMma2pfi_ePzeg, 25 events/24h).

The create model now carries `calendar_meeting_context` as a field, the same
way `CreateConversation` does, and `store_meeting_context` treats both create
models as field carriers. A model that can carry the context neither way is
left untouched with a warning instead of raising: losing the context is always
better than failing the conversation that carries it.

`_get_conversation_obj` moves the field into
`external_data['calendar_meeting_context']` on the persisted `Conversation`,
using the model's hand-built `to_storage_dict()` shape, so every existing
reader keeps working and no new Firestore field appears. Client input is
discarded by a `SkipJsonSchema` field validator, matching `content_kind`, so
the set of conversations that get a context cannot change through the request
body.

Unchanged: the `Conversation` path (`external_data['calendar_meeting_context']`)
and the `CreateConversation` path (`calendar_meeting_context`), and the
resolver that decides which conversations get a context.

Tests: `tests/unit/test_meeting_context_storage.py` covers storing on both
create models, the persisted `Conversation`, the client-input discard, and the
never-raises guard; `test_meeting_context_enrichment_wiring.py` pins the raise
site end to end (`_enrich_meeting_context` -> `_get_conversation_obj`).

ones without one are listed under C.

This PR changes the INV-UI-3 contract and its guard
(`product/invariants/mobile-ux-contract.md`): it adds §17 and the new
MUST NOT lines, and extends §2 so inline editors and full-page forms
also guard unsaved input.

## Product invariants affected

- INV-UI-3: §17 Outcomes, new MUST NOT lines, four new ratchet rules.
- INV-CAP-1: `capture_controller.dart` gains
`finishCaptureWithOutcome()` and a typed mic-denied start error. The
capture ownership order is unchanged (see B).

### A. Contract and guards

- `app/docs/ux-contract.md` §17 Outcomes keeps all nine rules from the
audit draft, tightened. It names the shared pieces: `FinishOutcome` /
`presentFinishOutcome`, `OmiMissingTarget`, `applyOmiSetting` and
`OmiUnsavedChangesGuard`.
- §2: the dirty guard now covers inline editors and full-page forms
through `OmiUnsavedChangesGuard`.
- `product/invariants/mobile-ux-contract.md`: matching MUST NOT lines.
- New ratchet rules. Each uses the per-file no-increase shape and the
`omi-ux-allow` escape, and each has a failing case plus precision cases
in `test_check_mobile_ux_contract.py`. The new `--totals` flag prints
the tree-wide counts below.

| Rule | Counts | Tree-wide at merge base (`2779f1adc04`) | After this
PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `silent-catch` | `catch (…) {}`, and catch bodies that only log, under
`pages/` and `providers/` | 135 | 132 |
| `generic-error` | `somethingWentWrong*` in a call with no way forward
(`actionLabel:` with `onAction:`, or `onRetry:`) | 64 | 60 |
| `material-page-route` | `MaterialPageRoute(` in code (not comments) |
8 | 7 |
| `pop-before-await` | a `Navigator…pop(` whose next `await` in the same
block is a request | 10 | 10 (one new deliberate pop is allow-commented)
|

`pop-before-await` ships because it was tuned on `app/lib` until it was
precise. The naive version counted 32 hits, about half of them false
positives: arrow handlers such as `() => Navigator.pop(ctx, true)`, and
a pop followed by `await showOmiConfirm(…)` or `openAppSettings()`,
which moves on to the next surface. The rule now:
- counts only a pop in a `{}` block, not an arrow handler;
- counts only when the first `await` after the pop is a request, not
`show*`, `open*`, `push*` or `launch*`;
- stops at a `case` label.

That leaves 10 hits on main. All of them are real "close, then request"
sites, for example `add_app.dart` Submit, the summary template sheet and

"Finish this capture" now returns one typed outcome everywhere

- `FinishOpened`
- `FinishProcessing`
- `FinishNothingNew(alreadySaved)`
- `FinishDiscarded`
- `FinishNotReceived`
- `FinishSavedForLater` (phone Transcribe Later)

`finishLiveCapture` in `pages/episodes/finish_capture.dart` is the one

`presentFinishOutcome` shows the outcome the same way from every entry

backend-go: drain workers and refund interrupted claims (#25812) ## What changed and why Adds `Workers.Drain(ctx)` for the shutdown path requested by #25804. Call it before cancelling the context passed to `queue.Start`. The caller’s deadline bounds the grace period. Intake closes immediately, including scheduled resumes, while already-running handlers retain their context and heartbeat. At the deadline Drain cancels handlers and refunds still-owned leases in a single token-fenced update, with up to three additional seconds for database cleanup. It returns the context cause and any cleanup error. The database row determines whether the next claim should run, wait for a fresh secret, or reconcile durable intent. A repeated drain can retry cleanup. A slow adapter inside a guard holds its advisory locks until the call returns or the session closes. Lane 1 can wire this API into workerd. The binary must keep the parent context and worker dependencies alive through its shutdown sequence. ## How it was verified | Rule | Test | | --- | --- | | Intake closes while an active handler renews its lease, saves its checkpoint and finishes. | `TestDrainLetsRunningHandlerSaveAndFinish` observes a renewal after the cutoff, a refused resume, and a newly enqueued job with zero attempts. | | At the deadline a second Workers can claim immediately with a larger token and the original attempt count. | `TestDrainDeadlineRefundsWorkAndReconciliationForAnotherReplica` holds the original handlers past cancellation and uses a one-minute lease. It checks ordinary work, secret-gated work, and a gated job that entered reconciliation during the same claim. The checkpoint and reconciliation intent survive. | The focused Postgres tests passed ten repetitions under the race detector. ## Summary

On the dev deployment's dogfood journey `proj-delete-account-cleanup`, a
synthetic customer with two workspaces got only the first workspace's
project from `GET /v1/projects`. The second workspace's project was
reachable only with `?account_id=`. The handler resolved one account
(`resolveProjectAccount`, which defaults to the earliest-joined
membership) and filtered by it. So a leftover project in a second
workspace was invisible to the journey's absence check, and to any API
user who lists projects.

Now a person who names no account lists every account: the same
per-account read, run once per membership, merged and sorted by
`updated_at` descending. `?account_id=` behaves as before. Every
credential bound to one account behaves as before.

Root cause: `apps/api/src/projects/routes/projects.ts` `GET /` scoped
the list to `resolveProjectAccount(c).accountId`, a single default
account, for every caller.

Closes KRTX-4926

## Demo video

No demo video: code-only change. The proof is the request/response
transcript in "How was this tested?" (journey before/after on the local
stack).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (`fix(api)`): restores the listing a person expects from
`GET /v1/projects`.
- [ ] Migration, flag, or SDK public-export change: none.

## What is affected

- `GET /v1/projects` with no `account_id`, for a person (Supabase
browser session or unscoped PAT): lists every account. Response element
shape unchanged (`ProjectSchema`).
- Not affected: `GET /v1/projects?account_id=…` (one account, same 400
`invalid_account_id` / 403 checks), workspace-bound keys
(`tokenProjectId`), service accounts, API keys, OAuth clients,
impersonation, `GET /v1/workspaces` (only its local `isRevokedSession`
moved to an import).
- CLI: no code change. `kortix projects ls --all` and `kortix workspaces
ls` read `GET /v1/workspaces` and already list every account (checked
below). `kortix projects ls` (the older name) stays scoped to the active
account by design and prints the `kortix projects ls --all` hint.
- Docs and spec: the route's OpenAPI `description`, the
`workspaces/routes.ts` and `workspace-records.ts` header comments that
said "GET /v1/projects lists one account", and
`tests/spec/end-to-end.md` (WS-ROUTE-4, WS-AUTH-4).

## Security & data review

- Authorization: the union adds no access. Each account in it goes
through the same `actorOf` + `listAccessible('project.read', 'project')`
decision as `GET /v1/projects?account_id=<that account>`. Only a person
reaches the union: `newWorkspaceCallerDenial(newWorkspaceCallerOf(c))
=== null`, which means a Supabase session or an unscoped PAT, not
impersonated and not workspace-bound. A workspace key is shown to list
its one workspace (TOK-4, WS-AUTH-13, local curl above).
- Session policy: an account's revoked session still gets nothing from
that account (WS-AUTH-4).
- Data: no write and no new column. Tests and this body use synthetic
data only.

## Rollout / rollback

- Contract change, additive. `GET /v1/projects` without `account_id`
returns more rows for a person in several accounts. The element shape,
the auth decision per row and every narrower credential are unchanged.
- Rollback: revert this PR. There is no migration, no flag and no data
change.
- Load: one per-account read per membership, run in parallel, the same
fan-out `GET /v1/workspaces` already does on every switcher open.

Before the web server failed, the controlled recovery ran green on the
local stack (worktree `krtx-4973`, fixed SDK, synthetic `@example.test`
user and session). A browser init script (`demo-init.js`, local only,
not committed) sent one synthetic `kortix.control.turn` frame (turn
already ended, no runtime log frames). It withheld the assistant from
the first stored-log page, answered the second read with 503, and let
later reads through to the real local API. Probe output (the page's own

Demo harness · turn ended (synthetic) · 18s · log reads: … → #3 200 → #4 200 | user:true reply:true

The reply appears about 2 s after the first page without a refresh,

follow-ups still relies on reconnect, visibility or a manual read.

## Quick verification

- Outcome: opening a session URL that does not exist no longer calls
`POST …/start` or mounts the session's presence, streams, log, turn and
panel readers. The screen title is "Session not found", not "Couldn't
start session". Closes KRTX-5025.
- Root cause: the route mounted `ProjectSessionView` (about 17 session
readers) at once and learned "missing" only from the `/start` 404.
`MissingSessionBoundary`
(`apps/web/src/features/session/missing-session-boundary.tsx`) now holds
an existing session's readers until its row (`GET …/sessions/<id>`)
answers: 404 → not-found screen, success → the session view. The row
read rides the session-open bundle the access boundary already started,
and the device cache and sidebar keep the row, so a known session is not
held at all. A session this tab just created skips the hold (create
race; `/start` retries own it). A failing row read (5xx, network)
releases the hold on its first failure.
- Copy: `sessionPage.missing.title` is "Session not found" in all 9
catalogs and in the generated `packages/ui/src/i18n/en.ts`. The key is
used only for the missing-session states.
- Try it: open
`/workspaces/<id>/sessions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`. Expect
"Session not found" and "Back to workspace", and no `start`, `presence`,
`events` or `log` request in the network tab. Open an existing session:
it loads as before, with one `POST …/start`.

Journey `pub-404-empty-error` step 4, re-run on the local stack
(`agent-browser`, network log filtered to the nil session id, OPTIONS
excluded):

```
before (origin/dev): 21 requests — snapshot, reminders, config, participants, watch, model-usage,
  PUT presence x4, POST start?wait_ms=15000, events?tab_id, log?limit=40, scope, GET row, audit, turn,
  prompts, events?channels=control (all 404) + sessions?parent=<nil> (200); title "Couldn't start session"
after (this PR):     5 requests — GET row x2, snapshot?transcript=0, config, scope (all 404, one-shot); title "Session not found"
```

The remaining 5 are one-shot reads that fire before the boundary
decides: the layout's tab-title sync reads the row, and
`ProjectAccessBoundary` prefetches `snapshot`/`config`/`scope` for open
latency (`session-route-prefetch.ts`). None is a write, a stream or a
poll.

fix(ui): the final answer streams in the web chat again (KRTX-4939) (#12915)

## Review in 60 seconds

- **What changed:** a pnpm patch for `streamdown@1.6.11`
(`patches/streamdown@1.6.11.patch`, wired in `package.json`
`pnpm.patchedDependencies` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`). In `mode="streaming"`,
Streamdown now renders the blocks parsed from the current text directly,
instead of pushing them through `useTransition` + `useState`. It also
drops that now-unused hook pair. That edit is applied to the same
expression in its four dist chunks (two ESM, two CJS).
- **Why (root cause):** Streamdown committed each new set of streaming
blocks inside a React transition. React abandons a pending transition
whenever another update lands first, and the chat re-renders the answer
about every 32 ms (`STREAM_COMMIT_MS`). So the transition never
committed while text kept arriving: the answer stayed blank (or stale),
then jumped in whole at the end of the turn. That's the reported "final
response appears in one jump, with a flash". The server was never the
problem: the `?schema=v2` stream delivered ~200 `log.block.delta` frames
at a steady pace.
- **Regression test:**
`packages/ui/src/markdown/unified-markdown-streaming.test.tsx` renders
`UnifiedMarkdown` with `isStreaming` through `flushSync` (no `act`,
which would flush the transition and hide the bug). Without the patch: 0
pass / 3 fail (an empty answer while streaming). With it: 3 pass.

**Risk:** low. Static mode (history) is untouched. Streaming mode now
runs the parse that the transition used to defer in the same commit.
That parse already ran on every render, because the `useMemo` sat
outside the transition, so no new work moves onto the main thread. Only
`packages/ui` imports `streamdown`. The patch is large (143 KB) only
because the dist files are minified onto a few long lines; its content
is one expression per chunk. Rollback: drop the patch entry.
**Verified:** the new test (red 0/3 without the patch, green 3/3 with
it); `pnpm test` in `packages/ui`: 9535 pass / 5 fail, all 5
pre-existing at `origin/dev` f11f765f3f; `tsgo --noEmit` and eslint
clean. On the local stack (real sandbox, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), the
answer's markdown grew 378 → 594 → 634 → 1964 → 2399 → 2494 chars while
`data-streaming="true"`, then settled at 2499. The same probe before the
patch saw no growth at all while streaming.

* fix(python): give each server conversation its own in-process shell

One process serves several server conversations, and the in-process
backend handed all of them the same module-global `InteractiveShell`.
A name defined in conversation A resolved in conversation B, and
`sys.path`/interpreter state was shared (gptme/gptme#4951).

context variable, with a conversation-level registry so SESSION_END can
drop it. CLI sessions have no conversation id and keep the
process-global shell that `chat()` expects. Registered tool functions
are pushed into every new shell.

through `current_workspace()` instead of `Path.cwd()`, so both follow
the conversation rather than whichever conversation chdir'd last.

The working directory itself stays process-wide: `os.chdir` cannot be
scoped to a shell, so relative-cwd isolation still requires kernel mode.

Tests run two conversation contexts in one process and assert distinct
shells, no variable leakage, and that the CLI context keeps the global
shell.

fix(subagent): keep each run's completion when two conversations run the same ID (#4991)

* fix(subagent): keep each run's completion when two conversations run the same ID

Two conversations can run a child with the same agent_id at the same time.
The result cache holds one slot per agent_id, and the newest run holds it.

- set_subagent_result_if_absent treated any newer same-ID registry entry as a
  continuation superseding the attempt, so the older run's completion was
  dropped. A newer run of the same conversation still supersedes it; a newer
  run of another conversation now leaves the attempt shadowed with its own
  outcome, as #4987 does for other non-holders.
- The thread-mode finalizer found its run by agent_id (the oldest same-ID
  entry, possibly another conversation's run) and published without an
  attempt, writing into the other run's slot. It now uses the run it was
  launched for and passes it as the attempt.
- _timeout_subagent compared the oldest same-ID entry with its expected run,
  so a newer run's watchdog never fired while an older one was registered.

Fixes #4990.

commits.message:
docs: list the avatar overlays and the board motion hooks (#476)

devices/README.md names the avatar-sync and avatar-animations overlays,
and the muse_board_t field table in devices/AGENTS.md covers
motion_enable and motion_read.

esp32: keep the TLS session across network failures (#475)

The VM WebSocket forgot its saved TLS session on any failed connect, DNS and
TCP failures included, so a reconnect after a Wi-Fi outage or a router
restart always paid for a full handshake. It now forgets the session only
once TLS itself has failed (a handshake or verification error, or a server
refusing the offered session), and keeps it when the connect never got as
far as TLS (esp-tls still in ESP_TLS_INIT: DNS, the TCP connect or a proxy
failed).

test_link_tls_resume runs the helpers, sliced from noise_control.cpp, on
the host.

esp32: add optional Muse avatar sync and phone clip playback (#466)

Add an opt-in My Muse avatar source (CONFIG_MUSE_AVATAR_SYNC, off by
default) for full-UI boards with PSRAM. Settings > Avatar switches between
Built-in and My Muse without a restart and can refresh or clear the saved
image.

- The gadget reads the paired Muse's identity and fetches the current still
  over the existing session with bounded Range reads, decodes static WebP
  (libwebp 1.6.0, decoder only, pinned by SHA-256) into at most 466x466
  RGB565, and keeps a last-good copy in a private cache bound to the pairing.
- It refreshes after connecting, on wake when stale, on request and every
  15 minutes while awake. It never wakes the screen, and it defers during
  voice, sleep and other foreground work. A stopped or timed-out request
  frees its buffer at once and later frames for it are dropped.
- With the optional UI appearance (CONFIG_MUSE_UI_THEME), Automatic follows
  a confident background sample of the personal avatar.
- CONFIG_MUSE_AVATAR_ANIMATIONS (ESP32-S3, off by default) adds an
  experimental preview of phone-avatar clips. Clips are converted on a
  computer (tools/muse/avatar_clips.py) into a bounded constrained-baseline
  H.264 pack, installed over USB and decoded with the existing tinyh264
  decoder under a new opt-in reference-frame limit. No network listener is
  added.
- libwebp is listed under License in both READMEs.
- Host and simulator tests, two CI firmware profiles, and
  esp32/docs/avatar-sources.md.

Co-authored-by: Paden Clayton <padenc2001@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: add lift-to-wake and face-down quiet for Waveshare 1.75C (#464)

Adds two opt-in motion controls to the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75C,
using its on-board QMI8658 accelerometer (low-power 21 Hz, gyroscope off) on
the board's shared I2C bus:

- Lift to wake: lifting and tilting the screen toward you wakes it without
  starting a recording; lowering it or setting it down does not.
- Face-down quiet: playback is silenced while the device lies face-down and
  resumes when it is turned back, without changing the saved speaker or
  volume settings. Recording, calls and the microphone are unaffected.

Both are under Settings > Auto-sleep, off by default and saved separately;
the setup commands `motion.lift` and `motion.quiet` set them too, and
`>motion` on the USB console reports the sensor state. Polling runs only
while one of them is on. A sensor error turns the feature off and clears the
temporary mute. The option is built only for the 1.75C profile; other boards,
including the 1.75 that shares its board file, are unchanged.

Host tests cover the classifier, the runtime, the I2C driver and playback
muting, with replays of recorded pickups, put-downs and landings.

Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: add optional light and dark UI appearance (#465)

Adds an optional Light appearance to the native LVGL UI behind
CONFIG_MUSE_UI_THEME (off by default; not available on FreeInk builds).
Settings > Appearance offers Automatic, Dark and Light and applies a change
live, without rebuilding the current page or losing typed text.

- The choice is saved in the ui_theme_v1 NVS key from a small worker task,
  outside the UI task. Rapid changes coalesce and a failed write rolls back.
- Home controls, Settings, the keypad, option sheets, the latest reply and
  the system menus share semantic colour styles that follow the palette.
- Automatic keeps the existing dark look unless a content provider supplies
  a background hint through muse_theme_set_hint(). Dark is the existing look.
- The bundled avatar can adapt its backdrop through an optional weak hook;
  existing custom avatars keep building unchanged.
- The serial console accepts theme, theme=auto, theme=dark and theme=light.
- CI builds a Waveshare 1.75C profile with devices/sdkconfig.muse-ui-theme.
  Host and simulator tests cover the palette, persistence and live changes.

Co-authored-by: Paden Clayton <padenc2001@gmail.com>

esp32: Wi-Fi: rejoin after a failed boot join; stop pinning a vanished AP (#474)

A paired Link-only board joins its saved networks once at boot, and
wifi_mgr only reconnects after a first association, so a board that booted
before its router stayed offline until power-cycled. The heartbeat now
retries the join under the setup operation gate, backing off from 30 s to
5 minutes, until one works; later drops stay with wifi_mgr. Boards with the
full UI already rejoin through Muse's keeper.

After an association, a dropped link reconnects with the same pinned BSSID,
so when that access point goes away for good (a mesh node unplugged, a
replaced router) every retry looked for it. When a reconnect reports no AP
found, drop the BSSID and channel and scan every channel for the network,
joining the strongest access point.

Tests: test_link_wifi_rejoin and test_wifi_reconnect_unpin.

esp32: no token characters in logs; pairing decrypt hygiene (#471)

Log lines that mentioned the SDK token printed its first 12 characters. They
now say only whether there is a token, its length and the first 4 bytes of its
SHA-256 (token_fp_text()), or just that one is present; the boot warning about
a token changed since pairing no longer prints the old one either.

Pairing's AES-GCM decrypt now wipes its plaintext buffer when the decrypt
fails, and pairing's transient buffers (base64 scratch, records) are taken from
PSRAM first, falling back to internal RAM on boards without it.

Host test: token_fp_text() never returns any of the token's characters and
matches SHA-256.

esp32: /link-control messages may span BodyChunks; setup's timeouts on esp_timer (#470)

A /link-control message cut across BodyChunks is now held for its session
until the rest arrives, as the Linux client already does, instead of being
dropped with whatever followed it in that chunk. A partial length prefix or
message is freed when its session ends and is never finished by a later
session. A message over 32 KB that arrives split is skipped whole and logged,
so the stream stays in step. A 200 Response's inline body on the control
stream is read the same way, and the session ends (reconnects and registers
again) once the VM ends the control stream.

Setup's two confirmation timeouts, the press window and the confirmed
session's idle limit, now run on a one-shot esp_timer instead of a 4 KB task
that slept them out. This spares internal RAM during setup on boards that
keep setup stacks internal. A timeout that runs out hands its status message
and disconnect to a short-lived task, so nothing blocks the esp_timer task,
and a timeout re-armed meanwhile isn't cut short. The timeouts and their
status messages are unchanged.

Tests: test_link_control_stream runs the framing under ASan/UBSan, with
messages cut inside length prefixes, bodies and oversized messages;
test_link_noise_session checks the end of the control stream. The BLE
lifecycle and helper-task contract tests follow the timer change.

Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: a Wi-Fi rejoin goes straight to the access point it last joined (#469)

After a drop, join_saved_networks() probed the saved network's channel and
often scanned before it connected, and the BSSID cache usually held a scan's
strongest access point rather than the one the gadget had actually been on.

- main/wifi_mgr.c: at IP_EVENT_STA_GOT_IP the BSSID cache records the access
  point actually joined (BSSID, channel, RSSI), and a drop updates its RSSI
  to the last one heard; wifi_mgr_has_cached_ap() says whether a connect
  would go straight to one heard at a given signal or better. A miss still
  drops the cache, so the next attempt scans.
- The BSSID cache gets its own spinlock, because the event loop now writes it
  and can't take the scan mutex.
- main/app.c join_saved_networks(): with a cached access point for the first
  saved network at -75 dBm or better (the channel probe's floor), JOIN_ANY
  joins it at once (capped at 12 s or half the time left), before the channel
  probe; a miss goes on to the probe and the full scan. A weak one, such as a
  far mesh node, goes through the probe and the scan. The shortcut doesn't
  count as a try, so a miss away from home is still "not nearby".
- DHCP stays plain.

Tests: test_wifi_rejoin_shortcut runs the join against a fake radio.

Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: the VM WebSockets resume their last TLS session (#468)

When the device reconnects to the VM (after a Wi-Fi drop, a VM switch or a
session that went silent), it offers the TLS session from its last good
connect. A server that kept the session resumes it, which skips the
certificate chain and the ECDHE.

- sdkconfig.defaults: CONFIG_ESP_TLS_CLIENT_SESSION_TICKETS is on for every
  build.
- main/noise_control.cpp and components/muse/muse_chat_session.cpp: each
  WebSocket keeps one session, in RAM only. It's offered only to the host it
  was made with, and dropped after a failed connect. A server that doesn't
  resume gets a full handshake, verified against the CA bundle as before.
- Link's control session copies the VM host once per handshake, so a host
  changed by setup meanwhile can't relabel the kept session.

Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: Noise's X25519 on HACL* Curve25519, with a PSA fallback (#463)

Noise's X25519 (key pairs and DH) can now run on HACL* Curve25519, the
formally verified, constant-time implementation that mbedTLS ships as its
Everest driver, compiled from ESP-IDF's own copy instead of going through
PSA's generic Montgomery-curve code. The new Kconfig option
NOISE_CORE_X25519_HACL selects it, and sdkconfig.defaults turns it on.
Results are byte-for-byte the same as PSA's, so the protocol doesn't change.
The all-zero shared-secret check is kept, so low-order peer keys are still
refused.

One X25519 operation, HACL* against PSA: 44.5 vs 344.5 ms on an ESP32-C6,
32.1 vs 163.3 ms on an ESP32-S3.

The Everest paths are private to ESP-IDF, so HACL* is built only on ESP-IDF
v6.0.x and only when the Everest files it uses are present. Elsewhere the
build prints a CMake warning and keeps PSA's X25519. Each build compiles only
the backend it uses (#else), so PSA builds are unchanged.

Tests: tests/test_noise_core.py runs cacophony's Noise_XX_25519_AESGCM_SHA256
vector, RFC 7748 5.2 (including 1,000 iterations) and 6.1, and random keys
against PSA, once with each backend.

Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

web-flasher: offer the StopWatch, StickC Plus2, Core2, and Waveshare 1.75 and 2.16 (#473)

All five run the full Muse UI and the CI already builds them. Each gets
its console's USB device (the Core2 shipped with a CP2104 or a CH9102)
and a note: back up the factory firmware first, the Core2 port is for
v1.0 only, and the 1.75 is not the 1.75C.

web-flasher: offer the AIPI Lite, StickS3, ideaspark and HA Voice PE (#472)

The CI already builds all four, so listing them is enough. Each gets
its console's USB device for the port picker, and a note where the
first install needs one: back up the AIPI's and Voice PE's factory
firmware, and the StickS3's UiFlow2 steps (it turns off the USB serial
port, so the first install can't start from the page).

ci: time out hung ESP32 firmware jobs (#467)

Hung ESP32 firmware jobs (mostly stalled Docker image pulls) sat until GitHub's 6-hour default. Each job in esp32.yml now has a timeout of about twice the p99 of its successful runs: builds 20 min, host tests 45, UI simulator 15, web flasher assemble 10 and deploy 15.

esp32: Add the M5Stack CoreS3 Lite as a board with the full UI (#455)

Adds the M5Stack CoreS3 Lite (K128-Lite) as a board with the full UI:
avatar, push-to-talk on PWR, touch, settings, images from Muse and
battery status.

The Lite is the CoreS3 without the camera, proximity sensor, IMU, RTC and
SD slot, with a 200 mAh battery. Everything the firmware drives is the
same part on the same pins, so it builds from the CoreS3's board file and
BSP, with its own name, board choice, overlay, device model, helper alias
and CI build. Units with the newer ILI9342E panel are detected by the BSP.

Checked on one unit: boot, display, touch, the battery gauge, BLE pairing,
Wi-Fi and the control connection. The other features follow the CoreS3
and are marked unverified.

Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: Add the M5Stack CoreMatrix (#446)

A Link gadget profile for the M5Stack CoreMatrix (ESP32-C61, 16 MB flash,
8 MB PSRAM). Its 16x16 white LED matrix shows the status as a picture and
Muse's images, and BtnA is the setup button.

- components/m5stack_corematrix: the board. Its I2C bus, BtnA-C on the M5PM1
  power chip, and the TM1680 matrix (powered through the M5IOE1 expander) as
  a one-bit esp_lcd panel, following M5's drivers. It builds nothing on other
  boards.
- main/matrix_status.c (CONFIG_HOMEHUB_LED_MATRIX): the status pictures and
  Muse's images on a 16x16 one-bit panel, in place of led_status.c.
  display.draw_url and display.draw_file describe the matrix: a pixel lights
  where the image is brighter than mid-gray.
- button.c: button_set_reader(), for a setup button that isn't a GPIO.
- sdkconfig.defaults.esp32c61, for any C61 build: unsigned apps, and Wi-Fi,
  lwIP and BLE code in flash and buffers in PSRAM, so enough internal RAM is
  left while advertising.
- sdk_token_console.c: turn the USB Serial/JTAG interrupts off before
  installing the driver, as the factory firmware leaves one on across a
  reset and the first boot after it hung.

CI builds the profile. On a unit flashed over the factory firmware it boots,
pairs, connects, registers with Muse and opens the tunnel; drawing an image
there hasn't been tried yet. The IMU, buzzer, microSD, BtnB and BtnC aren't
used.

Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: five Text sizes for replies, on bigger screens too (#457)

Text size now has five sizes, Extra small to Extra large, and bigger
screens' reading page follows it: Montserrat 14, 16, 20 and 28, or
unscii 16 doubled from 400 px at Extra large, as before. Small screens'
full-screen replies go from unscii 8 to Montserrat 28. Touch boards get
a Text size slider under Brightness in Settings; the two-button menu
cycles through the five sizes.

Until someone picks a size, screens keep today's look; Brazilian
Portuguese builds start bigger screens at Large, since unscii has no
accented letters. The three-size setting carries over under a new key.
Changing the size while a reply is on the reading page lays the page out
again in place, and on boards with rim controls the reading column stays
clear of the rim hints at every size. With emoji captions on, the reading
page's Montserrat sizes fall back to the emoji font, so emoji show at
every size. The UI simulator and its settings test stub the new calls.

Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: add Seeed reTerminal E1003 board support (#456)

Add a Link profile for the Seeed reTerminal E1003. Its IT8951 controller
shows the status screen and images as full-screen 1872×1404 black-and-white
refreshes, the green button confirms pairing, and `device.health` reports the
battery voltage and estimated charge through the existing reTerminal battery
reader (divider enable on GPIO40). The IT8951 driver keeps its own SPI lock,
so it builds without any other peripheral.

Also adds the overlay, the `board.sh` entry, docs, the license listing for
the Seeed_GFX2-derived driver, battery wiring tests for the new backend, and
an ESP32 firmware CI entry. Other boards' builds are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Lukilyy <15199121375@163.com>
Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: show Muse's Markdown replies as plain text (#454)

Muse often answers in Markdown, and the captions and the latest reply
screen showed it as is. muse_text_strip_markdown() takes the markers out
of the text about to be drawn: bold, italic and struck text keep their
text, code keeps its text as it is, headings and quotes lose their marker,
"* " and "+ " bullets become "- ", links keep their text, table rows keep
their cells separated by ", ", and table dividers, rules and code fences
go. A lone * or _ that isn't emphasis ("2 * 3", "snake_case") stays.

It runs on each caption page and on the latest reply, so the stored reply,
the page turns and their sync with the speech don't change. Line markers
count only at the start of a line of the reply, so a caption line that
wraps before the "+" of "7 + 5" or the ">" of "x > 3" keeps it.

Fixes #106

Co-authored-by: Hassan Naeem <nhassan_1990@yahoo.com>
Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: keep sending a voice note until Muse has it (#460)

Adds CONFIG_MUSE_RESEND_NOTES, off by default, for boards with Muse's own
voice session and PSRAM. With it, up to CONFIG_MUSE_RESEND_NOTES_MAX notes
(default 6) in CONFIG_MUSE_RESEND_NOTES_KB of PSRAM (default 1536 KB) wait
to be sent again, and a new note drops the oldest instead of refusing the
press. Each is tried again after 5, 15 and 30 s, then every 60 s, oldest
first. The screen says SAVED, WILL TRY AGAIN once and SAVED NOTE SENT when
it lands.

A note is sent again only if Muse can't have it: its last body chunk never
went out, or Muse answered with an error that isn't a refusal. A refused
note (4xx other than 408 and 429) is dropped, and a note that went up whole
without an ack is dropped with MAY HAVE SENT - SEE MUSE APP, so it is never
posted twice. Kept notes are in RAM only. With a photo attached
(CONFIG_MUSE_PHOTO_NOTES), the note counts as up once the photo's end has
gone, and a kept note is sent again without its photo, which is freed with
the failed try. Builds without the option are unchanged.

Closes #444.

Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: add Restart to the touch boards' Power page (#459)

Adds Restart to the touch boards' Power page, between Power off and
Cancel. Like a power-off, the input task picks the request up from its
loop: it ends a live call the same bounded way, shows RESTARTING... for
1.5 s and restarts the chip. Settings are saved as they change, so a
restart keeps them and the pairing. "Restart" is translated in Brazilian
Portuguese with the other settings pages, and RESTARTING... in Vietnamese
and Brazilian Portuguese. The button menu, the e-paper settings and boards
without the Power page are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: send a photo with a voice note on the SenseCAP Watcher (#219)

A voice note can now carry a photo. muse_chat_attach_jpeg() checks a
base64 JPEG of up to 256 KiB and sends it as an image item after the
note's audio, in the note's own /chat/stream request, so Muse gets the
question and the photo as one message and the reply shows on the gadget.
It goes up in 16 KB pieces straight from its buffer and is freed once it
has gone up or been dropped. A press or cancel during the upload resets
the request between pieces, and a photo only joins the note it was taken
for while that note records.

On the SenseCAP Watcher with the camera built in, Settings > Sound has
Photo with voice notes (CONFIG_MUSE_PHOTO_NOTES), off by default. With
it on, a hold that starts a note takes a photo at the press (the live
view's frame if it's open, which then closes) and shows TAKING A PHOTO,
then PHOTO TAKEN or NO PHOTO. The note's end waits up to 3 s for it.
Wake word notes and notes saved to send later take none. Builds without
the option are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Temiloluwa <valentinetemi32@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Anant Narayanan <anant@kix.in>

esp32: say how to turn on the Hey Muse wake word (#458)

The esp32 README said the "Hey Muse" wake word was "not enabled on any
board yet", which read as if it couldn't be used. It now says how to try
it: build a board that has PSRAM and the LVGL UI with
`MUSE_WAKEWORD=1 tools/muse/board.sh build|flash <board>`, then turn
listening on at the device (Sound > Wake word in Settings, the quick
menu's Wake word row on button boards, or `>wake.on` over serial). It
also says the web flasher's images don't include it, that listening
keeps the microphone powered while the screen sleeps, and points to the
component README for the details.

Docs only; no code or build changes.

esp32: AIPI Lite: put setup stacks and static buffers in PSRAM (#445)

With Wi-Fi, BLE and the tunnel up, the AIPI Lite's largest free internal
block is about 7 KB. The 8 KB Muse VM lookup task couldn't start, so every
voice turn failed with "Can't reach Muse's server".

The AIPI Lite overlay now turns on two existing options, as other ESP32-S3
boards already do:
- CONFIG_HOMEHUB_SETUP_TASKS_IN_PSRAM: the setup tasks' stacks (pairing
  timers, Wi-Fi scan refresh, provisioning, the Muse VM lookup) go to PSRAM.
  Code and read-only data already run from PSRAM on this board, so flash
  and NVS writes from those tasks leave the cache on.
- CONFIG_MUSE_STATIC_BUFFERS_IN_PSRAM: the avatar's and audio's
  zero-initialized statics (about 18 KB) go to PSRAM.

A host test pins both options and what they depend on. Only the AIPI Lite
images change. The overlay lines come from the patch attached to #384,
whose reporter confirmed voice notes and live calls work on the board.

Fixes #384

Co-authored-by: Hassan Naeem <nhassan_1990@yahoo.com>
Co-authored-by: garychungf-bit <315654297+garychungf-bit@users.noreply.github.com>

esp32: show emoji in captions on the full UI (#461)

Adds CONFIG_MUSE_EMOJI (off by default). With it, screens whose captions use
the 16 px caption font show 190 common emoji in colour: Twemoji v16.0.1
graphics (CC-BY 4.0), scaled to 16x16 RGB565A8 and drawn as the caption
font's last fallback. Emoji outside the set, skin tones, style selectors and
anything joined with U+200D are still dropped, so nothing shows as a box.
Small screens keep dropping emoji, and builds without the option are
unchanged. The pager counts an emoji as two columns, or its 16 px when it
wraps by pixels.

tools/muse/gen_emoji_font.py regenerates the font from the pinned release
(SHA-256 checked); the simulator previews it with -DMUSE_SIM_EMOJI=ON.
Attribution is in both READMEs, fonts/README.md and fonts/LICENSE-twemoji.txt.
About 150 KB of flash when on.

Refs #105.

image_fetch: start each JPEG from a clean decoder state and bound its blocks (#462)

The ROM JPEG decoder takes the image and MCU size only from a SOF0
segment and doesn't clear them. Clear the decoder object before
jd_prepare() in image_fetch.c and in the SenseCAP Watcher's camera
preview, and refuse any output block larger than the one-MCU buffer.

The image_fetch harness now models the ROM decoder: a 4:2:0 JPEG is
drawn MCU by MCU, a stream without SOF0 is refused, and an oversized
block is refused.

test(llms): remove image-model assertion on the generated catalog (#15815)

The test pinned specific model ids in the generated models.dev snapshot.
OpenAI deprecated gpt-image-1.5 upstream, so the next catalog regeneration
drops it and the test fails. Image-model handling in the generator is
already covered by the fixture-based tests in this file.

Co-authored-by: Saoud Rizwan <saoudrizwan@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(sdk): keep bun.lock when bumping SDK versions (#15810)

version.ts deleted bun.lock before running `bun install --lockfile-only`, so
every publish re-resolved the whole dependency tree and shipped versions CI
never tested. The delete was a workaround for `bun pm pack` reading stale
workspace versions from the lockfile; `--lockfile-only` alone refreshes those
lines and leaves third-party pins untouched.

Co-authored-by: Saoud Rizwan <saoudrizwan@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(cli): do not read .env or bunfig.toml from the launch directory (#15781)

* fix(cli): do not read .env or bunfig.toml from the launch directory

The desktop build of the CLI already compiles with Bun's launch-directory
autoload turned off; the npm platform builds did not pass the flag.

Make autoload opt-in in compileCliBinary so every build target gets the
same behaviour by default, and add a build smoke test that runs the
compiled binary in a directory holding a bunfig.toml preload and .env
files and fails if either is honoured.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): keep the launch-directory smoke test from starting a hub

Bare `config --json` creates a core in auto backend mode, which can
prewarm a detached hub that the check never stops. Read the MCP settings
through `config mcp --json` instead, which only reads the file. Also drop
the extra progress logs around the check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

This reverts commit de5a736defdcc3b84d6c091ef183cb2d978ec42e.

Tests: give the SyntheticDataKit short-timeout wall-clock test room for runner jitter (#18721)

## Problem


`tests/test_synthetic_vllm_startup_failure.py::test_a_short_timeout_returns_promptly`
failed on an unrelated PR (#18705, base `fe5340fc99`) in `Repo tests
(CPU, rest-2)`:

```
AssertionError: took 0.58s to honour a 0.05s timeout
assert 0.5803256030001194 < 0.5
```

## Cause

The test measures wall-clock time under xdist on a shared runner. It
used `poll_interval = 1.0` and a `0.5s` bound, so only 0.45s of headroom
separated a correct run from a failure, and a busy runner used it up.
`SyntheticDataKit._await_vllm_server` itself is correct: each wait is
capped at the time left (`min(poll_interval, remaining)`), and the
arithmetic is pinned deterministically by
`test_no_single_wait_outruns_the_callers_timeout`.

## Fix

The test now uses `poll_interval = 10.0` with a `5.0s` bound. The
regression it guards (an uncapped lap waiting the whole interval) now
takes 10s, so it still fails clearly, while a correct run has seconds of
slack instead of under half a second. Test-only change.

## Verification

- `tests/test_synthetic_vllm_startup_failure.py`: 23 passed (0.84s).
- Sabotage: making `_await_vllm_server` wait the full `poll_interval`
(dropping the `min(..., remaining)` cap) fails the test with `took
10.00s to honour a 0.05s timeout`. Restored afterwards.

Studio: bound skill frontmatter merge keys on the composed nodes so PyYAML 6.0.4 cannot hide the expansion (#18704)

## Problem


`studio/backend/tests/test_skill_archive.py::test_import_refuses_frontmatter_whose_merge_keys_explode[_nested_merges]`
fails on `main` in the `(Python 3.13, rest)` backend shard. It shows up
on unrelated PRs (#18694, #18700, both on base `03a3073b2c`):

```
{'failed': []} != {'failed': [{'name': 'bomb', 'error': 'SKILL.md contains invalid YAML frontmatter.'}]}
```

## Cause

CI now installs PyYAML 6.0.4. That release changed
`SafeConstructor.flatten_mapping` to drop repeated merges of the same
anchored mapping. `_FrontmatterLoader.flatten_mapping` sized each merge
by reading `len(merged.value)` after the nested mapping was flattened,
so on 6.0.4 it saw the de-duplicated size, the nested-merge document
stayed under `MAX_SKILL_FRONTMATTER_PAIRS`, and the skill was imported.
On 6.0.3 the same document is refused. Nothing in this repo changed;
`pyproject.toml` lists `pyyaml` unpinned.

The test is right: whether a skill archive is accepted should not depend
on which PyYAML patch release happens to be installed.

## Fix

- `_FrontmatterLoader.expanded_pairs` counts the pairs a mapping holds
once its merge keys expand, reading the composed nodes before PyYAML
flattens them. Results are memoized per node, so the count is linear in
the document size.
- `flatten_mapping` refuses the mapping when that count is over the
limit, then calls the base implementation as before.
- Both versions now refuse the same documents, and small merges still
load (`test_small_yaml_merges_still_load`).

New test `test_merge_key_bound_does_not_depend_on_the_pyyaml_version`
drives the loader on the composed nodes directly, so it pins the bound
independently of how the installed PyYAML flattens.

## Verification

| skills.py | PyYAML 6.0.3 | PyYAML 6.0.4 |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 123 passed | 2 failed (the CI failure and the new test) |
| this PR | 123 passed | 123 passed |

Run over `tests/test_skill_archive.py` and `tests/test_skills.py`. The
other skill test files (`test_skill_mention_semantics.py`,
`test_explicit_skill_loading.py`) also pass on 6.0.4.

Studio tests: read the startup-crash rung gates by shape instead of counting them (#18698)

## Problem


`studio/backend/tests/test_llama_cpp_single_sequence_retry.py::test_the_fit_recovery_rungs_stand_down_for_this_refusal`
fails on `main` since #18695:

```
assert src.count("and not _capability_crash") == 4
E   assert 5 == 4
```

It shows up on unrelated PRs (for example #18646, a CSS-only change) in
the `(Python 3.13, g-l)` backend shard.

## Cause

#18695 added a context-halving recovery rung to
`LlamaCppBackend.load_model`, and that rung correctly stands down on a
capability crash (`and not _capability_crash`), the same as the `--fit`
rungs and the MoE cache rung. The PR is right; the test pinned an exact
occurrence count, so any new rung that follows the rule breaks it.

## Fix

The test now reads the gates by shape with `ast` instead of counting a
substring:

- every `and` expression in `load_model` that includes
`_startup_crashed` is a recovery rung, except pure crash classifiers
(`_startup_crashed and self._is_...(...)`);
- each rung must carry `not _capability_crash`, except exactly one HIP
rung that carries `not _tensor_capability_crash` together with
`_hip_rocr_mismatch`;
- no rung may be ungated, and at least four full-gate rungs must be
found so the scan cannot pass empty.

This keeps the original guarantee and is stricter than the count: the
old check would still pass if one rung lost its gate while another
gained a duplicate.

## Verification

- `tests/test_llama_cpp_single_sequence_retry.py`: 14 passed on current
`main`.
- Sabotage: removing `and not _capability_crash` from the new
context-halving rung makes the test fail with `assert [(8180, [...])] ==
[]`, naming the ungated rung. Restored afterwards.

Studio diffusion: real-step CUDA graph warm-ups by default (#18533)

## Summary

Stacked on #18532 (the INT8 attention sink path repeats a seed from the
first render); merge that first.

Today a resident denoiser's step CUDA graph runs three warm-up forwards
on a side stream for each graph key, on the first render of every load,
and throws them away before recording. With this change the key's first
three real steps are the warm-ups: they run eagerly on copies laid out
like the capture statics, and the fourth step records. The first render
of a load runs three fewer denoiser forwards per graph key.
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_GRAPH_REAL_WARMUP=0` keeps the side-stream warm-ups.

Real-step warm-ups are used only where the key is sure to reach its
recording step inside the render: Studio passes the render's denoise
steps (after img2img strength) to the graph handle before the pipeline
call, and a key takes real warm-ups only when

- the render has more than 3 steps,
- the pipeline has one denoiser (experts that split the steps keep the
side-stream path), and
- the key follows no step-dependent branch (NVFP4 per-step precision, a
pre-hook's branch flag), since such a key may appear on only 1 to 3
steps.

Every other key records on its first call with side-stream warm-ups,
exactly as on main. So SDXL-Turbo's 1-step default, any 1 to 3 step
render, and low-strength img2img or inpaint replay from their first
render as before. A caller that names no step count (anything outside
Studio's render path) also gets main's behaviour.

Before its first real warm-up, a key does what the capture does before
its warm-ups: its NVFP4 GEMMs are tuned at the step's row counts, and
NVFP4 activation scales that are still calibrating go to the capture's
refusal (eager for the load), as before.

## Evidence

Colab L4, torch 2.13.0+cu130, one VM per run, base = merge base
`0b278200d2`, head = this stack, the same prompt and seed for every
render of a process.

FLUX.2 klein (4 steps, so real warm-ups apply), INT8 by Auto, 1024 px,
processes m h | h m m h h m (the first two cold, then race files shared
and warm restarts):

| | first-render denoise, warm restarts (median of 3, range) | cold
first render | second-render denoise (median) | graph engagement, render
1 | images |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 4.777 s (4.770-4.784) | 10.63 s | 0.793 s | 1 capture, 4
replays | `6aff2096` in all 4 |
| head | 3.739 s (3.713-3.780), -21.7% | 10.16 s | 0.782 s | 3 real
warm-ups, 1 capture, 1 replay | `6aff2096` in all 4 |

From render 2 on both arms replay all 4 steps; 0 graph fallbacks.

SDXL-Turbo, Studio's 1-step default, 512 px, default (deferred) speed
profile: graphs engage once the background compile finishes
(`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_BG_COMPILE_YIELD=0` in every arm, so image 4 waits
for it), so images 4, 5 and 6 of the process are the first three graphed
renders. Replays per render:

| | renders 1-3 after the graphs engage |
|---|---|
| base | 1, 1, 1 (recorded on the first call) |
| this PR's previous head | 0, 1, 1 (one real warm-up, then a
side-stream recording) |
| head | 1, 1, 1 (recorded on the first call, 0 real warm-ups) |

All 6 renders of each process are byte-identical across the three trees.

The earlier L4 run of the same real warm-up path (median of 3 warm
restarts, first-render denoise): Qwen-Image-2.1 12.72 -> 10.30 s,
Z-Image-Turbo 9.92 -> 7.89 s, MOSS-Image 16.82 -> 13.20 s, FLUX.3 klein
about equal; second renders and images unchanged (MOSS-Image varies VM
to VM on main itself). All of these run 8 or more steps on one denoiser,
so the step-count rule leaves them on real warm-ups.

- B200, correctness only: Studio's MOSS transformer (tiny random config,
compiled, bf16, true CFG with two graph keys, 12 steps, two renders) is
bit-identical to the side-stream path on all 24 calls; a toy DiT on the
real INT8 attention kernels is `torch.equal` with 16 executed forwards
instead of 19.
- CPU: the CUDA graph, offload graph, block graph and INT8 attention
suites pass on main (595), on #18532 (607) and here (635), no failures.
`test_differential.py` against #18532's head is API only (every new test
names the new switch or `note_render_steps`); reverting the switch alone
fails the 11 real warm-up tests, and removing only the step-count gate
fails the 10 tests that pin main's behaviour for 1 to 3 step renders,
branch keys, several denoisers and a caller with no step count. Against
this PR's previous head, the no-step-count 1-step test is FIXED (replays
per render `[0, 1, 1, 1, 1]` before, `[1, 1, 1, 1, 1]` now, as main).

## Not covered

- Only FLUX.2 klein and SDXL-Turbo ran on this head; Qwen-Image-2.1,
Z-Image-Turbo, MOSS-Image and FLUX.3 klein numbers are from the previous
head, whose path is unchanged for them. A100, T4, G4, a LoRA change,
low-strength img2img on GPU and Windows did not run.
- A key that is not a branch key but first appears in the last 3 steps
of a render (for example a short second stage inside one pipeline call;
no current Studio pipeline was found doing this) still records on the
next render's first call, not on its own first call.
- Video families (graphs opt-in) render through a path that passes no
step count, so they keep main's side-stream warm-ups.

Studio diffusion: keep the checkpointing budget with DiT block swap (#18684)

#18604 added DiT block swap and switched the gradient checkpointing
budget off whenever a run swaps blocks (`gc_budget = None if swapping`),
so every block was checkpointed. On an L4 with Z-Image at 512 px and 10
of 34 blocks swapped, that run trained at 1.19 s/step with a 10.5 GiB
loop peak, leaving about 12 GiB of the card unused. The same model
without swap trains at 0.79 s/step with the budget.

## Change

The budget now runs alongside block swap:

- `install_dit_block_swap` marks each swapped block.
`BudgetedCheckpoint` always checkpoints a marked block and never
measures or plans it, because kept activations would hold its streamed
weights on the card until backward. Only resident blocks are planned,
into the room the swap leaves after step 1.
- Swapped blocks go through a plain non-reentrant checkpoint without the
saved-attention policy. Their swap hooks copy the next block's weights
inside the checkpointed region, and in the other direction during the
recompute. The selective checkpoint rejected that in backward
(`aten.copy_.default encountered during backward but not found in
storage`). Resident blocks keep saved attention.
- On an out-of-memory rerun, `reset_block_swaps` returns every slot to
the pool before the step replays.
- The swap pool's auto prefetch growth gets no reservation. The pool
only grows into the room left by the previous step's peak, and that peak
already includes the kept activations.
- With `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_GC_MODE=plain` or `partial`, or on ROCm,
nothing changes: `_checkpoint_mode(swapping)` still forces plain
checkpointing for a swapped run.

## Results

Colab L4 (22.5 GiB), torch 2.14.1, Z-Image bf16 at 512 px, LoRA r16, 50
steps, `block_swap=10`, compile auto. Base is origin/main. Each arm ran
in a fresh process, arms interleaved, 6 runs per side over two passes on
the same VM.

| arm | steady s/step median [range] | loop peak alloc GiB | mean loss
over 50 steps [range] |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (every block checkpointed) | 1.186 [1.168-1.196] | 10.49 |
0.40719-0.40723 |
| this PR (24 of 24 resident blocks kept) | **0.921** [0.917-0.930] |
14.02 | 0.40722-0.40739 |
| no swap, budget (reference) | 0.788 [0.783-0.793] | 17.29 |
0.40723-0.40735 |

- **Speed:** 1.29x faster per step with the same 10 blocks streamed. The
two ranges do not overlap.
- **Loss:** the largest per-step loss gap between main and this PR has a
median of 0.0014, inside the spread between this PR's own repeats
(median 0.0016). Mean losses agree to 2e-4.
- **Compile:** 0 graph breaks, 5 unique graphs and 0 recompiles on both
sides.
- **Out-of-memory retry:** a test allocation after the plan left room
for only a third of the kept activations. Step 2 ran out of memory and
stepped down five times, from 24 kept blocks to 12, 6, 3, 2 and 1,
replaying the step each time. All 50 steps finished (2 of 2 runs), with
mean loss 0.40725 and 0.40723, the same as main. Steady speed was then
1.19 s/step, the same as main.
- **FLUX.2-klein 9B, 1024 px, `block_swap=auto`, L4 (14 of 32 blocks
swapped):** tested on an earlier revision of this branch that held back
room for pool growth. That revision planned 0 of 18 resident blocks and
ran at 5.44 s/step against 5.53 on main, 4 runs each, losses inside the
A/A spread. This is the reason the reservation was dropped.
- **No-swap path on A100 40 GB:** FLUX.2-klein 9B auto swaps 0 blocks
there. Main and this PR are identical, at 0.959-0.961 s/step, 21 of 32
blocks kept and a 31.9 GiB peak.

## Tests

New file `tests/test_diffusion_block_swap_budget.py`, CPU only:

- `test_trainer_keeps_the_budget_with_block_swap`: the trainer enables
the budget for swapped runs, and the out-of-memory rerun resets the swap
pools before replaying. Fails on main, passes here.
- `test_swapped_blocks_are_never_measured_or_kept`: swapped blocks
always go through the plain checkpoint, are never measured, and are
never kept after the plan. Resident blocks are planned. Fails on main,
passes here.
- `test_swapped_blocks_use_a_checkpoint_without_the_selective_policy`:
the swapped-block checkpoint has no saved-attention policy, and its
backward runs.
- `test_install_marks_only_the_swapped_blocks`: `install_dit_block_swap`
marks exactly the planned blocks (BlockSwap stubbed).
- `test_rerun_resets_the_swap_pools`: `reset_block_swaps` resets every
installed swapper.

`tests/test_diffusion_block_swap*.py`,
`tests/test_diffusion_gc_budget*.py`,
`tests/test_diffusion_gc_saved_attention.py` and
`tests/test_diffusion_train_speed.py` all pass. Differential test
against main: 1 fixed, 4 new, 117 unchanged, 0 failing on this branch.

## Not proven here

- The final revision has no L4 run with a model that needs
`block_swap=auto`. On FLUX.2-klein 9B at 1024 px it should now plan some
resident blocks into the room the pool reservation used to hold. The
out-of-memory step-down still covers a plan that turns out too large.
- The CPU tests cannot reproduce the selective-checkpoint `copy_`
failure, because it needs the real CUDA swap hooks. It showed up on the
L4 runs before the fix and is gone after it.
- Only L4 and A100 were tested. No consumer 24 GB card, no Blackwell, no
AMD. Block swap is CUDA-only.
