Studio: keep the drafter and shrink a Studio-chosen context when the target context does not fit (#18695)

Two fixes for a long-context load where the target model's context does
not fit, so that the load still comes up and keeps its speculative
drafter.

## 1. Keep the drafter when the target context fails before it loads

When a launch with a speculative drafter fails, Studio retries once with
`--spec-default` and no drafter, on the assumption that the drafter may
be the cause. Every later retry rung (`--fit on`, projector on CPU) then
inherits the drafterless command.

llama-server creates the target context before it loads a drafter file.
So when the target's own compute buffer does not fit:

```
E ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 112679.75 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate compute pp buffers
E cmn  common_init_: failed to create context with model '<target>.gguf'
```

the drafter never started loading, yet it is dropped. A later rung that
does fit then runs n-gram speculation instead of the DSpark / DFlash /
EAGLE-3 drafter.

`_target_failed_before_drafter` is true when the failing context is the
target's and no `loading draft model` line was printed. In that case the
no-drafter retry is skipped. A failure after the drafter started
loading, in the drafter's own context, any other crash, and embedded MTP
heads keep the old behaviour.

## 2. Halve a context Studio chose when it cannot be allocated

Studio picks the context from an estimate before launch. When that
estimate runs low, the context fails to allocate, and the `--fit`
retries keep the same `-c`, because `--fit` only changes offload. The
load then fails.

Now, when Studio chose the length (Auto, or filled in from the model)
and the context could not be created for lack of GPU memory, `-c` is
halved and llama-server relaunched. This goes down to 8192 tokens, at
most 8 times, and the reported context length follows the launch. A
context typed by the user (`-c` / `--ctx-size` in the extra arguments)
is never changed.

## Tests

- `test_spec_start_failure_message.py`: the target OOM, a
drafter-context failure with and without the load line, other crashes,
and the no-drafter-file case.
- `test_ctx_halving_after_oom.py`: a fake llama-server that runs out of
memory above 131072 tokens.
- A Studio-chosen 1M context goes 1M, 512K, 256K, 128K and loads,
keeping the DSpark drafter (no `--spec-default`).
  - A typed `-c 1048576` is never halved.
  - The helper needs a context-creation failure and stops at the floor.
  - Without fix 2 the first case does not load.
- The 19 test files that exercise the spec fallback give the same result
with fix 1 and on `main` (2689 passed, 170 skipped). The same 99 test
IDs error on both: the CPU-test CUDA guard trips on a host with GPUs.

Studio: size Inkling 2's banded relative-bias attention for the next llama.cpp prebuild (#18692)

> **Note:** this targets the next llama.cpp prebuild, not the one
shipped today (`b12572-mix-8eebad4`). It assumes the pin set on
`unslothai/llama.cpp` master, which adds unslothai/llama.cpp#385
(chunked dense bias) and unslothai/llama.cpp#386 (banded flash
attention), plus unslothai/llama.cpp#389 at `3b34f4f`. On today's build
the dense rate from #18689 is the right one.

## Problem

#18689 sized the Inkling 2 compute buffer for the dense
relative-position bias (`512 * (8 * n_head + 4 + 2)` bytes per context
token at ub=512). The next llama.cpp prebuild replaces that path in the
common case:

- #386 runs the relative bias through banded flash attention when flash
attention is on, the cache is f16/bf16/f32, the head size is 64 or 128,
there is one stream and the ubatch is above 32 tokens. Studio's default
launch (flash attention, f16 cache, `--kv-unified`, ub=512) takes this
path.
- #385 chunks the dense bias over query rows once it passes 2^29
elements, for the configurations that still take the dense path.

With the dense rate, Studio would overestimate the banded buffer by
about 11x (77531 vs 7236 MiB at 800K) and pick a much shorter context
than fits.

## Fix

In `_compute_buffer_ctx_bytes`, the `inkling2` branch now:

- takes the banded path when it applies: 18 bytes per cell and
micro-batch token, plus a flat f32 `[ub, ub, n_head]` block;
- keeps the dense rate for the rest (quantized cache, flash attention
off, ubatch of 32 or less). With #385's chunking that rate is exact up
to the first split (32K at ub=512 for 24 heads) and an upper bound after
it.

## Verification

CUDA0 compute buffer of llama-server from the shipped mix source plus
#385, #386 and #389 at `3b34f4f`, on an RTX 6000 Ada, Inkling-2-Mini
UD-Q4_K_XL, `--kv-unified`, compared with Studio's estimate:

| n_ctx | ubatch | slots | cache | flash attn | measured (MiB) |
estimate (MiB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 65536 | 512 | 4 | f16 | on | 781 | 786 |
| 262144 | 512 | 4 | f16 | on | 2509 | 2514 |
| 800000 | 512 | 4 | f16 | on | 7236 | 7241 |
| 65536 | 256 | 4 | f16 | on | 387 | 389 |
| 65536 | 2048 | 4 | f16 | on | 3350 | 3428 |
| 262144 | 2048 | 4 | f16 | on | 10236 | 10340 |
| 65536 | 512 | 1 | f16 | on | 672 | 781 |
| 65536 | 512 | 4 | q8_0 | on | 4574 | 6522 |
| 131072 | 512 | 4 | q8_0 | on | 6175 | 12858 |

Studio: size Inkling 2's dense relative-position bias in the GGUF compute buffer estimate (#18689)

## Problem

Loading Inkling-2-Mini (`unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF`, UD-Q4_K_XL) on a
48 GB RTX 6000 Ada fails every time. Studio picks an 800K context and
starts llama-server with `--fit off`, and the server dies allocating its
compute buffer:

```
llama_kv_cache:      CUDA0 KV buffer size = 25000.00 MiB
ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 77530.77 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate compute pp buffers
```

The `--fit on` retry and the CPU-mmproj retries fail the same way (87676
MiB), and the load ends with "Couldn't allocate memory. Try lowering the
context length".

## Root cause

The GGUF architecture is `inkling2`. `_compute_buffer_ctx_bytes` has a
branch for `inkling`, but not for `inkling2`, so the model got the
generic rate of about 1 KiB per context token (the KQ mask). For the
800K launch Studio estimated a 928 MiB compute buffer, and llama.cpp
needed 77531 MiB.

Inkling 2 does not have Inkling's banded flash-attention path. In
`src/models/inkling2.cpp` (b12568) every layer gathers its
relative-position bias as a dense f32 `[n_kv, n_ubatch, n_head]` tensor
and permutes it into a second copy. `build_attn` then adds it to the
mask before attention, using an i32 `[n_kv, n_ubatch]` distance index.
That costs `n_ubatch * (8 * n_head + 4)` bytes per context cell, about
96 KiB at 24 heads and ub=512.

Two smaller gaps hid this:

- `attention.head_count` is a per-layer array in Inkling 2 GGUFs, and
only `head_count_kv` arrays were parsed, so `_n_heads` was None.
- The ctx-independent estimate missed the block attention residuals:
every block's output stays live, and each depth mix holds three `(blocks
+ 1) * n_embd` copies. It came out at 146 MiB against 187 MiB measured
at ub=512.

## Fix

- Parse `attention.head_count` arrays into a new `_n_heads_by_layer`,
and `attn_res.block_size` into `_attn_res_block_size`. `_n_heads` stays
unset for array GGUFs, so other architectures keep their existing
fallbacks.
- Add an `inkling2` branch to `_compute_buffer_ctx_bytes`: the KQ mask
plus two f32 bias copies and the i32 index per cell, sized by the widest
full-attention layer. Without flash attention it also adds the f32
scores, as the generic path does. The sliding layers' smaller bias
reuses the same allocation, so it adds no extra term. There is no
dequant term, because a q8_0 cache measured the same as f16.
- `_compute_activation_width` adds the live residual blocks and the
depth-mix copies when `attn_res.block_size` is present.

## Verification

Measured the CUDA0 compute buffer from llama-server (bundled b12568, 4
slots, `--kv-unified`) on an RTX 6000 Ada, compared with Studio's
estimate (flat + context terms):

| n_ctx | ubatch | cache | flash attn | measured (MiB) | before (MiB) |
after (MiB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 65536 | 512 | f16 | on | 6523 | 210 | 6522 |
| 131072 | 512 | f16 | on | 12859 | 274 | 12858 |
| 262144 | 512 | f16 | on | 25531 | 402 | 25530 |
| 800000 | 512 | f16 | on | 77531 | 928 | 77530 |
| 65536 | 256 | f16 | on | 3261 | 107 | 3263 |
| 65536 | 1024 | f16 | on | 13049 | 419 | 13042 |
| 65536 | 512 | q8_0 | on | 6517 | 466 | 6522 |
| 32768 | 512 | f16 | off | 4936 | 2514 | 4922 |
| 65536 | 512 | f16 | off | 9672 | 4882 | 9658 |

With experts on CPU (`-ot exps=CPU`) or a partial offload (`-ngl 30`),
the per-token slope is unchanged (101376 B/token at ub=512). Only a
ctx-independent term is added.

End to end, loading the same model on the same machine with no context
set, Studio now picks `-c 192512` with `--fit off` and loads on the
first attempt. The real compute buffer was 18790 MiB against an estimate
of 18798 MiB, GPU 0 ended at 46.9 of 49.1 GB, and a chat completion
returned normally.

Tests: `test_compute_buffer.py` checks the measured table above (within
1%), the per-token rate, the head choice from full-attention layers, the
layer-split delta and the residual-block width.
`test_kv_cache_estimation.py` checks parsing of the per-layer
`head_count` and `attn_res.block_size`. The compute-buffer, KV-estimate
and fit suites pass locally.

GRPO packing: MoE-aware self-check and varlen attention for packed rows (#18685)

## Problem

Two problems keep GRPO sequence packing from paying off on models that
run on the transformers modeling path (FastModel).

**1. The packing self-verify rejects MoE models.**

The first-use self-verify compares the packed forward's logprobs against
per-row forwards and requires `max|d| < 0.7` nats. On real MoE weights
it fails every time. Example: Qwen3-30B-A3B, bnb-4bit QLoRA, A100:

- no-grad: `packed-vs-perrow max|d|=0.78-1.08` at T=5128
- grad: `0.56-1.33`

So packing marks the shape unsafe and falls back for the whole run. The
MoE PrefixGrouper opt-in (`UNSLOTH_GRPO_PREFIX_GROUPER_MOE=1`) verifies
against the packed result, so it never engages either.

This is not a packing bug. bf16 rounding changes with batch composition
and flips a few tokens' top-k experts. Two unpacked forwards of the same
rows (batched vs per-row) show the same tail: max 0.92-1.07, mean
0.031-0.034, p99 0.36-0.46.

**2. Packed GRPO forwards run SDPA over a dense [T, T] mask.**

SFT packing installs the varlen attention wrapper from
`unsloth/utils/hf_packed_attention.py`. GRPO packing never did, so
packed rows go through SDPA's memory-efficient kernel over a dense 5128
x 5128 block mask instead of flash.

Profile: Qwen3-30B-A3B 4-bit, 8 rows of 641 tokens, A100. The packed
forward spends 260 ms in `fmha_cutlassF` vs 16 ms of flash attention in
the padded one.

| forward | padded | packed, dense mask | packed, varlen wrapper |
|---|---|---|---|
| no-grad | 0.32 s | 0.55 s | 0.29 s |
| fwd+bwd | 1.32 s | 2.59 s | 1.13 s |

So fixing (1) alone made MoE GRPO 15.7% slower (9.35 -> 10.81 s/step).

## Fix

**1. MoE noise rule.** When the max-abs check fails on a MoE model, also
accept the batch if the mismatch is sparse
(`_unsloth_seq_packing_moe_noise`):

- mean |d| under 0.1 nats over the scored tokens
- at most 2% of scored tokens at 0.7 nats or more
- no row (one document) with half or more of its tokens at 0.25 nats or
more
- at least 64 scored tokens, all finite

A cross-document leak or a position error moves most of a document's
tokens, so it still fails. The leak probe
(`_unsloth_grpo_packing_leaks`) is unchanged and still runs for every
model.

Unchanged:

- Dense models (no `num_experts` / `num_local_experts` /
`n_routed_experts` / `moe_num_experts` > 1 on the config or text
config).
- Batches that pass the old rule.
- The kill / cap / skip verdicts when a batch fails both rules.

The rule is applied at four sites:

- no-grad packing verify
- no-grad PrefixGrouper verify
- unsloth_zoo's grad packing verify and grad PrefixGrouper verify,
through a source rewrite (`_patch_grpo_accumulated_loss_moe_noise`) that
only fires when the compared tensors exist under the expected names

`UNSLOTH_GRPO_PACKING_MOE_NOISE=0` restores the old rule.
`model._unsloth_seq_packing_moe_noise_passes` counts acceptances.

**2. Varlen attention.** Next to the packing boundary check (once per
model), install the same varlen attention wrapper SFT packing uses. This
is skipped when packing is off (`UNSLOTH_GRPO_SEQ_PACKING=0`) or when
the model is refused for packing. Calls without `packed_seq_lengths`
pass through unchanged.

## Results

Setup:

on Colab. Head arms run the same install with this branch's
`rl_replacements.py`, and each arm asserts which tree it imports.

0.04, LoRA r16 on all linear layers, 4-bit, 10 steps.
- Median of steps 4-10, 3 runs per arm, interleaved. Fresh process and
fresh compile caches per run. Exclusive VM per job.

phase |

0.307 s | 0.459 s |

0.314 s | 0.584 s |

Studio diffusion: the INT8 attention sink path repeats a seed from the first render (#18532)

## Summary

On the INT8 attention sink route (FLUX.3, FLUX.2, Z-Image,
Qwen-Image-2.1, HunyuanVideo-1.5), a launch plan runs the sink path
while it learns over its first 32 calls whether any head clipped V (an
attention sink), and races at its 48th call. When a head clipped and the
race picked the kernels without the sink path (Qwen-Image-2.1 on L4 and
A100), or torch's attention, every call of the next render ran that
winner. So the first render of a load was a different image from the
next render of the same seed.

On main this only shows when no thrown-away CUDA graph warm-ups use up
those 48 calls first: CUDA graphs off, a LoRA scale in
`attention_kwargs`, or a prefix K/V over 1 GiB. Qwen-Image-2.1 runs 31
INT8 attention calls per step, so its decision landed inside step 2.

## Change

The race, its call, its inputs and its scope stay as they were: a sink
race verdict is per load, never persisted, so every load races on its
own inputs (#18156).

- Every undecided call before the decision (not only the first 32)
records its clipped-key counts, and whether its output was used. A call
inside a capture's side-stream warm-ups is thrown away; anything else is
used.
- At the decision, a verdict other than the sink path is taken only
where no used call clipped on the sink path. Otherwise the plan keeps
the sink path for the load, which is what its earlier calls computed, so
the next render repeats the seed. The bucket still keeps the race
verdict for later plans of the same load.
- A torch attention verdict does not move routes (floor raise or stock
processor) that another plan of the load already ran used INT8 calls on.
- Main's default path (CUDA graphs on, side-stream warm-ups) is
unchanged by these rules: its learning calls are thrown away.

## Evidence

Colab L4, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Qwen-Image-2.1 INT8 (Auto), 1024 px, 8
steps, CUDA graphs off, the same prompt and seed twice per process, one
VM:

| | load 1: render 1 | load 1: render 2 | load 2 (new process, same
Studio home): render 1 | render 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | `fede6637` | `b80aa53a` | | |
| this branch | `b2d547c3` | `b2d547c3` | `b2d547c3` | `b2d547c3` |

- The second load raced again: its plan carries its own race result, and
the Studio home's caches hold no sink verdict entry after either load.
- Second-render s/step: main 1.352, this branch 1.366 and 1.367 (one
sample per arm). Peak allocation is unchanged on the first load (17681
MiB in both arms).
- With CUDA graphs on (the default), the stacked warm-up PR's tree
(which contains this change) renders FLUX.2 klein byte-identical to main
(`6aff2096`) in all 8 processes on the same VM.

- B200, correctness only (earlier revision with the same rule): a toy
8-block DiT on the real INT8 attention kernels with V sinks on the first
tokens, eager and `torch.compile`d, 8 steps, two renders of the same
inputs. Main with graphs off differs between render 1 and render 2 for
every verdict; this rule gives `torch.equal` on every step. With every
call treated as a thrown-away warm-up (main's rule) the mismatch comes
back. No new dynamo graphs, breaks or recompiles.
- CPU (`-o addopts=`): the INT8 attention, CUDA graph and probe cache
suites, 595 passed on main and 607 here, no failures on either.
`test_differential.py` against the merge base: DISCRIMINATING, 12 fixed,
0 head failures. New tests cover the kept sink path after a used clip, a
bucket verdict of the same load after a used clip, thrown-away clips
taking the verdict as before, the route guard, the used/thrown-away
mark, every undecided call being checked, and a load that kept the sink
path persisting nothing (the next load and process race again).

## Not covered

- HunyuanVideo-1.5's known first-render difference may be the same
mechanism; it was not run.
- Only L4 and B200 ran this rule; A100, T4, G4 and Windows did not.

Tests: ignore torch.compile resume functions when counting MLP-skip arming layers (#18688)

## Summary

`Repo tests (CPU, rest)` fails intermittently on current `main`. It is
seen on #18650 and #18532, both based on recent `main`, and both runs
include #18607 and #18641:

```
FAILED tests/test_gc_skip_replay_mlp_down.py::test_only_the_post_norm_free_layer_arms
E   AssertionError: assert ['LlamaDecode...e_at_514_178'] == ['LlamaDecode...fast_forward']
E     Left contains one more item: '__resume_at_514_178'
```

## Cause

#18607 added this test. It collects every module-level function in
`unsloth.models.{llama, gemma, ...}` whose source calls
`arm_mlp_output_unread(` and expects exactly
`LlamaDecoderLayer_fast_forward`.

When an earlier test in the same xdist worker compiles that layer and
hits a graph break, Dynamo parks the continuation function
(`__resume_at_<offset>_<n>`) in the compiled function's module globals.
That puts it in `unsloth.models.llama`. Its code object points at
`LlamaDecoderLayer_fast_forward`'s lines, so `inspect.getsource` returns
the same source, and it counts as a second arming layer. The test passes
alone and fails only when such a compile ran first in the worker. The
product code is right; the test's view of the module namespace was not.

## Change

`tests/test_gc_skip_replay_mlp_down.py`: only count a function when its
code name matches the name it is bound under (`fn.__code__.co_name ==
fn_name`). Dynamo's resume functions are bound as `__resume_at_*` but
named `torch_dynamo_resume_in_*`, so they drop out. Every function
defined in the module with `def` still matches.

## Testing

need CUDA).
- Reproduced the CI failure with a conftest that plants a resume
function exactly as Dynamo does: same code with `co_name =
"torch_dynamo_resume_in_LlamaDecoderLayer_fast_forward_at_514"`, bound
as `__resume_at_514_178` in `unsloth.models.llama`. The test from `main`
fails with `Left contains one more item: '__resume_at_514_178'`; this
version passes.
- The guard still does its job: planting a real second arming function
in `unsloth.models.gemma` still fails it (`Left contains one more item:
'GemmaDecoderLayer_arming'`).

PrefixGrouper Qwen3-MoE: accept per-module config copies from the vLLM rebuild (#18660)

## Summary

With `fast_inference = True`, the Qwen3-MoE GRPO PrefixGrouper opt-in
(`UNSLOTH_GRPO_PREFIX_GROUPER_MOE=1`) never engaged. Nothing reported
it: GRPO quietly used the packed path, and the flex kernel was never
called.

**Root cause:** the vLLM rebuild gives every module its own copy of the
config.
- `unsloth_zoo.empty_model.copy_attributes` deepcopies the config once
per module. After the rebuild, every attention module holds a different
config object from `model.config` (4 distinct objects on a 4-layer
model, 28 on Qwen3-0.6B).
- `enable_hf_prefix_seg_info` required `module.config is text_config`,
so every layer was refused. `prefix_seg_info_applied` was cached as
False.

**Fix:** keep the identity fast path, and also accept a copy that
matches on the fields the gate and the span cap read: `model_type`,
sliding window fields, `attention_dropout`, `output_router_logits`, head
counts, `head_dim`, `num_hidden_layers`. A layer whose config differs on
any of these is still refused.

**Scope:**
- Dense models are not affected. Llama, Qwen3, Mistral, Gemma-2, Cohere
and Granite use Unsloth's marked attention forwards, and engage under
vLLM today.
- The default path is unchanged. The new comparison only runs for
`Qwen3MoeAttention`, after the MoE opt-in check has passed.

## Tests

- `test_fast_inference_rebuilt_model_is_covered`: deepcopies each
module's config the way the vLLM rebuild does, then asserts
PrefixGrouper is applied and that its log-probs match unshared rows
(fp32, at most 1e-4). It fails on main and passes with this change.
- `test_rebuilt_model_with_a_different_layer_config_stays_off`: one
layer with a different `sliding_window` keeps PrefixGrouper off.
- The existing 9 tests still pass.

## GPU check (Colab L4)

Setup: torch 2.13, transformers 5.17, vLLM 0.29.0, TRL 1.15. GRPO with
G=8, 3 steps. The counts are PrefixGrouper flex-kernel calls on no-grad
(old/ref logp) and grad forwards.

Keep tokenizers loading when the Hub rate limits the Mistral tag lookup (#18662)

**Problem:** On transformers 4.57.x through 5.5.4, loading any tokenizer
with a vocab over 100k by repo id (Qwen3, Llama 3, Gemma, and so on)
makes an anonymous `model_info` call to read the repo's tags and spot a
Mistral base. That call has no error handling, so a single 429 fails
`from_pretrained` even when every tokenizer file is already cached.
Anonymous users on shared IPs (Colab, Kaggle, CI runners) are the ones
who hit this: the anonymous API limit is 500 calls per 5 minutes per IP.
On transformers 5.x the 429 also surfaces as a misleading `OSError:
Unable to load vocabulary from file`.

transformers 5.6.0 fixed it upstream by treating a failed lookup as "not
Mistral".

**Fix:** `fix_transformers_mistral_regex_hub_error` in `import_fixes.py`
back-ports that guard. It wraps `_patch_mistral_regex` on
`PreTrainedTokenizerBase` (4.57.x) or `TokenizersBackend` (5.0 to 5.5).
An exception raised inside the `is_base_mistral` tag lookup returns the
tokenizer unchanged, exactly as 5.6.0 does; any other error still
raises. It is applied only when the installed `is_base_mistral` has no
`try:`, so it does nothing on 5.6.0 and later, and applying it twice
wraps once.

**Testing**

Warm-cache
`AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen3ForCausalLM")`
with the tag lookup answering 429:

| transformers | without the fix | with the fix |
|---|---|---|
| 4.57.6 | `HfHubHTTPError: 429 Client Error: Too Many Requests` |
loads, same token ids |
| 5.0.0 | `OSError: Unable to load vocabulary from file` | loads, same
token ids |
| 5.5.4 | `OSError: Unable to load vocabulary from file` | loads, same
token ids |
| 5.18.0 | loads (guarded upstream) | loads, guard not installed |

- `tests/test_mistral_regex_hub_guard.py` (new, 4 tests): a 429 in the
lookup keeps the tokenizer, unguarded transformers fails the load, an
error outside the lookup still raises, and the fix is idempotent. Run
against `main`'s `import_fixes.py` (`UNSLOTH_IMPORT_FIXES`), the 429
test fails.

together).

Studio: expanding a collapsed model picker opens at full height (#18661)

## Summary

With a model loaded and the model picker collapsed, expanding it kept
the panel below the composer and squeezed it into the room left under
the collapsed view. Closing and reopening the picker showed the proper
height. Expanding now gives the same full-height panel as a fresh open.

## Cause

`PopoverContent` carries
`max-h-(--radix-popover-content-available-height)` by default. The
collapsed panel opens below the composer with the normal gap, so Radix's
available height is only the room under it. On expand the panel hit that
cap first, and the drop offset (which lets a downward panel ride up over
the composer) measured the capped height, saw it fit, and never moved it
up. A fresh open measures before that cap is set, which is why reopening
looked right.

## Fix

The expanded panel now uses the same
`max-h-[var(--picker-floor,calc(100dvh-16px))]` the collapsed view and
Run settings already use. Opening upward is unchanged (`--picker-floor`
is the available height there); opening downward is capped to the
window, so the drop offset sees the real height and lifts the panel.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`,
`tests/composer-model-picker.test.ts` (97 pass).
- Isolated Studio on CPU with a loaded thinking GGUF, driven with
Playwright on the new chat page: open collapsed, expand, then close and
reopen.

| Window height | Expand before | Expand after | Reopen |
|---|---|---|---|
| 820 | 356px, below the composer | 400px | 400px |
| 760 | | 400px | 400px |
| 1000 | | 420px | 420px |

Not checked here: the Desktop shell on macOS / Windows / Linux.

## Summary

`Repo tests (CPU, rest)` is red on `main` (seen on #18650, reproduced on

```
AssertionError: unsloth/kernels/fast_lora.py:686 LoRA_MLP: i.fill_(_SKIPPED_FILL)
```

## Cause

#18607 (skip the LoRA MLP down projection in gradient checkpoint
replays) builds the skipped output as `i = X.new_empty(X.shape)`. When
the test-only `_SKIPPED_FILL` sentinel is set, it then calls
`i.fill_(_SKIPPED_FILL)`. `i` is returned from `LoRA_MLP.forward`.

The guard exists because torch 2.11 compiles a wrong gradient for an
ATen in-place op on a fresh tensor a `torch.autograd.Function` forward
returns (#14712), and the block-compile path (#18641) traces this
forward. The guard is right, and the skip itself is right: only the
mutation needs to go.

filled, `X.new_full(X.shape, _SKIPPED_FILL)`, when the sentinel is set.
Otherwise it stays `X.new_empty(X.shape)`. The values are identical
(`new_empty` + `fill_` and `new_full` both give a tensor of that shape

PrefixGrouper flex: skip the doomed compile on small-smem NVIDIA GPUs, opt-in small tiles (#18645)

## Summary

On a T4 (sm75, 64 KB shared memory), the GRPO PrefixGrouper
FlexAttention kernel cannot compile. The 16-bit 128 / 64 tile needs
98304 B at head_dim 128, and the one-stage retry needs the same amount.
Today the compile check spends about 3 minutes failing, twice, at the
first training step. It then switches PrefixGrouper off.

This PR does two things, both inside the compile-options and
compile-check code in `unsloth/utils/prefix_grouper_kernel.py`:

1. **Skip the failing compile.** The skip applies on NVIDIA GPUs below
96 KB of shared memory, for fp16 / bf16 at head_dim >= 128 when the user
has not opted in. The check is skipped up front and PrefixGrouper
reports itself off with a clear reason. The result is the same as today
(the packed path), minus about 185 s of startup per run on T4.
2. **Opt-in small tiles.** `UNSLOTH_GRPO_PREFIX_GROUPER_SMALL_SMEM=1`
pins forward and backward tiles that fit 64 KB. The tiles are chosen
from the device's queried shared memory limit (Triton `max_shared_mem`,
falling back to the torch device properties), never from the GPU name.
The settings are forward 32 / 32 with 1 stage and 4 warps, and backward
32 / 32 / 32 / 32 with 1 stage and 8 warps. Every key is pass-prefixed
(`fwd_*`, `bwd_*`), so nothing leaks between passes. That gives one
compiled variant per call site, and the one-stage retry adds no second
one.

GPUs with 96 KB or more shared memory (sm80+, sm86 / sm89 / sm120, V100)
keep exactly the same `kernel_options` as before. ROCm keeps today's
behaviour; the opt-in tiles are available there for testing.

## Why the small tiles are not the default on T4

Triton 3.8 emits no tensor-core MMA on sm75. A plain `tl.dot` in fp16
compiles to 0 `mma.sync` and 256 `fma.rn.f32`, and the flex kernels
compile the same way. Attention therefore runs on CUDA cores:

- Isolated kernel test (Qwen3 attention shape, prompt 512 + 8 x 128):
flex forward + backward takes about 46 ms, against 9-11 ms for the
unshared SDPA rows.
- The shared forward wins on larger models, but the flex backward loses
that time again.

| T4, fp16, GRPO, 768-token prompt, 8 x 128 completions | PG off (A/A, 3
runs) | opt-in small tiles (3 runs) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B step time (s), run 1 | 4.939 / 4.964 / 4.968 | 6.908 /
6.935 / 7.025 | +39.7% (slower) |
| Qwen3-1.7B step time (s), run 1 | 10.214 / 10.279 / 10.290 | 9.982 /
9.992 / 10.022 | -2.8% |
| Qwen3-1.7B step time (s), run 2 (other VM) | 11.136 / 11.190 / 11.294
| 10.734 / 10.738 / 10.805 | -4.0% |

On 1.7B the logps phase drops from 1.30 to 0.87 s and the compute_loss
forward from 1.50 to 0.96 s, with peak memory going from 4.56 to 4.43
GB. Most of that is lost again in the backward.

Default path, Qwen3-0.6B, base vs head without the opt-in:
- **Steady state:** 5.56 / 5.67 s for base and 5.56 / 5.60 / 5.61 s for
head, against a PG-off A/A of 5.47 / 5.58 / 5.67 s. All of these are
inside the A/A spread.
- **Wall time per run:** 292 s for base and 107 s for head.

## Correctness on T4 (opt-in path)

The check uses real Qwen3 FastLanguageModel with LoRA. It compares the
PrefixGrouper stream against unshared per-row log-probs and LoRA grads,
and the flex kernel was called 56 times.

| | fp32 PG vs per-row | fp16 PG vs fp32 per-row | fp16 per-row vs fp32
per-row |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6B max abs dlogp | 3.2e-5 | 0.024 | 0.014 |
| 0.6B total rel grad | 6.4e-6 | 5.2e-3 | 5.1e-3 |
| 1.7B max abs dlogp | 2.5e-5 | 0.022 | 0.028 |
| 1.7B total rel grad | 7.1e-6 | 5.0e-3 | 4.5e-3 |

So the fp16 PrefixGrouper error is at the level of fp16 rounding of the

## Attention dispatch: automatic saved attention only inside Unsloth's
checkpoint (follows up #18488)

#### Summary

Follow-up to #18488. With `UNSLOTH_GC_SAVE_ATTENTION` unset, automatic
saved attention now routes a long training call only where a
saved-attention frame can exist. That means under Unsloth's smart
checkpoint (`use_gradient_checkpointing = "unsloth"`) and, when the call
is traced, only inside Unsloth's own compiled block.

#### What broke

#18488 routes every unpacked SDPA training call at or above the
threshold through `unsloth_zoo.saved_attention.saved_attention_call`.
The zoo creates frames only inside `UnslothCheckpointFunction` (zoo
`gradient_checkpointing.py:2074`). With `use_gradient_checkpointing =
True` or `False`, `apply_unsloth_gradient_checkpointing` unpatches it,
so no frame ever exists. `saved_attention_call` is
`@torch.compiler.disable`d and with no frame it just runs the plain
call. Inside a compiled decoder block (per-block compile is on by
default for FastLanguageModel on torch >= 2.11), each long attention
call therefore becomes a graph break that saves nothing. Under a user's
`torch.compile(..., fullgraph=True)` it raises `Unsupported: Skip
calling torch.compiler.disable()'d function`.

This only happens where zoo turns on automatic mode: T4 and A100 from 8K
tokens, L4 from 16K.

#### Repro (CPU, automatic mode simulated with a threshold of 16,
32-token call, no smart checkpoint)

| arm | default compile | `fullgraph=True` |
|---|---|---|
| automatic mode off (before #18488) | 0 graph breaks | compiles |
| main | 3 graph break records (`Skip calling torch.compiler.disable()'d
function`), no frame active | `Unsupported` |
| this branch | 0 graph breaks | compiles |

#### Fix

`_auto_saves_attention` now also requires
`_saved_attention_frames_possible()`:

- `torch.utils.checkpoint.CheckpointFunction` is
`UnslothCheckpointFunction`. Dynamo cannot read a Function class's name,
so this read goes through `_constant_probe`. The patch is installed at
`get_peft_model` / load time, before any trace.
- When traced, `unsloth.models._block_compile._IN_COMPILED_REGION[0]`
must be set. That flag marks Unsloth's own block (`fullgraph=False`,
where a break is legal) and not a user's compile. zoo's sequence tiling
reads the same flag.

- In automatic mode the setting must still be `auto` when the call is
made. `UNSLOTH_GC_SAVE_ATTENTION=0` set after `import unsloth` stops
zoo's frames (`new_saved_attention_frame`), but before this change it
did not stop the routing, so it still produced a graph break per layer
inside Unsloth's own block.

The explicit `=1` / `offload` setting (min_seq None) is unchanged.

#### Tests

New `tests/test_attention_dispatch_saved_attention_scope.py` (CPU):
- automatic mode routes only under the smart checkpoint;
- a user's compile has 0 graph breaks with and without the smart
checkpoint, and `fullgraph=True` compiles;
- inside Unsloth's block under the smart checkpoint the call is still
routed;
- the explicit setting still routes;
- `UNSLOTH_GC_SAVE_ATTENTION=0` / `false` set after import stops routing
and leaves 0 graph breaks inside Unsloth's block.

`tests/test_attention_dispatch_saved_attention.py`: the two
automatic-mode routing tests now install `UnslothCheckpointFunction`, as
a real "unsloth" run does.

## ROCm SDPA self-check: no enable_gqa on torch without it (follows up
#18453)

#### Summary

Follow-up to #18453. On torch 2.4, the declared floor, the ROCm SDPA
self-check refused AOTriton flash for every Unsloth attention call on an
RDNA GPU. The kernel was never the cause: the check sent an argument
that torch 2.4 does not have.

#### What broke

The flash child in `unsloth/utils/rocm_sdpa_check.py` runs a
`segments_gqa` case that calls `F.scaled_dot_product_attention(...,
enable_gqa=True)`. torch added `enable_gqa` in 2.5. On 2.4 the call
raises `TypeError: scaled_dot_product_attention() got an unexpected
keyword argument 'enable_gqa'`. The child records any exception other
than "No available kernel" or out of memory as a failed kernel case, so
the report says `ok: false` and `rocm_sdpa_verdict` refuses flash for
that device. Unsloth itself never passes `enable_gqa` when SDPA lacks it
(`SDPA_HAS_GQA` in `attention_dispatch.py`), so no real call can reach
that layout there.

#### Repro (CPU)

The real child script runs in a subprocess. CUDA calls are mapped to CPU
(torch's CPU flash kernel, which is correct), and
`F.scaled_dot_product_attention` is replaced by one that rejects
`enable_gqa`, as torch 2.4's operator does.

| arm | flash child report |
|---|---|
| main (635532fede) | `ok: false`, ran 8, every failure is `segments_gqa
...: unexpected keyword argument 'enable_gqa'` |
| this branch | `ok: true`, ran 4 (expanded K / V segments, fp16 and
bf16, head dims 64 and 128) |

#### Fix

When `enable_gqa` is not in `F.scaled_dot_product_attention.__doc__`,
the child drops the `segments_gqa` case. That is the same test
`attention_dispatch` uses. The expanded K / V and masked cases still
run, so a broken kernel is still refused.

#### Tests

New `tests/utils/test_rocm_sdpa_check_no_gqa.py` (CPU). Command (per
worktree): `python -m pytest -o addopts= -m "not server and not
native_mxc" -p no:cacheprovider -q
tests/utils/test_rocm_sdpa_check_no_gqa.py
tests/utils/test_rocm_sdpa_check.py`. Each arm imports its own tree.

change makes no difference.
- torch >= 2.5 keeps the `segments_gqa` case unchanged.

## Block SDPA align guard: cache tag also under the override (follows up
#18462)

#### What broke

#18462 adds the cache tag `unsloth/efficient-backward-guard` so that
graphs compiled without the efficient-backward guard are not served
again. The patched SDPA lowering is not part of the FX / AOT cache key.
`UNSLOTH_BLOCK_SDPA_ALIGN_GUARD=1` returned before adding that tag.

On CUDA torch < 2.14, a run with the override therefore has the same
cache key as a run of the same Unsloth version from before the tag
existed. The version string is 2026.11.7 both before and after #18462.
That older run compiled the efficient backward without the guard. A user
who set the override as the workaround for the `attn_bias is not
correctly aligned` fault, and kept it after updating, keeps being served
the faulting backward from a warm cache. The PR's own evidence notes the
override was not a reliable workaround once a failing run had warmed the
cache.

#### Fix

`unsloth/models/_block_compile.py`, `_sdpa_alignment_without_guard`:
under the override on an affected torch, add the same cache tag before
returning. The lowering stays stock as before. Torch 2.14+ and ROCm are
unchanged.

#### Tests

New `tests/test_block_sdpa_align_guard_override_cache_tag.py` (CPU, no
compile): with the override set, the lowering must stay untouched. The
tag must be added exactly once on an affected torch and not on 2.14+.
The test loads `_block_compile.py` from its own tree and asserts it.

`cache_key_tag`) the tag tests skip with that reason |

`tests/test_block_sdpa_efficient_backward_guard.py` passes on both arms.

Skip the replayed LoRA MLP down projection under block compile (#18641)

## Summary

Follows up #18607 (and its zoo companion unslothai/unsloth-zoo#2630),
both merged. #18607 skips the LoRA MLP down projection while a gradient
checkpoint replays a Llama-style decoder layer, but only on the eager
path. On torch >= 2.11, the default, block compile traces each decoder
layer, so the eager thread-local token never fires and the skip runs 0
times. This PR brings the skip to the compiled block.

## How

- `_block_compile._wrap.forward` (eager, outside the compiled region)
decides per call whether this is a checkpoint replay of exactly this
layer (`gradient_checkpoint_replay_module() is layer`) and whether the
layer is eligible:
- its forward is tagged `_unsloth_mlp_output_unread` (only
`LlamaDecoderLayer_fast_forward`, which Llama / Qwen2 / Qwen3 / Mistral
use; its MLP output only feeds `residual + mlp(x)`);
- the MLP's own `forward` is `apply_lora_mlp_swiglu`, with no accelerate
hook or tiled MLP around it;
  - there are no forward hooks on the layer or the MLP, and none global.
- If so, it sets the plain global `fast_lora._BLOCK_SKIP_DOWN` around
the compiled call. The traced `LoRA_MLP.forward` reads it, so dynamo
guards on it, and the replay graph returns an unfilled tensor instead of
running `act(e) * g` and the down GEMM (plus its NF4 dequantize).
- The block's grad-mode trial (run on the first no-grad call, which
under Unsloth checkpointing is the checkpointed forward) now trials the
skip graph, which is the graph the replay will use. So each layer kind
still compiles two graphs (no grad, grad), as before. Later steps
compile nothing, and there is no graph break.
- A grad-mode call that is not an eligible replay keeps the full graph,
through its own `checked` bit (2 = full, 4 = skip). For example,
training without checkpointing or with a hooked layer compiles that
graph on first use, through the usual strict compile and demotion path.
- LoRA dropout or a LoRA bias takes `LoRA_MLP`'s other branch, which
always runs the down projection.
- `UNSLOTH_GC_SKIP_MLP_DOWN=0` turns it off, as in #18607.

## Tests

`tests/test_gc_skip_replay_mlp_down_block_compile.py` (CPU, torch >=
2.11). It wraps the real `Qwen3DecoderLayer` with block compile's
`_wrap` (aot_eager backend), uses real PEFT LoRA,
`LlamaDecoderLayer_fast_forward` and Unsloth's reentrant checkpoint,
with the skipped output NaN-filled.
- Every replayed layer output is NaN and the skip count is exactly
N_LAYERS. Every LoRA gradient and the input gradient match the same
compiled run with the skip off (bitwise on Intel CPU and Colab CUDA; the
test allows a few ulps, rtol 1e-5, because Inductor CPU codegen on the
AMD CI runners with torch 2.11 rounds the two graphs a few ulps apart),
and are close to the uncompiled, uncheckpointed layers.
- The graph count is unchanged against the skip off. Two more steps add
0 graphs, 0 recompiles and 0 graph breaks.
- A forward hook, LoRA dropout, or a call outside a replay does not
skip.
- On #18607's head the same file fails (skip count 0 vs 3).

`use_gradient_checkpointing = "unsloth"`, bs1. Each arm takes 3 warmup

range over the 3 runs. Every arm compiles cold
(`TORCHINDUCTOR_FORCE_DISABLE_CACHES=1`).

## ROCm packed attention: rows eager varlen rejects stay dense in the
block (follows up #18435)

#### Summary

Follow-up to #18435. On ROCm builds where torch's flash varlen cannot
run inside a compiled graph, packed layers that the eager varlen wrapper
rejects anyway now stay inside the compiled block on the dense path.
Before this change they left the block, which costs a graph break per
layer, and then ran the same dense attention eagerly.

#### What broke

#18435 made `_block_varlen_prepare` return `_LEAVE_BLOCK` for every fp16
/ bf16 packed layer with head dim up to 256 whenever the in-graph varlen
probe refuses. The eager wrapper then checks the call with
`_static_window`, which rejects:

- attention sinks (gpt-oss) and logit softcapping (`_softcapped`);
- a head dim that is not a multiple of 8;
- non-causal attention;
- attention dropout in training.

For those layers the eager wrapper calls the original dense SDPA. So the
row left the compiled block only to run the attention it would have run
inside the graph before #18435.

#### Repro (CPU, ROCm faked through `torch.version.hip`, in-graph probe
refusing)

|---|---|---|
| sinks, softcap, head_dim 20, `is_causal=False`, dropout 0.1 in
training | `_LEAVE_BLOCK` (graph break, then dense) | `None` (dense
inside the block) |
| eligible layer (also dropout 0.1 in eval, dropout 0.0 in training) |
`_LEAVE_BLOCK` (eager varlen) | `_LEAVE_BLOCK` (eager varlen) |

#### Fix

`_eager_varlen_rejects(attention, kwargs, head_dim)` mirrors the
layer-level conditions of `_static_window`, which need no tensors. When
it is true, the ROCm branch returns `None` and the layer keeps the
existing dense path. It does not count as `compiled`. Eligible layers,
CUDA builds and ROCm builds whose varlen traces are unchanged.

## GRPO rollout scope: off when a tool is async (deadlock) (follows up
#18452)

#### What broke

#18452 wraps TRL's tool-calling `_generate` in `vllm_rollout_scope` by
default (zoo #2610). The scope keeps the merged-rollout fold entered,
and with it the process-wide `_MERGED_ROLLOUT_LOCK`, until `_generate`
returns. TRL 1.18 runs async tools on its event-loop thread through
`asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(...).result()`
(`trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:2128`) while the main thread waits. An
async tool that calls a vLLM engine wrapped for merged rollouts needs
that lock, and the main thread holding it is waiting on the tool. So the
rollout hangs with no error. This applies both to the policy's own
engine (an agent that asks the policy a sub-question) and to another
engine.

#### Repro (CPU, zoo merged-rollout test doubles, TRL-style async tool
on a separate event-loop thread, 2 s timeout)

- main: `DEADLOCK` (the async tool blocks on the lock held by the scope)
- this branch: completes, `['out']`

#### Fix

`_unsloth_rollout_scope` returns a null context when any tool is async,
checking both TRL's per-batch `_async_tool_dicts` and
`inspect.iscoroutinefunction` over `trainer.tools`. Each engine call
then folds and restores on its own, as before #18452. Rollouts with sync
tools only keep the scope.

2 failed, branch passed

## GRPO packing leak probe: a child shared by two parents (follows up
#18438)

#### What broke

The GRPO packing leak probe (#18438) saves each module's mode and
restores it through `module.train(mode)` in `modules()` order.
`modules()` yields a child shared by two parents only once. So when the
later parent was in training mode, its recursive `train(True)` switched
the shared child back on after the child's own restore had run. Example:
one `Dropout` shared by two decoder blocks and kept in eval mode came
back from the probe with `training == True`, so its dropout stayed
active for the rest of training.

#### Fix

After each module's own `train(mode)` runs (this keeps side effects such
as `Int4PackedLinear` syncing its quant state), every saved flag is set
directly once more.

## Fused label smoothing: tuple outputs and custom smoothers (follows up
#18495)

#### What broke

(`unsloth/models/fused_label_smoothing.py`):

returns `(loss, logits, ...)`. When that forward did not reach the fused
CE, the fallback passed the whole tuple to `LabelSmoother`.
`LabelSmoother` reads `output[0]` of a tuple, which was the scalar loss,

GRPO: score old / ref logps under no_grad, not inference_mode (#18642)

## Summary

With `num_iterations > 1`, GRPO scores the old-policy logprobs once in
`_generate_and_score_completions` and then trains on the same batch for
several iterations. On the first iteration the weights and tokens are
the same ones the old logprobs were scored with, so the PPO ratio should
be exactly 1.

On main it was not. Every iteration-1 token carried a log ratio of about
0.01 nats on average, up to 0.2-0.6 nats, and 0% of tokens matched.
Measured on Qwen3-0.6B LoRA with `fast_inference = True` on an L4, and
it happens with PrefixGrouper off too.

The cause is the grad mode of the scoring forward. Unsloth scored old /
ref logprobs under `torch.inference_mode()` (via
`_get_inference_mode_context_manager`), while the loss scores the policy
under grad mode. With the default compiled packed forward, those two are
not bit-equal. TRL scores old logprobs under `torch.no_grad()`.

This PR runs the four scoring forwards in
`_get_per_token_logps_and_entropies` under `torch.no_grad()` instead:
PrefixGrouper, packed, packed verify, and the padded loop. With that
change the two passes agree bitwise.

## Evidence (Colab L4, torch 2.13, transformers 5.17, TRL 1.15, vLLM
0.29)

Setup: GRPO on unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B, LoRA r16, bf16, G = 8, bs = 8, GA =
2, `num_iterations = 2`, 96 completion tokens, a shared ~1.2k token
system prompt. The loss's `grpo_compute_loss` is wrapped to record
masked `|new - old|` on iteration-1 calls, 3072 tokens per run.

Iteration-1 `|new - old|`, mean over all iteration-1 tokens (4 loss
calls = 2 generations per 4-step run, 30 calls per 30-step run):

| config | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `UNSLOTH_GRPO_PREFIX_GROUPER=0`, vLLM, compiled | 0.0105-0.0124 nats,
0% bitwise (5 runs) | 0 nats, 100% bitwise (2 runs) |
| `UNSLOTH_GRPO_PREFIX_GROUPER_VLLM=0`, vLLM, 4 steps | 0.0113, 0%
bitwise (30-step row below) | 0.0042-0.0043, 50% bitwise (2 runs) |
| `UNSLOTH_GRPO_PREFIX_GROUPER=0`, no vLLM | not run | 0.0042, 50%
bitwise |
| `UNSLOTH_GRPO_PREFIX_GROUPER=0`, `UNSLOTH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1` |
0.0047-0.0049, 50% bitwise (2 runs) | 0.0049, 50% bitwise |
| vLLM, `UNSLOTH_GRPO_PREFIX_GROUPER_VLLM=0`, 30 steps | 0.0113, 0%
bitwise | 0 and 0.00016, 100% and 98.7% bitwise (2 runs) |
| stock TRL GRPOTrainer, same setup | 0, 100% bitwise | n/a |

The 30-step runs scored completions on whether they contain the right
answer. In them, iteration-1 optimizer steps had a clip fraction of
0.00078 on main and exactly 0 with this PR. Step time did not change:
generation steps took 3.00 s vs 3.00-3.05 s, and train steps 1.48 s on
both.

Not covered by this PR:
- With PrefixGrouper on, both passes run the shared-prefix FlexAttention
forward, but over a different set of rows (the whole generation batch vs
one shuffled loss slice). Those forwards are not bit-equal, and the gap
stays at about 0.012 nats on main and with this PR alike. Turning
PrefixGrouper off under vLLM closes it, but makes the train step about
2x slower (0.75 s to 1.48 s), so it stays on.
- The no-grad pass packs the whole generation batch (16 rows) while the
loss packs one 8-row slice. The GEMM shapes differ, so some generations
still come out about 0.004 nats apart (the 50% rows above: the first
generation matches bitwise and the second does not).

Bisection that led here (main, PrefixGrouper off):

| arm | iteration-1 tokens bitwise equal |
| --- | --- |
| main | 0% |
| `UNSLOTH_GRPO_SEQ_PACKING=0` | 100% |
| scoring forward under `torch.no_grad()` instead of `inference_mode` |
100% |
| same 16 rows in both passes (GA 1, bs 16) | 0% |
| stock TRL GRPOTrainer, same model and data | 100% |

So on the compiled path, the gap does not come from batch composition or
from the scorer: it comes from the inference-mode forward. A side
effect: the no-grad packed-vs-per-row self-verify now reads `max|d| =
0.0000`, where main read 0.27-0.59.

Studio: wait out a published image load's tail instead of refusing generate with 409 (#18626)

`/api/inference/images/status` reports `loaded: true` as soon as an
image load publishes its pipeline. The load is not finished at that
point: it still waits for the text encoder host pins
(`finish_encoder_pins_at_load`, for example "pinned 8.7 GiB of
Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration host weights in the background ... the
load waited 1.2 s for the encoder pins") and trims the host heap. Until
it returns, `load-progress` reads `finalizing`, so `/images/generate`
refuses every run with HTTP 409 "An image model is loading. Generate
again once the load finishes." A client that waits for `loaded`, as the
API docs suggest, could still be refused. An outside benchmark lost 11
cells on small simulated cards to this.

The Studio frontend is not affected, because it waits for
`load-progress` to read `ready` before it reads status. The video route
is not affected either: its generate admits a run once the state is
committed and waits for the pins inside the render
(`finish_background_pins`).

## Change

- `DiffusionBackend._publish_state_locked` is now the one place that
assigns a loaded pipeline. Both commit sites (the general load and the
MiniMax-H3-Image load) go through it, and it marks the in-flight
`_LoadingState` as `committed`.
- New `DiffusionBackend.load_tail_pending()`: True when the in-flight
load has published its pipeline, has no error, and is only finishing its
tail.
- `/images/generate`: when a load is in flight and it is only that tail,
the route waits for it, polling every 0.1 s with a 300 s cap, and then
runs. A load or switch that has not published yet still gets the same
409 as before, and so does a tail that outlasts the cap. Engines without
`load_tail_pending` (sd.cpp, MLX) behave exactly as before.

Status answers are unchanged, and so is every frontend path.

## Tests

`tests/test_images_generate_load_tail.py`, CPU only, with the backend
faked:

- `test_generate_in_a_published_loads_tail_waits_and_runs`: status
loaded, `load-progress` reads `finalizing` for three polls and then
`ready`. The generate runs once, after `ready`. On main it gets the 409.
- `test_generate_before_the_pipeline_is_published_is_still_refused` and
`test_a_tail_that_outlasts_the_cap_is_refused`: both still get the 409.
- `test_engine_reports_the_tail_only_after_publishing`,
`test_a_synchronous_load_without_a_loading_marker_publishes`,
`test_every_image_commit_site_publishes_through_the_helper`: the engine
marker.

`test_differential.py` (base `2c21acdc79`, head `1f1d690ba1`):

Studio NPU: run FastFlowLM without Lemonade on Windows (#18554)

Stacked on #18553 (signed FastFlowLM 1.0.13).

Even with FastFlowLM signed, `lemond.exe` is not: the Lemonade 2026.47.1
zip and the files inside its signed MSI are unsigned. Whether Smart App
Control allows `lemond.exe` depends on cloud reputation and changes over
time. On the test machine it was refused for most of a day, then
allowed. This PR removes Lemonade from the Windows path, so everything
Studio starts for the NPU is either Studio's own Python or AMD-signed.

## Design

Studio only uses a small slice of lemond: `/v1/health`, `/v1/models`
(plus `/{id}/options`), `/v1/install`, `/v1/pull`, `/v1/load`,
`/v1/unload`, `/v1/delete`, `/internal/set` and the OpenAI chat routes.
FastFlowLM's own CLI already covers that slice (`flm list --json`,
`pull`, `serve`, `remove`, `version`).

- `core/inference/flm_host.py` (new): serves that slice from Studio's
Python and starts the signed `flm.exe`.
- Catalog rows keep lemond's ids (`qwen3:0.6b` -> `qwen3-0.6b-FLM`) and
labels, so saved chats and settings still resolve.
- Load starts `flm serve <tag> --ctx-len N` with any `flm_args`. Health
reports `recipe_options.ctx_size` the way lemond does.
  - Chat is proxied, with the `model` field rewritten to the tag.
- flm's output is relayed to stdout, so Studio's load-failure
explanations keep working.
  - It exits, stopping `flm serve`, if Studio dies.
- `install_lemonade_prebuilt.py`: on Windows, `install()` downloads the
pinned FastFlowLM zip, checks its sha256 and extracts it where lemond's
`/v1/install` would. `installed_lemond()` then returns `flm_host.py`.
  - Linux runs the same way (see below).
  - `UNSLOTH_NPU_LEMONADE=1` keeps Lemonade on Windows too.
- `lemonade_server.py`: a `.py` binary runs on `sys.executable`.
- `npu_backend.py` is otherwise unchanged. Enable stops a running server
before an upgrade install, since Windows locks the files being replaced.

Existing installs migrate on first use. The old `{"lemond": ...}` marker
reads as a pending upgrade, so the next catalog read runs Enable. That
installs FastFlowLM directly and keeps every downloaded model, which
lives in `flm/`, not in the binary folder.

## Testing

On a Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 with Smart App Control on:

- Fresh Enable takes 7 s: `versions={'lemonade': None, 'fastflowlm':
'1.0.13'}` and 58 catalog rows, with the decision models hidden.
- Download `qwen3-0.6b-FLM` through `/api/npu/models/.../download`, load
it through `/api/inference/load`, then stream and non-stream
`/v1/chat/completions`. No `lemond` process exists at any point.
- A real UI run against the patched backend (built frontend): pick the
model, it loads on the NPU, the answer streams with the Thinking block.
Passed in Chromium and Edge.
- Migration: a root installed by Lemonade 2026.44.1 with a validated
marker switches to `flm_host.py` on first catalog read. The downloaded
model still loads and chats.
- Found and fixed during these runs: flm prints emoji, and the output
relay died on Windows' cp1252 pipe. flm serve then blocked on a full
stdout pipe and non-stream chats timed out after 300 s. The relay now
writes UTF-8 and never stops draining (there is a regression test).

Parity with lemond, on one root (same `flm.exe` and model files), with
the same requests sent to `lemond.exe` 2026.44.1 and to `flm_host.py`:

- All 72 catalog rows match: ids, checkpoints, labels, sizes, downloaded
flags and context windows.
- Identical answers for auth, an unknown load (404), an unknown delete
(422), pull of a downloaded model, load, health (`ctx_size` 4096), chat
(non-stream and stream, same greedy output and usage fields), tools,
`/v1/completions`, 3 concurrent chats and unload.
- Prompt text kept in Studio's log: 0 for both. flm's output is tagged
`(Process)` in lemond's line format, so Studio keeps it only while a
load is open, as with lemond.
- The one difference: lemond loads a model when a chat names one that is
not loaded, flm_host answers 503. Studio never sends a chat without a
resident model.

Switching paths, through `LemonadeNpuBackend` with a Studio restart each
time: Lemonade, Lemonade, direct, direct, Lemonade, direct on the same
root. Every run passes Enable twice, lists the same 58 rows, keeps the
downloaded model, loads it and gets the same answer. `lemond.exe` runs
only on the Lemonade runs. `lfm2.5-it-1.2b-FLM` downloaded fresh through
each path gives byte-identical files, and loads, answers and deletes the
same way.

Unit tests in `tests/test_npu_flm_host.py` (17 cases) pass on Windows
and Linux. They cover:

- catalog mapping, the context window from the downloaded config, and
auth (only `/live` is open)
- flm output tagged `(Process)` so prompts stay out of Studio's log
- install, plus pull complete and error events
- load with ctx and `flm_args`, health, a chat proxied by tag, and
unload
- a failed load naming flm's reason, and delete of a serving model
- `[ERROR]` printed with exit code 0 counting as a failure
- the direct install's layout, reuse and pin change
- when Lemonade is still used, and the `.py` launcher

Existing NPU suites: 475 passed on Linux, 188 on Windows. `ruff-unsloth`
format is AST-identical and `ruff check` passes.

Not covered: macOS (no NPU path), and Linux NPU hardware. Linux
behaviour is unchanged.


## Linux too, and hardware results

Linux now runs FastFlowLM through `flm_host.py` as well, so no platform
starts Lemonade. `UNSLOTH_NPU_LEMONADE=1` still selects lemond.

Checked on the AMD Strix Halo runners (Windows 11 and Ubuntu 24.04,
XDNA2 NPU), current `main` against this branch on the same machine, plus
lemond 2026.44.1 on the same FastFlowLM 1.0.13 files as a reference:

- Windows `main` starts `lemond.exe` and nothing else unsigned; this
branch starts only `python.exe` (PSF), `conhost.exe` and AMD-signed
`flm.exe`, and never `lemond.exe`.
- flm_host matches lemond on all 72 FastFlowLM catalog rows, the Studio
catalog before and after a download, load context, health, options,
greedy answers (stream and non-stream), usage tokens, finish reasons,
the 404 / 422 error statuses and pull.
- A second Enable after a restart changes none of FastFlowLM's files and
downloads nothing. A `main` install with a downloaded model switches to
flm_host on first use and keeps the model.
- `xrt-smi examine -r aie-partitions` lists the `flm serve` process
during generation, on both hosts.
- Decode speed through flm_host equals lemond's (101 tok/s on
Qwen3-0.6B), and time to first token matches (0.61 s each) after pooling
the upstream client and turning off Nagle for the event stream.

Studio: pick DiT block swap from the training API and the Train tab (#18640)

#18604 added a block swap for DiT LoRA training (`cfg.block_swap` /
`UNSLOTH_DIT_BLOCK_SWAP` = off, auto or a block count). It could only be
turned on through the trainer config dict or the env var. The training
API dropped the field, because `DiffusionTrainingStartRequest` did not
declare it, and the Train tab had no control for it. This PR lets you
pick it from both.

## Change

Backend:
- `DiffusionTrainingStartRequest.block_swap`: optional, `"off"`,
`"auto"` or an integer 0..1024. The default is unset, which sends
nothing to the trainer, so behaviour is the same as today, and
`UNSLOTH_DIT_BLOCK_SWAP` still applies. A count is passed on in the
trainer's string form.
- `/api/train/diffusion/start` now calls `block_swap_start_error`, which
runs before any GPU residents are freed. It refuses a block swap the
trainer would only refuse after loading the base, plus families whose
trainer has no swap path:
  - families outside the DiT trainer (SDXL, MiniMax-H3)
  - `base_precision` other than `bf16`
  - `gradient_checkpointing` off
  - the pre-Ampere fp16 fallback
  - no CUDA device
  - an integrated GPU
`off` and `0` are accepted for every family. Only the request field is
checked here, not the env var.
- `family_train_infos` reports `supports_block_swap`, which is true for
DiT families that list `bf16` and are not on the fp16 fallback.
- The DiT trainer emits a `block_swap` event right after the swap is
installed. The fields are `swapped_blocks`, `total_blocks`, `host_gib`
and `pinned_gib`. The training service folds it into a new `block_swap`
field on `/api/train/diffusion/status`. Before this, the only trace was
a warning message that the first progress event overwrote.

Frontend (Images > Train):
- A Block swap select (Off / Auto / Fixed number of blocks, plus Blocks
to swap). It shows only when all of these hold:
  - the family reports `supports_block_swap`
  - Base precision is bf16
  - gradient checkpointing is on
- the host passes the same hardware rule as core LLM layer offload
(`offloadHardwareSupported`, reused from
`features/training/api/mappers.ts`)
- When hidden or set to Off, nothing is sent.
- While a run is going, the run card shows the resolved outcome under
the stats, e.g. "Block swap: 21 of 57 blocks from host RAM (8.1 GiB
pinned)".

## Tests

- `studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_block_swap_api.py` (18, CPU)
covers:
  - request parsing
- forwarding of `auto` and a count through the real route to the
service, and that the forwarded value parses back in the trainer
  - unset stays unset
  - every refusal returns 400 without freeing the GPU
  - `off` is accepted for SDXL
  - the env var is not judged at the route
  - the family flag
  - the status fold
  - the trainer emitting the event
`test_differential.py` against b57c06fcb8: DISCRIMINATING, 3 FIXED + 15
NEW_API, head_fail 0.
- Existing suites (`test_diffusion_training.py`,
`test_diffusion_block_swap.py`, `test_diffusion_base_precision.py`,
`test_diffusion_dit_trainer.py`, checkpoint resume, samples, LTX-2): all
pass.
- `studio/frontend/tests/diffusion-train-block-swap.test.ts` covers when
the control shows, the payload, the status line and the panel wiring.
The full `npm test` passes (16915 tests, 0 failures), and so does `npm
run build`.

## GPU check (Colab L4, 22.5 GiB, standing in for a 24 GB card)

Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, bf16 base, 512 px, rank 16, 50 steps, seed 0. Each arm
ran in a fresh process, interleaved off / N / auto / N / off, plus one
more repeat of each. The request went through
`DiffusionTrainingStartRequest` and the route preflight, using the
host's real GPU facts. The status came from the service's event fold.

| arm (request `block_swap`) | runs | steady s/step, median [range of
run medians] | peak alloc GiB | loop host RSS GiB | status `block_swap`
| mean abs dloss vs off_1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

0.00031-0.00032 |

Notes on the results:
- At this size Wan 5B fits on the L4. So `auto` swaps nothing and runs

- A forced N=10 frees 3.5 GiB of peak allocation and costs about 3x per

Studio: image and video loads read the cache only under HF_HUB_OFFLINE (#18628)

With `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` and every file in the Hugging Face cache, image
and video loads still failed. An outside benchmark saw this in
`load-progress`: `Cannot reach
https://huggingface.co/api/models/unsloth/flux-3-image-klein-base-FP8/revision/main:
offline mode is enabled`.

`begin_load` passed the request's `local_files_only` (False) straight
through, so the load path kept asking the Hub:

- the planner listed the FP8 mirror (`model_info`) and read the FLUX.3
pipeline index (`get_hf_file_metadata`);
- the pipeline build then ran with `local_files_only=False`;
- the loaders' own revision and `model_info` lookups raise
`OfflineModeIsEnabled`, which is a `ConnectionError`, and that failed
the load.

A probe on main ran the background load with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, an
empty cache and every Hub API call recorded. The pipeline build got
`local_files_only=False` and the load made these calls:

- FLUX.3 Klein: 3 calls (FP8 mirror `model_info`,
`_flux3_pipeline_index`, `diffusion_flux3._read_index`).
- Wan2.2 TI2V 5B: 3 calls (FP8 mirror `model_info`, then `repo_info` and
`model_info` from `load_pipeline`).

## Change

- New `hub_reachability.offline_mode()`: True when the user or operator
set `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` or `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE`, or
`huggingface_hub.constants.HF_HUB_OFFLINE` is on. Another thread's short
`force_hf_offline` window (an offline-first config resolve, a llama.cpp
load) does not count: `utils.utils.hf_user_offline()` reads the values
saved before that window, so a load that starts inside one is not
cache-only for its whole run.
- `DiffusionBackend.begin_load` and `VideoBackend.begin_load` treat
offline mode as `local_files_only=True`. That is the cache-only mode
Studio already uses for API-initiated loads, so every planner probe and
loader resolves from the cache. A file that really is missing now fails
as "not in the local cache" instead of with a Hub error.

Online loads are unchanged.

## Tests

`tests/test_media_load_hub_offline.py`, CPU only, with every `HfApi`
metadata call and `get_hf_file_metadata` patched to record and raise,
and the pipeline build stubbed:

- `test_hf_hub_offline_load_asks_the_hub_nothing[image klein, image
klein-base, video Wan2.2 TI2V 5B]`: the build gets
`local_files_only=True` and the load makes no Hub calls. On main the
build gets False and the Hub is asked.
- `test_transformers_offline_and_the_hub_constant_count_too`,
`test_online_loads_keep_their_flag`.
-
`test_another_threads_force_offline_window_does_not_make_a_load_cache_only`.

`test_differential.py` (base `2c21acdc79`, head `15566f037c`):
DISCRIMINATING, head_fail=0.

Regression run (`test_diffusion_backend.py`, `test_video_backend.py`,
`test_diffusion_offline_source.py`,
`test_offline_local_cache_discovery.py`,
`test_diffusion_prequant_cache.py`, `test_diffusion_routes.py`,
`test_video_routes.py`): 1718 passed, 2 skipped and 1 failed on both
base and head. The failing ID is the same on both,
`test_diffusion_backend.py::test_mirrored_base_still_trips_the_flux2_shape_guard`,

## Not proven here

The real pipeline build was only run against an empty cache, where it
makes no Hub call before it fails as not cached. A full offline load
