GRPO tools: trim TRL's dummy tool-call prefix at EOS only when whitespace follows (#18612)

## Summary

GRPO with `tools=` on an `unsloth/gemma-4-*` tokenizer feeds a fake,
empty-argument tool call back into every tool round. This PR fixes that.

TRL's tool loop (`GRPOTrainer._tool_call_loop`, TRL 1.14 through main)
never re-renders the conversation. It appends a suffix to the sampled
ids, and `_get_tool_suffix_ids` derives that suffix from a dummy
conversation: it renders `[user, assistant(tool_call)]`, trims the
render at its **last EOS**, and slices off what the render with the tool
results adds after that point. The trim exists for Qwen-style turns,
where `<|im_end|>\n` should end at `<|im_end|>`.

The Gemma 4 case breaks this:

| tokenizer | `eos_token` | a tool call turn ends with | last EOS in the
dummy prefix | suffix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `google/gemma-4-*` | `<eos>` | `<\|tool_response>` | none, no trim |
correct |
| `unsloth/gemma-4-*` | `<turn\|>` | `<\|tool_response>` | end of the
**user** turn |
`\n<\|turn>model\n<\|tool_call>call:get_weather{}<tool_call\|><\|tool_response>response:...`
|

On `unsloth/gemma-4-*`, everything after the sampled `<|tool_response>`
starts with a second model turn containing the dummy call
`call:get_weather{}`. That text becomes part of the next rollout's
prompt and of the training sequence. Unsloth's own
`get_chat_template(tokenizer, "gemma-4")` also maps EOS to `<turn|>`, so
it is affected as well. TRL masks the suffix out of the loss, but the
corrupted context still conditions every later turn and every logprob
after it.

## Fix

This adds a source edit on `_get_tool_suffix_ids` for `GRPOTrainer` and
`DistillationTrainer` (same code in both). It keeps TRL's trim only when
nothing but whitespace follows the last EOS. That covers `<|im_end|>\n`
and is a no-op when the EOS is the last token. Every other template
behaves as before. TRL versions without this function are untouched,
since the regex then does not match.

## Evidence

**Template sweep, CPU.** For each tokenizer and template, a real
two-round tool conversation is run through TRL's exact
`_get_tool_suffix_ids` (and TRL's training-template swap). Each suffix
is compared with what the template itself renders after the sampled tool
call, i.e. after the first generation stop token from
`generation_config.eos_token_id`. Run on TRL 1.15.0 (the pin ceiling)
and TRL main.

| template | TRL trim | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it`, `unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it`,
`unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (native) | MISMATCH | OK |
| Unsloth `gemma-4`, `gemma-4-thinking` (`chat_templates.py`) | MISMATCH
| OK |
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` | OK | OK |
| Qwen3-0.6B (TRL training template), Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B,
Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, gpt-oss-20b,
Ministral-3-3B, SmolLM2-135M-Instruct | OK | OK |
| Unsloth `qwen-2.5`, `llama-3.1`, `phi-3`, `gpt-oss` | OK | OK |

**Tests.** `tests/test_grpo_tool_suffix_trim.py` runs on CPU with no
downloads. It runs TRL's function body, before and after the edit,
against toy chatml and Gemma 4 tokenizers. It also checks that the edit
still matches the installed TRL's source, read from the file without
importing TRL. On main: 5 failed, 1 passed. On this branch: 8 passed
with TRL 1.15.0 / 1.17.1 / 1.18.0 installed.

**GPU (Colab L4).** The generated
`UnslothGRPOTrainer._get_tool_suffix_ids` was checked with the real
`unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it` tokenizer. On main it returns the suffix
containing the dummy `call:get_weather{}`; with this change it returns
`response:get_weather{...}<tool_response|>`.

## Not covered

- I did not run a full Gemma 4 tool-calling GRPO training run.
- AMD and Windows: no device code changed, so I did not run them there.

Send frozen weights without an adapter to TRL's vLLM engine once, not every sync (#18609)

## Summary

With `fast_inference = False`, GRPO and online DPO send every model
weight to TRL's own vLLM engine on every sync. That includes frozen
weights with no adapter: embeddings, `lm_head`, norms, unadapted
projections and frozen vision towers. These weights never change, so
after the engine has them once there is no need to send them again.

This PR sends those weights on the first sync only. It covers both sync
paths Unsloth owns:

- TRL < 0.28: `_unsloth_vllm_sync_peft_merged` (out-of-place LoRA merge,
colocate and server).
- TRL >= 0.28: `_unsloth_vllm_sync_colocate`, called from the patched
`VLLMGeneration.sync_weights`. This covers both PEFT and dense models
with frozen parts, for example a full fine-tune with a frozen vision
tower.

## When a weight is still sent

- Every trainable weight and every adapter-bearing base weight. For PEFT
this means everything `merge_adapter` touches, which are always sent.
- A frozen weight that was edited in place. Its `_version` changes, so
it is sent again.
- Any vLLM name whose last sent tensor came from a different parameter.
One case is `modules_to_save`, where the trained copy and
`original_module` share one vLLM name.
- All weights, after the engine drops its weights:
- `llm.sleep(level >= 2)`, which TRL's sleep mode calls after every
generation;
  - `llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights")`;
  - or when the receiver changes (a new vLLM model or `vllm_client`).
- All weights, every sync, when the run is sharded (ZeRO-3 / FSDP).
Those paths are unchanged.

Set `UNSLOTH_VLLM_SYNC_FROZEN_WEIGHTS=1` to restore the full sync every
step.

Not covered:
- Server mode on TRL >= 0.28, where TRL streams a fixed metadata list.
- TRL 0.28 to 1.9 colocate layouts that the bucketed loop patch does not
match.

These paths behave as before.

## Bytes per sync after the first (bf16, computed from the model
configs)

| Model | LoRA targets | Full sync | Per sync after | Saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B | all linear | 1.40 GiB | 0.82 GiB | 41% |
| Qwen3-4B | all linear | 8.22 GiB | 6.77 GiB | 18% |
| Llama-3.2-3B | all linear | 6.72 GiB | 5.25 GiB | 22% |
| Llama-3.1-8B | all linear | 14.96 GiB | 13.00 GiB | 13% |
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B (vision frozen) | all linear | 7.57 GiB | 5.17 GiB | 32%
|
| Llama-3.1-8B | q, v | 14.96 GiB | 1.25 GiB | 92% |

## Measured on an L4 (Colab)

Setup:
- Libraries: unsloth `cf3eb59` + zoo `a515275`, TRL 1.15.0, vLLM 0.29.0.
- Run: Qwen3-1.7B 16-bit LoRA r = 16, GRPO with `use_vllm = True`,
`vllm_mode = "colocate"`, `fast_inference = False`.
- Timing: each arm is a separate process that runs 3 training steps,
then 20 timed `VLLMGeneration.sync_weights()` calls.

| Arm | LoRA targets | sync median | min / max |
|---|---|---|---|
| base run 1 | all linear | 466.9 ms | 464.6 / 474.5 |
| base run 2 (A/A) | all linear | 468.3 ms | 466.8 / 472.3 |
| head run 1 | all linear | 383.5 ms | 382.4 / 389.7 |

All 5 runs logged bitwise identical rewards and grad norms.

AsyncGRPO fast_inference: export vLLM preemptions and engine counters on /metrics (#18605)

## Summary

With `fast_inference=True`, TRL's `AsyncGRPOTrainer` talks to Unsloth's
in-process vLLM server (`unsloth/models/_async_grpo_vllm.py`). TRL's
KV-cap control loop scrapes `/metrics` and logs
`rollout/vllm_preemption_count` from `vllm:num_preemptions_total`, but
the in-process server never exported that line, so the metric always
read 0 under fast_inference even when vLLM was preempting rollouts.

vLLM keeps a per-request count (`Request.num_preemptions`, present in
every V1 release from 0.11.2 to main) but only sums it into the
Prometheus counter when `log_stats` is on, which an in-process `LLM`
leaves off. This PR banks each request's count when the scheduler drops
it (`Scheduler._free_blocks`, the one place a request leaves
`scheduler.requests`), so banked plus live requests is the same
monotonic total `vllm serve` reports. The wrapper is installed once per
scheduler (the engine outlives each trainer's server) and costs one
integer add per finished request; the sum over live requests runs only
when `/metrics` is scraped, on the engine thread, with no device sync.

`/metrics` also now exports the engine thread's existing host-side
counters (`unsloth:async_grpo_*`: finished requests, generated tokens,
engine steps and seconds, max batch, syncs, steps decoded during a
sync). TRL ignores them; they are there for anyone scraping the server.

If the scheduler is unreachable or lacks `_free_blocks`, the preemption
line is omitted (same as before), never a non-monotonic value.

## Tests

`tests/test_async_grpo_fast_inference.py` (CPU, fake engine):
- preemption total stays monotonic across finished requests, and a
second server on the same engine shares one counter
- no line without a countable scheduler
- engine counters exported
- installed vLLM still has the hooks the count reads (source check,
skipped without vLLM)
- TRL's own `_control_loop` (TRL main) reports
`rollout/vllm_preemption_count` deltas 0, 1, 2 from this server

On the merge base the three behaviour tests fail; with this change the
file passes (35 passed, 1 skipped with TRL main on the path).

GPU: one Colab A100 AsyncGRPO run (Qwen3-0.6B, fast_inference) per arm,
base vs head, with a KV-overflowing burst whose preemptions are counted
independently by wrapping the scheduler's own preemption routine.
Results:

| arm | preemptions counted by the scheduler | `/metrics`
`vllm:num_preemptions_total` | TRL `rollout/vllm_preemption_count` |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | 19 | line absent | always 0 |
| head | 50 | 50 (26 after the first burst, +24 in the second) | 24 in
the poll covering the burst during training |

Both arms trained 30 steps (trl 1.18.0, vllm 0.29.0, torch 2.13.0,
transformers 5.23.0). The vLLM hooks used (`Request.num_preemptions`,
`Scheduler._free_blocks` removing the request from `scheduler.requests`)
are present in v0.11.2, v0.12.0, v0.15.1, 0.29.0 and main.

Unsloth Studio video: run Restyle on Apple Silicon, with the VAE on Metal once sd.cpp has IM2COL_3D (#18590)

## Problem

Video Restyle (Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Transfer through stable-diffusion.cpp's
`sd-server`) was refused on every Mac, although the pinned sd.cpp macOS
arm64 prebuilt already carries the Cosmos3 port and runs it on Metal.
The only blocker was the darwin refusal in `hardware_plan`.

Lifting it exposed one real cost: ggml-metal has no `IM2COL_3D`, so the
Wan2.2 VAE's 3D convolutions fall back to a naive direct Metal kernel
that is 4.5-5.3x slower than the CPU (9 frames: encode 70 s / decode 329
s on Metal vs 13 s / 72 s on the CPU).

## Change

- **Sizing** (`video_restyle_setup.py`): a Mac is sized from Metal's
recommended working set, the same budget the MLX image and video paths
plan against, with the existing 42 / 31 GiB bf16 / q8_0 thresholds.
Intel Macs, and x86_64 installs under Rosetta (whose sd.cpp installer
picks the x86_64 prebuilt, which Restyle has not been run on), are
refused with a message saying a native arm64 install on Apple Silicon is
needed. CUDA sizing and its refusal text are unchanged.
- **VAE placement** (`video_restyle.py`): on macOS, `sd-server` gets
`--backend vae=cpu` unless the installed sd.cpp build embeds the
`kernel_im2col_3d` Metal kernel (scanned in `sd-server` and the
`libstable-diffusion` next to it, like the existing Cosmos3 marker scan;
the scan cache is now keyed per marker). A paravirtual GPU keeps its
existing all-CPU pin.
- Setup copy now says Restyle was tested on Linux with an NVIDIA GPU and
on an Apple Silicon Mac.

The VAE check is for unslothai/stable-diffusion.cpp#98, which adds Metal
`IM2COL_3D` and makes the VAE 3.5x faster on Metal than on the CPU. The
current pin (`master-982-0518b34-u27b9ddc`) does not have it, so with
this PR alone a Mac runs the VAE on the CPU; once a prebuilt with #98 is
pinned, the VAE moves to Metal with no further Unsloth Studio change.

## Results (M3 Max 128 GB, macOS 26, 832x480, one GPU job at a time)

| 121 frames, bf16 | end to end | VAE encode | DiT | VAE decode | peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| current pin, VAE on CPU (what this PR runs today) | 24.6 min | 209 s |
200 s | 1055 s | 29.2 GiB Metal + 11.1 GiB CPU |
| sd.cpp with #98, VAE on Metal | 9.4 min | 72 s | 212 s | 264 s | 41.4
GiB Metal |

Both footprints fit the 42 GiB bf16 threshold, which matches the 39.8
GiB CUDA peak it was set from. q8_0 also renders on Metal (14.7 GB of

ROCm: pack hybrid models by default when flash varlen passes its self-check (#18611)

Follow-up to #18313 and #17738.

## Why ROCm was opt-in

#13383 made hybrid packing (Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE, Qwen3-Next, and the
PLE layers from #14011) default-on for CUDA only. At the time
`UNSLOTH_EXPERIMENTAL_HYBRID_PACKING=1` failed closed on gfx1151 because
the boundary-aware causal conv was not allowed on HIP (unsloth-zoo #2503
fixed that), and once it worked, the full attention layers still ran
SDPA over a dense `(T, T)` mask on ROCm, so packing was a wash (#17738).
#18313 moved ROCm packed rows onto torch's flash varlen behind a
one-time self-check, which removes that cost.

## Change

With the variable unset, `_auto_hybrid_device_ok` now also accepts a
ROCm GPU when the #18313 self-check
(`hf_packed_attention._torch_varlen`) passes on that device. The check
runs once per device (about 0.3 s on gfx1151) and is cached. Everything
else is unchanged:

- The same mixer kinds as CUDA (gated delta and PLE), and the existing
exactness probe still runs before any packing.
- A ROCm build whose flash varlen fails the self-check keeps the padded
path, with the reason logged.
- `=0` still turns packing off and `=1` still opts in Mamba2 / split QKV
mixers and other devices.
- CUDA is unchanged.

The opt-in note from #17751 now says the path is "not on by default on
this device" instead of naming CUDA only.

Fake Qwen3.5-4B shaped model (real 4B layer sizes, 4 layers, random
weights), LoRA r=16, `packing = True`, `max_length 2048`, batch 4,

Studio: let the tool output length setting raise MCP results on connections (#18557)

On a llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama or Custom connection, MCP tool results were
cut to 16,000 characters whatever Settings > Chat "Tool output length"
said. Raising it did nothing. Reported in the Discord help thread by an
Unsloth Desktop user reading files with the filesystem MCP server.

This came in with #17553. Since then, the tool loop for connections
works out how much room is left for a tool result and passes it along
with `context_tokens=0`. With that room set, MCP results go through
`_fit_result_to_room`, which calls `_tool_result_char_budget`. That
function sees no window and clamps any raised setting to the 16,000
default. Before #17553 a connection never set that room, so an MCP
result came back whole unless the setting was lowered.

The fix keeps that clamp only when both the window and the room are
unknown. When the room is known, it comes from the server's real window
and already limits the result, so a raised setting can't overflow a
small window: a 40,000-character result with a 4,000-token room is still
cut to fit. Python and Terminal results on a connection use the same
budget and get the same fix. Hosted providers (OpenRouter, Anthropic,
OpenAI, Gemini) never set a room and are unchanged.

Tests in `test_tool_result_limit_setting.py`:
- a raised setting applies to an MCP result on a connection
- a result larger than the room is still cut to fit it
- a lowered setting still lowers the cap
- Python output on a connection follows a raised setting

`test_mcp_results_keep_the_default_where_the_window_is_unknown` asserted
the 16,000 clamp even when the room was known, which is the case this
fixes, so it now asserts that the setting applies.

Tested on a MacBook Pro M5, macOS 26, with unit tests only. The four new
tests fail on main and pass here. The related suites pass (2465 passed,
16 skipped).

Not tested: a real Unsloth Desktop run, a real provider or llama.cpp
connection, and a real MCP server.

Studio chat: stop re-reading a chat after this tab's own writes (#18483)

The open chat polls `/api/chat/revision` every 4 s (#18143) and re-reads
the thread when its counter moves. The counters are bumped by SQLite
triggers on every write to `chat_messages` and `chat_threads`, so
nothing separates this tab's own writes from another device's. Every
finished turn moves the counter (user message, assistant message, the
final sync). The poll holds the change while the reply streams, then
within 4 s of the reply ending `recoverCurrentThread` re-reads the chat
this tab just wrote: a thread GET, the full message list, an IndexedDB
read and two `thread.export()` calls. On a 150 turn chat that list is
about 720 KB, every turn. Renames, title updates and thread settings
saves from this tab do the same. The history counter echoes too, so the
sidebar refreshes a second time.

There is a second source of extra re-reads on other devices.
`_bump_chat_thread_updated_at` ran `UPDATE chat_threads SET updated_at =
MAX(...)` even when the value did not change. AFTER UPDATE triggers fire
on no-op updates, so re-saving an unchanged message list still moved the
counter, and every other open device re-read a chat that had not
changed.

## Change

- `storage/studio_db.py`: `chat_revision_probe(thread_id)` is a context
variable that `upsert_chat_thread`, `update_chat_thread`,
`upsert_chat_message` and `sync_chat_messages` fill. Right after `BEGIN
IMMEDIATE` and right before `COMMIT` they read the thread's and the
whole history's revision. `chat_revision_span` returns the before and
after values only when every probed transaction committed, and committed
back to back. Without a probe (generation runs, research, imports) the
writers behave exactly as before.
- `routes/chat_history.py`: `POST /threads`, `PATCH /threads/{id}`, `PUT
/threads/{id}/messages/{mid}` and `PUT /threads/{id}/messages` return
`X-Unsloth-Chat-Revision: <thread before>,<thread after>,<history
before>,<history after>` on success. A rejected or failed write sends no
header. `main.py` exposes the header for cross-origin clients (Tauri,
tunnels).
- `_bump_chat_thread_updated_at` skips the write when `updated_at` would
not change. Rows whose value does change are written exactly as before.
- `chat-api.ts`: `threadWriteFetch` reads the header and publishes it to
`subscribeOwnChatHistoryWrites` listeners. An older server sends no
header, nothing is published, and the poll re-reads as it does today.
- `remote-history-sync.ts`: `noteOwnWrite` records each own write as a
step `before -> after`. The baseline follows these steps only from the
revision it last saw, so a write from anywhere else leaves a gap and is
still re-read. Steps can arrive out of order or after a poll already saw
the new counter, and they still chain. A poll answer that an own write
overtook while it was in flight is ignored instead of rolling the
baseline back. Own writes only skip the re-read once the open chat has
synced through one successful re-read, because a chat's first baseline
can already count another device's write that the loaded view lacks; so
the first own turn after opening a chat still re-reads once, as `main`
does, and later turns do not. The history baseline works the same way,
so the sidebar refresh fires only for other devices. Re-reads still wait
while a reply runs, and a failed re-read is still retried. That retry
also holds if this tab writes while the re-read is in flight.

Focus, wake and thread-switch recovery, the busy hold, cross-tab
`localStorage` sync and error handling are unchanged.

## Results

Production builds of `main` and this branch. The real
`routes/chat_history.py` runs on a temporary `studio.db`, the rest of
`/api` is stubbed, and Chromium is headless. The chat has 150 turns (306
messages). Each assistant turn has reasoning, two tool calls, six
sources, code, a table and math, so the message list is about 720 KB.
The reply is a fixed 10 ms per frame stream. Counts cover the 14 s after
each reply ends (at least 3 polls). There were 3 runs of 3 turns per
side, `main` and this branch interleaved. Earlier runs that were not
interleaved (2 more on `main`, 3 more on this branch) gave the same
counts.

| per own turn, after the reply | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /threads/{id}` | 1 | 0 |
| `GET /threads/{id}/messages` (full list) | 1 (722 KB) | 0 |
| chat API bytes received | 727.6 KB | 4.5 KB |
| `POST /sidebar/rows` | 4 | 2 |
| `GET /threads/{id}/forks` | 2 | 1 |
| thread remounted / scroll moved | no | no |

The re-read never remounted the thread: every mounted row survived, and
the distance to the bottom did not change, on both sides. Main-thread
time over the same window was 163 ms median on `main` (126 to 263) and
112 ms on this branch (62 to 172). On this shared host the repeated
`main` runs alone spread from 134 to 208 ms, and idle 14 s windows from
46 to 106 ms, so no time saving is claimed. In the page, the network
part of one re-read costs 2.9 ms to read the body and 1.8 ms to parse it
and build the per-message keys (median of 15). The IndexedDB read, the
two exports and the reconcile pass come on top of that.

Two clients on one backend, same thread:

| check | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tab B sends a turn while A is idle: A shows it, separate browser

fix(studio): open MLX Run settings in the model picker instead of the Hub (#18562)

## Problem

In the composer model picker, Run settings on an MLX model (the gear, or
Run settings in the row menu) was slow and often sent the user to the
model hub instead of opening the Run settings panel. GGUF models were
not affected.

Measured against a running Unsloth Studio, before this change:

| Row | Variant listing Run settings waited on | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Cached `mlx-community/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-4bit` | 500 "Failed to
list GGUF variants: timed out" after 5.6 s | Redirect to the model hub |
| Cached `mlx-community/LFM2.5-2.6B-8bit` | 200 with `variants: []`
after 5.6 s | Panel, after 5.6 s |
| Discover `mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit` | 200 with `variants: []` |
Redirect to the model hub |

## Root cause

`settingsMeta` awaited `rowQuants(quantTarget(row))` before opening the
panel. For a cached MLX row that target is `remote: true, everyQuant:
true`, the listing a pick uses so it can download a missing precision
folder, so every click waited on a Hub listing. `openSettings` turns any
failure into `null`, and `null` hands off to `/hub`. An empty listing on
a Discover MLX row also returned `null`. The pick path (`pickQuantRow`,
`toggleOffer`) already falls back to whole-checkpoint metadata for MLX
repos; Run settings did not.

## Change

All in `settingsMeta` (`composer-model-picker.tsx`):

- A complete cached MLX row first asks for the offline listing. With no
precision folder on disk (a plain snapshot, the common `mlx-community/*`
case) it opens as one checkpoint (`cachedMeta`) with no Hub listing.
- A cached repo that does have precision folders on disk, and a partial
cached row, keep the pick's original listing, so Run settings opens the
precision a pick of the same row loads.
- Discover MLX rows list every precision, as `toggleOffer` does.
- For MLX repos (the same predicate `toggleOffer` uses), a failed or
folder-less listing yields the whole-checkpoint metadata (`cachedMeta`,
or `wholeHubMeta` for Discover rows), matching the pick's failure paths,
instead of handing off to the hub.

GGUF rows and every other row kind are unchanged.

## Known limitations

- A cached precision-folder repo whose root checkpoint alone was
downloaded configures the root checkpoint, which is what is on disk.
- On a managed account without a Hugging Face token, a refused offline
cache read returns the same 404 as a plain snapshot, so a
precision-folder repo configures its root. Telling these apart needs the
Hub round trip this change removes for every plain MLX snapshot.

## Validation

Live, against Unsloth Studio built from this branch:

| Row | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Cached plain MLX (`mlx-community/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-4bit`) | 5.6 s,
then a hub redirect on timeout | Panel in about 20 ms (offline listing,
23 ms) |
| Discover MLX (`mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit`) | Hub redirect | Panel
in about 0.3–1 s |

```bash
cd studio/frontend
node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/composer-model-picker.test.ts   # 95 pass
npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit
npm run build
```

The new test in `tests/composer-model-picker.test.ts` fails under each
of 12 targeted mutations of the change: the disk shortcut, the partial
gate, the every-precision target, the MLX predicate, the failure
fallback, and the returned metadata. The offline precision-folder
listing this relies on is covered by the existing backend test
`test_offline_lists_a_cached_precision_folder`. No precision-folder MLX
repo was available locally to exercise that path live.

[Bug] Unsloth Desktop: pinned sidebar glass haloes the logo on WebKitGTK before 2.54 (TextureMapper backdrop includes later layers) (#18600)

## What it fixes

On Linux with WebKitGTK older than 2.54 (Mint 22.1 ships 2.52.6), with
Glass on and the sidebar pinned, the unsloth logo at the top of the
sidebar sits in a soft halo tinted by the logo. Tester's 2.54.2 doesn't
show it.

## Why it happens

The pinned strip's glass is a `backdrop-filter` on
`[data-windows-glass-frame]::before`, with the sidebar's content painted
over it. Before 2.54, WebKitGTK composites with TextureMapper, and
TextureMapper's backdrop includes layers painted *after* the filtered
one. So the strip blurs the logo that sits on top of it, and the blurred
copy shows around the logo. 2.54 replaced TextureMapper with a Skia
compositor ([2.54
highlights](https://webkitgtk.org/2026/09/16/webkitgtk-2.54-highlights.html)).
The closest WebKit change I found is
[WebKit/WebKit#75441](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/pull/75441) (bug
325847, 322384@main, Oct 1 2026), which stops a backdrop paint from
including layers that come after the owning layer. I haven't confirmed
which 2.54.x first carries it, and 2.54.0 / 2.54.1 were not run.

A surface's own `backdrop-filter` leaves its children out. So on the old
compositor, `sidebar-inner` blurs for itself over the strip and carries
the strip's fill, and the logo no longer feeds the blur under it.

## What decides when the rule applies

The first commit (ce8a9af87f) keyed the rule on `webkit-cpu-paint`. That
class comes from `paints_on_cpu` in `src-tauri/src/linux_webkit.rs`.
It's true when the GPU setting is Off or the unsafe flag is set, when
WebKitGTK is older than 2.54 (`(major, minor) < (2, 54)`, because before
2.54 it paints on the CPU on every path), or, from 2.54 on, when
`WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER`, `WEBKIT_SKIA_ENABLE_CPU_RENDERING` or
`WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE` is set.

Tester (2.54.2) with `WEBKIT_SKIA_ENABLE_CPU_RENDERING=1` paints on the
CPU (`cpu_painting=true` in the log) and shows **no** halo on main. So
the bug follows the compositor, not CPU painting, and the CPU gate would
have changed the look on 2.54 CPU paths for nothing. 112a048620 moves
the gate to a new `legacy_compositor(webkit_version)` (`< 2.54.0`). It
goes out on the GPU rendering status as `legacyCompositor`, `main.tsx`
adds `webkit-legacy-compositor`, and the CSS rule keys on that class. On
2.52 and older both classes are set, so Mint behaves exactly as with the
first commit.

Tradeoff: on WebKitGTK < 2.54 only, the sidebar's own blur and the
strip's blur meet inside the 34px titlebar band, so a faint seam can
show there.

Studio MLX: cut the prompt cache's in-turn memory (own the cached prefix, capture at mlx-vlm's hook) (#18578)

## Summary

Reduces the memory Unsloth Studio's MLX prompt cache costs during a
turn, mainly on the mlx-vlm route that most new models load through,
without changing what the cache reuses, the prefill schedule, or decode
speed. Four commits, each self-contained:

1. **Free a resumed VLM turn's live cache without the cycle collector.**
A reference cycle kept the finished turn's whole live KV alive until a
generation-2 GC on every reused VLM turn (0.3 GiB at 9K tokens on
Qwen2.5-VL-3B, 2.9 GiB at 20K on Molmo2-8B).
2. **Capture VLM snapshots at mlx-vlm's `generate_step` checkpoint hook
instead of swapping the model's class.** The class swap broke
class-keyed dispatch, so with the cache on and MTP drafting on (the
default for Qwen3.5) greedy output diverged from cache-off already on
the first turn. Captures now happen at the hook mlx-vlm exposes, at the
same checkpoint lengths, so forwards keep their shapes. On an mlx-vlm
without the hook the previous recorder stays (drafting off only).
3. **Hand the text route's cached prefix to a single stream instead of
deep-copying it.** On the single-stream text path a stored strict-prefix
hit is lent to the request and its slot (LRU position, charge, spare
rows) is restored exactly at turn end, on Stop, or on error. Batch rows
keep the copy.
4. **Let a single VLM request own its cached prefix instead of copying
it.** The served conversation's stored entries become skeletons while
the turn runs; at the end the turn publishes exact copies of the rows
its final cache still holds, and shorter boundaries of the same
conversation re-share those rows. Each entry is charged its exact
allocation. The store's eviction keeps the boundaries the next turn
needs (a replay that would evict its own conversation's shorter entry is
held instead). Batched rows, nested cache layouts, layouts with no
movable layer, expert-offloaded loads and the no-hook recorder keep the
copy path unchanged.

## Impact

Decode-phase memory above the weights, per turn of a three-turn
~6K-token chat, main vs this branch (M3 Max; cached tokens identical):

| model | main (GiB) | this branch (GiB) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B 4-bit | 0.683 / 0.676 / 0.713 | 0.260 / 0.240 / 0.253 |
| Qwen3.5-4B 4-bit | 0.799 / 0.861 / 0.766 | 0.416 / 0.415 / 0.296 |
| Gemma 4 E2B 4-bit | 0.280 / 0.153 / 0.172 | 0.208 / 0.065 / 0.073 |

Turn peaks are lower or equal. Reuse is unchanged per request on linear
chats (next turn, regenerate, last-message edit) and equal or higher in
total on mixed histories.

## Validation

- `studio/backend/tests/test_mlx_vlm_prompt_cache.py` (67, real MLX),
`test_mlx_inference_backend.py` and `test_multi_model_primary_fit.py`:
all pass after rebasing on current main (626 + 67).
- Added tests were mutation-checked (each stage's guarded behaviours
fail their test when broken).
- Parity, cache on vs off: replies equal on every drafting-off turn
across Qwen2.5-VL-3B (text and image), Qwen3.5-4B (presence penalty,
JSON format), Gemma 4 E2B (short chats, regenerate, image) and
GLM-4.6V-Flash (image), plus KV-8 and TurboQuant-4 loads. With MTP
drafting on, Qwen3.5 now matches cache-off. The only drafting-on
difference (Gemma 4 E2B, a turn with nothing reused) also occurs between
two identical cache-off runs, i.e. drafter non-determinism.
- Prefill chunk boundaries are identical to main on every measured turn.
- Performance, main vs branch, interleaved `--stable` runs: TTFT
0.98-1.00x, decode 0.99-1.02x (Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma 4 E2B regenerate on
the final commits; Qwen2.5-VL-3B edit and Qwen3.5-4B with MTP drafting
on an earlier revision of commit 4, whose later changes only narrowed
which loads take the new path).
- A fake-cache harness replayed thousands of random histories against
main at fixed and random budgets: no stored entry aliases the live
cache, no resident bytes go uncharged, and the store stays within its
budget plus the held slot.

## Risks / not changed

- The cache budget (a flat 15% of the recommended working set, reserved
by auto-fit and admission) is unchanged. It is the right ceiling for a
store of full-context conversations at the native context, but
over-reserves for loads pinned to a short context; sizing it per model
interacts with the drafter fit, the offload planner and admission, so it
is left for a follow-up. `cache_ram` / `UNSLOTH_MLX_PROMPT_CACHE_BYTES`
still override it.
- VLM reuse still stops at the last 2048-token checkpoint and does not
bank reply KV (bitwise cache-independent output is kept).
- Commit 4 relies on mlx-vlm's `generate_step` checkpoint hook; older
mlx-vlm keeps the copy path.
- Batched rows: this PR keeps them on the copy path. Their extra memory
came from a reference cycle in unsloth-zoo's resumed batch row, fixed
separately in unslothai/unsloth-zoo#2627 with no Unsloth Studio change
needed. With both, the memory left after a batched turn equals the
prompt-cache charge, and decode with two rows on Qwen2.5-VL-3B drops
from 1.42-1.99 to 0.95-1.01 GiB above the weights.

Studio: keep the MCP tool list fixed per chat and add each message's matches as a search (#18529) Closes #17015. Also reported on [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/unsloth/comments/1xr5e7o/prompt_processing_is_triggered_almost_every_prompt/), still present after #17326. ## Problem When the MCP tools are too large to list in full, Studio lists `mcp_tool_search` plus up to 5 tools ranked against the newest message, and replaces them when a message's best match is not listed. #17326 fixed their order, but which tools are listed still changes with almost every topic, even for messages that need no tool ("What is 3+4?"). The tool list is at the start of the prompt, so any change there makes llama-server process the whole conversation again. Hybrid models (Qwen3.5 and later) and sliding-window models (Gemma) also lose the system prompt before it, so they process the entire prompt. ## Change - A chat keeps the MCP tools its first request listed. - On later messages, the tools that match the message and are not listed are added after it as an `mcp_tool_search` call and result, the same way the knowledge-base auto-search works. The UI shows it as a search card and keeps it in history. The model can call those tools directly. - Tools the chat ran, and tools an earlier search in the chat returned, stay callable. - The tool list keeps the existing preload share of the context (33%), and the added search has its own 15%, so a list that fills its share still leaves room for a later topic's tools. The list is fitted again only when it no longer fits, for example after a reload with a smaller context or a schema update. ## Results Qwen3.6-27B Q6_K, 64K context, 8-message chats with 6 tool lookups: | MCP tools | main: full re-processes | main: tokens processed | this PR: full re-processes | this PR: tokens processed | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 servers x 24 tools | 6 of 7 | 28,846 | 0 | 4,787 | | One 346-tool server | 6 of 7 | 38,804 | 0 | 4,898 | Prompt processing time for the first chat went from 17.1 s to 7.0 s. With the 4 servers, the model called the right tool first on all 6 lookups (main: 5 of 6), for both Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3-4B. Ranked tools are still sent with each message because small models rarely search: with a fixed list alone, Qwen3-4B found 0 of 6 tools. A document lookup on main and on this PR. Studio adds the matching tools as a search card, and the model calls the same tool directly on both sides. ## Notes - Unchanged: requests without a thread id (API clients), `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_MCP_SEARCH_ONLY=1`, and catalogs that fit the window. - The search is not added for `tool_choice: none`, a forced tool, or a resumed reply. - The search cards stay in the chat, so the prompt grows by up to 5 schemas per message. ## Tests - New tests, all failing on main: incidental wording keeps the tool block byte-identical; a later lookup adds the search after the message; the tool loop accepts the matched tools; the GGUF and safetensors loops add and skip the search correctly. - Listing tests that described the old replacement now describe the fixed list. - Further tests cover a smaller context, a schema that grows, large schemas that fill the list's share, a resumed reply, a "yes" after a clarifying question, and a tool the chat ran staying callable after several topic changes. - MCP, tool-loop, permission, passthrough, compaction, skills and token-count suites pass. --------- Co-authored-by: Daniel Han <23090290+danielhanchen@users.noreply.github.com>

Studio diffusion: report per-render engagement (untiled vs tiled VAE decodes, FBCache computed vs skipped steps) (#18606)

The untiled-when-fits video VAE decode shows up in `speed_optims` as
`vae_untiled_when_fits` once it is installed, but nothing reported
whether a given clip actually decoded untiled, fell back to tiles, took
the wide tiles or recovered from an OOM. The wrapper kept those
counters, but nothing read them. First-Block-Cache kept no count of
skipped evaluations at all, so a cache could be reported as engaged
while it skipped nothing. Static step skip already reports its counts.

## Change

- `video_vae_untiled`: the wrapper's counters are also reachable as
`vae._unsloth_untiled_stats`, plus `untiled_decode_stats(pipe)` (a copy)
and `decode_stats_delta(before, after)`.
- `diffusion_cache.install_fbcache_counter()` (installed by
`apply_step_cache` just before `enable_cache`): wraps
`FBCHeadBlockHook._should_compute_remaining_blocks` and counts each
decision on the head hook. diffusers already decides on the host
(`.item()` returns a Python bool), so the count is a dict increment with
no extra sync. It runs under `torch.compiler.disable` like the decision
itself, so it adds no graph break. A decision that is not a bool is not
coerced, and the counter carries the length guard's marker (and the
length guard carries the counter's), so neither installs twice.
`fbcache_counts(pipe, reset=)` sums over `transformer` /
`transformer_2`.
- Per render: the video backend snapshots the VAE counters and resets
the FBCache counters before the denoise. After it, it logs
`video.engagement: vae_decode={...} fbcache={...}`. The image backend
logs `diffusion.engagement: fbcache={...}`. The last render's record is
held in a weak map beside the pipe, never written onto it, and status
reports it as `render_engagement` (new optional field on both status

Studio: keep every tab signed in when a refresh answer is lost (#18353)

Every open Unsloth Studio tab could still sign out at once when the
answer to a successful session refresh never reached the browser. With
this change the session survives that.

## What was wrong

Refresh tokens are single-use. When `/api/auth/refresh` rotates a token,
the server deletes the old one and returns a new pair. If that answer is
lost on the way back, the browser keeps the old token, which is already
gone on the server:

- a tab is closed or reloaded while the refresh is in flight
- a reverse proxy times out the request after the server committed
- a phone or tablet suspends the page mid-request

The next refresh sends the spent token, gets a 401, and the client
clears the tokens in shared storage. That signs out every tab on that
browser.

#16468 (Web Locks) and #16755 (plain-HTTP peer wait) fixed the two-tab
race reported on Discord. This lost-answer case is the one path that
still ends the session.

## The fix

A token rotated by `/api/auth/refresh` stays exchangeable for 60 seconds
(`REFRESH_REUSE_GRACE_SECONDS`). Presenting it again in that window
rotates once more and returns a fresh pair instead of a 401. This makes
a retried refresh idempotent, the same idea as Supabase's refresh token
reuse interval and Okta's grace period.

- **Revocation is unchanged.** Logout, password changes, account revokes
and renames delete the grace rows in the same transaction as the live
tokens. All five call sites go through one helper,
`_delete_refresh_rows`. A password change is also caught by the existing
credential generation check.
- **Downgrade safe.** The grace rows live in a new `refresh_token_reuse`
table, and the spent token is still deleted from `refresh_tokens`. An
older build never reads the new table, so it cannot revive a spent
token.
- **Bounded.** One spent token mints at most `REFRESH_REUSE_MAX` (8)
pairs inside the window; later replays get a 401, which the client
already answers from a peer's stored pair.
- **Only stamped tokens get the window.** A token without a credential
generation stamp (legacy rows from before that column existed) stays
strictly single-use, so every reuse row is voided by any credential
change, including the CLI password reset that rotates the secret with
its own SQL.
- **Scope.** Only the rotation path opts in. `consume_refresh_token`
stays strictly single-use, and expired rows and rows older than the
window are purged on every rotation.
- **Frontend.** Without Web Locks (plain HTTP), two tabs racing on one
token now both get a 200. A tab whose own 200 lands after a peer already
stored a pair now reuses the peer's pair through the existing
`peerRotated` check, as the 401 path already did, instead of handing its
caller the original 401.

No new UI: the only visible change is that the tabs stay signed in.
Desktop, which runs on a secure origin with Web Locks, follows the same
path as before.

401 |

Studio installer: skip the int8 GEMM torch probe where no wheel is published (#18476)

`_ensure_int8_gemm` in `studio/install_python_stack.py` runs on every
Studio setup and update. Whenever the int8 GEMM wheel is not installed,
it calls `probe_torch_wheel_env(include_windows = True)`, which starts a
child Python that imports torch. Then `int8_gemm_wheel_url(env)` returns
None unless the platform tag is in `_I8GEMM_PLATFORMS` (`linux_x86_64`,
`win_amd64`). On Linux aarch64 (DGX Spark, GH200) and Windows ARM64 no
wheel is published, so the wheel is never installed and every run
imports torch for a result it throws away. That is about 1.2 s on the
x86_64 Linux host measured below, and usually more on Windows. The step
often runs right after `_ensure_flash_attn`, which has already done the
same probe.

The probe also had no timeout. `_ensure_flash_attn` limits the same
probe on Windows with `_FLASH_ATTN_IMPORT_PROBE_TIMEOUT` so a wedged
driver cannot hang setup.

## Change

- `backend/utils/wheel_utils.py`: new `int8_gemm_platform_supported()`,
which returns `wheel_platform_tag() in _I8GEMM_PLATFORMS`. The probe
builds `env["platform_tag"]` from the same `wheel_platform_tag()` and
the URL resolver checks the same table, so this is the resolver's own
platform check, done without torch.
- `install_python_stack.py`: `_ensure_int8_gemm` returns before probing
when the platform has no wheel. On Windows the probe now gets
`_FLASH_ATTN_IMPORT_PROBE_TIMEOUT`, the same as the flash-attn step. A
probe that times out returns None, and the optional wheel is skipped, as
it was already for any failed probe. Linux keeps no timeout, as in the
flash-attn step.

Not changed: reusing the flash-attn probe result. Between the two steps,
the ROCm flash-attn path runs a pip install with dependencies, so torch
is not guaranteed to be the same. The flash-attn step also skips its
probe when flash-attn already imports.

Studio: render the export log in its own memoized list with stable row keys (#18485)

`ExportRunPanel` subscribed to `logLines` together with the rest of the
run state and the 1 s elapsed tick, so every log line re-rendered the
whole panel. Each render mapped up to 4,000 rows keyed by index and ran
`getExportLogLineClass` (three warning regexes) and `formatLogLine` on
every row. Once the log reached its 4,000 line cap, `appendLog` sliced
off the head, every index shifted by one, and React rewrote the text of
all 4,000 rows. The follow-tail effect then read `scrollHeight`, which
forced a layout of the whole list. `llama-quantize` and the converters
print one line per tensor, so a multi-quant or MoE GGUF export passes
the cap early, and from then on the panel kept the main thread close to
100% busy for as long as the export ran.

## Change

- `stores/export-runtime-store.ts`: new `logBase`, the number of lines
trimmed off the head in this run (reset by `runExport` and `reset`). Row
`i` is absolute line `logBase + i`, so a trim removes head rows instead
of renumbering the rest. `appendLog`, the new `appendLogBatch` and the
poll path `appendLogs` share one trim helper. `appendLogBatch` applies
`appendLog`'s rules to each event in order (skip a numbered event at or
below `lastSeq`, unnumbered events always append, a `status` line sets
the stage), all in one store update.
- `hooks/use-export-runtime-lifecycle.ts`: the SSE parser handles all
the frames of one network chunk synchronously. Their log events are now
queued and flushed once in a microtask through `appendLogBatch`, so a
chunk costs one store update instead of one per line. The poll path is
unchanged.
- `components/export-run-panel.tsx`: the log box moves into
`ExportLogBox`, which subscribes to `logLines` and `logBase` only, and
the follow-tail effect and the 24 px scroll rule move with it. The panel
now reads only whether any log exists. `followTail` stays in the panel
so it lasts as long as it did before. Rows (`ExportLogRow`) are memoized
on the entry object, and rows are grouped into memoized blocks of 100
absolute lines (`groupExportLogLines` in `lib/log-style.ts`). An append
re-renders only the last block, and a trim only the first. Row text,
classes and order are unchanged. Each block is a plain `<div>` with no
class.
- Once lines have been trimmed, the box sets `overflow-anchor: none`.
Removing head rows would otherwise let the browser's scroll anchoring
move a scrolled-up view along with its lines. The old in-place rewrite
kept the scroll offset, and so does this.

Studio: remember a found GPU when resolving the embedding backend (#18478)

Opening the Settings General or Data tab calls `GET
/api/settings/embedding-model/resolve` for the effective embedding model
(`documents-rag-section.tsx`). The default `unsloth/bge-small-en-v1.5`
has no stored backend, so with no embedder loaded the plan reaches
`_resident_hardware_choice` and then `_resolve_auto`. That calls
`LlamaCppBackend._get_gpu_free_memory()`, which runs `nvidia-smi
--query-gpu=index,memory.free,...` on every call. The read is never
cached because free memory counts as a critical field. On ROCm or other
hosts it goes to amd-smi or torch instead. `_resolve_auto` only checks
whether a GPU is present, yet each tab open pays for a fresh spawn. The
cached answer from #10390 only applies once an embedder is loaded.

## Change

- `core/rag/embeddings.py`: when the `_resolve_auto` probe finds a GPU,
the answer is kept under a key made of the probe function, the
llama-server binary path plus its stat identity (device, inode, size,
mtime), and the full process environment. A later call with the same key
skips the spawn.
- The probe and the llama-server fallback reuse the binary path the key
already looked up, so a miss does one llama-server lookup instead of two
(about 4.5 ms each here).
- An empty or failed probe is never kept, so a host without a GPU, or a
probe that timed out, is asked again next time, as before.
- `_reset_backend` and `release_backend` drop the kept answer, so
unloading the embedder starts fresh.
- Nothing else changes: a stored backend, a local GGUF, a `-GGUF` repo
name and an explicit `RAG_EMBED_BACKEND` still answer before the probe,
and the loaded-embedder path from #10390 is untouched.

call (imports, static `-L` read) is excluded, so each row is the median
of the 5 warm calls with min to max in brackets. Spawns were counted
with a wrapper `nvidia-smi` on `PATH`. The stub sleeps 150 ms and
reports one GPU, and "fast CLI" is a host whose `nvidia-smi` answers in
a few ms. `main` was run twice as an A/A.

searched from Appearance, still asserted to land in the Chat tab under

reads that constant (via `ast`, without importing Playwright) and checks

Studio diffusion training: offer mxfp8 on sm100 / sm103 only, not sm120 (#18608)

The Train tab offers `base_precision='mxfp8'` on every CUDA card at
sm100 or newer, so an RTX PRO 6000 or RTX 50 (sm120) lists it next to
frozen `fp8`. Measured on a Colab G4 (RTX PRO 6000, sm120, torch 2.14.1
+ torchao 0.18.0, Studio installed from main): mxfp8 does engage there,
but frozen fp8 is faster at both sizes and also halves the stored base
weights, and mxfp8 is slower than plain bf16 at 512 px.

## Measurements

FLUX.2 klein base 4B LoRA (rank 16, tarot set, 50 steps, seed 0,
regional compile on), one process per arm, run order mxfp8, bf16, fp8,
fp8, bf16, mxfp8. Steady s/step is the median over steps 3-50. Each pair
of runs agrees to within 1.3%.

| res | bf16 | fp8 (frozen) | mxfp8 | mxfp8 vs bf16 | mxfp8 vs fp8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 0.0805 / 0.0809 | 0.0644 / 0.0648 | 0.0871 / 0.0882 | 8% slower
| 36% slower |
| 1024 | 0.2632 / 0.2632 | 0.2177 / 0.2178 | 0.2445 / 0.2443 | 7% faster
| 12% slower |

- Engagement: all 100 targeted linears are `MXFP8Linear`, and the
profiler shows `cutlass3x_sm120_bstensorop_..._block_scaled_ue8m0xe4m3`
GEMMs (194 per step). There was no bf16 fallback warning.
- Why it trails: the block-scaled GEMMs are faster than the bf16 ones
(33.8 vs 56.1 ms per step at 512 px), but torchao re-casts the frozen
weight and the activations on every step. `to_mxfp8_dim0_kernel` (294
calls) plus `mxfp8_quantize_kernel` take about 16 ms per step at 512 px
and 23 ms at 1024. Weight storage stays bf16, so the train peak equals
bf16's (11.35 GiB at 512, 18.92 GiB at 1024). Frozen fp8 stores the base
in e4m3 (3.9 vs 7.3 GiB).
- Loss: the mean loss over 50 steps is 0.7077 (bf16), 0.7086 (fp8) and
0.7086 (mxfp8) at 512, and 0.7313, 0.7321 and 0.7322 at 1024. Per-step
curves follow bf16 to the third decimal.

Studio: read the browser cookie jar once per page cookie state (#18470)

`site_cookie_state` runs on every proxied browser navigation (`_fetch`)
and on every relayed same-site request (`_page_request`). It returned
`page_cookies(...)` and `has_site_cookies(...)`, and each of those was a
full pass of `_site_cookies` over the whole account jar: `list(jar)`,
then a new `urllib.request.Request` per cookie and a `return_ok` on it,
for every cookie of every site. All of this holds `jar._cookies_lock`,
so with the jar near its 3,000 cookie cap one call took 40 to 80 ms and
other requests for the same account waited on the lock meanwhile.

`_fetch` also computed this state for non-HTML responses (scripts,
images, JSON, downloads). Only the HTML branch of `_build_response`
reads those fields.

## Change

- `routes/browser_cookies.py`:
- `site_cookie_state` collects `_site_cookies` once, under the same
lock. `has_site` is "the list is non-empty" and the page cookies come
from the same list with the same HttpOnly filter, 64 KiB room cap and
order (`_page_entries`, shared with `page_cookies`).
- `_site_cookies` first drops jar domains that `domain_return_ok` rules
out for the page host (the stdlib's own prefilter, which
`CookieJar._cookies_for_request` runs before `return_ok`), then walks
the rest with `http.cookiejar.deepvalues`, the same walk `list(jar)`
does, so the order is unchanged on every Python version.
- It builds one `Request` per distinct cookie path instead of one per
cookie. `return_ok` only reads the request, so the result is the same.
- `page_cookies` and `has_site_cookies` stay public with unchanged
behaviour.
- `routes/browser.py`: the HTML test from `_build_response` moves into a
shared `_is_html`. `_fetch` still reads the cookie state right after
`store_cookies`, but only when the response is HTML.

## Results

`site_cookie_state` per call, 50 sites, median of 7 repeats of 30 calls,
each arm in a fresh process, run base / PR / this / base / this / PR on
one busy CPU host (so absolute numbers are noisy; the two runs of each
arm are shown).

| cookies | page | main | first version of this PR | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | site with cookies | 3.78 / 4.10 ms | 1.86 / 1.49 ms | 0.43 /
0.19 ms |
| 200 | site without cookies | 6.04 / 5.71 ms | 1.93 / 1.42 ms | 0.30 /
0.13 ms |
| 1,000 | site with cookies | 15.89 / 15.28 ms | 7.63 / 6.49 ms | 0.47 /
0.31 ms |
| 1,000 | site without cookies | 27.77 / 25.04 ms | 10.77 / 6.38 ms |
0.27 / 0.13 ms |
| 3,000 | site with cookies | 43.19 / 51.13 ms | 23.47 / 20.67 ms | 0.39
/ 0.62 ms |
| 3,000 | site without cookies | 76.45 / 79.63 ms | 22.10 / 24.53 ms |
0.22 / 0.17 ms |

Non-HTML responses no longer pay for this call at all.

## Tests

New `tests/test_browser_cookie_state_one_pass.py`:
- 6 seeded random jars (200, 1,000 and 3,000 cookies) mixing Domain= on
the host, a leading dot and a parent domain, host-only cookies,
subdomain pages, IP hosts with and without a port, `localhost`, nested
paths and trailing slashes, Secure on http and https pages, HttpOnly,
expired cookies still in the jar, all SameSite values, values big enough
to hit the 64 KiB room cap, and invalid or non-http page URLs. For every
page, `site_cookie_state` equals the previous two-pass implementation
exactly (order included), and it agrees with `page_cookies` and
`has_site_cookies`.
- One `Request` for the page plus one per distinct path among the page
site's cookies, and only the page `Request` for a site with no cookies
(fails on `main`).

Passes on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13. `test_browser_cookies.py`,

Studio transcribe: keep the engine's speaker for an interruption instead of guessing by overlap (#18537)

## Problem

With the diarizing models (MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize, VibeVoice-ASR),
Transcribe can label an interruption with the speaker who was
interrupted. The wrong label reaches the transcript, the speaker list
and exports, and an interrupter who speaks only once disappears from the
speaker list.

## Root cause

audio.cpp emits `segments` and `speaker_turns` in pairs: segment *i* and
turn *i* share a span and text (`moss_transcribe_diarize/session.cpp`,
`vibevoice_asr/session.cpp`). `stt_details.normalize` ignores the
pairing, and `_assign_speakers` picks the speaker with the most
overlapping time. That ties whenever the other speaker's turns cover a
segment, and `max()` then keeps the speaker listed first:

- an interruption nested in one turn, or covered by two turns that meet
inside it
- two speakers saying the same words on one span

A payload with only `speaker_turns` takes the same path, because its
segments are rebuilt without the speaker.

## Fix

In `normalize`:

- Segments rebuilt from `speaker_turns` keep each turn's speaker.
- When the two arrays line up (same length, and each pair has the same
span and, where the turn has text, the same text), segment *i* takes
turn *i*'s speaker.
- Otherwise `_assign_speakers` runs as before, after first trying a turn
with the segment's exact span that names a single speaker.

Only speaker labels change. Transcripts already saved or exported keep
their old labels.

## Verification

MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize q8_0 ran once per clip, and the old and new
`normalize` received the same model response.

**AMI meeting `ES2002a`**: the first ten minutes of the headset mix, in
one-minute clips, checked against the manual transcript. Each
participant wore a separate microphone. 5 of 150 segments changed
speaker:

| Time | Speech | Old | New | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9:26.17 | D says "Um." while B says "for a remote control" | B | D | D
|
| 9:40.66 | B and D both say "Yeah." | B, B | B, D | B, D |

Of the other three changes, two match the reference speaker but MOSS's
words differ from the reference text, and one at 0:08.62 has no
reference words to score against.


[Recording](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/AMICorpusMirror/amicorpus/ES2002a/audio/)
· [B's microphone at
9:26](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/AMICorpusMirror/amicorpus/ES2002a/audio/ES2002a.Headset-1.wav#t=562,572)
· [D's microphone at
9:26](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/AMICorpusMirror/amicorpus/ES2002a/audio/ES2002a.Headset-3.wav#t=562,572)
· [Manual annotations](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/download/)

**Broadcast recordings**: no label changed on 774 segments.

Studio: overlap the Hub search listings and ask only for rows that are read (#18477)

A typed model search (`mergedModelIterator`, used by the Model hub, the
composer picker, the legacy picker, the export page, the voice tab and
the embedding picker) reads up to 3 rows from the `owner=unsloth`
listing first, then the general listing. The general listing is an async
generator that does not start until it is first read, so its request
only went out after the Unsloth answer arrived. Every debounced search
paid two Hub round trips in a row before the first page of 48 rows could
fill.

Several listings also asked the Hub for 500 fully expanded rows while
reading far fewer:
- the Unsloth pass of a typed search reads 3 rows (for `qwen3` on the
live Hub that answer is 2.52 MB, against 31 KB for 3 rows),
- the trending pool of the Latest sort reads 100 rows per task,
- `fetchChannelFirstPage` (the Model hub feed rows) reads at most
`MAX_RAW_ITEMS_PER_BATCH` (192).

The training picker had a smaller version of the same wait:
`priorityThenListingIterator` waited for all its priority `modelInfo`
lookups (3 at a time) to finish before it requested the listing.

## Change

- `use-hub-model-search.ts`: new `prefetchListing` helper. It requests a
listing's first item right away, one microtask after the listing read
first, so request order stays the same. It hands the listing over later
through `read()`. A rejection is handled at once and thrown again where
`read()` is iterated, which is where the error used to come out.
`cancel()` aborts the listing and closes it. The listing gets its own
`AbortController`, which follows the search's signal.
- `mergedModelIterator` starts the general listing with it. The Unsloth
pass is unchanged: same order, same `seen` dedupe, same cache priming.
If that pass throws or the consumer stops during it, the general listing
is cancelled. A new keystroke aborts both listings through the search's
signal, as before.
- With no client-side filter (`filterPriority`) and no parameter filter,
the Unsloth pass passes `limit` (3 for a typed query) to `listModels`.
The SDK then sends `limit=3` and stops after 3 rows. Phase 1 never read
more than that.
- `priorityThenListingIterator` starts its listing while the priority
lookups finish, and yields in the same order.
- `createChannelIterator` takes an optional `limit`. The fresh trending
pool passes its pool size (`FRESH_POOL` times the task count). Task
listings never share a model, so no single task listing can give more
than the whole pool. The newest listing is read past its pool and stays
unbounded. `fetchChannelFirstPage` passes `MAX_RAW_ITEMS_PER_BATCH` (now
exported), the most `pullBatch` reads. On the Latest sort, this caller
limit is dropped.

A smaller `limit` gives the same rows only if the Hub returns the
leading rows of the same ordering, the same assumption the SDK's own
pagination makes. I checked this on the live Hub for 7 listings (typed
`owner=unsloth` searches sorted by downloads, trending and likes at
limit 3, the trending pool at 100 for everyone and for `unsloth`, and
the two feed channels at 192). Each smaller answer was exactly the first
rows of the 500-row one.

Tests: build fake-CUDA Linear fixtures that run on a CPU-only torch (#18617)

## Summary

`Backend CI / (Python 3.13, diffusion)` is red on `main` with two
failures. #18589 merged with this shard already red, and staging runs on
unrelated PRs show the same failures (e.g. #18473, a frontend-only
change):

```
FAILED tests/test_diffusion_native_w8a8_rdna.py::test_layer_probes_the_card_its_weight_is_on
FAILED tests/test_diffusion_int8_attention.py::test_streamed_weights_on_another_card_are_staged_too
E   RuntimeError: PyTorch is not linked with support for cuda devices
```

## Cause

Both tests were added by #18588 and #18589. The code they cover is
right. The problem is how the tests build their fixtures: they create
`torch.nn.Linear(..., device = "cuda:N")` inside `FakeTensorMode`.
Constructing the layer runs `reset_parameters`, and on the CPU torch
build the shard installs, the fake `uniform_` goes to CUDA's generator
and raises. Moving a fake CUDA tensor that requires grad goes further
and aborts the process on that build. So the tests could only pass on a
CUDA-linked torch.

## Change

Test-only. Each test builds its layer through a small `_fake_linear`
helper:

- the `Linear` is created on `meta`;
- its weight and bias are replaced with uninitialised fake tensors on
the requested card, with `requires_grad = False` (inference weights
carry no grad).

The assertions are unchanged: `cuda:1` is still the card probed, and the
weights still move to the stage card and back.

## Testing

On a CPU-only torch (2.10.0+cpu):

- both tests fail on `main` with the `RuntimeError` above and pass with
this change;
- `test_diffusion_native_w8a8_rdna.py` and
`test_diffusion_int8_attention.py` pass in full.

The guards still catch the bugs they were written for. Reverting the
source fixes from #18588 (`diffusion_native_quant.py`) and #18589
(`diffusion_minimax_h3_image.py`) makes both tests fail on the CPU
build, with `assert [None] == [device(type='cuda', index=1)]` and
`assert device(type='cuda', index=0) == device(type='cuda', index=1)`.
Before this change they could never run there.

Studio Translate: skip repeat Hub listings and OCR past the kept text (#18475)

Two wasted costs on the Translate page:

1. After every translation (and every auto-translate pause), an effect
keyed on `busy` re-lists both Hy-MT2 repos through
`/api/models/gguf-variants` without `offline`, which on the backend is a
live `HfApi.model_info(files_metadata=True)` per repo with no cache. The
result only feeds the "Downloaded" / download size label in the model
menu.
2. Opening a long PDF in Translate runs `/api/rag/extract-text`, which
OCRs up to 20 scanned pages (a vision model at roughly 2 to 10 s per
page, or Tesseract) even when the typed pages before them already exceed
the 50,000 characters Translate keeps. Everything past that point is
thrown away by the page.

## Change

- `translateModelDownloaded` asks the disk first (`localOnly`, the same
listing `pickMine` already trusts). A quant complete on disk never
triggers a Hub listing; otherwise the Hub is asked as before.
- The page's post-run check passes `remote: false` for a model already
known missing, so after the first answer it is re-checked from disk
only. A download made by a run still flips the label, because the disk
listing reports it.
- `/extract-text` takes an optional `max_chars` form field (`ge=1`).
With it, scanned pages are OCR'd in page order and OCR stops before any
page whose preceding joined text already passes `max_chars`. Pages past
that point are dropped from the response (`truncated: true`). Lengths
are counted in code points, which are never more than the UTF-16 units
the page measures, so the page still sees more than 50,000 characters
and shows the same truncation toast. `pdf_ocr.ocr_pages` gains a
keyword-only `until(number, out)` so the Tesseract loop keeps its one
open document and its stop-on-engine-failure behaviour.
- `parsers.render_pdf_pages` loads only the requested pages instead of
walking the whole document, since the capped path renders one page per
call. The PNG bytes are identical; on a 3,000 page PDF with nothing to
skip, rendering 20 scans one by one takes 0.78 s against 0.67 s for one
batch on main (1.47 s without this).
- Only Translate sends `max_chars` (`TRANSLATE_SOURCE_MAX_CHARS`). The
chat composer sends nothing and goes through the unchanged code path.

## Results

Model listings over 5 translations with Hy-MT2 1.8B, Translate page in
Chrome against a production build with the backend mocked, 3 repeats per
arm (counts identical across repeats):

| Scenario | Base: Hub listings | Base: disk listings | Head: Hub
listings | Head: disk listings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Both models on disk | 13 | 0 | 0 | 13 |
| 7B not on disk | 13 | 0 | 1 | 13 |

The single Hub listing in the second row is the first check of the
missing 7B on page open.

`/extract-text` time per request, OCR stubbed to a fixed 0.25 s per
page, median of 3 (spread at most 0.29 s). Base was run twice (A/A):

| PDF | OCR path | Base / Base A/A | Head, chat (no `max_chars`) | Head,
Translate (`max_chars=50000`) | Pages OCR'd base / head Translate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 typed pages (59,646 chars) then 30 scans | vision | 5.97 s / 5.81 s
| 6.02 s | 0.40 s | 20 / 0 |
| same | Tesseract loop | 5.36 s / 5.32 s | 5.37 s | 0.33 s | 20 / 0 |
| 30 typed pages then 30 scans (about 1,750 chars each) | vision | 5.77
s / 5.79 s | 5.69 s | 3.56 s | 20 / 12 |
| same | Tesseract loop | 5.19 s / 5.19 s | 5.19 s | 3.17 s | 20 / 12 |

With a real vision model at 2 to 10 s per page, the first row saves 40
to 200 s per file. In every run the first 50,000 UTF-16 units of the
Translate response were byte-identical to the base response, the text
stayed over 50,000 so the truncation toast still fires, and the chat
path response (text, `truncated`, `warning`) was identical to base. The
one visible difference: base also showed a warning naming the unread
scanned pages past the OCR limit, all of which lie beyond the text
Translate keeps; head no longer warns about them. Unread scans inside
the kept text still warn.

## Tests

- `studio/backend/tests/test_rag_extract_text_max_chars.py` (new, 7
tests, all fail on base): no OCR past the kept text, in-order stop for
vision and Tesseract, a cap that is never reached changes nothing,
unread scans inside the kept text still warn, `until` stops the
Tesseract loop, and the form field over HTTP (optional, `0` refused).
- `studio/frontend/tests/translate-hub-ocr.test.ts` (new, 6 tests, fail
on base): disk-first listing, one Hub listing for a missing model,
five-translation call counts, a finished download read from disk, and
only Translate sending `max_chars`.
- Backend rag / pdf / extract / ocr suites (67 files): base 3120 passed,
head 3127 passed, no failures on either side.
- Frontend translate, gguf-variants and document extract tests: base 67
passed, head 73 passed. `npm run typecheck` passes; eslint on the
touched files reports the same 17 pre-existing findings as base.

Studio diffusion training: DiT block swap, used by auto where int8 was the only fit (#18604)

Studio diffusion LoRA training can now stream frozen bf16 DiT blocks
from pinned host RAM (block swap), and `base_precision=auto` uses this
instead of int8 in the band where the dense base only just fits.

## Why

When a bf16 transformer barely fits, `auto` picks weight-only int8, and
int8 trains eager. On an L4 that is 1.4x to 1.5x slower than bf16 at the
same loss. unsloth_zoo already has the block swap the LLM trainer uses
(`unsloth_zoo.block_swap.BlockSwap`). It keeps the host copy
authoritative, so nothing is copied back, prefetches on a side stream
with a depth+1 slot pool, and prefetches in reverse during the
checkpoint recompute. This PR wires it into the DiT trainer.

## Change

- New `core/training/diffusion_block_swap.py`. `block_swap = off | auto
| N` (also `UNSLOTH_DIT_BLOCK_SWAP`), bf16 only. N blocks are spread
over every repeated block list (FLUX has two). `auto` swaps the fewest
blocks that keep a training reserve free, net of the slot pool.
- The swapped base loads on the host. Everything except the swapped
frozen weights goes to the GPU. Swapping blocks need every block
checkpointed, so the checkpointing budget is off while blocks are
swapped. A plan that swaps nothing keeps the budget.
- Regional compile of a swapped model compiles each block's `forward`
instead of calling `compile_repeated_blocks`. The swap hooks live in
`_call_impl`, and inside a fullgraph compile they would raise. With
`suppress_errors` that would silently fall back to eager. Measured: 0
graph breaks, the same unique-graph count as the unswapped model.
- `base_precision=auto`: when the policy picks int8, train bf16 with
`block_swap=auto` instead. If the swap cannot be installed (for example,
host RAM), it falls back to int8 from the same host copy. It stays int8
on ROCm, on integrated GPUs, without gradient checkpointing, or with
`UNSLOTH_DIT_AUTO_BLOCK_SWAP=0`. The nf4 and bf16 bands and every
explicit precision are unchanged.

## Numbers (Colab L4, torch 2.14.1, diffusers 0.42.1, fresh process per
arm, interleaved, steady = median over steps 11+)

| model, res | main auto (int8) | this PR auto (bf16 + swap) | swapped |
|---|---|---|---|
| FLUX.2-klein 9B, 512 | 2.343 / 2.357 s/step | 1.585 s/step | 0 of 32 |
| FLUX.2-klein 9B, 1024 | 7.539 / 7.552 s/step | 5.343 / 5.353 s/step |
14 of 32 (7.3 GiB) |

Loss: mean abs per-step difference between head and int8 is 0.00012 to
0.00028. That is close to the bf16 A/A spread of 0.00007 to 0.00019.
Peak allocated is 19.0 / 14.6 GiB here vs 18.0 / 16.6 GiB on main. Host
RSS is about 10 GiB steady with 7.3 GiB pinned, and about 20 GiB peak
while loading.

FLUX.1-dev on the L4 (bf16 does not fit) stays on nf4, because nf4 +
compile is faster than bf16 + swap:

| arm | s/step | peak GiB | mean abs dloss vs bf16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| nf4 + compile (auto, unchanged) | 1.297 [1.274-1.310] | 14.0 | 0.0054
|
| int8 eager | 2.826 [2.825-2.827] | 18.7 | 0.0002 |
| bf16 + `block_swap=auto` (21 of 57 blocks, 8.1 GiB) | 1.829
[1.822-1.833] | 17.7 | A/A 0.00015 |

There the swap is opt-in, for exact bf16 maths at 1.55x the speed of
int8. Copies ran at 12.3 GB/s, about 16 GB per step.

## Host RAM guard

A swapped base loads dense on the host, while the int8 path it replaces
streams the load. So `auto` takes bf16 + swap only when available host
RAM (cgroup-aware, the same reading the prequant cache uses) is at least
1.3x the dense bf16 size plus 4 GiB; otherwise, or if the reading is
unavailable, it keeps int8. Covered by
`test_auto_swap_needs_host_ram_for_the_dense_base`.

## Tests

`tests/test_diffusion_block_swap.py` (CPU, 21 tests) covers request
parsing, gating, both planners, block list discovery, compile routing,
and the auto int8-band decision including every exclusion.
`test_diffusion_dit_trainer.py` + `test_diffusion_gc_budget.py` + the
new file: 98 passed.

## Not proven here

- Only an L4 was measured. Consumer cards (3090 / 4090 / 5090) and PCIe
Gen3 hosts were not, and the int8 vs swap gap depends on PCIe bandwidth.
- Not run: Qwen-Image, video DiTs, batch > 1, previews during training
with blocks swapped, and resume while swapping.
- The int8 fallback after a refused host-RAM check is unit-tested at the
decision only.
- The auto reserve is conservative: at 1024 px about 7.9 GiB of VRAM was
left free. It has not been tuned.
- ROCm discrete GPUs were not measured, and auto keeps int8 there.

Studio: let Desktop start on Windows AMD when the Triton pairing fails (#18527)

## Problem

On Windows with an AMD GPU, Unsloth Desktop can get stuck in a state
where it refuses to start Studio, and its built-in repair does not help.
This was reported on Desktop 0.1.920-beta:

- Desktop said the install was incomplete (`studio_install_incomplete`).
- Repair ran `unsloth studio update`, then the bundled installer. Both
finished with exit code 0.
- Desktop still refused to start Studio: "Repair finished, but Unsloth
install is still not desktop-ready."

## Why it happens

Two pieces of code disagree about what a failed Triton swap means.

**Desktop needs the install manifest.** Setup writes
`unsloth_install_manifest.json` into the venv when an install finishes.
Desktop only starts Studio if this file is there. If it is missing,
Desktop calls the install incomplete.

**On AMD, setup can delete the manifest and still report success.**
#16074 added a step that runs after the dependencies are installed. When
ROCm torch 2.11 or 2.12 ends up next to Triton 3.9, this step replaces
it with Triton 3.8, because 3.9 breaks fused flex attention decode with
those torch versions. The step works like this:

1. Move the manifest aside, so an interrupted swap is never marked as
finished.
2. Install Triton 3.8.
3. Check what is installed now.
4. If 3.8 is in place, put the manifest back.
5. If not, print a warning ("flex attention decode may run unfused"),
delete the manifest, and let setup exit 0. Setup only fails here if the
swap broke a Triton that worked before.

Step 5 is the bug. Setup reports success, but Desktop now sees an
incomplete install. Repair runs setup again, which reaches the same
step, fails the same way, and deletes the manifest again. On a machine
where the swap keeps failing, Desktop never recovers.

The swap can fail for several reasons: the install fails, the check
after it fails or times out, or a uv `override-dependencies` setting
keeps 3.9 while the install still exits 0. The report does not show
which one the reporter hit.

**Desktop also hid the reason.** Its check after repair returned only
yes or no, so the error message never said why the install was not
ready.

## Fix

**`studio/setup.ps1`:** when the swap ends with only a warning, put the
manifest back instead of deleting it.

This is safe because a warning means Triton is no worse than before the
step:

- If Triton 3.9 still works, the cost is unfused flex attention decode.
- If Triton was missing or broken before, it still is, and the backend
keeps `torch.compile` turned off, as it already did
(`gate_torch_compile_on_windows`).

In both cases Studio can still start. The swap is also retried on the
next update, even with the manifest in place, because the update's fast
path checks the installed Triton directly
(`Test-RocmTritonPairingNeedsPass`). The old code comment said the
manifest had to go so that the next update would retry; that is not
needed.

Setup still fails, as before, when the swap breaks a Triton that worked.
It now also fails if it cannot put the manifest back, instead of
reporting success without one.

**Desktop (`studio/src-tauri`):** when repair ends with the install
still not ready, the error names the reason, for example:

```
Repair finished, but Unsloth install is still not desktop-ready (studio_install_incomplete).
```

The log line written when repair falls back from the update to the
installer includes the reason too.

**Tests (`tests/studio/test_rocm_triton_windows_pairing.ps1`):** cases
where the swap only warns now expect the manifest to be kept. A new case
checks that setup fails when the manifest cannot be put back.

## Testing

### Live A/B on Windows AMD hardware

Both versions ran on AMD Strix Halo machines (Windows 11, Radeon 8060S,
Python 3.13, torch `2.11.0+rocm7.14.0`). "Main" is the base commit and
"fix" is the same commit plus this change.

To make the swap fail on purpose, a uv config set `override-dependencies
= ["triton-windows==3.9.0.post30"]`. With that in place, installing
Triton 3.8 exits 0 but leaves 3.9 installed.

Each version ran three commands. After each one, the table shows whether
the manifest exists and what `unsloth studio desktop-capabilities
--json` reports for `studio_install_ok`. That value is what Desktop
checks before it starts Studio. Every command exited 0.

| Command | Main | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1. `install.ps1 --local --python 3.13`, swap forced to fail | Manifest
missing, `false` | Manifest kept, `true` |
| 2. `unsloth studio update` (the update Desktop's repair runs), swap
still forced to fail | Manifest deleted again, `false` | Swap retried,
manifest kept, `true` |
| 3. `unsloth studio update --local`, override removed | Triton 3.8
installed, `true` | Triton 3.8 installed, `true` |

Rows 1 and 2 reproduce the reported failure on main and show the fix.
Row 3 shows that both versions install Triton 3.8 once the cause is
gone.

Logs:
[main](https://github.com/oobabooga/unsloth/actions/runs/44585530606/job/135777305749),
[fix](https://github.com/oobabooga/unsloth/actions/runs/44585530606/job/135777305355).
The "Evidence after ..." steps print what the table is based on: exit

Harness:
[workflow](https://github.com/oobabooga/unsloth/blob/2636b6485613da72731aaa684b3de37533e250c1/.github/workflows/rocm-triton-manifest-ab.yml),
[evidence

The main job's last step (Verdict) is red because of a harness problem

main's own tests. The likely cause is that the runner checked out the

### Unit tests

The main job is red because those 8 failures are the expected result;
