Studio diffusion training: keep long attention outputs of checkpointed blocks (#18601)

When the Studio diffusion trainer checkpoints a block, the backward pass
reruns that block's whole forward, attention kernels included. This
change passes a selective checkpoint policy to the blocks the gc budget
still checkpoints. Attention kernels with at least 1024 keys keep their
output and logsumexp from the first pass, and every other op is
recomputed as before. On Wan 2.2 5B the kept outputs are about 0.9 GiB
across all 30 blocks. A whole kept block costs about 0.75 GiB, so for
memory spent this saves roughly 4x more time than keeping whole blocks.

## Change

All edits are in `studio/backend/core/training/diffusion_gc_budget.py`:

- `save_attention_context_fn()` builds a
`create_selective_checkpoint_contexts` policy. Flash, mem-efficient,
cuDNN and CPU SDPA forwards are saved when the key length is at least
1024. Shorter calls, such as Wan's 512-token text cross-attention, are
recomputed. The policy only turns on when torch's selective checkpoint
modes report `ignore_compile_internals()` (torch 2.10+). On older torch,
dynamo would skip a compiled frame while such a mode is active, so those
versions keep the plain recompute.
- `_Checkpoint(save_attention=...)` passes `context_fn` and counts the
kept outputs and their bytes. Only first-pass calls are counted, because
torch 2.10 and 2.11 ask the policy again during recompute.
`BudgetedCheckpoint` builds its base checkpoint with it on.
- Planning: step 1's peak already holds the kept attention outputs of
every checkpointed block. The second block of each class records its
kept attention bytes per proxy element (`class_attention`), and
`estimate()` subtracts them, because a kept block does not hold them a
second time.
- Out of memory: `can_retry` is also true when attention outputs are
being kept. The step-down that ends in `fall_back()` drops them, so the
rerun recomputes everything, as before.
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_GC_SAVE_ATTENTION=0` turns it off. ROCm, `plain` /
`partial` modes and non-CUDA devices do not use the budget and are
unchanged.

## Numbers

Colab G4 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), torch 2.11.0+cu130, diffusers 0.42.1.
Real transformer configs with random bf16 weights, PEFT LoRA r16 on the
trainer's targets, fp32 LoRA params, bf16 autocast,
`compile_repeated_blocks(fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)`, cuDNN SDPA off
as in the trainer. 50 steps (40 for the ballast runs), seeded latents,
fresh process per arm, main and branch interleaved ABBA. Steady state is
the median of steps 6 onward. Smaller cards are emulated with an
in-process ballast, so the plan sees only the given free memory.

| Run | main s/step | this branch s/step | change | peak alloc GiB main
/ branch | kept blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wan 5B 832x480x49 (5070 tok), 40 GiB free | 0.5460, 0.5477 | 0.5352,
0.5357 | -2.1% | 26.20 / 26.50 | 19 / 19 |
| Wan 5B 832x480x49, 32 GiB free | 0.6066, 0.6064 | 0.5858, 0.5856 |
-3.4% | 19.41 / 19.97 | 10 / 10 |
| Wan 5B 832x480x49, every block checkpointed | 0.6700, 0.6700 | 0.6391,
0.6390 | -4.6% | 11.90 / 12.75 | 0 |
| Wan 5B 832x480x81 (8190 tok), every block checkpointed | 1.1987 |
1.1265 | -6.0% | 13.17 / 14.55 | 0 |
| Wan 5B 832x480x49, full 96 GB card | 0.4734, 0.4741, 0.4744 | 0.4738,
0.4740, 0.4743 | tie | 33.75 / 33.75 | 30 / 30 |
| FLUX.2 klein 4B 1024, full card | 0.2818, 0.2815 | 0.2818, 0.2817 |
tie | 19.52 / 19.54 | 25 / 25 |

- A/A spread within each arm is at most 0.0017 s/step. Every delta above
is larger than that, except the rows marked tie.
- When the card already keeps every block, nothing is checkpointed, so
nothing changes. The step-1 peak is 0.7 GiB higher there, because during
measurement the checkpointed blocks keep their outputs.
- Loss over 50 steps: the step-49 relative difference between main and
this branch is under 1e-5 (largest 1.6e-5 at 81 frames). That is the
same size as the main-vs-main run-to-run difference (up to 1e-5).
Results are not bitwise identical even main vs main, because the flash
backward is not deterministic.
- torch.compile: 0 graph breaks and the same unique graph count (2 for
Wan, 3 for FLUX.2) in both arms, with no extra recompiles after step 1.
- Engagement: the saved-output counter is non-zero only on this branch
(809 outputs and 25.6 GB kept over the 40-step 32 GiB run). The peak
rise also matches the expected output plus logsumexp bytes (about 31 MB
per Wan block at 5070 tokens).

## Tests

New `studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_gc_saved_attention.py`, CPU
only. A counting dispatch mode around backward shows that the
checkpointed 1024-key self-attention is not rerun while the 8-key
cross-attention is. Gradients are bitwise equal to the plain checkpoint,
and the kept bytes match the output plus logsumexp size. Other tests
cover short sequences, the env switch, the out-of-memory fall back
dropping the outputs, a torch without compile-safe modes, and the plan
credit. These tests fail on main and pass here. Existing
`test_diffusion_gc_budget*.py`: all pass.

## Not proven here

- These runs used a harness that reproduces the trainer's setup, not a
full Studio training job. No A100 run was made, because A100 capacity
was taken at the time.
- No measurement on a 24 GB consumer card and no bucketed
(multi-resolution) run.
- No run on torch 2.10, 2.12, 2.13 or 2.14 on GPU; the CPU tests ran on
2.14.
- FLUX.2 was only measured where the budget keeps every block, so this
shows no regression for images but no speedup either.

Studio: rate GGUFs on a GGUF-only Mac against Metal, not half of free RAM (#18552)

## Problem

On an Apple Silicon Mac without a usable MLX stack, the Model Hub shows
**"Unavailable" VRAM** and marks small GGUFs **"Does not fit"**, even
though llama.cpp runs them on Metal.

Affected: every Desktop "Chat only (GGUF)" install on a Mac, and Macs
whose MLX stack is missing, outdated or under repair.

## Cause

These Macs are detected as CPU, so `/api/system` reports no GPU. The Hub
then rates GGUFs against half of free RAM, and the memory estimate
prices every load as CPU-only. llama.cpp itself still uses Metal.

## Fix

**Backend:** `/api/system` lists one shared-memory Metal device in
`inference_gpu` for these Macs, only when llama.cpp will really use
Metal:

- the llama.cpp build includes Metal (`libggml-metal` beside
`llama-server`, or a prebuilt marker)
- `GGML_METAL_DEVICES` is not set to 0
- the GPU is not virtualised (the loader pins those to CPU)

The check stays cheap: no MLX or torch import, no `system_profiler`.
System-wide AGX memory is not reported.

**Frontend:** badges use the same Metal budget as an MLX Mac, and the
Hub GPU chip falls back to this inventory.

Training detection is unchanged, and MLX Macs are unaffected.
Side effect: a host whose only GPU is a separately installed Vulkan
llama.cpp now shows that GPU in the Hub chip instead of "Unavailable".

## Results

Real 8 GiB M1 Mac mini, with torch and MLX imports blocked to reproduce
a chat-only install:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Hub GPU chip | Unavailable VRAM | 0 GiB VRAM + 8 GiB shared |
| Qwen3.5-4B quants (4.13 GiB free) | 22 red | 1 green, 19 amber, 2 red
(larger than 8 GiB) |
| Memory estimate, Qwen3-0.6B | 0 GiB on GPU | 0.84 GiB on GPU |

Studio diffusion training: route masked attention to cuDNN on measured cards (#18602)

Diffusion training turns cuDNN SDPA off on every card
(`_apply_perf_flags`, added after a FLUX training crash on B200 with
torch 2.10 + cu130). Flash attention takes no mask, so every masked
training attention call (Krea-2 text padding, LTX-2, Qwen-Image) falls
back to the mem-efficient kernel. On A100, L4 and RTX PRO 6000 that
kernel is 1.4x to 3.6x slower than cuDNN for fwd+bwd, and cuDNN is just
as accurate.

## Change

`_apply_perf_flags` in `diffusion_train_common.py`:

- On sm80 (A100), sm89 (L4) and sm120 (RTX PRO 6000) with torch 2.10 or
newer, cuDNN SDPA stays enabled and the SDPA priority becomes flash >
cuDNN > mem-eff > math. Unmasked calls still go to flash, which is
faster than cuDNN on these cards. Masked calls now go to cuDNN instead
of mem-eff.
- `torch.compiler.config.cache_key_tag` gets an extra tag. The inductor
/ AOT autograd cache key covers the traced graph but not the SDPA
priority, so without the tag a warm cache from an earlier run hands back
the old mem-eff graph. This was measured: a shared cache kept the head
arm on mem-eff until the tag was added.
- The card checked is the training device passed to `_apply_perf_flags`,
not whichever CUDA device is current.
- Every other card (sm90, sm100 and anything unmeasured), older torch,
or `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_TRAIN_CUDNN_SDPA=0` keeps the old behaviour.
`_restore_perf_flags` restores the priority and the tag.

## Numbers (Colab, torch 2.14.1 + cuDNN 9.24 unless noted)

SDPA fwd+bwd, B=1, head_dim 128, bf16, diffusers layout. Median of 5
interleaved rounds. Max relative Frobenius error over out/dq/dk/dv vs an
fp32 reference:

cuDNN / flash |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24 heads, 1536 tokens, 400 masked keys | A100 | 2.12 | 1.29 | 1.64x |
0.0048 / 0.0045 / n.a. |
| 24 heads, 4608 tokens, 400 masked keys | A100 | 13.25 | 9.45 | 1.40x |
0.0048 / 0.0045 / n.a. |
| same, 1536 tokens | L4 (torch 2.10, cuDNN 9.15) | 5.11 | 2.57 | 1.99x
| 0.0048 / 0.0045 / n.a. |
| same, 4608 tokens | L4 (torch 2.10) | 45.37 | 21.26 | 2.13x | 0.0048 /
0.0045 / n.a. |
| same, 1536 tokens | RTX PRO 6000 | 1.82 | 0.61 | 2.98x | 0.0048 /
0.0045 / n.a. |
| same, 4608 tokens | RTX PRO 6000 | 15.18 | 4.19 | 3.62x | 0.0048 /

Studio Triton kernels: resolve factory closure names on Triton 3.2 / 3.3 (#18591)

Triton 3.2 and 3.3 (the Triton of torch 2.6 and 2.7, and the newest
torch on CUDA 11.8 wheels, all inside Studio's `torch>=2.4,<2.12`
install range) resolve the names a `@triton.jit` kernel reads in the
kernel's module globals only. Newer Triton also reads the function's
closure. Most Studio kernels are built inside a lazy factory
(`_kernels()`, `_kernel()`, ...) that imports `triton.language as tl`
locally and often defines JIT helpers and constants next to the kernel,
so on Triton 3.2 / 3.3 they fail to lower with `NameError('tl is not
defined')` (or the same for a helper). Three factories
(`diffusion_vae_fused`, `diffusion_int8_fused`, `video_minimax_h3_vae`)
already worked around this with `globals().update(triton = triton, tl =
tl)`; the other fourteen did not. Depending on the call site the result
is a crash at the first launch, a silent fallback to a slower path (the
frozen FP8 transpose), or a kernel probe that fails and keeps the stock
path.

Found in a recheck of #17966 (`_rows_residual` in the VAE strip decode,
confirmed with an offline Triton 3.3.0 compile for sm75 and sm80: fails
on main, compiles with the name in module globals, still compiles on
3.8.0).

## Change

- New `core/inference/triton_closure_globals.py`: `publish(result)`
finds every JIT kernel reachable from a factory's result (namespaces,
containers, plain launcher closures, and the JIT helpers a kernel calls)
and copies each kernel's closure names into its module globals with
`setdefault`, so an existing module global is never overwritten.
`publishes_closure_globals` is the decorator form.
- The decorator sits under the existing `lru_cache` on the factories in
`diffusion_convrot_quant`, `diffusion_flux2_rope`,
`diffusion_flux3_qk_rope`, `diffusion_int8_fused`,
`diffusion_int8_gemm`, `diffusion_int8_gemv`, `diffusion_moss_fused`,
`diffusion_native_w8a8_rdna`, `diffusion_qwenimage21_eager`,
`diffusion_rocm_fused`, `video_minimax_h3_qknorm`,
`video_minimax_h3_rowmod` and `video_wan_fused`; `diffusion_frozen_fp8`
publishes its transpose kernel when it builds it. `diffusion_vae_strips`
binds `tl` like the fused VAE module (first commit).
- No kernel source changes. On current Triton the published names are
the same objects the closure already holds.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_triton_closure_globals.py` (CPU, nothing compiles):
for each of the 17 factories, every reachable JIT kernel must find every
closure name in its module globals. 16 fail on main (for example
`_f3_qk_norm_rope:tl`, `_qk_norm_rope_kernel:_rsqrt`, `i8mm_dq:_rbf16`,
`transpose:tl`); `diffusion_vae_fused` passes on both. A second test
checks that a kernel reached only through a plain launcher, and the JIT
helper it calls, are published, and that an existing module global is
left alone.
-
`tests/test_diffusion_vae_strips.py::test_kernel_names_resolve_from_module_globals`:
fails on main, passes here.

Base vs head over the changed test files: 16 fixed, 56 unchanged, 0
failing on this branch.

## Not proven here

- No real launch on torch 2.6 / 2.7: only the offline Triton 3.3 compile
of the VAE strip kernel and the module-globals check above. A T4 run on
torch 2.7.1 is the follow-up.
- Triton 3.4 to 3.6 were not checked for which release started reading
closures.

Studio RDNA W8A8: probe the weight's card and follow the operand's card (#18588)

Each `NativeWeightOnlyLinear` with INT8 activations set `self._rdna`
from an argumentless `rdna.prepare()`, which probes whichever card is
current at build time. `_rdna_on(x)` checked that Boolean before it
looked at the operand's card. So a linear built while an unsupported
card (or no ROCm card) was current kept the stock maths for its whole
life, even when its operands ran on an RDNA card the kernels were proven
on. The launchers already use the operand's device. Since #18199 the
explicit INT8 route checks RDNA readiness for the load's ordinal, so a
mismatch here silently drops a W8A8 path the route selected.

## Change

In `diffusion_native_quant.py`:

- The build-time probe now uses the device of the weight being quantised
when it is on a GPU (the load's card). It only falls back to the current
card when the weight is on the host.
- On a ROCm build, a linear whose build-time probe said no still lets
`_rdna_on` check the operand's card. `_rdna_on` already probes an unseen
card in eager and gates on `rdna.enabled_for(index)` for that card.
- On NVIDIA and CPU hosts nothing changes: `_rdna_rocm` stays False and
`_rdna_on` returns at the first check, as before.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_diffusion_native_w8a8_rdna.py`, CPU only:

- `test_layer_probes_the_card_its_weight_is_on`: a linear built from a
fake-tensor weight on `cuda:1` probes `cuda:1`. Fails on main (it probed
`None`, the current card), passes here.
- `test_layer_built_off_its_card_follows_the_operand_card[True]`: on
ROCm, a host-built linear whose build-time probe failed takes the RDNA
kernels for an operand on a ready card 1, and not for card 0. Fails on
main, passes here.
- `test_layer_built_off_its_card_follows_the_operand_card[False]`: off
ROCm it never engages. Passes on main and here.

`test_diffusion_native_quant*.py`,
`test_diffusion_flux3_rdna_shared_quant.py`): 358 passed, 19 skipped, 0

Studio int8 early prewarm: start the warm-up thread before publishing it (#18587)

#18455 added an early int8 probe warm-up that
`start_early_probe_prewarm` runs on its own thread during the load. It
published the `Thread` in `_EARLY_PREWARM` under `_EARLY_LOCK`, released
the lock, and only then called `start()`. A `join_early_probe_prewarm`
that ran in that gap found the unstarted thread, and `Thread.join()` on
a thread that was never started raises `RuntimeError`. The broad handler
in the join swallowed it, so the join returned before the warm-up had
even started, and the warm-up could then run beside a timed probe. A
`start()` failure (for example `can't start new thread`) also left the
dead entry in `_EARLY_PREWARM`, so later loads on that card could never
retry.

## Change

`start_early_probe_prewarm` now starts the thread before releasing
`_EARLY_LOCK`, and adds the entry only after `start()` returns. A joiner
that sees the entry always gets a started thread. If `start()` fails, no
entry is left and the call returns False, as before. The worker never
takes `_EARLY_LOCK`, so starting it under the lock cannot deadlock.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_diffusion_early_probe_prewarm.py`, CPU only:

- `test_a_joiner_racing_the_start_waits_for_the_warm_up`: a `Thread`
subclass runs a joiner just before the real `start()`. On main the
joiner returns before the worker runs (0 warm-up calls when it returns).
Here it blocks on the lock and returns after the warm-up (1 call). Fails
on main, passes here.
- `test_a_failed_thread_start_leaves_no_entry_and_allows_a_retry`: a
failing `start()` leaves no `_EARLY_PREWARM` entry and a second start
works. Fails on main (stale entry, retry refused), passes here.

Suite (`test_diffusion_early_probe_prewarm.py`,
`test_diffusion_probe_prewarm.py`,
`test_diffusion_probe_prewarm_rng.py`,
`test_diffusion_deferred_prewarm.py`,
`test_diffusion_int8_cutlass_lib_digest.py`,
`test_diffusion_int8_gemm.py`): 113 passed, 114 skipped, 0 failed here.
On main the same set has the two new tests failing and everything else
unchanged.

## Not proven here

No GPU run. The tests force the interleaving instead of waiting for it
to happen in a real Studio load, where the single-backend model
transition usually serialises the start and the join. I did not measure
how often a real load hits the gap.

given as `cuda` without an index resolves to the current card, which is

or the parked VAE rollback.

stayed on `cuda:0`), passes here.

Studio int8 GEMM: a huge race skipped for memory is raced again on a later load (#18585)

#18105 added the 16,384-row CUTLASS race for video row counts and skips
it when the card has no room for its operands (`_huge_race_fits`). The
skip writes `None` into the plan entry, which is right for this process:
today's path runs at that size. But the same `None` was written to the
disk race cache, where `None` already means "every tile lost the race".
The cache reader accepts that entry as complete, so every later load of
that shape on that card read the skip back as a lost race and never
timed the 16,384-row point again, even once the memory pressure was
gone. A one-off low-memory load therefore kept video-size calls on the
slower path across restarts until the cache key changed.

## Change

`_cutlass_plan` in `diffusion_int8_gemm.py` stores a point skipped for
memory as `"skipped"` in the disk cache instead of `None`. The reader
accepts that marker as a known value (so the entry is still complete for
the older-format check) but leaves the point out of the cached plan, so
the next load races that one point and nothing else. A real lost race is
still stored and read back as `None`, and the in-process plan is
unchanged (`None` there, today's path at that size). An older build that
reads a cache with the marker sees an unknown value and re-races the
shape, the same as any other foreign entry.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_diffusion_int8_cutlass.py`, CPU only, with the race
and the card stubbed:

- `test_a_huge_race_skipped_for_memory_is_raced_again_on_a_later_load`:
the first load has no room (races 512 and 4096 only), a fresh process
with the room back races the 16,384-row point alone and takes its
winner, and a third load reads the completed race without racing. Fails
on main (the second load runs zero races and keeps `None`), passes here.
- `test_a_lost_huge_race_is_still_read_from_the_cache`: a cached lost
race (`None` at 16,384) is reused without racing. Passes on main and
here.

Studio INT8 attention: key the strided cuDNN race by the call each card times (#18584)

#18140 gave a strided cuDNN incumbent its own INT8 race verdict name,
`dispatch:_native_cudnn:strided`, because the strided call differs from
diffusers' contiguous `_native_cudnn` call. But the name was taken from
the marker's class alone. The marker only takes the strided call on the
cards it probed and at the dtype it probed; on any other card or dtype
`plain_qkv` declines and the race times diffusers' call. The dispatch
install races each module on the load card and on every secondary card
(layer split, CFG replica), so a marker for `{0}` raced on `cuda:1`
timed the contiguous call and cached that verdict as `cuda:1 ...
:strided`. A marker for `{0, 1}` then read that verdict on `cuda:1`,
although its real call there is the strided one, and the reverse order
had the same mix-up. The INT8 token floor on that card could then come
from a different incumbent call than the one the route replaces.

## Change

`_race_name` in `diffusion_int8_attention_dispatch.py` takes optional
`card` and `dtype` and keeps the `:strided` suffix only when the
marker's `cards` contains the card and its probed dtype matches (or is
unset). Elsewhere it returns the plain `dispatch:_native_cudnn` name, so
those races share the verdict of the call they actually time. The
dispatch install computes the name per raced card with the race dtype.
Called without the new arguments, `_race_name` returns what it did
before, and the persisted verdict names are unchanged.

fp16; a `{0, 1}` marker is `:strided` on card 1. Fails on main, passes
here.
- `test_dispatch_race_keys_each_card_by_its_timed_call` (3 cases): runs
the real dispatch install with a load card and a secondary card, records
the verdict name each card races under. `{0}` bf16 gives strided on 0
and plain on 1; `{0, 1}` fp16 under a bf16 load gives plain on both.
Both fail on main (every card raced as `:strided`) and pass here. `{0,
1}` bf16 gives strided on both and passes on main and here.

Studio Windows ROCm: decode compile only off for wide-head VAEs, fp64 kept, nested-safe SDPA guard (#18582)

Three fixes to the Windows ROCm attention routing added in #17953 and
#17960, found in a recheck of the kernel PRs. Each is its own commit.

## 1. VAE decode compile is dropped only for wide-head VAEs

#17953 keeps the Windows ROCm VAE decode eager so a compiled decode
cannot skip the attention routing that keeps head dim 512 off the fused
SDPA kernels. But `_vae_decode_compile_allowed` returned False on the
platform alone, before looking at the VAE or the
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_COMPILE_VAE` setting. A VAE with no attention head
wider than 256 (attention-free video VAEs, or a narrow AutoencoderKL)
lost decode compilation too, even when the env asked for it.

- `diffusion_vae_attn_chunked.py`: new `vae_has_untrusted_head(vae)`. It
walks the same attention modules the routing patches and reads each head
dim (`inner_dim // heads` on diffusers `Attention`). Any head wider than
256, any attention module whose head dim it cannot read (the single-head
blocks of Wan, Qwen-Image and HunyuanImage), and any VAE it cannot
inspect count as wide.
- `diffusion_speed.py`: on Windows ROCm `_vae_decode_compile_allowed`
returns False only when `vae_has_untrusted_head` is True. The check
still runs before the U-Net shortcut and the env override, so a
wide-head VAE never compiles past the routing there.

Studio's own AutoencoderKL and AutoencoderKLFlux2 VAEs have a
single-head mid-block at 512, so they stay eager on Windows ROCm exactly
as before.

## 2. fp64 stays fp64 in the wide-head math path

`fp32_math_sdpa` ran `.float()` on Q, K and V and cast only the result
back, so an fp64 call was silently reduced to fp32. With fp64 `[1, 1, 3,
512]` operands filled with `1e20`, stock SDPA returns finite output
while the routed path overflowed and returned NaN. It now upcasts only
fp16 and bf16; fp32 and fp64 run in their own precision. Half inputs
keep the existing fp32 upcast, so `UNSLOTH_VAE_ATTN_HALF_MATH=0` is
unchanged. Studio loads VAEs in fp16, bf16 or fp32, so this only matters
to code handing a double VAE to the routed attention.

## 3. The SDPA guard checks the device before the query shape

The Windows ROCm SDPA wrapper's `_wide_cuda_head` read `query.shape`
before checking the device. A strided NestedTensor raises
`NestedTensorImpl doesn't support sizes` on `.shape`, so a valid CPU
nested SDPA call failed inside the wrapper. It now returns False for any
non-CUDA query without touching the shape, judges a nested CUDA query by
`size(-1)`, and sends the call to the stock dispatch if even that
raises. Dense CUDA queries are judged as before.

Studio int8 GEMM: T4 native W8A8 tile race is read back from the race cache (#18586)

On a T4, `NativeWeightOnlyLinear.forward` calls `native_prepare` on the
first fp16 W8A8 forward of each (card, N, K). That races the CUTLASS
native-epilogue tiles at 512 and 4,096 rows and keeps the plan in
process memory only (`_NATIVE_PLAN`). Since #18149 the 4,096-row race
also runs sustained timings: the incumbent and up to three finalists
each run back to back for about 0.25 s to settle and 0.25 s to measure,
with a device sync after every settling call. The torchao path keeps its
plan in the disk race cache, but the native path never did, so every
fresh Studio process paid this again inside the first render.

Measured on a Colab Tesla T4 with the `unsloth-studio-i8gemm` 1.0.0
wheel, seven FLUX-sized weight shapes (3072x3072, 9216x3072, 3072x9216,
18432x3072, 27648x3072, 3072x12288, 6144x3072), each arm in its own
fresh process:

| Arm | `native_prepare` total, 7 shapes |
|---|---:|
| main, default timing | 21.1 s, 21.5 s (two runs) |
| main, `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_INT8_CUTLASS_SUSTAINED=huge` (the policy
before #18149) | 7.2 s, 7.0 s |
| this branch, first process | 21.6 s |
| this branch, next process (same cache) | 0.2 s |

So the sustained 4,096-row race adds about 14 s to the first render of
every fresh T4 process for these shapes, on top of the 7 s the races
already cost. It is not wasted work: the drift gate picked the sustained
timings for 4,096 rows on 13 of the 14 cold main races here, and the
sustained winners were steadier between runs than the short ones. So
this change keeps the timing policy and stops repeating it.

## Change

`native_prepare` in `diffusion_int8_cutlass.py` reads and writes its
plan in the same disk race cache as the torchao plan
(`diffusion_int8_cutlass_race.json`). The key is the torchao plan's key
(card, capability, torch, CUDA, Triton, tile env, timing mode, source
and library digest) plus `|native|` and the CUTLASS switch, so a forced
pick is never read back as a raced one. One slot per `NxK`. A cached
entry is used only when it has both race points and every tile is still
one the library probes, otherwise the shape races as before. A race that
raises (for example an OOM) is not cached. Any cache read or write
failure keeps today's in-process behaviour. The first process on a card
still pays the race once per shape.

## Tests

the race, the card and the cache file stubbed:

- `test_the_native_cache_follows_the_timing_mode_and_switch`: a forced
CUTLASS pick gets its own cache slot and races. Fails on main (nothing
is cached), passes here.
- `test_a_cached_tile_the_library_no_longer_probes_races_again` and
`test_a_failed_race_is_not_cached`: a stale tile races again, and a
raising race writes nothing. Pass on main and here.

Studio multi-GPU: CFG replicas of other models no longer import MOSS-Image (diffusers) (#18595)

## Summary

Since #18559 merged, `Backend CI / (Python 3.13, diffusion)` fails on
`main` with 52 failures and 1 collection error. The shard runs without
`diffusers`, and every CFG replica build now fails:

```
core/inference/diffusion_moss_image.py:373: in _model_bases
    from diffusers.configuration_utils import ConfigMixin
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'diffusers'
...
E   AssertionError: replica unavailable: No module named 'diffusers'
ERROR tests/test_diffusion_cfg_replica_fused_qkv.py
```

The failures are spread across `test_diffusion_multigpu.py`,
`test_diffusion_cfg_parallel_tier.py`,
`test_diffusion_auto_multigpu_policy.py`,
`test_diffusion_cfg_replica_shared_state.py`,
`test_diffusion_unet_cfg_parallel.py` and
`test_diffusion_qwenimage21_dense_fused.py`.

## Root cause

#18559's goal is right: a CFG replica should re-fuse MOSS-Image's Q/K/V
on its own card. But `_replica_copy` calls
`diffusion_moss_fused.is_replica_record` for every attribute of every
model, and that helper imports `diffusion_moss_image` to read
`FUSED_QKV_ATTR`. That module builds its model classes on `diffusers` at
import time. So without a working `diffusers`, every replica build
raises and CFG parallelism turns off for all models, not just
MOSS-Image. The new test file also imports `diffusion_moss_image` at
module level, so it fails to collect where `diffusers` is missing.

## Fix

- `diffusion_moss_fused.py`: the two replica hooks read
`diffusion_moss_image` from `sys.modules` instead of importing it. A

an unloaded module means there is nothing to drop or re-fuse:

Studio diffusion probe cache: key persisted verdicts on the installed GPU driver (#18574)

#18156 made INT8 attention verdicts persist across processes, keyed by
the shared probe-cache fingerprint (torch, CUDA, driver, card). The
quant probe verdicts use that same fingerprint. The driver part comes
from `torch._C._cuda_getDriverVersion`, and no current torch build has
that function (2.12.1+cu130, 2.13.0, 2.14.1+cu130 checked). So the
fingerprint always records `driver=None`. After a driver update, a
passing persisted INT8 attention verdict is still adopted with only a
launch warm-up, a negative one skips even that, and the quant verdicts
are reused the same way.

## Change

`fingerprint()` now reads the driver itself, once per process and
without creating a CUDA context:

- NVIDIA: the kernel module version from `/proc/driver/nvidia/version`,
or if that file is missing (WSL, some containers, Windows) the name,
size and mtime of the driver library this process loaded (`libcuda.so*`
from `/proc/self/maps`, or `System32\nvcuda.dll`). `cuDriverGetVersion`
is added when it answers.
- ROCm: the existing `_rocm_driver_version()` from `diffusion_attention`
(HIP driver version, plus the amdgpu module version or kernel release).

If no driver identity can be read, `fingerprint()` returns None. Then
nothing is stored or adopted and the probes run fresh, as they did
before persistence. Every namespace built on `fingerprint()` gets this
fix. Existing cache entries were keyed with `driver=None`, so each one
misses once and is probed again on the first start after the update.

## Tests

`tests/test_diffusion_probe_cache_driver.py` (CPU only; the card, the
proc file and the driver library are faked):

- a driver update changes the fingerprint key
- a verdict stored under one driver is not adopted under another, for
both `Namespace` and `load`/`store`
- an unreadable driver stores and admits nothing
- the same driver still reuses the verdict
- ROCm keys on the HIP driver identity and refuses one it could not read

On main, 4 of the 5 fail. The same-driver reuse case passes on both, as
it should. With this change, all 5 pass. The existing probe-cache users
(`test_diffusion_int8_attention_persisted.py`,
`test_diffusion_transformer_quant.py`, `test_early_quant_probe.py`,
`test_diffusion_probe_overlap.py`, `test_diffusion_cold_start.py`,
`test_diffusion_early_probe_prewarm.py`,
`test_diffusion_compat_preflight.py`,
`test_diffusion_rocm_tag_detect.py` and one more block test) fail the
same 36 test IDs on main and with this change. The 35 in
`test_diffusion_compat_preflight.py` come from `gguf` not being
installed in the test venv; the remaining one, in
`test_diffusion_cold_start.py`, fails identically on main. There are no
new failures.

## Not proven

- Not run on a real GPU. The NVIDIA reader was checked by hand on a
Linux host (`cuda13010,nvrm590.48.01`). The WSL, Windows and ROCm
readers were exercised only through fakes.
- We have not measured whether a particular driver update actually
changes INT8 attention numerics. This change only makes sure such an
update is noticed.
- The library-identity fallback keys on file metadata, so reinstalling
the same driver also causes one re-probe.

Studio VAE attention: gate ROCm half math on the autocast dtype that actually runs (#18573)

#18077 keeps ROCm VAE attention in bf16 half math but sends fp16 through
the fp32 upcast, because fp16 scores overflow at real VAE magnitudes.
The dtype gate reads the caller's `q.dtype` before autocast casts it. A
bf16 query under fp16 autocast passes the bf16-only gate. The mode then
casts Q/K/V to fp16 and computes the scores in fp16 with autocast off.
On FLUX-scale VAE inputs every score overflows and the output is all
NaN. In the other direction, an fp16 query under bf16 autocast missed
bf16 half math.

## Change

The mode casts to the active autocast dtype once, before the half math
gate, so the gate sees the dtype that actually runs. A bf16 query under
fp16 autocast now takes the fp32 upcast and stays finite. An fp16 query
under bf16 autocast takes bf16 half math. Without autocast nothing
changes. The Windows wide-head branch reuses the same cast instead of
repeating it. The stock chunked path now gets pre-cast tensors, which is
what autocast would hand the kernel anyway.

## Tests

`test_bf16_vae_under_fp16_autocast_gates_on_the_fp16_it_runs` uses
FLUX.1 VAE-scale bf16 inputs `[1,1,4096,512]` under fp16 autocast, with
the real dtype / ROCm / env gate and CPU tensors. On main it takes half
math, and a direct run of the same case gives 2,097,152 NaNs out of
2,097,152 outputs. Here it takes the upcast and every output is finite.
`test_fp16_vae_under_bf16_autocast_keeps_half_math` fails on main
because half math is skipped, and passes here.
`tests/test_diffusion_vae_attn_chunked.py`,
`tests/test_diffusion_windows_rocm_wide_head.py` and
`tests/test_diffusion_vae_full_map.py`: main has 2 failures, both of
them the new tests, with 89 passed. This branch: 91 passed.

## Not proven

The tests run on CPU with ROCm eligibility simulated. This PR was not
run on real ROCm hardware. That check would be the cross-dtype autocast
VAE decode on gfx103x and gfx1151 (`python -m pytest -o addopts="" -rs
studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_vae_attn_chunked.py`, then a 512 px
and 1024 px decode under each autocast direction, checking for finite
output and comparing against fp64). It is also not known how often
shipped pipelines call the VAE with a dtype that differs from the
autocast dtype.

Studio ROCm: an unanswered probe on an unverified card reads as math-only in split-device plans (#18571)

#17997 made Studio probe fused SDPA with AOTriton's experimental kernels
off on ROCm archs where they are not verified (gfx1103 and the other
iGPUs that hung in #17985), and when no probe child answered on such a
card, the parent turned flash and mem-efficient SDPA off and reported
MATH. That fail-safe only ran for a direct probe. Split-device placement
probes candidate cards read-only, so they do not flip the running card's
switches. A read-only probe that got no answer returned an empty tuple,
and `guard_rocm_fused_sdpa_cards` drops empty answers before
intersecting. So a split plan over a healthy gfx1151 primary and an
unanswered gfx1103 secondary left both fused flags on, and the secondary
ran unconfirmed experimental kernels under the parent's opt-in. The
read-only timeout also started the 120 s retry backoff without recording
forced math, so a direct check of the same card inside that window read
as unknown too, and the flags stayed on.

## Change

In `_probe_rocm_sdpa_kernels`, an unanswered fp16/bf16 probe on an
unverified card now reports MATH and records it as forced math in
read-only mode too. Read-only still never touches the process-wide
switches. During the backoff, a direct (not read-only) check that reads
a recorded forced MATH applies the math guard, so the parent runs what
the probe reports. As a result, split placement treats the card as
math-only (it drops a math-only secondary when the primary has fused
kernels, as it already did for a card that answered math-only), and the
committed guard disables fused kernels if such a card is still engaged.

Verified archs (gfx90a, gfx942, gfx950, gfx1100, gfx1101, gfx1151,
gfx1200, gfx1201) and `UNSLOTH_ALLOW_ROCM_FUSED_SDPA=1` are unchanged:
an unanswered probe there stays unknown, and the cards that answered
decide. Single-card loads already went through the direct probe and
behave as before.

## Tests

New in `tests/test_rocm_attention_recovery.py`:
- `test_split_guard_disables_fused_for_an_unanswered_unverified_card`:
real `guard_rocm_fused_sdpa_cards` over a gfx1151 card that answers and
a gfx1103 card that does not. Fails on main (both fused flags stay on),
passes here.
- `test_read_only_timeout_keeps_math_through_the_retry_backoff`:
read-only timeout, then a direct check inside the backoff. Fails on main
(reads `()` and keeps the flags), passes here.
- `test_split_guard_keeps_fused_for_an_unanswered_verified_card`: the
same split with a gfx1100 secondary keeps both flags on. Passes on main
and here.
- `test_unanswered_read_only_probe_leaves_the_flags` now expects the
read-only answer to be `("math",)` and still checks that the flags are
untouched.

`tests/test_rocm_attention_recovery.py`: 63 passed here, the 3 tests
above fail on main. The 33 Studio backend test files that touch
`diffusion_attention` or the split-plan SDPA helpers: the same 452 tests
fail on main and here (identical IDs, all in `test_video_backend.py` /
`test_diffusion_backend.py` and a few others, from this CPU
environment), with 3 more passing here. The ROCm, split and SDPA cases
of `test_diffusion_backend.py` / `test_video_backend.py`: 20 passed in a
full environment.

## Not proven

These are CPU tests with the probe children and arch reads mocked. No

Studio Restyle setup: keep a blob any other snapshot link still resolves to (#18570)

#18116 added a cleanup step to Restyle setup. Once the outputs are
verified, it removes the Hub shards that setup itself downloaded.
`_remove_cached()` unlinks the snapshot link and then deletes the blob,
unless another snapshot still references it. The reference check only
looked at the same relative file name in each other snapshot. Hub blobs
are content-addressed, so another cached revision can link the same blob
under a different file name. That link was left dangling, and an offline
load of that revision could no longer read the file.

## Change

Before the blob is removed, every symlink under the repo's `snapshots/`
directory is resolved. The blob is kept if any link still resolves to
it, whatever its name or revision, including another name in the same
snapshot. Paths outside Studio's cache for the repo and copy-only
(non-symlink) caches behave as before.

newer link and checks that the older one still reads the blob. It then
removes the older link and checks that the blob is gone. It fails on

Studio MiniMax-H3: bound reference audio resampling memory for rates coprime with 32 kHz (#18569)

#17764 added `resample_h3_audio`, which converts MiniMax-H3 reference
audio to 32 kHz before either engine (Diffusers or sd.cpp) sees it. It
builds the sinc filter as one dense table of shape `[new, 1, 2 * width +
orig]`, where `orig` and `new` are the two rates divided by their gcd.
For common rates the table is tiny (44.1 kHz is `[320, 1, 459]`), but a
rate that shares almost no factor with 32 kHz makes it enormous
regardless of clip length. A valid WAV at 44,099 Hz gives `[32000, 1,
44117]`, 5.3 GiB per float32 intermediate, and the filter construction
holds several of them at once. Resampling 1,024 samples (23 ms) of such
a clip peaked at 22.2 GiB of host RAM and took 8.6 s on CPU. The rate
comes straight from the uploaded container
(`stream.codec_context.sample_rate`), so any user upload can hit it.

## Change

When the dense table would exceed 4M elements (16 MiB in float32),
`resample_h3_audio` now evaluates the same filter only on the `2 * width
+ 1` taps around each output sample, in chunks of 65,536 output samples.
Every tap outside that window is clamped to the edge of the filter
window, where the dense kernel is below 1e-20, so dropping them changes
nothing beyond float rounding. The kernel values are computed with the
same float32 expressions as the dense path. Memory now scales with the
output length instead of the rate ratio.

Rates whose table fits under the threshold (44.1, 48, 22.05, 11.025, 16,
8, 96, 192 kHz and every other common rate) still take the existing
dense path, so their output is bit for bit unchanged and still equals
torchaudio's default kernel.

## Tests

- `test_resampler_memory_does_not_scale_with_the_rate_ratio` (44,099,
44,101, 8,001 and 32,001 Hz) runs the resampler on meta tensors and
records the largest tensor any op produces, requiring it to stay under
64 MiB. It fails on main (largest intermediate 5.3 GiB at 44,099 Hz) and
passes here.
- `test_windowed_resampler_matches_the_dense_kernel` forces the windowed
path on five rates and compares it with the reference dense
implementation: within 1e-12 in float64 and within 1e-6 in float32.
- Measured on CPU, 1,024 stereo samples at 44,099 Hz: peak RSS 22.2 GiB
and 8.6 s on main, 0.01 GiB and 0.03 s here; a 15 s clip at 44,099 Hz
takes 0.5 s and 0.03 GiB. Against a float64 oracle the float32 error is
the same on both sides (1.42e-4 main, 1.42e-4 here, dominated by the
float32 phase computation both share); main and this branch differ by at
most 7.2e-7 on unit-variance input. 44.1 kHz and 22.05 kHz output is
identical to main.
- `tests/test_h3_reference_recipe.py` plus the H3 and video test files
that import `video_minimax_h3`: same failing test IDs on main and on
this branch, no new failures.

## Not proven

- No comparison against `torchaudio.functional.resample` at a coprime
rate (torchaudio itself builds the same dense table, so it needs the
same tens of GiB); the windowed path is checked against the dense
formula instead.
- No GPU render with a coprime-rate reference clip; the resampler runs
on CPU before either engine starts.

Studio MiniMax-H3-Image: roll back a parked VAE upload that runs out of memory (#18566)

#18183 parks the MiniMax-H3-Image VAE on the host and uploads it around
each VAE phase with `HostParked.enter()` / `leave()`. `enter()`
increased `depth` before it uploaded, and `_put()` installs each tensor
on the module as it is moved. If the card ran out of memory part way
through the upload, some VAE tensors were left on the card, the rest
stayed on the host, and `depth` stayed at 1. Both VAE callers
(`_encode_references` and `_decode`) call `_enter("vae")` before their
`try/finally`, so `leave()` never ran for that failed entry. The next
request, including the render retry that streams more DiT blocks after
an out of memory error, then only increased `depth` to 2 and skipped the
upload, so the VAE ran with weights split across host and card.

## Change

`enter()` uploads first and counts the entry only when the upload
succeeds. If the upload raises, every tensor is put back on its existing
host copy before the error is raised again, so the module returns to its
parked state and `depth` is unchanged. Nested entries (depth already
above 0) do not upload and behave as before. The per-forward hooks still
work: when the pre-hook upload fails, the `always_call` forward hook
calls `leave()` at depth 0, and that call does nothing. The successful
path is unchanged.

## Tests

`test_a_parked_upload_that_runs_out_of_memory_rolls_back` parks a Linear
on the `meta` device and injects an out of memory error on the second
tensor upload. It checks that `depth` is 0 and both tensors are back on
the host after the failure, that a retry uploads both tensors again, and
that `leave()` parks them again. It fails on main (`depth` is 1 after
the failed upload) and passes here. I also checked by hand that a
per-forward parked module whose pre-hook upload fails returns to depth 0
on the host, and that its next forward runs on the device.

`tests/test_diffusion_h3_image_stream_layout.py`,
`test_diffusion_minimax_h3_image.py`,
`test_diffusion_minimax_h3_image_default_size.py`,
`test_diffusion_minimax_h3_image_parity.py`,
`test_diffusion_minimax_h3_image_speed.py`,
`test_h3_image_resident_route.py`, `test_h3_image_te_partial_pin.py` and
`test_diffusion_h3_image_trainer.py` on CPU: 220 passed, 59 skipped, 10
failed here. Main has the same 10 failures
(`test_backend_loads_and_generates`,
`test_the_request_ceiling_admits_every_family_side`, and the 8 tests in
`test_diffusion_minimax_h3_image_default_size.py`) plus the new test.

## Not proven

No GPU run. A real out of memory error during a parked VAE upload on a
CUDA card is untested. To settle it, cap a card to 8 GB, raise a
one-time `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` on the second tensor transfer in
`HostParked._put` during the VAE upload, then render an edit and a
text-only image. `depth` should go back to 0, the next request should
upload the VAE again, and the output should match a control render. The
sequential placement path in `_enter` (`module.to(device)` before the
`try`) is outside this change. Its next request moves the module again,
so a retry still works.

Studio ModelOpt FP8: never run the cold act-quant check or GEMM probe inside a CUDA graph capture (#18565)

#18432 added a fused static e4m3 activation quantiser to the ModelOpt
FP8 Linear (Cosmos 3). Before its first use on a card it runs a cold
byte-for-byte check against the eager formula (`_verify`), which builds
device tensors, calls `.tolist()` and turns `torch.equal` results into
Python decisions. `quantize_static()` skipped that check under Dynamo
tracing but not under CUDA graph capture. If the first call on a card
ran inside a recording, the check ran there, and any failure was cached
as `False` for that card for the rest of the process, so later eager
calls also lost the fused path. The W8A8 GEMM probe the same forward
runs first (`_gemm` calling `fp8_gemm_runs`, which reads `.item()` from
a probe `_scaled_mm`) had the same gap and the same cached-failure
behavior.

## Change

- `diffusion_fp8_act_quant.capturing(device)` asks whether a recording
is active on the operand's card (it selects that card when it is not the
current one; an unanswerable query counts as capturing).
- `ready()` with no verdict for the card returns `False` inside a
capture without running the check or recording anything. That call takes
the eager formula, and the first eager call outside the capture verifies
the card as before.
- `_gemm` with no probe result for the card returns `False` inside a
capture without probing or recording anything, so the recorded call
takes the existing dequantized path.

Warm cards are unaffected: a cached verdict or probe result is returned
before the capture query, so the fused path and the GEMM keep recording
into graphs exactly as now.

## Tests

- `test_cold_check_never_runs_inside_a_capture`: card 0 current, a
capture active on the operand's card 1, a cold card. Fails on main (the
check runs and `False` is cached), passes here (no check, nothing
cached, then the first call outside the capture verifies and caches
`True`).
- `test_gemm_probe_never_runs_inside_a_capture`: same setup for the GEMM
probe. Fails on main (the probe runs), passes here.
- `tests/test_diffusion_fp8_act_quant.py`,
`tests/test_diffusion_modelopt_fp8.py`, `tests/test_video_cosmos3.py`:
370 passed, 1 skipped here; on main the same files fail only the two new
tests.

## Not proven

These are CPU tests with the capture query and card selection mocked.
Studio's own graph wrappers (`diffusion_cuda_graph`,
`diffusion_block_graph`) run each forward eagerly on its card before
recording it, so this guards a first call made under capture rather than
a path those wrappers are known to take today. A real capture on a cold
sm_89+ card (and on a second card while card 0 is current) was not run
on hardware.

Studio multi-GPU: CFG replicas re-fuse MOSS-Image and Z-Image Q/K/V on their own card (#18559)

A guided load placed as one card plus a CFG replica copies the denoiser
with `diffusion_multigpu._copy_module`. MOSS-Image and Z-Image keep
their fused Q/K/V Linear outside the module tree
(`_unsloth_moss_fused_qkv`, `_unsloth_fused_qkv`), so the deep copy left
that Linear on the source card:

- MOSS-Image: the replica's record names the replica's own q / k / v, so
its identity check passes and the compiled `_qkv` runs the fused GEMM
with source-card weights on replica-card activations.
- Z-Image: the processor sees the device mismatch and runs three GEMMs,
but the source card holds a second copy of every fused Q/K/V weight.

FLUX.3 and Qwen-Image-2.1 already drop their fused records from the copy
and re-fuse on the replica. This does the same for MOSS-Image and
Z-Image: each gets `is_replica_record` (drop from the deep copy) and
`rebuild_replica` (re-fuse, on the replica's card, each module the
source fused, through the same `_fuse_linears` / `_share_storage` the
load uses).

## Tests

`tests/test_diffusion_cfg_replica_fused_qkv.py` (CPU): the replica
carries its own fused Linear whose storage the replica's q / k / v view,
with outputs equal to the source's; a copy to another device never keeps
the source's record. All 3 fail on main and pass here.

The multi-GPU, CFG replica, MOSS-Image and Z-Image suites (486 tests)
fail the same 11 test IDs on main and on this branch in this environment
(missing `jwt`, sd.cpp transport tests), none touching this code.

Not run here: a real two-GPU guided MOSS-Image / Z-Image render. On such
a host, a load placed as one card plus a CFG replica now keeps the
source card's fused weights to one copy, and the MOSS replica runs its

Studio: wallpaper composer fade, steady model picker height, effect render fixes, settings tidy (#18576)

## Summary

A set of chat polish fixes: wallpaper conversations no longer show text
through or under the composer, the model picker keeps one height across
tabs again, wallpaper effects stop failing on transient errors, the
header matches the wallpaper shade without glass, and a few settings and
composer sizes are tidied.

## Wallpaper: thread fades out behind the composer

With a chat wallpaper, the conversation scrolled behind the composer and
kept showing through it and in the gap below it, because the wallpaper
hides the solid bottom fade that normally covers that area. The thread
now runs to the composer's top edge and fades out within the 10px
beneath it (scaled with interface scale), so no text shows through the
composer body or below it.

- `ThreadComposerDock` measures the composer surface against the bottom
of the thread viewport and publishes `--thread-composer-clip` and
`--thread-composer-fade` on the thread root (cleared when the thread is
empty or the dock unmounts).
- The wallpaper mask on `.aui-thread-viewport` gains a steep fade
starting at that height.

Without a wallpaper nothing changes: only the wallpaper rules read these
variables.

## Wallpaper: header shade without glass

The wallpaper wash now sits on the thread root for every material (it
already did for Glass), so the header strip has the same shade as the
conversation instead of the brighter raw wallpaper. The extra header
darkening (`.chat-wallpaper::after`) is dropped for conversations
without glass. Glass, the new chat view and page routes keep their
current look.

## Wallpaper: "Could not render the effect"

The message, with blank previews, came from steps that fail for reasons
unrelated to the image:

- `HTMLImageElement.decode()` may reject while the image still loads
(the HTML spec allows it), and every wallpaper load awaited it directly.
Images now load through `loadImage`, which only fails when the image
itself fails to load.
- A tab still running the previous build asks for an effect worker file
the new build no longer has (404), so every effect failed until reload.
A worker that cannot start now falls back to the same transform on the
main thread.
- A later successful render clears a stale effect error instead of
leaving it up until the next setting change.

Both failure modes were reproduced by fault injection (a 404 for the
worker asset, and `decode()` rejecting every other call): before, the
error showed for Dither, Halftone and ASCII; after, no error and the
effect paints. Without injection I could not reproduce the error in
Chromium or WebKit.

## Model picker height

Since #18074 the open picker grew from 420px up to 540px with the number
of rows in the current tab, so it changed size when switching tabs. Its
height now comes from the window only, so every tab has the same height:
400px on short landscape windows, 420px up to a 1080px-tall window,
rising to 540px at 1380px and taller. It is measured in on-screen
pixels, so zoom does not change it, and it is still capped to the
window. The growth into the room under Select model
(`--composer-picker-max-h`, `--picker-room`) is removed; Run settings
keeps its own height.

Measured on every tab: 1440x900 = 400, 1920x1080 = 420, 2560x1230 = 480,
2560x1440 = 540.

- **Customization section:** Settings > Chat gets a Customization
section under Composer, holding Chat width, Composer position, Composer
outline and Monochrome model icons (moved from Model selection).
Composer keeps Send shortcut, Follow-up behavior, Share drafts and Plain
text composer, and gains Scroll while generating and Speed and context
stats from Chat defaults. The title is added to every locale.

- **New chat composer:** 8px shorter on the new chat page only (118px at
100% scale), all from the gap between the text and the bottom row. An
empty saved chat or the floating chat keeps 126px.
- **Compare composer:** reserves one row, like a conversation's

Studio sd.cpp: fall back to the PNG decode when a latent response cannot be parsed (#18572)

#18521 added a torch VAE decode for CPU FLUX.2 renders. The sd-server
returns the final latent and Studio decodes it, with a promised fallback
to the server's own PNG decode when the torch path fails. That fallback
only covered failures inside the torch decode.
`SdCppServer.img_gen_latents()` already parses and validates the latent
payload (float32 dtype, positive shape, base64, byte count) before it
returns, and it was called outside the fallback `try`. A completed job
whose latent was missing, misshapen or short therefore raised out of
`_generate_server` and failed a render that the PNG endpoint could still
produce. The path stays dormant with the default sd.cpp pin, which does
not advertise `output_latent`. It goes live once a server that does is
installed.

## Change

`_decode_latents` now raises `SdCppLatentFormatError`, a `RuntimeError`
subclass, so existing callers that catch `RuntimeError` behave the same.
The latent request moves inside the fallback `try`. A latent response
the client cannot use now takes the same fallback as a failed torch
decode: the decoder is switched off for the request, the fallback is
recorded, and the chunk is rendered again through `img_gen`. Every other
failure of the latent request is re-raised unchanged, including a failed
job, a timeout, a dead server and a cancel.

## Tests

In `studio/backend/tests/test_sd_cpp_torch_vae.py`:

- `test_a_malformed_latent_response_falls_back_to_the_server_decode`
sends completed jobs through the real `SdCppServer._decode_latents`
parser and `_generate_server`. Three responses are covered: a 1-byte
payload for a `[1,32,2,2]` latent, a zero-sized shape, and an image-only
response with no latent. On main all three fail, because the render
raises and only the latent request is made. Here all three pass: the
calls are `latent, png`, the PNG image comes back and one fallback is
recorded.
- `test_a_failed_latent_render_is_not_retried_as_png` checks that a
server-side generation failure during the latent request still raises
without a PNG retry. It passes on both main and here.

All 40 `tests/test_sd_cpp_*.py` files: 1791 passed, 134 failed on this
branch, and 1788 passed, 137 failed on main with the same test files.
The only difference is the three new fallback cases, which fail on main.
The 134 shared failures come from the CPU test environment (for example
a missing `av` module) and are unrelated to this change.

## Not proven

- Not run against a real latent-capable sd-server build. The malformed
responses are synthetic.
- A server that refuses the `output_latent` request itself (a submit
rejection or a failed job, for example a conditional refusal) still
raises rather than falling back. That error cannot be told apart from a
genuine generation failure, so this change leaves it out.

Studio LoRA placement: price PEFT embedding adapters (lora_embedding_A/B) in the measured reserve (#18568)

#17986 added a measured placement reserve for attached LoRAs, priced
from the widest adapted layer's unfused forward. The estimator only
looked for adapters in `lora_A`, but PEFT keeps an Embedding's factors
in `lora_embedding_A` / `lora_embedding_B`. An embedding adapter was
skipped as inactive, so a set that adapts an embedding next to a smaller
Linear got a positive price from the Linear alone and passed as
measured. Studio produces exactly this shape: Anima LoRAs that touch
`llm_adapter.embed` are converted to PEFT embedding keys on load.

With a rank-4 adapter on `Embedding(128, 8192)` and on `Linear(16, 8)`,
main priced the set at 80 bytes/token while the embedding forward
allocates 65,552 extra bytes/token.

## Change

`_widest_layer_bytes_per_token` now counts an adapter as active when it
is in `lora_A` or `lora_embedding_A`. For an embedding adapter it reads
the rank from `lora_embedding_A[a].shape[0]`, the dtypes from the two
Parameters, and the output width from the base layer's `embedding_dim`.
PEFT's embedding forward builds `[tokens, rank]` and then `[tokens,
out]` tensors, the same shape the Linear formula already prices, so the
existing `(2 * out + rank)` term and the dtype-mismatch term apply
unchanged. Linear, Conv, DoRA, merged and non-LoRA tuner handling are
untouched.

## Tests

`test_an_embedding_adapter_is_priced_at_least_its_forward` (fp16 and
fp32 adapter weights on an fp16 `Embedding(128, 2048)` plus a small
`Linear`) measures the embedding forward's live op-output bytes with a
dispatch mode and requires the price to cover them. Both cases fail with
main's estimator and pass here.

`tests/test_diffusion_lora_measured_placement.py`,
`tests/test_diffusion_lora_files.py`, `tests/test_diffusion_lora.py`
(PEFT 0.21.2, transformers 5.17.0, torch 2.14.1, CPU): 738 passed, 3
skipped here; main's estimator fails only the two new cases.

## Not proven

No GPU run: the reserve is checked against CPU op-output accounting, not
a real Anima load and render near a card's limit. Other PEFT versions
(0.18.0 floor) were not run here, though the `lora_embedding_A/B` layout
is the same across them.

Studio DiT training: record a failed text-encoder streaming setup as type and message only (#18567)

#18123 added text-encoder layer streaming for DiT training captioning.
When the streaming setup fails, `place_text_encoders` undoes any
half-streamed encoder and lets the caller move the encoders whole, but
first it stores the exception object in the module global
`diffusion_te_stream.LAST_ERROR`. The exception's traceback keeps the
placement frame alive, and that frame references the training pipeline,
the candidate encoders and, when the streamer constructor failed, its
partially built state (the host arena). So after one failed setup, the
pipeline and those host / GPU buffers stay referenced for the life of
the worker, even once training releases its own references. Nothing
reads the object itself: `LAST_ERROR` is only a diagnostic.

## Change

`LAST_ERROR` now holds `"Type: message"` (a plain string) instead of the
exception. The status a reader would need is still there. The traceback,
its frames and anything they reference are dropped when the handler
returns. Nothing else changes: the fallback, the undo of a half-streamed
encoder and the return value stay the same.

## Tests


`test_a_failed_setup_records_the_error_without_keeping_the_pipeline_alive`
makes the streamer constructor allocate a buffer and then raise through
the real `place_text_encoders` entry point. It checks that the error
type and message are recorded, then drops the last caller reference to
the pipeline, runs `gc.collect()`, and checks that the pipeline and
encoder are freed. On main it fails because the pipeline is still alive
through `LAST_ERROR`. With this change it passes.
`tests/test_diffusion_train_te_stream.py`: main 13 passed, 2 skipped
(CUDA) plus the new test failing. Head: 14 passed, 2 skipped.

## Not proven here

The test is CPU-only and uses a fake streamer. The real CUDA arena
release after a failed setup (memory returned to the allocator /
unpinned) was not measured on a GPU. That would need a run that injects
a failure into `TextEncoderStreamer` on a CUDA card and compares
`torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` and the pinned host total before and
after `gc.collect()`.

Studio training cond cache: evict only entries the cache wrote (#18564)

#18519 added a size cap to the persistent training conditioning cache,
with least recently used eviction. Eviction decided ownership from the
file name alone: any `*.safetensors` starting with `lat_v`, `txt_v`,
`h3clip_v` or `h3img_v` was counted and could be unlinked. The cache
directory can be set by the user (`cond_cache_dir`), so a user's own
file in that directory such as `txt_vintage.safetensors` or
`txt_v1_my_embeddings.safetensors` was deleted once a write crossed the
cap.

## Change

- Every entry written by `PersistentConditioningCache.put` now carries
an owner marker (`unsloth_cond_cache: 1`) in its safetensors metadata.
- `_entries()` only considers a file that passes all of these checks:
  - it is a regular file, not a symlink;
- its name matches a cache key (`lat|txt|h3clip|h3img`, then `_v` and a
version digit);
- its safetensors header has the marker. Entries written before this
change are also accepted when their header holds exactly the metadata
the cache wrote then (`version`, `family`, `none_slots`, `count` over
`t<i>` tensors), so existing caches stay bounded.
- Only the header is read, at most 1 MiB. Files that are unreadable or
unexpected are never counted or removed.
- Files already confirmed are remembered per instance by name, inode and
size, so a rescan does not read their headers again.

Reads, keys and stored tensors are unchanged.

## Tests

- `test_eviction_never_touches_a_user_file_named_like_a_cache_key`
writes valid user safetensors files named with every cache prefix, plus
one with a partial lookalike header. It then fills the cache past a 1
byte cap. It fails on main (the user files are unlinked) and passes
here.
- `test_entries_written_before_the_owner_marker_are_still_evicted`
checks that an entry with the pre-marker metadata is still evicted
oldest first. It passes on both.
- `tests/test_diffusion_train_cond_cache_default.py`,
`test_diffusion_cond_cache.py`, `test_diffusion_cond_cache_rekey.py`,
`test_diffusion_h3_trainer.py`, `test_diffusion_train_extras.py`,
`test_diffusion_bucketing.py`, `test_diffusion_cond_blocks.py`,
`test_diffusion_dit_trainer_ltx25.py` and
`test_diffusion_prompt_cache.py`:
  - main: 348 passed, 15 failed;
  - this branch: 350 passed, 15 failed.

The same 15 test IDs fail on both. They are environment failures
(missing `jwt` and similar optional modules on the CPU test host).

## Not proven

- The cost of the header read on a very large cache directory (tens of
thousands of entries) was not timed. It runs once per instance and again
only when eviction triggers.

Studio SDXL LoRA training: route the VAE's attention on ROCm before encoding latents (#18560)

#17953 fixed wrong training latents on Windows ROCm: the VAE's
single-head attention (head dim 512) went through fused SDPA kernels
that return garbage at that width. The fix routed the VAE's attention
through the exact path inference uses
(`diffusion_vae_attn_chunked.install`), but only in the DiT trainer. The
SDXL LoRA trainer runs in its own training process, never installs the
wide-head guard, and encodes every training latent through `pipe.vae`,
so SDXL LoRA training on Windows ROCm still encoded its latents through
the broken kernels.

## Change

The SDXL trainer calls the same `install(vae)` right after the VAE moves
to its card, before any latent is encoded. `install` acts only on ROCm
torch (CUDA, MPS and CPU builds return without patching), so nothing
changes off ROCm. On ROCm Linux, the VAE takes the same routed path the
DiT trainers and inference already use.

## Tests


`test_the_sdxl_trainer_routes_its_vae_attention_before_encoding_latents`
runs a real 1-step SDXL LoRA training on the tiny SDXL pipeline with a
ROCm torch reported. It checks that the pipeline's AutoencoderKL is
patched and that every encoder forward runs after the patch. It fails on
main (nothing patched) and passes here.

`tests/test_diffusion_gc_budget_trainers.py`: 62 passed.

Studio: clear the pending CUDA error after a refused host registration (#18502)

## Summary

A refused `cudaHostRegister` stays the calling thread's pending CUDA
runtime error. The callers already fall back to the pinned allocator
when registration is refused, but the next kernel launched on that
thread then raises the old error. For example, `CUDA error: part or all
of the requested memory range is already mapped`.

This PR clears the pending error with `cudaGetLastError` right after a
refusal, in:

- `_RegisteredHostBuffer.register()` (inference registered host buffers:
fast background pins, registered slabs, exact pinned chunks)
- `diffusion_te_stream._Registered` (training text-encoder stream)

The helper `consume_cuda_error()` lives in
`core/inference/host_pinning.py`. It resolves `cudaGetLastError` from
the process (or, if torch loaded the runtime locally, from the
`libcudart` the process already mapped), never raises, and with no CUDA
runtime (CPU or ROCm builds) does nothing. A successful registration
does not change.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_host_register_refusal.py`:
- CPU: the helper is safe without a runtime, and a refused registration
consumes the error.
- CUDA: register the same range twice, then launch a kernel, for both
call sites.
- On a B200:
- base fails both CUDA tests with the stale
`cudaErrorHostMemoryAlreadyRegistered`;
  - with this change all 5 pass;
- `test_video_fast_pin.py`, `test_video_exact_pin.py` and
`test_diffusion_registered_slabs.py` pass (34 passed, 3 skipped).
- CPU tests pass on torch 2.6.0 and 2.14.1.


## Second runtime mapped in the process (L4, torch 2.14.1+cu130)

A refused `cudaHostRegister` (the same range registered twice, error
712), then a kernel launch, each arm in a fresh process, with and
without NVIDIA's CUDA 12.9 runtime preloaded
(`LD_PRELOAD=libcudart.so.12`):

| clear | no preload | CUDA 12.9 runtime preloaded |
|---|---|---|
| none | next kernel raises 712 | next kernel raises 712 |
| `cudaGetLastError` from the global namespace (`CDLL(None)`) | runs |
next kernel raises 712: the clear went to libcudart.so.12 |
| `cudaGetLastError` through `torch._C` (this PR) | runs | runs |

Studio MiniMax-H3-Image training: key cached captions on the encoder that actually loaded (#18558)

MiniMax-H3-Image LoRA training caches caption embeddings keyed on the
text encoder scheme. The key used the requested scheme
(`UNSLOTH_H3_IMAGE_TEXT_ENCODER`, int8 by default), while
`load_h3_image_text_encoder` falls back to the bf16 encoder when the
hosted int8 file is unusable and reports which one it engaged. The
trainer dropped that report, so a run whose int8 load fell back stored
bf16 embeddings under the int8 key, and every later int8 run reused them
without loading the encoder: mixed conditioning that persists across
runs.

## Change

- `load_text_encoder` records the engaged scheme on the encoder.
- After the load, the cache is reopened under that scheme (the same
reopen that already handles a conditioner revision read after the first
download), so fallback embeddings are written under the bf16 key, and
anything served under the int8 key before the load is dropped.
- Nothing changes when the requested scheme loads, which is the normal
case.

## Tests

`test_h3_image_bf16_fallback_captions_never_serve_an_int8_run` (tiny
H3-Image release, CPU): a run whose loader reports a bf16 fallback, then
an int8 run, must load the encoder again, and a further int8 run must
hit its own entries. It fails on main (the int8 run is served the
fallback embeddings, 1 load instead of 2) and passes here.

`tests/test_diffusion_train_cond_cache_default.py`,
`tests/test_diffusion_h3_image_trainer.py`,
`tests/test_diffusion_gc_budget_trainers.py`: 69 passed.
`test_backend_runs_only_the_load_time_lora_set_for_h3_image` fails the
same way on main in this environment and is unrelated.

Studio: stop re-extracting a llama.cpp bundle that ships no DiffusionGemma visual-server (#18556)

## Summary

`Unsloth Updating Tests (macOS)` fails on every PR that runs it since
the llama.cpp prebuilt `b12540-mix-c4017f9` was published (02:00 UTC
today), e.g. #18550, which only touches `setup.ps1`:

```
FAILED tests/studio/install/test_update_idempotency.py::test_a_second_update_downloads_no_payload - release-assets.githubusercontent.com served a single 13456611 byte transfer to an update with nothing to do
FAILED tests/studio/install/test_update_idempotency.py::test_a_second_local_update_reuses_everything_it_can - a prebuilt was re-validated instead of answered from its marker
FAILED tests/studio/install/test_update_idempotency.py::test_the_desktop_update_path_keeps_a_verified_install_offline
... 7 failed, 10 passed
```

The tests are right: every macOS update now re-downloads and
re-validates a llama.cpp install that is already complete, including the
Desktop update path that is supposed to stay offline.

## Root cause

Two things combine:

1. The `b12540` macOS bundles ship without
`llama-diffusion-gemma-visual-server` (and `llama-diffusion-cli`). Every
other platform's bundle in that release has it. In the macOS release job
the best-effort DiffusionGemma build step failed under
`LLAMA_FATAL_WARNINGS=ON` (`'llama_batch_init' is deprecated ...
[-Werror,-Wdeprecated-declarations]`) and the bundle was published
without the binary, as that step allows.
2. `diffusion_visual_server_backfill_needed` (from #6267) re-extracts a
tag-matching install whenever a fork bundle's pattern list names the
visual-server and the binary is not on disk. That is meant for installs
made before the binary entered the copy allowlist, which a single
re-extract fixes. When the bundle itself does not contain it, the
re-extract can never land it, so the check fires on every update.
`_diffusion_visual_server_missing_for_marker` has the same gap on the
marker-only fast path.

## Fix

- After activation, `record_visual_server_absence` writes
`diffusion_visual_server_absent_from: <asset>` into
`UNSLOTH_PREBUILT_INFO.json` when the bundle just installed still leaves
the backfill check firing.
- Both backfill checks return False when the marker records that absence
for the installed asset.
- Nothing is recorded when the release also approves a standalone
visual-server artifact for this host: a failed fetch of that is
transient, and the next update's backfill retries it. The matching rule
is shared with `ensure_diffusion_visual_server` through
`_standalone_visual_server_artifacts`.

The record is keyed on the asset name, so:

- an older install without the field still gets its one backfill, as
before;
- a later release whose bundle does carry the binary is a different
asset and installs or backfills normally;
- a complete install or an upstream bundle never gets the field.

The write is best-effort through the existing atomic `_write_marker`,
and a failure only costs one more re-extract. DiffusionGemma
availability on macOS is unchanged: the binary is missing from this
release either way, and nothing else about install or update behaviour
moves.

## Testing

New tests in
`tests/studio/install/test_install_llama_prebuilt_logic.py`:

- the backfill still fires on an unrecorded install, stops once the
absence is recorded (plan and marker-only checks), and fires again for a
newer asset;
- a complete install, or a marker for another asset, is never rewritten;
- a release with a standalone visual-server artifact keeps its retry
path (a Windows-only `.exe` artifact does not count on macOS);
- an end-to-end `install_prebuilt` twice on a bundle without the
visual-server: the second run takes the already-matches skip and
installs nothing.

Removing the `record_visual_server_absence` call fails the end-to-end
test (`the second update re-extracted a bundle that has no
visual-server`).

Local runs:

- `test_install_llama_prebuilt_logic.py`,
`test_windows_cuda_lines_and_keep_coverage.py`,
`test_pr10648_host_matrix.py` and
`studio/backend/tests/test_llama_backend_selection.py`: 619 passed, 16
skipped.
- `tests/studio/install`: 2364 passed. The one failure,
`test_dependency_pass_skips.py::test_a_clean_manifest_plans_a_skippable_pass`,
fails the same way on `main` on this host.
- On Linux, `install_llama_prebuilt.py` run twice against `b12540` still
answers the second pass with "already matches".

The macOS release build itself is a separate follow-up in
unslothai/llama.cpp: the DiffusionGemma step should not inherit
`-Werror` from the main configure.

Studio video: Wan umT5 encodes only the real prompt tokens on a CPU or MPS text encoder (#18517)

## What

(512), run umT5 over every padded position,
then keep `hidden[:seq_len]` per prompt and zero the rest. The padded
keys are masked, so the kept rows do not depend
on them. `core/inference/video_t5_trim.py` wraps the pipeline's
`_get_t5_prompt_embeds` so the encoder runs on
`ids[:, :longest]` and the output is zero-padded back to 512: the same
embeddings up to fp32 reduction order, for a
fraction of the work.

Only when the encoder executes on `cpu` or `mps` (on a GPU the encode is
about a second), only for right-padded masks,
only for pipelines whose class name starts with `Wan`. Installed before
the prompt cache wraps `encode_prompt`.
`UNSLOTH_VIDEO_T5_TRIM=0` turns it off; `video_t5_trim.STATS` counts
trimmed and passed calls.

fp32), CPU, Colab VM (AMD EPYC 7B12, Zen 2,
8 threads), through diffusers' own `WanPipeline._get_t5_prompt_embeds`,
padded and trimmed in the same process, two
repeats each:

| Prompt | Real tokens | Padded (s) | Trimmed (s) | Speedup | Max abs
diff | Min token cosine |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| empty negative | 1 | 20.1 / 20.4 | 1.0 / 1.3 | 19.4x | 6.0e-7 | 1 -
3e-13 |
| short | 3 | 24.7 / 23.1 | 1.3 / 1.4 | 17.6x | 8.3e-7 | 1 - 2e-12 |
| one sentence | 26 | 26.4 / 24.9 | 2.8 / 3.9 | 8.9x | 9.5e-7 | 1 -
9e-13 |
| detailed | 66 | 23.8 / 25.1 | 4.5 / 4.8 | 5.2x | 1.5e-6 | 1 - 4e-12 |
| long | 196 | 21.9 / 20.9 | 9.0 / 8.6 | 2.4x | 2.5e-5 | 1 - 3.5e-9 |
| batch of 26 + 66 | 26, 66 | 40.4 / 38.5 | 5.8 / 6.2 | 6.6x | 1.5e-6 |
1 - 4e-12 |

`Security audit` / `pip scan-packages :: hf-stack` fails on `main` (push

Summary: 6 HIGH, 175 MEDIUM

    HIGH  unsloth-zoo  unsloth_zoo/compiler.py                           same matched code, file digest outside the pin
