provider: a relay key bills at its sub2api group rate times the provider's top-up rate (@YIXIE233 on X)

@YIXIE233 has several sub2api relays. Each reports a key's group rate at
GET /v1/sub2api/billing, and each sells its dollars at its own price (¥1
for $1 at one, ¥7 for $100 at another). Until now every key's rate was
typed by hand and typed again whenever a relay changed its prices.

Now a provider of API keys has a "Top-up rate" under Advanced, next to
Price rate (TopUpRate: above 0 up to 1000, at most four decimals). With
one set, the gateway's KeepKeyRatesRead asks each key's relay for its
rate in the background. It reads at start, every 6h, 30 min after a
failed read, and at once on a save that sets a new top-up rate. It is
never on a request's path. The relay asked is the origin of its sub2api
key query, else of its first base; loopback and vendor hosts are never
asked. Readings go to key-rates.json beside providers.json.

A key then bills at group rate x top-up rate, and that rate reaches both
places a price is used: PriceAt (Cheapest/By price routing) and
BaseKeyPriceIn (the ledger, Usage, spend caps). A group rate of 0 prices
at 0 (zeroRate), not at the list price.

- A key's own KeyPriceRates still wins.
- A key never read, or whose reads all failed, is unknown and bills at the
  provider's PriceRate, never 1x.
- A failed reread keeps the last rate it read.

The Usage caches key on a hash of the rates read, so a reread that finds
the same rates keeps them. /api/providers lists keyGroupRates, which the
editor names under the box. An empty per-key line's placeholder shows
group rate x top-up rate. `magpie provider key-rate` lists both. i18n:

Fix 106 redundant_void_return violations

Summary:
NOTE: This diff does not enable the rule. It uses SwiftLint's autocorrect to fix 106 violations in 37 files, mostly tests. The next diff fixes the other 67, which need a human review. 16 violations in 9 files stay: there the autocorrect doesn't compile or changes behavior.

It leaves these files unchanged:
- `fbobjc/Apps/Instagram/AppLibraries/BaselMac/MCEMacFontRegistrar/MCEMacFontRegistrar/MCEMacFontRegistrar.swift`: the autocorrect doesn't compile
- `fbobjc/Apps/Instagram/AppLibraries/Shared/IGQuantumSignalsKit/IGQuantumSignalsSwift/IGQuantumSignalsTrustedWallClock.swift`: the autocorrect doesn't compile
- `fbobjc/Apps/Instagram/AppLibraries/Shared/IGSearchChaining/IGSearchChaining/__tests__/IGSearchChainingFeedLifecycleTests.swift`: the autocorrect changes behavior. Without `-> Void`, each `will { … in Task.onMain { … } }` closure is a single expression returning a `Task`, so it picks another `will` overload and the stubbed `updateModels` never records a response (`IGSearchChainingTests` failed in CI)
- `fbobjc/Apps/Instagram/Features/Direct/IGMinorEducationFlowPlugin/IGMinorEducationFlowPlugin/IGMinorEducationFlowManager.swift`: the autocorrect doesn't compile
- `fbobjc/Libraries/CACapture/CACapture/core/mainview/CAMainViewModel.swift`: the autocorrect doesn't compile
- `fbobjc/Libraries/FWA/Common/AppleHealthKit/AppleHealthKit/__tests__/AppleHealthManagerTests.swift`: the autocorrect doesn't compile
- `fbobjc/Libraries/FWA/Common/FWAGallery/FWAGallery/FWAGalleryViewModel.swift`: the autocorrect doesn't compile
- `fbobjc/Libraries/FWA/Features/Ring/MuseLiveReplyVoice/MuseLiveReplySpeaker.swift`: the autocorrect doesn't compile
- `fbobjc/Libraries/Hatch/Voice/HCHVoiceCallUI/HCHVoiceInternalSettingsView.swift`: the autocorrect doesn't compile

## What the rule does
[redundant_void_return](https://realm.github.io/SwiftLint/redundant_void_return.html): Returning Void in a function declaration is redundant.

## Rule info
- **Type**: default (not opt-in), kind [idiomatic](https://realm.github.io/SwiftLint/Enums/RuleKind.html), correctable
- **Options**: `include_closures` (this diff keeps the defaults)

## Example
**Before**:
```swift
try { () throws -> Void in
```

**After**:
```swift
try { () throws in
```

## Why it helps
`-> Void` adds nothing to a function or closure that returns nothing, so dropping it removes noise from signatures.

Type `idb ui text` on the simulator's hardware keyboard layout (#1002)

Summary:
## Motivation

`idb ui text` maps each character to a key position with a US table in the client and sends key presses. On a simulator whose hardware keyboard layout is not US the guest types different characters: `idb ui text mobiletest@example.com` arrives as `,obiletest2exq,ple:co,` on French, and characters off the US keyboard fail with "No keycode found". See https://github.com/meta/idb/issues/666.

What changes:

- `HIDEvent` gains a `text` event (`HIDText`: the text and an optional layout name). The companion turns it into key presses for the layout with `Simulator.keyboard.typingEvent` (added in the framework pull request this depends on).
- The companion advertises this as `CompanionInfo.hid_text` (field 13).
- `Client.text(text, layout=None)` sends one `HIDText` event to a companion that advertises it.
- `idb ui text TEXT --layout LAYOUT` names a layout to type on, such as `US` or `French`. Without it the companion uses the simulator's own.
- A character the layout has no key for, or a layout the runtime does not have, fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before anything is typed. The message names the character's offset and the layout.

Compatibility:

- Old client, new companion: the client still sends key presses, which the companion handles as before.
- New client, old companion: `hid_text` is absent, so the client sends the same US key presses it always has. A `--layout` other than `US` is refused in the client before any event is sent.
- `--layout US` sends the key presses `idb ui text` sent before this change, on any simulator, for every character the US table has.
- On a simulator set to US, the default sends the same key presses as before. On any other layout the default now types the text itself, which is a change for callers who pre-mapped their text to US positions; `--layout US` restores the old behaviour.

Known limit: an app keeps the hardware layout it was launched with. The layout is read from the simulator's keyboard settings, so after changing the simulator's keyboards either relaunch the app or pass `--layout`.

The `hid` stream handler resolves a leading text event before taking the HID lease, so reading the simulator's keyboard settings does not hold up other HID streams. Orientation, shake and hinge actions still run only under the lease. Physical devices refuse `HIDEvent.text` as unimplemented, as they refuse other key presses.

Pull Request resolved: https://github.com/meta/idb/pull/1002

- `./build.sh test CompanionTests`: 225 tests pass. `./build.sh test CompanionLibTests`: 163 pass. `./build.sh test FBSimulatorControlUnitTests`: 513 pass. `./build.sh build all` succeeds.

It restores the keyboard settings it changes.

Type text on the simulator's hardware keyboard layout in FBSimulatorControl (#1001)

Summary:
## Motivation

`SimulatorHIDEvent` key presses are USB HID usages, which name key positions. The helpers that turn text into key presses (the REPL's `text` command here, and `idb ui text` in the client) map characters to positions with a US table, so on a simulator whose hardware keyboard layout is not US the guest types different characters: "azerty" arrives as "qwerty" on French. See https://github.com/meta/idb/issues/666.

This adds the framework support for typing text on a given layout:

- `SimulatorHIDEvent.text(_:layout:table:)` builds the key presses for a string from a layout table. Every character is resolved before any event is built, so text with a character the layout has no key for throws `SimulatorHIDError.characterNotOnKeyboardLayout` and sends nothing. The error names the character's offset and the layout, not the character, so typed text stays out of logs.
- `SimulatorUSKeyboardLayoutTable` is the US table that was private to the REPL's command dispatcher. A test pins it entry by entry to `KEY_MAP` in `idb/common/hid.py`.
- `SimulatorUCHRKeyboardLayoutTable` reads every other layout from the runtime's own `USBKeyboardLayouts.bundle`, the data the guest types with, including option and dead-key sequences. The planned key presses are replayed through `UCKeyTranslate` and refused if they would not reproduce the text.
- `Simulator.keyboard.typingEvent(for:layout:)` types on a named layout, or on the one the simulator's keyboard settings give a newly launched app (`AppleKeyboards`, `AppleKeyboardsExpanded`, `KeyboardLastUsed`, and `AppleLanguages` when the keyboards have not been written yet). A layout that cannot be determined is assumed to be US, and the reason is logged.

The REPL's `text` command now goes through this, so it follows the simulator's layout. On a simulator set to US it sends the same key presses as before for every character the US table has; characters outside that table that the runtime's US layout can type, such as "é", are now typed instead of refused.

Known limit: an app keeps the hardware layout it was launched with. The layout is read from the simulator's keyboard settings, so after changing the simulator's keyboards an app has to be relaunched before the two agree.

No change to `idb.proto`, the gRPC server or the Python client.

`FBSimulatorControl` now imports `CoreServices` for `UCKeyTranslate`. The Xcode build links it through autolinking; the generated `project.yml` and `LibraryPackage.json` do not list it and I have not edited them.

Pull Request resolved: https://github.com/meta/idb/pull/1001

End a device app's output streams once it has been stopped

Summary:
`launch -w` hands the target consumers for the app's stdout and stderr, and once the app has been stopped the companion waits for those consumers to finish before it ends the response. A device does not relay an app's output, so nothing ever ended those streams. Before the preceding changes this went unnoticed, because stopping a device app failed and the RPC ended with that error. Now that the stop succeeds, `launch -w` followed by Ctrl-C stopped the app and then hung: the client waited for a response that never ended.

Stopping a launched device app now ends the output streams it was given, after the stop has succeeded. If the stop fails, the streams stay open and the error is reported as before.

Cancel a launch when the client gives up before the app starts

Summary:
The launch RPC honoured cancellation only once the app was running, while it waited for Stop or exit. A client that disconnected while the launch itself was still in progress (Ctrl-C, or the client being killed) left the companion waiting on the launch. On a device that is a `devicectl` launch, which could hang indefinitely when CoreDevice could not reach the device.

`LaunchMethodHandler` now runs the launch under the RPC's cancellation, as it already runs the wait. A cancelled RPC cancels the launch, and the device library then stops its `devicectl` process.

Once Stop has been accepted, the app's termination now runs outside the RPC's cancellation and is joined before the handler returns. A client that disconnects right after sending Stop can no longer cancel a stop that is still in progress. Before, it ran inside the cancellable scope, so a termination that suspends, such as a device's `devicectl` kill, could be cancelled part-way and leave the app running.

A `launch -w` client that sends Stop before the launch has returned still waits for the launch to end, which the device library now bounds.

The wire is unchanged.

Bound devicectl runs and stop them with their caller

Summary:
`FBDeviceControl` runs `xcrun devicectl` to launch apps, kill processes and take screenshots on iOS 17 and later. Those runs had no time limit and were not tied to their caller. When CoreDevice cannot reach a device (`devicectl list devices` shows it as "connecting"), `devicectl device process launch` never returns, so `idb launch` hung for as long as the companion lived, and the `devicectl` process kept running after the client had gone.

Every `devicectl` run now:
- passes `devicectl` its own `--timeout` (60 s). The host also stops it if it is still running 10 s after that.
- is stopped when the calling task is cancelled. The run uses `Subprocess.withRunning`, which sends SIGTERM and escalates to SIGKILL. A kill is the exception: once asked for, it runs to completion within the same bound even if its caller is cancelled, and the caller waits for it. Stopping its `devicectl` part-way could leave the app running after a stop the companion had already accepted.
- fails with `DevicectlError.timedOut` when it times out. The message names the device's connection state as `devicectl list devices` reports it (itself bounded to 10 s), for example: `devicectl did not finish within 60s, so it was stopped. CoreDevice reports the device's tunnel state as 'connecting' (pairing state 'paired', transport 'localNetwork').`

Healthy runs finish in a few seconds: a launch in 1–2 s, a screenshot in about 3 s. The 60 s bound leaves room for `devicectl` to mount the developer disk image first.

Summary:

- **Running apps.** The trace relay's `PidList` keys processes by decimal string on current iOS, where it used to use numbers, so `running()` found no processes at all: `list-apps` showed no pids, and `terminate` could not find the app it was asked to stop. commits.message:
fix(mobile): name identity-link mention pills from their key (#9841)

Follow-up to [#9699 mention
typing](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9699), fixing two identity
problems found in its review.

**Identity-link pills name the key they open.** An edit writes each
mention as an identity link, `[@Name](nostr:npub1…)`, and every message
from any client draws such a link as a pill. Mobile showed the label
written in the link, so `[@Wes](nostr:<mallory>)` drew an ordinary
`@Wes` pill that opened Mallory's profile, and two namesakes in an
edited message both read `Scout`. The pill now shows the name its key
resolves to in the channel (with the namesake qualifier and agent icon),
as buzz-app's `ProfileMention` already does. The written label shows
only when the key has no name on this device (no profile, directory or
roster name), never a compact npub in its place. This holds whether or
not the link's key is also tagged. A pill requests its key's profile
when uncached, so a written label gives way to the key's name once it
loads.

Edits carry no `p` tag, so an identity-link pill resolves its own key.
In channel, thread and forum rows the pill watches that one key's
channel label (with the namesake qualifier and agent icon) and requests
the key's profile when it builds, so only links that actually draw a
pill cost a lookup, whatever Markdown surrounds them. Inbox and search
previews draw identity links the same way, taking keys from the preview
pieces they render. These keys never feed the text bindings, so plain
`@Name` text still binds only through signed tags.

**Typed names group the way the text scan reads them.** The composer
grouped the roster by `toLowerCase` while the scan folds names with
`foldMentionLabel`. With members `Sam` and `ſam`, typing `@ſam` sent
Sam's `p` tag. Grouping, lookup and the send-time key qualifier now all
fold, so namesakes under folding fail as ambiguous, as other namesakes
already do.

**Linked lookups stay current and bounded.** Pills and preview rows
request their keys through the profile cache's revalidation path. A name
restored from the last launch is revalidated, so a renamed key's link
shows its current name. A lookup that fails while offline is retried
once the relay reconnects, including when the reconnect comes while that
lookup is still on the wire. A key the relay says has no profile is not
asked for again for five minutes, and the cache remembers at most 1,000
such keys per community. Previews keep tilde and quoted code fences
literal and read blockquotes as the full message does, and load only the
links on lines they draw. Editing a message folds historical names the
way the scan does, so a name two tagged people share under folding seeds
no chip. Rendering binds signed names by the same fold, so with signed
`Sam` and `ſam` a plain `@Sam` stays text instead of drawing Sam's pill.

Desktop (buzz-app) already names identity-link chips from the key and
needs no change.

### Validation

Rows add no per-message work: message bodies are no longer scanned for
links. Each drawn identity-link pill adds one label watch for its own
key.

Added tests:
- [Channel page journey
step](mobile/test/features/channels/channel_detail_page_test.dart): an
edited message linking `[@Wes]` to Mallory's key draws `Mallory`, and
two edited `Scout` namesakes draw distinct qualified labels, through the
real channel row.
- [Channel page journey
step](mobile/test/features/channels/channel_detail_page_test.dart): a
link to a key with no name here keeps its written label.
- [Preview identity
link](mobile/test/features/channels/message_content/preview_text_test.dart):
an inbox/search preview shows the key's resolved name, or the written
label when unknown.
- [Preview
keys](mobile/test/features/channels/message_content/preview_text_test.dart):
a preview loads only links it draws (not ones in code or past its line
limit), including labels with brackets.

Full-app run (iOS simulator, debug build, signed in to a test
community): posted a message with a spoofed identity link, a link to a
key with no profile here, and a link inside inline code. The spoofed
link drew the key's real name as a pill and opened that person's
profile; the unknown key kept its written label; the code span stayed
raw. The same message drew matching pills in search results and in the
thread view.
- [Channel row
loads](mobile/test/features/channels/channel_detail_page_test.dart): a
row requests profiles only for links it draws as pills, not ones in a
quoted code fence or an HTML comment.
- [Folded chip
qualifiers](mobile/test/features/channels/compose_bar_test/exact_mention_tests.dart):
picked `@Sam` and `@ſam` chips both carry their keys on send.
- [Ambiguous typed names
table](mobile/test/features/channels/compose_bar_test/exact_mention_tests.dart):
`Sam` and `ſam` in either roster order now refuse `@ſam` as ambiguous.

- [Restart and reconnect
journey](mobile/test/features/channels/channel_detail_page_test.dart): a
restored old name and an offline first lookup both resolve after the
relay reconnects, on the same mounted pills, and a key with no profile
is not requested again.
- [Preview
fences](mobile/test/features/channels/message_content/preview_text_test.dart):
tilde and quoted fences keep links and Markdown literal and load no
keys.
- [Overtaken
lookup](mobile/test/shared/profile/user_cache_provider_test.dart): a
reconnect during a link's failing lookup asks once more after it
settles.
- [Folded signed
names](mobile/test/features/channels/message_content_exact_mentions_test.dart):
signed `Sam` and `ſam` in either tag order leave `@Sam` as text in the
message and its preview.
- [Folded edit
chips](mobile/test/features/channels/message_edit_sheet_test.dart):
`Sam` and `ſam` tagged in either order open as text, with no chip.
- [Non-member
labels](mobile/test/shared/identity_names/identity_names_test.dart): a
non-member labels the same with or without the roster shortcut,
including names shaped like qualifiers.

### Regressions

- **Performance:** rows do no new scanning; each drawn identity-link
pill adds one label watch. A non-member whose name can't collide no
longer re-resolves the whole roster.
- **Mention semantics:** unchanged for tagged mentions and plain text.
Only identity-link pills change, from the written label to the key's
resolved name.
- **Composer:** names that differ only under Unicode folding (`ſ`/`s`,
`µ`/`μ`, final `ς`/`σ`) are now one name when matching typed text, so a
typed one between two such members asks for a pick instead of silently
choosing one. Picked chips are unaffected.

---------

Signed-off-by: Tom Brow <tomb@block.xyz>
Co-authored-by: studio <dc2fc481343672df31a689840c09299972e704dac592e0da6f18486646a7ee3e@buzz>

fix(mobile): fence notification replies by the clock and settle ones whose community is gone (#9668)

Follow-up to #9439 (iOS notification reply), which merged before these
non-blocking review points landed.

- **Publish fence checks the clock.** `mayPublish` now compares
`DateTime.now()` with the publish deadline as well as the timer flag,
before and after writing the publishing mark. After a suspension, a
pending lookup can finish before the overdue timer callback runs;
without the clock check the reply could publish past its deadline, after
iOS already showed "Reply not sent".
- **A recovered reply whose community is gone settles.** If the
community was removed, or the user signed out, before the relaunch,
`_keepDraft` used to throw, so the reply stayed in the native journal
(with its text in `UserDefaults`) and was retried on every launch. It
now keeps no draft and the reply is settled as not sent.
- **Doc fix:** `SendMessage`'s `mayPublish` is asked after signing and
after the optimistic local message is shown; the doc now says so.
- **Test fix:** the resume test asserts the EVENT frame reached the
original socket before `onAppResumed`, so the injected OK can't pass it
on its own.

### Regressions

None expected. The clock check can only refuse a publish the timer would
also refuse moments later. A recovered reply for a missing community now
drops its text instead of keeping it forever in a journal no launch can
drain; there is no community left to show it in.

### Validation

-
[notification_reply_test.dart](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/notification-reply-fence-followup/mobile/test/features/channels/notification_reply_test.dart):
the recovered reply for a missing community now expects to be settled.
-
[relay_reconnect_resume_test.dart](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/notification-reply-fence-followup/mobile/test/shared/relay/relay_reconnect_resume_test.dart):
asserts the EVENT frame before resume.

Signed-off-by: Tom Brow <tomb@block.xyz>
Co-authored-by: studio <dc2fc481343672df31a689840c09299972e704dac592e0da6f18486646a7ee3e@buzz.block.builderlab.xyz>
Co-authored-by: studio <dc2fc481343672df31a689840c09299972e704dac592e0da6f18486646a7ee3e@localhost>

perf(mobile): stop measuring every character of long drafts on iOS (#9825)

On iOS, a long draft in the message composer could freeze the app. In
one case the main thread was blocked for 72 seconds.

Flutter's stylus handwriting support (Scribble) is on by default in
every iOS text field. After each frame whose text layout changed, it
measures the field's text one character at a time, so iOS knows where
each character sits on screen. Every measurement walks the paragraph's
lines, so one pass costs time proportional to the square of the draft's
length, and it runs again after every keystroke. Every sampled stack in
the hang reports sits in `EditableTextState._updateSelectionRects` →
`RenderEditable.getBoxesForSelection` → `getBoxesForRange`.

iOS also uses those character positions for the keyboard trackpad's
two-finger selection (hold Space, add a second finger, drag). So this
keeps handwriting on for drafts up to 2,000 characters and turns it off
past that, on iOS only, in the two fields where messages are written:
the composer and the message edit sheet. Android never takes these
measurements, so it keeps stylus handwriting at any length. The edit
sheet rebuilds only when its draft crosses the cutoff, not on every
keystroke. Whenever a draft crosses the cutoff, any open iPad Scribble
writing gap is closed first, because Flutter ignores iOS closing it once
handwriting is off. This holds even when the field no longer has focus,
since iOS can close the input connection itself (for example on keyboard
dismiss) without Flutter removing the gap.

At 2,000 characters a pass should cost under a millisecond,
extrapolating from the measurements below (cost grows with the square of
the length).

### Validation

One handwriting measurement pass in the running app (iPhone 17 Pro
simulator, debug build), timed in-app with a draft of `the quick brown
fox jumps over` lines:

| Draft length | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 23,250 chars | 100 ms | 0 ms |
| 46,502 chars | 360 ms | 0 ms |
| 93,000 chars | 1,376 ms | 0 ms |

Before the fix, this cost was paid on every keystroke. Release builds on
older phones run slower than the simulator on this Mac.

- Added test: [iOS measures each character only of shorter
drafts](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/brow/mobile-text-layout-hang/mobile/test/features/channels/compose_bar_test.dart)
checks that a short draft still sends iOS its character rectangles, a
draft past the cutoff clears them (iOS would otherwise keep the shorter
draft's), and shortening it again restores them. It also checks that a
draft crossing the cutoff while the composer doesn't have the keyboard
sends nothing, since iOS applies the clear to whichever field is
focused.
- Added test: [iOS closes a Scribble writing gap when a draft gets
long](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/brow/mobile-text-layout-hang/mobile/test/features/channels/compose_bar_test.dart)
opens a writing gap, pushes the draft past the cutoff, then sends iOS's
own close, and checks that no gap is left in the draft.
- Added test: [Android starts stylus handwriting in a long
draft](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/brow/mobile-text-layout-hang/mobile/test/features/channels/compose_bar_test.dart)
checks that a stylus tap still starts handwriting past the cutoff on
Android.
- Added test: [iOS closes a Scribble writing gap left after losing
focus](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/brow/mobile-text-layout-hang/mobile/test/features/channels/message_edit_sheet_test.dart)
opens a writing gap in the edit sheet, has iOS close the input
connection, then pushes the draft past the cutoff (as a late paste
would) and checks that no gap is left.
- Added test: [iOS turns stylus handwriting off only while the edit is
long](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/brow/mobile-text-layout-hang/mobile/test/features/channels/message_edit_sheet_test.dart)
opens the edit sheet on a long message and shortens it.
- Automated app run on the simulator, signed in to a test community:
typed in the composer, used the edit menu (Select All, Paste), sent a
message, then edited it in the edit sheet and saved.

### Regressions

- In iOS drafts over 2,000 characters, the keyboard trackpad's
two-finger selection and Apple Pencil handwriting stop working, and iOS
may place its autocorrection highlight at the field's corner instead of
over the word. Ordinary cursor movement with the trackpad, selection
handles, the edit menu, dictation and typing are unaffected.
- If a paste pushes a draft past the cutoff and undo brings back the
exact earlier text, Flutter skips resending the unchanged rectangles, so
iOS has none until the next edit or until the field scrolls (which a
long round trip usually does). Flutter offers no public way to force the
resend.
- The channel description and create-agent Instructions fields can also
hold long pastes and still pay this cost on iOS. They aren't in the hang
reports, so they're left for a separate change.

Co-authored-by: studio <dc2fc481343672df31a689840c09299972e704dac592e0da6f18486646a7ee3e@buzz.block.builderlab.xyz>

Cache recently opened mobile channel pages (#9809)

## What changed

Previously opened channels can show their newest saved page after a cold
launch, including offline. The same timeline provider combines the saved
page with live edits, deletions, and optimistic sends. When the relay
has loaded history, its timeline takes over and older-page navigation
becomes available. The chat labels saved messages until relay history
takes over. If a connected refresh fails, the chat offers Retry and
keeps the saved-message label visible during the retry.

- Keep verified relay events in a disposable, app-private SQLite cache
per community and signing identity on iOS and Android. Close SQLite
connections after each operation.
- Cap the main file at 45 MiB to leave room for a rollback journal
within the 100 MB per-community limit. Evict least-recently opened pages
and retry once when SQLite reaches the physical limit.
- Omit an oversized relay page as a whole so the cache cannot show a
message without an edit or deletion from the same response. Keep
readable pages available when only the recency write fails.
- Purge on leave, deletion, explicit channel access refusal, and
writer-confirmed loss of a known membership. Expired sessions leave the
cache intact. SQLite secure deletion clears removed payloads after
commit. A durable marker covers interrupted purges. Account switches and
removal retire old saves.
- Keep message-link lookups valid across the first connection. An access
refusal still discards a late result.
- After a confirmed leave or delete, record a durable cache purge before
refreshing the channel list. Disk cleanup runs in the background and the
refresh skips redundant writer confirmation for that channel.
- For joined, unarchived channels, remove stale saved rows on
channel-tagged deletions or edits the app receives while the
conversation is closed. Reuse deletions from the existing reconnect
catch-up.
- Give an already-connected relay one 250 ms head start before reading
the saved page. Offline opens start the read immediately.

## Screenshots and timing

[iPhone 17e simulator
captures](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9809#issuecomment-7050704433)
show the same seeded chat before the cache, with saved messages while
offline, and after the relay returns. In the debug capture run, the
baseline `9c0bcd623` showed no messages within 8 seconds. The updated
build `2cb28eda` showed the target saved message **752 ms** after the
tap.

For a first online open on the same simulator, the baseline and the
instrumented `2cb28eda` build took **449 ms** and **441 ms** median from
tap to target message. Each build had four measured opens after one
warm-up. The ranges were 437–481 ms and 414–447 ms.

In the earlier paired debug simulator experiment on `6e113d83`, the 250
ms preview delay reduced median first online open from **507 ms to 452
ms** across 15 measured opens per build. In the delay build, seeded
offline opens took **488–557 ms** across the two channel medians, and
reopens in the same app session took **174–245 ms**. All 20 offline
opens and reopens showed the target message.

## Verification

- The mobile pre-push gate and file-size check passed for `6650ebad`.
Regression tests cover oversized pages, session expiry versus channel
revocation, live mutations during preview, paging after relay history
loads, writer-confirmed membership loss, closed-chat edits and
deletions, the saved-message label across Retry and history takeover,
links held across first connect, and interrupted or overlapping purges.
- The host SQLite probe interrupted eviction, relay-key rotation, and a
synthetic table rewrite. All three reopened with a clean integrity
check. The largest observed database and journal footprint was 93.84 MB.
- Physical iPhone suspension, airplane-mode reopen, and profile-mode
timing are pending.

## Try it

1. While connected, open a populated channel and let its newest page
save.
2. Force-quit, turn on airplane mode, and reopen the same channel. The
saved page should appear.
3. Reconnect. The relay's newest page should take over without
duplicating messages.

A saved page can still show stale rows while the phone stays offline,
for a live edit missed while the app was stopped, for an archived or
unjoined public channel, or for a NIP-09 deletion without a channel tag.
Reconnect catch-up covers the deletions returned by its bounded unread
query. A direct online open refreshes the page. Offline thread replies
are separate follow-up work.

fix(mobile): keep Move to section working after the actions sheet closes (#9814)

Move to section has been failing on mobile: choosing a section, creating
a new one, or removing the channel from its section throws a
`StateError` ("Using ref when a widget is about to or has been
unmounted") and the channel stays where it was.

- **Disposed ref.** The section picker opens from the channel actions
sheet, which closes first. The picker read and wrote sections through
that sheet's `WidgetRef`, which is disposed by the time the user taps a
row. It now uses the page's `ProviderContainer`, which it already used
to listen for desktop's layout lock. Channel details passed its own
`ref` the same way and now goes through the same path.
- **New section never filed the channel.** It created the section, then
looked it up by name in the provider's state, which local edits only
reached after a relay round trip. The notifier now creates the section
and files the channel in one call, by the new section's ID, so a second
section with the same name can't catch it either.
- **Local edits show at once.** `createSection`, `assignChannel` and
`unassignChannel` now emit the notifier's state right away, as
`deleteSection` already did, so a picked or removed channel moves in the
sidebar immediately instead of after the relay echoes the edit.
- The New section dialog disposed its text controller while still
animating out; the dialog now owns its controller.

### Validation

- [Move to section
journey](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/0147d7a0f2f005e47dcb5aec201dc5d3f255846c/mobile/test/features/channels/channel_actions_sheet_test.dart):
opens the picker from the actions sheet with the real sections notifier
(storage and relay faked) and checks the shown and saved section after
picking a section, Remove from section, and New section, including when
a section with the new name already exists.
- Automated iOS simulator run (iPhone 17 Pro, signed-in Builderlab
account): long-press a channel, Move to section, then New section (with
a name that already existed), pick an existing section, and Remove from
section. Each move showed in the sidebar immediately and no errors were
logged. The recording shows real channel names, so it is shared
internally rather than here.

### Regressions

None expected. The picker reads the same provider from the same root
scope (mobile has a single `ProviderScope`), through a handle that
outlives the closed sheet. Emitting after local edits rebuilds section
listeners once per edit, which Delete section already did.

acceptance: read the probe key from a file; dial a connect address (#9773)

## Summary

Follows https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9771 (merged), which added
the acceptance CronJob.

Some NIP-FI issuers bind each key to one identity. A deployment that
mints a new identity for each run then needs a new key for each run,
written next to the assertion before the probe starts. The probe could
only take its key from an argument or the environment, which a
Kubernetes init container can't set.

- **Probe:** `--private-key-file` (`BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE`) reads the
key (hex or nsec) from a file. It conflicts with `--private-key`.
- **Shared read:** the key file and the assertion file use one bounded
reader, `acceptance::read_secret_file`. It needs a regular, non-empty
file under a size cap.
- **Report:** the JSON report now includes `pubkey`, the hex key the
probe ran as. An operator can match a run to the identity that was
minted for it.
- **Chart:** `acceptance.privateKeyFile` is passed as
`--private-key-file`, not as an env var, so a probe that predates the
flag fails instead of running with a new key. Exactly one of it and
`acceptance.privateKeySecret.name` must be set; rendering fails with
neither or both.
- **A new key per run needs an agent assertion** (`nip-fi-agent+jwt`
whose `nostr_owner_pubkey` is a relay member). A members-only relay
refuses a new person key, and an open relay joins it to every auto-join
channel. The README and `values.yaml` say so.
- **Connect address:** `--connect-addr` (`BUZZ_ACCEPTANCE_CONNECT_ADDR`)
dials a plaintext `host:port` for every WebSocket connection and for the
NIP-11 fetch, for a probe that can't reach the relay's public host. The
relay URL still sets the `Host` header, the NIP-42 relay tag and the
NIP-11 `Host`, so the relay serves the same community. On that path,
NIP-11 uses no proxy, follows no redirect and requires a 2xx answer. The
chart passes `acceptance.connectAddr` as `--connect-addr`, not as an env
var, so a probe that predates the flag fails the run instead of checking
the public URL. The default is empty.
`NostrWsConnection::connect_to_addr` now takes upgrade headers, so the
NIP-FI assertion goes on this path too; loadgen passes none. (Folded in
from #9830.)
- **Chart version 0.1.13** with an `artifacthub.io/changes` entry. It
publishes the acceptance CronJob from #9771, the key file and the
connect address.

- **Follow-up test from the #9767 review:** the fake relay gets an
`accept_mismatched` setting, and
`access_control_fails_when_the_relay_accepts_another_keys_write` expects
`access_control` to fail at `pubkey_mismatch_rejected`. A
`pubkey_mismatch_rejected` stage that always returns Ok now fails a
test.

## What got simpler

The assertion reader's inline bounded read is now the shared
`read_secret_file`, so both secret files follow one rule instead of two
copies of it. The probe's four connection call sites now share one
`open` helper, and `connect_to_addr` reuses the same `upgrade_request`
path as `connect_with_headers`.

## Testing

- `e2e_acceptance`:
`the_binary_authenticates_with_the_key_from_its_key_file` passes against
a live relay with the key path in `BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` (the same clap
argument as `--private-key-file`). It checks that the report's `pubkey`
is the file's key, so a probe that ignored the file and made a new key
fails.
- `e2e_acceptance`: `the_binary_exits_2_when_it_cannot_run` covers a bad
key, a bad key file, a missing key file, and both key flags at once.
Each exits 2 with no report and no metrics.
- Existing unit tests cover the shared reader through the assertion file
(missing, empty, oversized, directory, FIFO).
- `connect_addr_dials_the_address_and_keeps_the_relay_url`: the probe
runs at an unresolvable `wss://relay.invalid` with the fake relay's
address. Every upgrade has `Host: relay.invalid` and the assertion's
bearer header, and every AUTH relay tag is `wss://relay.invalid`.
- `nip11_goes_to_the_connect_addr_with_the_relay_host` (`GET
/relay?route=probe`, `Host: relay.invalid:8443`) and
`nip11_at_the_connect_addr_does_not_follow_a_redirect` (a 301 fails
`nip11` with no version).
- `caller_user_agent_replaces_default` now covers `connect_to_addr` too.
- `tests/acceptance_test.yaml`: `acceptance.connectAddr` renders
`--connect-addr <addr>` in the args, and the default args do not have
it. The key file renders as `--private-key-file <path>` in the args,
with neither `BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` nor `BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY`, a Secret
plus a file fails, and no key source fails.

fix(mobile): bring @mention typing in line with buzz-app (#9699)

## Summary

The mobile composer's @mention typing was an older port of the mention
rules that [block/buzz-app](https://github.com/block/buzz-app) follows
(`src/bundled/mentions/README.md` there), and it trailed buzz-app in
nine places. Most of them came from one difference: mobile tied a picked
person to the `@Label` text and looked for that text again at send time,
while buzz-app keeps the recipient on an atomic chip. Several of the
gaps meant a picked person was silently not notified.

This PR fixes all nine. Every change is in `mobile/`; no relay, CLI or
desktop code is touched, and the event payloads mobile writes keep the
same shape.

### Commits

| Commit | Fixes | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| 9152e91fe | 1, 2 | Picked people are atomic chips, as agents already
were. The recipient comes from the chips, so a pick after `(`, `[` or
`{` notifies. Backspace removes the trailing space, then the whole chip;
arrows step over a chip. |
| 2cbdabdae | 3, 4 | A chip is bound to its recipient by its position in
the draft and keeps it through punctuation, apostrophes, hyphens and
slashes. Namesake chips read `@Sam · a1b2`, and the draft text never
holds a public key. |
| c4d3f2072 | 5 | A chip's `@` never opens a query, so prose typed after
a pick sends no directory searches. A query that found nobody refutes
every longer query that continues it. |
| 4e4ac3efd | 6 | Name matching folds accents, full-width letters and
ligatures, and breaks words on hyphens and apostrophes. The vendored
contract fixture moves from version 1 to version 4, and all 125 cases
pass. |
| 38e8f2e1e | 7 | Closing punctuation (`. , ! ? ; :`, `)`, `]`, `}` and
closing quotes) selects an exact, unique name as Space does, and the
character stays after the chip. |
| e008151c6 | 8 | The chooser is shown only while the text field has
focus. The query and its rows are kept while hidden, so refocusing shows
the same rows without a new search. |
| 199606969 | 9 | The edit sheet mounts the composer's chooser through a
shared hook. A pick inserts a chip, and the saved edit adds no `p` tag.
|
| a1e4d69fa | 3 | The message renderer ends a mention where the composer
does, so a sent `@Honey's report` draws Honey's pill with the suffix as
text. |
| bf34af139 | 2 | iOS reports one Backspace as two editing updates
(select the character, then delete the selection). The controller
recognises that pair and removes the whole chip and its binding. |

### How to read the videos

Each video has three columns that follow the same numbered steps with
the same people and the same typed text: mobile before this PR on the
left, mobile on this branch in the middle, and buzz-app on the right.
The bar across the top names the current step, and a column that
finishes a step early holds its frame until the others catch up.

The dark panel on each phone is a readout added for the recording. Its
`p tags (notified)` line shows who a sent message would notify, and
`directory searches sent` counts requests to the directory. The readout
under the buzz-app composer shows the same facts.

### 1. A mention picked after a bracket keeps its recipient

`see (@Honey) please` went out with nobody notified, because the
send-time scan did not accept the brackets the chooser did. The
recipient now comes from the chip, and the typed-name fallback accepts
`(`, `[` and `{` too.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1f1c76b-b991-4f90-9079-a435c4475c2b

### 2. People mentions are atomic chips

A second Backspace used to leave plain `@Hone` (and `@Scou` for the
agent), which sent with no recipient. Now the first Backspace removes
the trailing space and the second removes the whole chip, and the arrow
keys step over a chip as one unit.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a198656c-d735-46a7-a954-9e0aa4af7dc3

### 3. A suffix after a mention keeps the recipient

`@Honey's report` and `@Honey-bot is back` notified nobody. A chip now
survives an apostrophe (straight or curly), a hyphen, a slash or
punctuation typed against it, and the sent bubble draws the pill with
the suffix as text. Only a letter, mark, digit or underscore typed
against the chip unbinds it.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c481110d-1633-4c01-9810-a8d750ce2ae2

### 4. No raw public key in the composer

Picking two people with the same name filled the draft with two
64-character keys. Each pick is now a chip with a short label, the draft
text stays `@Honey`, and each namesake gets their own `p` tag. The key
suffixes on the labels differ between the apps only because each
recording generated its own keys.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f56cddd-a96f-43cb-820b-511eb965a77b

### 5. No directory search while typing prose

Every character of a sentence typed after a pick was sent to the
directory as a name search: 20 searches in this clip. The count now
stays at 1, the same as buzz-app. A short query with no local match
still searches, so a person outside the channel is still found.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3575b2cf-e3a6-42f1-9779-6e1401f00dfc

### 6. Accent folding and contract fixture version 4

`@jose` could not find José María, so `@jose maria` went out as plain
text. Names now fold accents, the row stays listed, and the pick is a
chip that notifies José María. The vendored fixture is version 4 of the
shared contract, copied unchanged, with no case skipped.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/362f6b4b-a09c-4f69-910e-8903408be77e

### 7. Closing punctuation selects an exact name

A comma typed straight after `@Honey` or `@Outside Person` joined the
query and closed the chooser; for a person outside the channel the
message went out with no recipient and no prompt. The comma now selects
the exact name, and Send shows the outside-channel prompt, where Invite
adds the person and sends with their `p` tag.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b43a0663-489f-4ae3-ae36-7a2a92443f9e

### 8. The chooser follows the field's focus

Dragging the keyboard away collapsed the composer but left the chooser
row floating above it. The chooser now hides when the field loses focus
and returns with the same rows when focus comes back. Step 1 of the
mobile columns is sped up three times, because the on-screen keyboard is
slow to drive in the simulator.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ce0093d-03d0-4792-9b05-fb28980830fc

### 9. The chooser works in the edit sheet

The edit sheet was a plain text field with no chooser. It now uses the
composer's chooser with the same rules, and existing mentions open as
chips. The saved edit adds no `p` tag, matching buzz-app's rule that an
edit notifies nobody.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54d5620-ae2d-49b5-8cce-99536b8d81db

### Known gaps left for follow-up

- **Typed, unpicked names.** Mobile still notifies a typed name that
equals exactly one member and refuses to send an ambiguous one. buzz-app
does not do either, and the shared contract has not settled which is
right.
- **Directory-only names selected before the search finishes.** Space or
closing punctuation selects a directory-only name as soon as it is in
the ranked rows. buzz-app waits until that query's search has finished.
This predates the PR for Space and now also applies to punctuation.
- **Undo does not restore a chip.** After a letter typed against a chip
unbinds it, Undo restores the text but not the chip. iOS shake-to-undo
also bypasses the new undo detection.
- **Edits drop existing tags.** The timeline reads mention tags from the
edit event, so editing a message that already tagged someone still loses
that pill. Carrying the original tags through an edit is a separate
change.
- **`_@Name_` italics.** `_` now counts as a name character, as in
buzz-app, so `_@Honey_` no longer draws a pill.

### Related issue

N/A. None found; #9008 made the relay's name search accent-insensitive,
and fix 6 does the same for matching on the device.

### Testing

- `dart format`, `flutter analyze`, `just file-size-check` and the full
mobile `flutter test` suite passed on every commit. Two timing-sensitive
tests unrelated to mentions (relay socket liveness, community snapshot
cleanup) each failed once under full-suite load and passed solo.
- Each fix has a widget-test journey through the real composer, chooser
and send path, and each was shown to fail with its fix removed. The
shared contract fixture runs in full.
- The videos are harness recordings on an iPhone 17 simulator (iOS
27.2): the real channel page, composer, chooser, edit sheet and send
path on an in-memory relay, not the app against a live community. The
buzz-app column is a headless WebKit recording of buzz-app's fixture
pages.
- Android and physical devices were not exercised.
- The branch was pushed with `--no-verify`, so the pre-push lanes did
not run locally.

deploy: run buzz-acceptance from the relay image as a chart CronJob (#9771)

## Summary

Builds on #9767 (the `buzz-acceptance` binary, now merged). Based on
main.

- **Image:** the relay image now carries `buzz-acceptance` next to
`buzz-admin` and `buzz-pair-relay`, so no new image or workflow is
needed.
- **Chart:** `acceptance.enabled=true` adds a CronJob that runs the
probe from the relay image.
- Requires `image.tag` or `image.digest`. The chart fails to render
without one, because the default `Chart.AppVersion` image has no probe.
- Every 5 minutes by default, `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`,
`backoffLimit: 0` (a retry would hide a failure),
`activeDeadlineSeconds: 240`.
- Runs with `acceptance.serviceAccountName` or the namespace default,
never the relay's service account. No token mount, no service links.
- `acceptance.relayUrl` (defaults to `relayUrl`),
`acceptance.stageTimeoutSeconds`.
- `acceptance.privateKeySecret.name` is required. Without a key the
probe would sign with a new key each run: a members-only relay refuses
it, and an open relay joins each new key to every auto-join channel.
- `acceptance.statsdAddr` sends DogStatsD metrics. `$(HOST_IP)` expands
to the node IP, for a node-local agent.
- Every series carries `probe_revision`, the probe's own image
(`image.digest`, else `image.tag`), plus `acceptance.tags`. It does not
identify the relay build a run reached: during a rollout, or with
`acceptance.relayUrl` set, the probe can reach another build.
`acceptance.tags` keys must be canonical (lowercase `[a-z0-9_./-]`,
starting with a letter, not ending in `_`), so the probe-owned and
repeated-key checks see the key Datadog stores.
- NIP-FI: minting an assertion is deployment-specific, so the chart
takes it as a file. `acceptance.extraInitContainers`, `extraVolumes` and
`extraVolumeMounts` let an init container write it, and
`acceptance.assertionFile` points the probe at it. These follow the
existing relay Pod extension points.
- **README:** a new "Acceptance probe" section with an example. The
example gives the minter init container the key Secret, keeps
credentials in a memory `emptyDir`, and says how to size
`activeDeadlineSeconds` against `stageTimeoutSeconds`.
- **Chart version:** bumped once at the top of the stack, in
https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9773

## What got simpler

The chart no longer has a "no key" mode, so there is one way to give the
probe its identity. The probe reuses the relay image and the chart's
existing CronJob, image-identity, label-guard and extension patterns, so
it adds no new image, no new publish workflow, and no new extension
concept.

## Testing

- `tests/acceptance_test.yaml` (helm-unittest): off by default; the
default render (relay image, `relayUrl`, no key, no metrics, no extra
volumes); a full render with a key Secret, metrics, tags, a
digest-pinned image, and an init-container-minted assertion; the
chart-owned Datadog version label; the required image tag or digest;
`probe_revision` from the probe's image even with another `relayUrl`; no
service account inheritance or token mount; and rejection of a missing
probe key (also with an assertion file), a tag without a key, an
uppercase tag key, a tag key with a space or a trailing `_`, a
probe-owned tag key, a repeated tag key, and a chart-owned pod label.
The init-container test pins the full `initContainers`, `volumes` and
`volumeMounts`.
- CI builds the relay image from the changed `Dockerfile`.

Migrations up to `0104` dropped every trigger, function and foreign key.

`migrations_after_retirement_add_no_triggers_functions_or_foreign_keys`
scans each migration numbered after `0104`. It fails on `CREATE [OR
REPLACE] FUNCTION | PROCEDURE | TRIGGER | RULE`, `CREATE CONSTRAINT
TRIGGER`, `CREATE EVENT TRIGGER`, `REFERENCES` and `FOREIGN KEY`,
outside `--` comments. The error names the file and line, for example
`migrations/0105_probe.sql:2: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`. Nested `/*

except a string passed to `EXECUTE` or `format(`. Each dollar-quoted
body is scanned as SQL up to its closing delimiter, so DDL run through

--lib` unit lane.

feat(relay): list and revoke invite links (#9680)

Stack: this PR → #9690

## What this does

Adds listing and revocation for v2 invite links, and makes every reader
of an invite's expiry accept a missing value.

- **`GET /api/invites?limit=&before=`** lists the community's v2
invites, newest first: id, creator, created/expiry/revoked times, uses
and a computed `status` (`active`, `revoked`, `expired`, `exhausted`).
Owner/admin only. The NIP-98 signature covers the full URL including the
query. `limit` defaults to 50 (max 200). `next_before` is an opaque
cursor holding the last row's `created_at` (microseconds) and id, so
paging doesn't depend on that row still existing.
- **`POST /api/invites/revoke`** takes exactly one of `{"id": "<uuid>"}`
or `{"code": "v2...."}`. The code is hashed and looked up only inside
the request's community. v1 and malformed codes get `400
invite_not_revocable`; an invite not in the community gets 404. Revoking
twice returns the first `revoked_at`. Members who already joined stay.
- **Authorization.** Mint, list and revoke share one HTTP admission
helper (tenant bind → NIP-98 via NIP-FI → replay → membership/ban →
NIP-OA owner link → role gate). Revoke's final decision is made in the
write transaction, in the same order as mint: admission lock → actor's
role row `FOR SHARE` → restriction check → invite row `FOR UPDATE`.
Owners and admins can revoke any invite; any other member only one they
created. A removed or restricted actor is refused. Mint now uses the
same role-lock helper.
- **Mint response** now includes `invite_id`.
- **Nullable expiry readers.** Claim, list, the mint response and
operator mint treat a missing `expires_at` as "never expires". The
column is still `NOT NULL` here.
- **Secrets.** No list/revoke response or access-log line contains a
code or its hash; request errors are fixed strings that never echo
input. Revoke logs only `invite_id`. A revoke the database refuses is
logged as denied with its reason.

## Deploy order

A follow-up PR adds links that never expire (`expires_at` nullable).
**It depends on this PR being deployed everywhere first**, so every
serving relay can read a missing expiry before one is written.

## Tests

- DB (`relay_invite/manage_postgres_tests.rs`): revoke by code targets
exactly one of two near-identical invites, idempotent revoke, community
scoping, creator demoted to member can revoke theirs, a member who
didn't create it is refused, a removed creator is refused, a restricted
admin is refused, a demotion holding the role row or a restriction
holding the admission lock makes revoke wait and then refuse with the
row unchanged, a paused claim and a revoke serialize with the member
kept, revoke is refused while the community is quiescing, paging
survives deleting the cursor row, and a row with no expiry is listed,
claimed, kept by the reaper and revocable (on a scratch database with
`NOT NULL` dropped).
- Relay (`invites/postgres_tests/manage_tests.rs`): list/revoke by id
and code end to end, no code or hash in responses, member/non-member
refusals, bad selectors, other-community lookups, query-string signature
binding, malformed requests not echoing a code in responses or access
logs, refused revokes logged as denied, and replayed list/revoke
requests refused.

fix(push-gateway): answer 429, not 404, when the delivery quota is exhausted (#9803)

When an endpoint's delivery quota is exhausted, both authority stores
returned `AuthorityError::Rejected`, so `/v1/deliveries` answered `404
invalid_grant`. NIP-PL already specifies `429 {"error":"rate_limited"}`
for this case.

The 404 matters because the relay treats a 404 on a retry attempt as a
terminal replay and completes the wake, so a throttled wake was silently
dropped. On a first attempt it failed the wake. A 429 takes the relay's
existing retry-with-backoff path instead.

### Change
- Memory and Postgres stores return `RateLimited` on quota exhaustion.
`http.rs` already maps that to `429 rate_limited`.
- The rate-limited attempt still charges no quota and consumes no
auth-event or request-id fence, so the relay's retry with the same
request id is admitted once the window reopens.
- No doc change: NIP-PL and the deployment doc already describe 429.

### Validation
- Memory store: an exhausted quota returns `RateLimited`, leaves replay
rows and the quota counter unchanged, and the same auth event and
request id are admitted after the window.
- Postgres (ignored test, run locally against a temporary database): the
quota-ceiling race test now also asserts the loser is `RateLimited`.
- HTTP: the eleventh delivery under a quota of ten answers `429
{"error":"rate_limited"}` and reaches no transport.
- With the two store lines reverted, all three tests fail.

### Regressions
None expected. Only the quota-exhaustion result changes; grant,
authority and replay failures still collapse to `404 invalid_grant`.

fix(push-gateway): retry, don't drop, a delivery replayed while its first attempt is in flight (#9802)

The relay gives up on a push gateway delivery call after 2 seconds and
retries the same `request_id` with a fresh NIP-98 event. A gateway send
can take much longer than that: an FCM token mint has a 15 second
deadline, and the APNs and FCM sends each have a 15 second timeout. A
retry that arrived while the first attempt was still sending hit the
request replay fence and got `404 invalid_grant`. The relay reads a 404
on a retry as "the earlier attempt already finished" and completes the
wake. If the first attempt then failed retryably, nothing ever sent the
wake, and the notification was silently lost.

This change makes the gateway tell an in-flight request apart from a
finished one:

- Admission records the request id as in flight. A terminal outcome
marks it finished, and a retryable outcome releases it, as before.
- A replay of an in-flight id now gets `503
{"status":"retry","retry_after_seconds":5}`. Nothing is sent and no
quota is charged, so the relay's existing 503 path retries with backoff.
- A replay of a finished id still gets 404, so the relay's existing
handling of a finished attempt is unchanged.

Postgres gets a `finished` column on
`push_gateway_delivery_request_replays` (gateway migration 0009,
mirrored in relay migration 0105). It defaults to `true`, and the
gateway writes `false` explicitly on admission. Rows written before this
migration, or by an older gateway during a rollout or rollback,
therefore keep today's behavior. The constant default adds the column
without rewriting the table.

### Validation

-
[`replay_while_first_attempt_is_in_flight_is_retried_not_dropped`](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/3deaefb2b8f550484c8f15f8910e00d422c6f83e/crates/buzz-push-gateway/src/http_delivery_tests.rs)
holds a first send open in the transport. It checks that a retry of the
same request gets 503 retry without sending, that the first attempt's
retryable failure releases the id so the next retry sends, and that a
finished id still answers 404.
-
[`replay_of_unfinished_request_is_in_flight_until_it_finishes`](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/3deaefb2b8f550484c8f15f8910e00d422c6f83e/crates/buzz-push-gateway/src/authority.rs)
covers the in-memory store, and
[`unfinished_request_replay_is_in_flight_on_real_postgres`](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/3deaefb2b8f550484c8f15f8910e00d422c6f83e/crates/buzz-push-gateway/src/postgres.rs)
covers Postgres, including that an in-flight replay charges no quota.
- The gateway's Postgres suite, including the desired-state schema
parity test, ran against a local PostgreSQL 17.

### Regressions

- A gateway that crashes mid-send now leaves the request id in flight
until the request expires, so the relay keeps retrying until its attempt
limit (8 attempts, about 10.5 minutes) or the request expiry, whichever
comes first. Before this change it got a 404 and dropped the wake.
- Admission now runs one more indexed primary-key read inside the
transaction that already locks the installation row.

feat(test-client): add buzz-acceptance relay probe (#9767)

## Summary

Adds `buzz-acceptance`, a third binary in `buzz-test-client` (next to
`buzz-loadgen`). One run checks the relay's core jobs once against one
relay and exits. It is meant to run on a schedule (for example a
Kubernetes CronJob) or as a deployment step (for example an Argo
Rollouts `job` analysis against the canary Service).

Checks, in order:

| Check | Stages |
|---|---|
| `relay_info` | `nip11` (the response must be a NIP-11 document) |
| `connect_auth` | `ws_connect`, `nip42_auth` |
| `channel_create` | `create` (a private, per-run channel with a 1 h
TTL) |
| `publish` | `ok` |
| `fanout` | `connect_second`, `subscribe`, `publish`, `receive` |
| `history` | `req_eose` (the published event is in a fresh REQ, intact)
|
| `access_control` | `unauthenticated_rejected`,
`pubkey_mismatch_rejected` |
| `cleanup` | `connect`, `delete_channel` (on a fresh connection) |

`access_control` passes only on the relay's own denial reasons:
`auth-required:` for a write on a socket that sent the NIP-FI assertion
but skipped NIP-42 AUTH, and `invalid: event pubkey does not match
authenticated identity` for a write signed by another key. A closed
socket or any other reason fails the stage.

`fanout` reads the listener while the publish waits for its OK, so
`receive` measures delivery (publish → arrival on the second socket),
not the publisher's acknowledgement.

`fanout` and `history` verify the event they get back (`Event::verify`:
id and signature against its content). An event the relay corrupted
under its original id fails the stage.

A channel is never stranded on purpose. If the create times out or the
socket drops, the probe keeps the channel id and `cleanup` deletes it
over a fresh connection. A failed cleanup names the channel. The TTL
archives any channel a killed run leaves behind.

Output:

- A JSON report on stdout: each check's result, the stage that failed,
and each completed stage's duration.
- Optional DogStatsD metrics (`--statsd-addr`): `<prefix>.runs`,
`<prefix>.run.seconds`, `<prefix>.check.runs{check,result,stage}`,
`<prefix>.check.seconds{check,result}`,
`<prefix>.stage.seconds{check,stage}`. Every series also carries
`relay_version` (from NIP-11) and any `--tag k:v`.
- Exit code 0 when every check passed, 1 when a check failed, 2 when the
probe could not run or send its metrics.

A check whose prerequisite failed is reported as `skipped`, so each
failure is counted once, at its cause, and every run reports the same
set of checks.

### NIP-FI

On a relay that enforces NIP-FI, pass `--assertion-file` (a regular
file, at most 16 KiB; a FIFO or larger file fails the connection at
once). The probe reads the file before every connection and sends it as
`Nostr-Federated-Identity: Bearer …`. Another process (for example a
sidecar) keeps it fresh. How the assertion is minted is deployment
configuration and stays out of this repo.

## What got simpler

Nothing got simpler. This adds one binary. It reuses `buzz-ws-client`
and the crate's existing dependencies, and adds no new crate and no new
dependency (`clap` gains its `env` feature).

## Testing

- Unit tests drive the probe against a scripted relay: a publisher OK
that arrives 600 ms after delivery (`receive` stays under 300 ms), a
refusal with the wrong reason and a closed socket (both fail
`access_control`), an unanswered create and a socket lost after create
(both still delete that exact channel), and a failed cleanup (the error
names the channel). Also: metric lines and tags, one datagram per line,
stage timeout, assertion file limits, and an unreachable relay.
- `tests/e2e_acceptance.rs` runs in CI's Relay E2E lane against a live
relay. It runs the shared runner and the binary itself: exit 0 with JSON
and datagrams on a pass, exit 1 when a check fails, exit 2 when the
probe cannot run.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Image and CronJob / Rollouts wiring.
- Before the probe can gate a canary: a dial override that keeps the
canonical Host and signed relay URL (like `buzz-loadgen`'s
`connect_addr`).
- Before it can gate a promotion: a build identifier from the relay.
`relay_version` is the Cargo package version, which several image builds
can share.
- Confirm the delete took effect: read the channel back after
`delete_channel` returns `OK true`. This needs a stable relay read
contract for deleted channels. Until then the 1 h TTL bounds any channel
a silent delete failure leaves behind. The scheduled deployment can also
sweep stale probe channels at start.

feat(relay): add pinned messages (nip-pm) (#9729)

## Summary
Implements NIP-PM on the relay. A member signs one command to pin or
unpin a message, and the relay publishes the channel's pins as one
relay-signed list. The NIP is `docs/nips/NIP-PM.md`, added in #9712.

- **Kinds.** `40010` pin and `40011` unpin commands (one `h`, one `e`,
empty content) and the relay-signed `30623` pin list, one addressable
event per channel, newest pin first. The list carries the channel in `d`
and in `h`.
- **Ordering.** Every writer of a channel's list takes that list's
replacement lock, so pins, unpins and deletes of pinned messages apply
one at a time. A command, the new list and the notice are stored in one
transaction.
- **Idempotency.** A command sent again answers `duplicate:` and is not
applied again. Pinning a pinned message or unpinning an unpinned one is
accepted and changes nothing.
- **Validation.** The author must be able to post in the channel, and
the channel must not be archived. A pin target must be a live message of
that channel. A channel holds at most 250 pins.
- **Deletes.** A delete by the author, the owner of the agent that wrote
the message, a channel admin or a relay admin removes the message from
the list in the deleting transaction and publishes the new list. A
delete removes its messages first and then takes the list locks in
channel order, rewriting each list once. Each list write records its
timestamp, and a delete reads that first: a delete of a message that is
not pinned locks only its own month of `events`, plus the list month
when the channel has a list (#9743). The pin list itself cannot be
deleted.
- **Notice.** A pin that changes the list posts a `message_pinned`
system message naming the member, the message and the command.
- **Reads.** The list is readable by those who can read the channel.
Clients read it with `#h`, which names the channel under NIP-CL, and
each new list is delivered to `#h` subscribers.
- **Configuration.** None. A relay running this build accepts the
commands; it does not advertise pins in NIP-11.
- **Threads.** A pin or unpin command cannot be the parent of a reply or
the target of an edit or a vote.
- **Account erasure.** Content cleanup removes a member's pin and unpin
commands. One under an hour old keeps its ID, timestamp, kind and
channel so that a resend stays a duplicate. The leader's periodic
maintenance tick removes those records once the command is an hour old.
`docs/operator-user-account-retention.md` describes this.

### Related issue
N/A. #8809 is an earlier draft of message pins with a different event
model.

### Testing
- Postgres-backed store tests for the list writes: ordering, concurrent
pins, resends, the limit, deletes, the lock order of a delete of several
messages, the partitions a delete locks, the refusal to delete the list,
erasure records and their expiry across communities.
- Postgres-backed handler tests through ingest and REQ: the pin and
unpin journey with notices and live delivery, who can read the list
(private channel, DM and an unlisted channel read by a non-member),
every refusal, a reply to a command, and deletes that rewrite the list.
- `e2e_channel_pins` runs over WebSocket against a relay and is added to
the relay integration job.
- Run against a local relay started with no pins configuration: the
end-to-end test. On an earlier revision, the periodic tick removed
expired erasure records from an archived channel while leaving younger
records, live commands and other kinds.
- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with warnings denied on the touched
crates, and the file-size check.
- `just test-unit`, which includes the buzz-db source-policy tests.

fix(mobile): only dot channel-sent replies in the reader's threads (#9696)

## What changed

Mobile matches block/buzz-app#3938. A reply someone sends with **Also
send to channel** used to light the channel's attention dot and count
toward the app icon badge for everyone in the channel, even people who
never joined that thread.

Now it follows the same rule as any other reply:

- **Dot** if it mentions you, or it's in a thread you're part of (you
started it, replied in it, or follow it).
- **Bold only** otherwise, like a new top-level post. It no longer
counts toward the app icon badge.

Reading is unchanged. These replies are still marked read individually,
as desktop reads them, so reaching the bottom of the channel doesn't
silently mark them read on one device but not the other.

## How

- The "is this one of my threads" check that already decides which
ordinary replies count is now shared, and channel-sent replies go
through it when deciding attention.
- On mobile, "earns a dot" and "is read by reaching the bottom of the
channel" were one flag. Dropping a channel-sent reply's priority would
have also changed how it gets read, drifting from desktop. The dot now
comes from its own field; every other kind of message gets exactly the
same dot and read behavior as before.

## Tests

New cases drive live events through the channel list. For each, they
check the observed unread entry, whether its thread shows in Activity,
the app icon badge, the channel list's bold vs dot, and reading:

- reply sent to the channel in someone else's thread: bold, no dot, not
in Activity, counts as ordinary unread on the icon (same as a top-level
post)
- same, but mentioning the reader: dot, in Activity
- in a thread the reader follows: dot, in Activity
- in a thread the reader started: dot, in Activity
- in a thread the reader replied in: dot, in Activity

In every case, a channel catch-up mark leaves the reply unread and its
own read mark clears it.

The "someone else's thread" case fails on `main` (it gets a dot). The
pre-push mobile checks (format, analyze, full mobile test suite) passed
on this head.

## Known gaps (not changed here)

- Mobile only knows the threads you're part of from posts it has seen on
this phone. A fresh install doesn't know about older threads you joined
elsewhere, and a reply's first classification sticks even if later
loading shows you joined that thread. Desktop looks these up on the
relay.
- Mobile has no explicit "Unfollow" for a thread you started or replied
in (the menu only offers Follow there), so you can't silence one the way
desktop can. This applies to all replies, not just ones sent to the
channel.
- A reply sent to the channel still counts as unread in a muted channel.
That was already true before this change.

No screenshots: no visual element changes, only which existing state
(bold or dot) a channel shows.

feat(push-gateway): mint FCM tokens through AWS workload identity federation (#9692)

## Summary

Block's GCP projects forbid service account keys, so the push gateway
can now get its FCM access token by federating its AWS identity (Google
workload identity federation), with no key file.

- `BUZZ_PUSH_FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH` is renamed
`BUZZ_PUSH_FCM_CREDENTIALS_PATH` (no deployment sets it yet). The file
is dispatched on its JSON `type`: `service_account` keeps today's JWT
flow; `external_account` is Google's standard AWS credential
configuration, the file Block's `identity-federation-aws` Terraform
module generates.
- Only the minting step changed. `TokenSource` caching, refresh, backoff
and the Rejected/Unavailable split are as they were.
- A federated mint: AWS credentials (EKS Pod Identity, IRSA or static
env keys; no EC2 metadata), a SigV4-signed STS `GetCallerIdentity`
subject token, Google STS, then `generateAccessToken` for the FCM scope.
One 15 s deadline covers the whole chain.
- Faults: network errors, 5xx and 429 on any hop are Unavailable; other
4xx are Rejected.
- Startup checks the file's shape and the AWS environment but calls
neither AWS nor Google, so an outage can't stop the gateway from serving
iOS. The first mint's result is logged once.
- Helm: `android.fcmServiceAccount` is renamed `android.fcmCredentials`,
mounted as `credentials.json`.

impersonation servers: the full chain, each hop's failure
classification, a failed refresh keeping a valid cached token, the
overall deadline, and config rejection cases.
- SigV4 known-answer tests use AWS's documented example credentials,
checked against an independent implementation.

feat(mobile): report explicit diagnostic errors (#9673)

Step one of [mobile diagnostic
reporting](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/main/docs/mobile-diagnostic-reporting.md),
second piece: the explicit error reports the spec lists, through the
reporter added in [#9613 diagnostic reporting
module](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9613). A build without a
destination (every build from this repository alone) still reports
nothing.

### What's in it

Each report carries its `operation` tag, the error's type and stack
trace, and no error text (the filter replaces it).

- **Event subscriber (`eventSubscriber`):** a subscriber that throws
while the relay session delivers a buffered batch is reported, and the
rest of the batch is still delivered. In a build without a destination
the error still surfaces as uncaught, so it fails the test that hit it
and prints in development, as before. Before, one throw dropped the rest
of the batch, and those events never came back because their delivery
keys were already recorded.
- **Relay frames (`relayFrame`):** a frame the socket can't decode, or
whose body isn't a JSON array, is reported instead of silently skipped.
- **Relay queries (`relayQuery`):** an HTTP query body that can't be
decoded, including the read-state snapshot.
- **Invalid-request rejections (`relayRejection`):** an `OK false` or
`CLOSED` whose reason starts with `invalid:`, reported as a fixed
`RelayInvalidRequest` with no relay text, including an `OK` with no
pending publish (a typing indicator, or a reply after a timeout).
Refusals the app handles as expected outcomes (an archived channel, an
Unarchive of a channel that is no longer archived, an open channel name
that is taken, an agent whose `policy:` refuses being added, a sole
owner's Leave refused as the last owner, a guest's Add Members refused
because only members can add people, an event whose timestamp is outside
the relay's window, so a wrong device clock does not report every
publish) are left out. The long-lived relay session, the short-lived
sockets (hosted admission, the self-hosted probe, one-shot publishes
such as agent registration and push tombstones) and the account
assertion requests made for a community's key (relay access and push
stop assertions) report frames and rejections the same way, except while
reports name a member other than the key they sign with. A removed or
inactive community's tombstone, or the probe of a community being
joined, then reports nothing rather than naming the wrong member. With
no member set (first run, or after the last community is removed) it
reports under the install identifier.
- **Account responses (`accountResponse`):** a Builderlab account
response that isn't a JSON object, or a 2xx exchange or `/v1/auth/me`
response missing its credential, subject or expiry. Non-2xx statuses are
expected outcomes and aren't reported.
- **Push gateway responses (`pushGatewayResponse`):** a malformed push
capability descriptor from the relay. A relay that leaves
`supported_extensions` out or sends none has no push and isn't reported,
and a fetch that finishes after a community switch has begun isn't
reported either, since it would name the next member. Push gateway
replies aren't reported yet.
- **Stored data (`storedData`):** a saved community list that can't be
read back.
- **Member on switch:** switching communities now looks the new member
up in storage, not in the provider's list, which can still be the
previous one while it reloads after sign-in. It reads storage before
tearing anything down, so a failed read leaves the switch unchanged and
retryable.
- **Filter:** also drops a report's additional data (`extra`). Nothing
sets it today.
- The spec's status line now says what is implemented.
- Event delivery moves from `relay_session.dart` into a part file,
unchanged apart from the subscriber guard, so the session stays under
its size limit.

### Regressions

None expected: each change only adds a report where an error was already
caught or skipped. The one behavior change is that a throwing event
subscriber no longer costs the rest of its batch.

### Validation

Added tests for each report site (relay session, socket frames, one-shot
publishes, read-state snapshot, closed-reason policy, account client,
push descriptor and capability provider, community storage), for the
relay session (member changed mid-request), one-shot sockets and
assertion requests reporting nothing while another member is set and
reporting with none set, for the member on switch and a switch whose
read fails then retries, and for the filter dropping additional data and
leaving a message-less event without one.

Full-app run on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator at b4f05ad (debug build, no
reporting destination): signed-in launch and channel list, scrolling
history in several channels, a thread, sending a message and a reaction,
search, switching communities and back, background and foreground with
live updates afterwards, and kill and relaunch with saved communities
restored. No regressions and no exceptions from the changed code.

perf(push-gateway): evict the oldest signed-call window without scanning (#9799)

The push gateway's signed-call limiter keeps one counter per attested
key, capped at 100,000 keys. Once the map was full, every call from a
key not already in it scanned the whole map (once to drop expired
windows, again to find the oldest), all while holding the limiter's
lock. Under heavy load from many new keys, that serialized each signed
call behind a 100,000-entry scan.

The limiter now keeps a queue of window starts, oldest first, and evicts
from its front. A key whose window restarts leaves a stale entry behind,
which eviction skips; the queue is compacted once stale entries make up
half of it, so a call stays O(1) amortized. Rate-limit behavior is
unchanged, except that a full map now drops one oldest window per new
key instead of every expired window at once. The map and the queue share
one copy of each key; the queue can reach about twice the map's entries
before compaction, so memory stays bounded.

Follow-up from #9562.

### Validation

| 1,000 new keys on a full map (release build) | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Before | 277 ms (about 0.28 ms per call, under the lock) |
| After | 0.11 ms |

-
