perf(mobile): stop re-scanning the unread backlog on channel list rebuilds (#9780)

## Summary

Scrolling the mobile channel list hitched repeatedly after the app had
been closed for a long time.

To decide which rows are bold and which get a dot, the channel list read
every unread message held in memory, for every channel, on every
rebuild. After a long absence the unread catch-up holds up to 1000
messages per channel, so each list update cost more than a frame.

This change makes a list rebuild independent of the backlog size:

- A channel's messages stop being read once its bold and dot state is
decided.
- Each channel's result is reused until its messages or the read state
change. A new message re-reads only its own channel; reordering or
filtering the list re-reads nothing.

Which rows end up bold or dotted is unchanged.

### Related issue

N/A. None found.

### Testing

Before (left) and after (right), same script on an iPhone 17 simulator:
200 channels each holding 1000 unread messages, a list update every 150
ms, and a scripted finger (the crosshair) dragging at a steady 420 px
per second.

feat(mobile): add Dart notification body formatter (#9556)

Adds a pure Dart function, `notificationBody`, that turns a message's
Markdown content into the plain-text notification body defined by [ADR
0002](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-notification-message-text.md).
It is a port of the Swift `BuzzPushNotificationResolver.previewBody` in
`BuzzPushKit`, which today is the only implementation.

Android notifications will be built from the app's Dart code, as in the
[Android push design](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/9555), and will
reuse this function so the body reads the same on both platforms.
Nothing calls it yet and the Swift side is unchanged.

Notes on the port:

- The cap stays at 256 UTF-16 code units, the same as iOS (the fixtures
set `maxLength` to 256).
- Dart's regex engine differs from the ICU one the Swift code uses
(`\s`, `.` and `$`), so the patterns spell those out to keep identical
results. Trimming also matches Swift's `whitespacesAndNewlines`, which
trims U+200B and keeps U+FEFF, where Dart's `trim` does the opposite for
both.
- Truncation counts whole characters (extended grapheme clusters) via
`package:characters`.

### Validation

- A table-driven test runs every case in
`test-fixtures/notification-body.json` (47 cases) and checks the
fixture's `maxLength` against the function's cap.
- Added tests: 8 rows in the shared fixture pin the ICU details the port
must match. U+000B and U+0085 beside a marker keep it, U+000B and U+000C
inside a run keep its markers, U+200B is trimmed at the edges and
doesn't count toward the cap, and U+FEFF at the edges is kept. The Swift
fixture test runs them too and passes them unchanged.
- Proved falsifiable: with code-span and fence handling disabled, 18
fixture cases fail; restored, all pass.
- `just mobile-install mobile-check mobile-test` passes.

### Regressions

None: new code that nothing calls yet. The Swift formatter is untouched.
Its fixture test now also runs the 8 new rows and passes them unchanged.

fix(mobile): hand message action menu scrolling off to sheet dismissal (#9760)

## Summary

On mobile, the message action menu is a modal bottom sheet whose body
scrolls when the actions overflow (long menus, large text sizes). Before
this change, dragging down inside the body only scrolled or bounced the
content: the sheet itself could be pulled down only by its handle. Now a
downward drag in the body carries on into pulling the sheet down once
the content reaches its top, in the same touch, and the sheet can be
dismissed that way.

- **Handoff in both directions.** Drag updates are split between the
content and the existing modal route. Dragging down past the top of the
content moves the sheet; reversing without lifting restores the sheet
first and then scrolls the content again.
- **Release policy is the stock sheet's.** If the finger has displaced
the sheet at release, downward velocity strictly above 700 px/s closes
it; otherwise it closes when it has been pulled more than half its
height, and settles open if not. Where the gesture began, and whether it
scrolled content on the way to the top, does not matter.
- **Guards against accidental dismissal:**
  - a release with the sheet not displaced by the finger never closes;
- ballistic and programmatic scrolling cannot start a sheet drag, so a
content fling that reaches the top after the finger lifted stops there;
  - carried scroll momentum is not added to the release velocity;
- a slow return across the top that pulls the sheet less than half way
settles open;
  - an upward release velocity keeps the sheet open.
- **Unchanged:** handle and barrier behaviour, reactions, cancellation
recovery, reduced motion, and the action/focus contracts.

The handoff lives in a shared widget,
`mobile/lib/shared/widgets/modal_scroll_handoff.dart`;
`message_actions.dart` changes by three lines to use it.
`docs/mobile-message-action-scroll.md` records the design contract and a
manual native checklist.

### Related issue

N/A. None found (searched issues and PRs for the message action menu
dismissal and scroll).

### Testing

Run at `558a79710`:

- `just mobile-check`: passed (format; analyze: no issues).
- `just mobile-test`: passed (5462 Flutter tests, 71 skipped; 27 crypto
tests).
- `just file-size-check`: passed.
- Restoring the previous release rule fails 12 of the updated tests,
including all four message action journey variants.

Coverage: the message action journey (2x text scale, iOS and Android
platform settings) drives the production sheet with timed pointer
events; the shared widget tests cover the release table at several
scroll offsets, pointer flicks on both platforms, parity with the stock
sheet drag around both thresholds, trailing bounce on short menus,
cancellation and interruption.

**Simulator recordings.** Both videos are side-by-side captures from the
iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 27.2, text size `accessibility-large` so the
menu overflows). Each side replays the same touch script.

Scroll-to-dismiss handoff. Left: base (`9bcb3e45a`), the body only
bounces and the sheet never moves. Right: branch at `23c31e2e1`, the
same touches pull the sheet down, restore it on reversal, and dismiss it
on a slow drag past half and on a flick.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09b0cfc2-ed61-4822-8b35-b80d0f47e830

Scroll up slightly, then swipe down hard. Left: `23c31e2e1`, the menu
settles back open after both swipes. Right: `558a79710` (branch head),
the same touches close it, as a new touch and without lifting; the final
slow return across the top stays open on both sides.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/068faff4-a4d4-478f-aaf4-fc65c644632f

**Limits of this validation:**

- The touches were scripted synthetic touch events (linear motion, exact
timing), not a human finger.
- Both sides ran a dummy-data harness that calls the production
`showMessageActions` for a placeholder message, not the real channel
page. The harness is not part of this PR.
- Android, a physical device, VoiceOver and reduced motion were not
exercised natively; they are covered by widget tests only.
- The right side of the first video was built from `23c31e2e1`, one
commit before the branch head. `558a79710` changes only releases with a
fast downward velocity after content was scrolled. The gestures in that
video are slow or held releases and gestures that start at the top,
which resolve the same way under both rules; this follows from the
release rule and was not re-recorded.
- A human has not yet confirmed the behaviour by hand.

docs(incidents): I-62, prose above a table went over the table on every keystroke

Row for 59461505: introduced by d792e0c4, in the daily build between the two, caught by CI's run of the timing test and now by its relative limit.

fix(editor): prose typed above a table no longer goes over the table

d792e0c4 made a keystroke look one line without a pipe past the edit, to
hand the spacing back to rows a line break had just parted from their
line of dashes. Any table standing one empty line under the edited
paragraph, the usual layout, matched as well: every keystroke in that
paragraph measured the whole table again, 11 ms for 200 rows in a Debug
build where 0.6 ms is normal.

A table that merely stands there is now told from parted rows by its
second line (dashes drawn as markup) and left alone.

The timing test that guards this had an absolute limit of 20 ms, which
the regression passed on a fast Mac and failed on CI (30 ms), the only
place it was caught. It now also compares the prose keystroke with the
table keystroke, red on d792e0c4 here (11.3 ms against a limit of 3.1).

Verified: the whole app suite, both linters;
testRowsPartedFromTheirLineOfDashesArePlainLinesAgain still passes.

To revert: git revert this commit; the parted rows keep working, prose
above a table gets slow again.

feat(editor): a table is drawn as a table, columns lined up and its pipes quiet

The editor's face is proportional, so the spaces that pad a cell in the
file never put the next pipe under the one above, and a table tidied by
Tab still read as ragged lines. This was the largest gap left after the
table keys (reader feedback, 2026-11-20). The maintainer picked this look
from two drawn candidates on 2026-11-21.

Nothing in the note changes. TableColumnAligner gives every column the
width of its widest cell and raises or lowers the `.kern` of the spaces
around each cell until the pipes stand under each other; `--:` and `:-:`
move a column's words right or to the middle. The pipes and the line of
dashes take the markup colour, as `#` and `**` do. Widths come from the
words, not from the padding: the first version padded to the widest padded
row and wrapped every row in a narrow editor. A table wider than the
editor is left as typed and looked at again when the width changes; so
are a table past 300 rows and one with a tab or an image.

TableEditing.layouts (MiaoYanCore, Foundation only, additive) names the
tables and where their cells start, in one pass for a whole note and for
the run of pipe lines around an edit otherwise, with the same rule the
table keys use for what a table is.

Verified: the pipes' glyph positions in a laid-out editor are within
0.5pt per column, and 8pt and more apart with the plain spacing put back;
typing moves the column; a table whose line of dashes is typed over, and
rows parted from it by a line break, get their spacing and colour back
(red on the version before review); rows in a formula or a tilde fence
stay as typed after a keystroke; a keystroke in a 200-row table costs
27 ms in a Debug build and 0.6 ms in the prose beside it. The layouts
agree with the keys on 600 made-up texts at every offset. App suite and
core suite pass whole, both linters clean. Run in the built app on a
scratch library: opening, typing in a cell, Tab, Shift-Return in a table,
and the split editor too narrow for the table.

An independent review found four things; three were fixed here (a lint
error, the parted rows, and the keystroke pass asking the highlighter's
code blocks where the whole-note pass follows fences and formulas), and
one did not hold (every note in this app is Markdown).

Not done: the iPhone and iPad editor; typing `~~~` or `$$` far above a
table does not redraw it until the note is opened again, as the
highlighter already behaves.

To revert: git revert this commit. It adds no setting and stores nothing.

feat(editor): the quick-input templates use the interface's language

/table, /markmap, /mermaid, /plantuml, /fold and /task plus Tab wrote
their placeholder words in Chinese for every reader, so an English,
Japanese or Spanish interface got 列1, 主题 and 开始 in the note. The
words now come from Localizable.strings (es, ja, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, English
from the key); the Chinese ones are the words the templates always had,
so a Chinese interface inserts the same text as before.

/table is written through TableEditing: "Column 1" is wider than the
three dashes and five spaces the template had under 列1, so the dashes
and the two empty rows are made as wide as the headers, the way Tab and
Format leave a table.

Verified: testTheTableTemplateIsTidyInEveryLanguage, red on the old
template file (列1 where Column 1, 欄1 and Columna 1 were expected, Chinese
words in the English /fold and /markmap); the app suite and both linters
pass.

docs(incidents): I-61, the split preview left behind by a fast scroll to the end

The row names 31e409c7, the fix, and the two tests that fail without it. Checked with scripts/check_incidents.py (61 rows, 0 problems).

feat(editor): Tab, Shift-Tab and Return move through a table, and a Table menu

A reader keeps to Bear because a table here is typed pipe by pipe: Tab
indented the row by two spaces and Return broke it. A table is still edited
as text (no WYSIWYG table, as #454 was answered), now with keys:

- Tab and Shift-Tab move between cells and select the cell's words; Tab in a
  row's last cell goes on to the next row.
- Return goes to the first cell of the next row. Both add a row after the
  last, and Return on a last row left empty hands the line back, as it does
  for an empty list item. Shift-Return, and Return before a row's first pipe,
  stay plain line breaks.
- Format > Table inserts and deletes rows and columns and aligns a column,
  in the five languages; the items go to the first responder and are on only
  where they can act.

The logic is TableEditing in MiaoYanCore (Foundation only, new public API,
nothing existing changed), so the iPhone and iPad editor can take the same
keys after the merge. The keys follow the table editor behind Obsidian's
Advanced Tables (tgrosinger/md-advanced-tables), except that Tab in a last
cell wraps to the next row as in Bear, where theirs starts a column. Every
command writes the table as Format (Prettier 2) prints it, checked against
the bundled formatter, and replaces only the text that changed. The /table
template's line of dashes is written the same way.

Every Return and Tab in the editor now passes through TableEditing.locate,
which reads outward from the caret and answers nil for anything that is not
a table: prose with a pipe, a quote or list item, a selection across lines,
a fence of backticks or tildes, four columns of indent, a $$ formula, a line
of pipes not closed at both ends.

An independent review of the first version found a trap on any line ending
in "[[" (a range that ran backwards), cells losing a no-break or ideographic
space to an over-wide trim, |x| lines turned into tables, tilde fences read
as tables and a walk from the top of the note for every row (664ms a key in
a 1MB note); all fixed here, each with a test, plus a test that runs every
command at every offset of 400 made-up texts and fails on a lost character.

Verified: the whole suite (478 tests) and the core package (95 tests); the
key tests fail with the two keyDown lines taken out. In the running app on a
scratch library: Tab, Tab, Return, typing into the new row, saved to disk.
The editor's face is proportional, so the padded columns do not line up on
screen; that is as before for a table Format had padded.

Revert: git revert this commit. Notes are not migrated; a table tidied by a
key stays valid Markdown.

fix(split): the preview reaches the end with the editor and follows the last scroll

A reader scrolled the split view fast to the end and found the editor on
its last line with the preview a third of the way up, right only after
another scroll; a tall image in the preview also put the two panes out of
step. Three causes, in both windows (ViewController+Editor, ShellEditor):

- An editor scroll inside the 50ms window in which the preview's echo is
  ignored was dropped and nothing followed it, so the preview stayed where
  the editor had been a moment before it stopped. It is now remembered and
  followed when the window closes.
- The editor reported a whole line number. A paragraph wrapped to many rows,
  or the one line an image takes, moved the preview in a jump. The place
  inside the line now travels as a fraction over all its rows, the same box
  in both directions (EditTextView.sourceLine(atDocumentY:)).
- At the editor's end the page showed the block of the editor's top line and
  stopped, short of its own end whenever the note's tail (images, tables,
  code) is taller in the page than in the source. scrollToLine(line, endLine,
  pull) adds the missing part over the editor's last screenful, and the first
  line maps to the page's top edge.

The page also keeps quiet about a scroll that leaves it where the editor put
it, so an echo later than 50ms no longer moves the editor on its own. Not
done: the way back (preview scrolled by hand) has no inverse of the end pull.

Verified: the whole suite (478 tests, 0 failures) and the core package (95);
the new tests fail with each fix taken out (the dropped scroll, the end pull,
the page top, the echo). In the running app on a scratch library, a note
ending in a table and an 1800px image: the old build left the preview at
paragraph 59 with the last line out of view, this build brings both panes to
the end, and the top and the tall image in the middle stay aligned.
An independent review of the diff found the patch-in-progress resync and the
late echo, both fixed here.

Revert: git revert this commit; no stored data or preference changes.

fix(core): the list date takes the system's Region setting over the language's region

A Mac whose language carries its own region and whose Region setting
differs reports both, as in en_GB@rg=uszzzz (British English, United
States). displayLocale read the region subtag and so formatted days for
Britain while the system formats them for the United States. The second
review round of 298183c3 pointed at it; the first version of the
function had the same gap. The `rg` keyword's region wins now, and the
hour cycle already followed it through the `j` template.

Verified: MiaoYanCore 71 tests with two new identifiers
(en_GB@rg=uszzzz, a keyword list with calendar and rg), full xcodebuild

repos.name: ly05010419/MacNativeGames
repos.description: Play your own Tears of the Kingdom and Breath of the Wild natively on Apple silicon Mac, iPhone and iPad. Not an emulator: the game's ARM64 code runs directly, NVN rebuilt on Metal. Bring your own game.

commits.message:
feat(ios): Zelda's pipeline archive in Animal Crossing and Odyssey; no full warm-up at every start

The ports warmed every shader library at every start (Odyssey: 61,896 items). They now use Tears of the
Kingdom's pipeline archive, shared rather than copied:
- totk_pipeline_archive{,_files,_folders,_publish}.h, nvn_archive_map.h and nvn_compiler_retry.h move to
  shared/ unchanged and are linked into totk, acnh and odyssey; the ports' old private archive (schema 3,
  one file per pipeline) is gone. totk_pipeline_archive_port.h / _port_fill.h: TotK's pso_new / cs_new_
  archive flow and its pipeline-archive packaging mode for the ports.
- The ports' hosts get the pipeline-archive mode (loader.c) and a bundle id (game_info.plist, Mac only) so
  Metal's archive builder can write; with a valid archive the warm-up skips libraries-only work, as TotK's.
- device_pipelines.py make(): TotK build_ipa.py's pipeline steps, called by it and by build_port_ipa.py, so
  the port IPAs carry pipelines-<gpu> files for the device GPUs (--device-gpu).
- Tests: PipelineArchive in test_ios_ports_unified.py (shared headers, archive hooks, host mode, make()).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(odyssey): Chinese text instead of Japanese: the game takes zh-CN / zh-TW

Super Mario Odyssey's code predates zh-Hans / zh-Hant (system 4.0) and knows only zh-CN / zh-TW (its CNzh /
TWzh text); the newer codes fell to its fallback, Japanese. As a Switch hands an older game the code it
supports: Traditional for a Hant script or Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macao, Simplified otherwise; the settings'
choice is converted too. tests/test_odyssey_language.py compiles runtime_desired_language and runs it per locale.

commits.message:
feat(runtime): upgrade to embassy 0.10 with dynamic TMR0 alarms (#52)

Replace the embassy 0.3/0.1 stack that could never sleep: __pender and
set_alarm_callback were no-ops, so a waking task was only re-polled when
a yield_now() spin loop happened to run, and TMR0 fired at a fixed 1 Hz
no matter which deadline had been registered.

Restore the real executor contract. __pender records work in
WORK_PENDING; run() clears the flag, polls, and only then enters the CPU
idle stall (reg_pwdn_ctrl = 0x80, FldPwdnCtrl::Sleep) when no work
arrived. The stall is entered under irq_disable()/irq_restore() with the
wake mask copied from the live reg_irq_mask, so wake sources match the
enabled ones: masking with 0x00ff_ffff drops the FLD_IRQ::EN field in
bits 24-31, and USB_250US_EN stays out because that mask never enables
it. read_reg_irq_en() after the restore flushes the bus write, so a
pending interrupt re-masks before the next poll.

Drive embassy-time from a real queue instead of a stub. MyDriver
implements embassy_time_driver::Driver with now() and schedule_wake(),
and TMR0 is reprogrammed to the earliest queued deadline, capped at one
second so clock_time64() keeps extending the 32-bit reg_system_tick
across its wrap. arm_tmr0() touches only the 8-bit reg_tmr_ctrl8 view of
0x620: a 32-bit reg_tmr_ctrl read-modify-write also covers 0x623
(reg_tmr_sta), where writing a stale value back would silently clear a
pending TMR1 or watchdog flag. The arm order is disable, tick 0,
capt = clamp(delta, 32, 1 s), clear TMR0_STA, enable.

Give the executor static storage with static_cell::StaticCell and drop
the nightly type_alias_impl_trait feature. Delete `static mut SPAWNER`:
it stored &spawner from the init closure over a stack temporary and was
then dereferenced from UART interrupt context. uart_receiver and
uart_sender are now spawned in App::run before irq_enable(), and
uart_sender parks on a new started_signal until handle_rx accepts the
first host frame, so a headless light no longer retries DMA TX of its
boot banners every 100 ms.

Rebase the OTA timeout on elapsed time. TMR0 no longer ticks at 1 Hz, so
dispatcher.rs gates the OTA_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS decrement on a
module-scoped LAST_OTA_TIMEOUT_TICK plus clock_time64(); it restamps
while OTA is idle, so the first interrupt after OTA starts cannot
decrement the counter immediately.

Verified on 12 MHz and 16 MHz TLSR8266 boards with the 6-stage HIL
acceptance suite; cargo fmt --check, clippy with -D warnings, 1038 unit
tests and both make check size gates pass.

Closes #39
fix(ble): read status response payload from flat PacketAttValue.val overlay (#51)

chore(build): drop the unused libgcc archive from the link (#50)

The TC32 link line passed libgcc.a after merged.o and the startup object,
but no archive member was ever pulled: compiler_builtins, built from
source by -Z build-std=core, already defines every __aeabi_* helper, mem*
routine and division helper the backend emits.

Prove it by linking the same merged.o with and without the archive: both
produce a byte-identical ELF, and nm -u on the final ELF is empty. Removing
the input makes a future missing helper a link error instead of a silent
fallback to the 2010-era GCC runtime, and drops the 599 KB vendored
binary plus its manifest hash input.

Bump the manifest schema to 2 because libgcc_sha256 is gone, forcing one
relink for existing caches.

chore(toolchain): harden TC32 build driver and bump nightly to 2026-11-20 (#49)

* chore(build): harden TC32 build driver diagnostics and LLVM version gate

- Render Cargo JSON compiler-message diagnostics to stderr on both
  success (warnings) and failure (errors)
- Probe rustc -vV and llc --version into manifest provenance, print a
  one-line toolchain summary, and fail with exit 2 if rustc's LLVM
  major exceeds the TC32 fork's LLVM major
- Support Cargo 1.100+ build/<crate>/<hash>/out/ root .rlib resolution

* chore(toolchain): bump nightly to 2026-11-20 and update CI and docs

- Bump rust/rust-toolchain.toml from nightly-2025-08-06 (LLVM 20.1.8)
  to nightly-2026-11-20 (rustc 1.102.0-nightly, LLVM 23.1.6) to match

- Apply rustfmt doc-comment formatting in rust/src/sdk/app_att_light.rs

test(wire-contracts): add shared golden vectors for rust and python

- Add tests/wire_vectors.txt, a generated, language-neutral fixture of 143
  keys covering the 15 wire struct sizes, CRC-16-MODBUS, UART framing and
  opcodes, GATT UUIDs, pairing constants, AES CTR/CBC-MAC packets, the

- Add rust/src/wire_contract_tests.rs (10 tests) asserting the fixture
  byte-for-byte against the firmware types, enums, constants and crypto,
  plus a consumed-key orphan guard.
- Add utilities/meshutils/tests/test_wire_contracts.py (22 tests) asserting

- Production edits are inert: pub(crate) visibility on the items the tests

Closes #38

feat(build): add deterministic incremental TC32 build driver (#47)

`make` globbed every `.ll` file ever emitted into Cargo's `deps/` into
`llvm-link`, marked `_build/lightblemesh` `.PHONY` so a no-op run still
relinked, and ran `sdk/increment_version.sh` while rebuilding the
startup object, dirtying tracked version files on every build.

Replace the IR/link half of the Makefile with `sdk/build_firmware.py`
(pure stdlib), leaving the Makefile as target wiring only:

- Select IR exactly: Cargo runs from `rust/` with
  `--message-format=json`, and each reported `.rlib` maps to its own
  `.ll` (a hashed dependency crate, or the root crate's inode /
  `(size, sha256)` twin under `deps/`). Nothing globs `deps/*.ll`, so a
  stale `stale-deadbeef.ll` is never linked and feature switches share
  one `rust/target/` without rebuilding `core`.
- Cache the link: a deterministic per-feature manifest records IR
  hashes, the startup object, linker script, libgcc, tool identity and
  the flag strings. On a match the six LLVM/TC32 commands are skipped,
  `merged.o` is left untouched, and `_build/lightblemesh{,.bin}` is
  resynced from `_build/<slug>/`.
- Keep the tree clean: the driver only reads `sdk/version.in` and
  `rust/src/version.rs`, fails loudly when their `BUILD_VERSION`
  integers differ, and rebuilds `cstartup_8266.o` from a SHA-256 input
  manifest instead of bumping the version. `make bump-version` is now
  the only mutator.

CI gains a stdlib-only `sdk-tests` job and asserts the manifest cache
hit on a consecutive `make` in the firmware job.

Closes #37

docs(tc32): add recovered instruction set reference (#35)

Document the TLSR8266 code-16 opcode table, operand ranges, toolchain limitations, and assembler/disassembler discrepancies.

feat(firmware): detect crystal at runtime, drop 12/16 MHz split (#34)

Replace the build-time 12 MHz / 16 MHz split with one universal image. Only
one branch in the whole firmware actually depended on the crystal -
rf_drv_init() loading the last 4 of the 61 TBL_RF_INI entries; everything else
that varied with clock speed varied with the post-PLL system clock. A ~1 ms
boot measurement therefore replaces a build axis, a header bit, an assembly
constant, a Python constant, a flash guard and a bricking footgun.

Firmware detection (rust/src/sdk/mcu/clock.rs):
- read_ana_32k() reads the free-running 16-bit 32K_RC counter from analog
  0x41/0x40/0x41 and retries while the two high-byte samples differ, so a
  carry cannot tear the value.
- detect_xtal_is_16mhz() switches CLK_SYS to SEL_16M_PAD (divider 0), aligns
  to a 32K_RC tick edge, counts reg_system_tick over 32 ticks (~1 ms) and
  restores reg_clk_sel verbatim. >= 14_500 ticks means 16 MHz, < 14_500 means
  12 MHz; bench ranges are 12,483-12,535 and 16,286-16,656 ticks.
- Every loop is bounded by XTAL_DETECT_MAX_POLLS, and a window that never
  completes reports 12 MHz: a 16 MHz part then loads the 57-entry table and
  loses the radio, but still boots and can be reflashed over SWire.
- clock_init() runs the measure-and-publish inside critical_section::with and
  caches the result in IS_16MHZ_XTAL; is_16mhz_xtal() is the accessor. The
  existing HS_DIV and watchdog writes stay byte-identical.

RF table selection (rust/src/sdk/ble_app/rf_drv_8266.rs):
- rf_init_table(bool) returns all 61 TBL_RF_INI entries for a 16 MHz crystal
  and the leading 57 for the default 12 MHz crystal; the four dropped
  commands are 0x4eb, analog 0x99, analog 0x82 and analog 0x9e.
- rf_drv_init() calls it with is_16mhz_xtal() in place of the two cfg arms.
  The helper exists because load_tbl_cmd_set's mock skips its argument.

Build and header (Makefile, sdk/, rust/Cargo.toml):
- cstartup_8266.S emits .word (BUILD_VERSION); sdk/version.in and
  sdk/increment_version.sh lose XTAL_16MHZ and the crystal argument, and the
  script rejects stray arguments so a stale caller fails loudly.
- The Makefile drops the xtal FEATURES parsing and the FEATURE_STAMP/FORCE
  rebuild machinery; the startup object now depends on sdk/version.in.
- rust/Cargo.toml loses the commented xtal-16mhz feature and its warning.
- The Makefile dot-sources ./.env instead of .env, which dash resolved
  through PATH and so failed the build whenever a .env existed.

probe-tlsr:
- flash takes only <PATH> [--reset]; --force, CrystalMismatch, its exit-3
  branch and the pre-erase target header read are gone.
- info reports {jedec_id, build_version, magic_ok} with build_version =
  version & 0x7fff_ffff; the human line and JSON drop xtal_mhz.

Python tools (utilities/meshutils):
- mesh_common.py drops VERSION_16MHZ and keeps VERSION_MASK.
- flash_fw.py and flash_fw_uart.py drop the crystal rejection and the
  "16MHz device:" log field; --force still only overrides dev_ver >= fw_ver.

Docs:
- swire.md, ble.md, uart.md, ble_hardware_reference.md and README.md describe
  boot-time auto-detection instead of a build-time split, the crystal guard,
  exit-3 crystal aborts and VERSION_16MHZ.
- The boot banner is now "Booting FW version <n>, xtal: 12MHz|16MHz".

User-visible contract changes:
- The image header word at offset 2 carries a plain BUILD_VERSION with bit 31
  always 0.
- probe-tlsr flash no longer accepts --force and no longer aborts on a crystal
  mismatch.
- probe-tlsr info no longer reports xtal_mhz.

  --force remains the downgrade override.

Verified on host (1021 firmware tests, 99.74% region / 99.81% line / 100%
functions; 205 probe tests; make check PASS at 82,220 B and 85,352 B) and on

patch: Stop re-running failed background message deliveries (#2494) ## Why `MessagingRateLimiter.fire_and_forget` re-enqueued a failed background task up to twice when the error text contained "connect", "timeout" or "broken". Since #2428, delivery retries belong to the platform adapters, so this was a second, text-matched retry layer: - **Duplicate calls.** Telegram's `_with_retry` already spends up to 3 calls on a network error. A final `ConnectError` then went through the limiter loop twice more, so one background edit could take up to 9 Telegram calls plus extra sleeps. - **Stale edits.** Edits to one message share the dedup key `edit:{chat_id}:{message_id}`. A retry re-enqueued the old edit under that key. Queue compaction then swapped it in for a newer pending edit, or it ran after a newer edit that had already landed. Either way the message was left showing old text. - **Inconsistent matching.** Telegram's `TimedOut` reads "Timed out", which never matched "timeout", while connect errors did. Removing that loop exposed a gap on Discord, which had no app-level retry. discord.py retries 429s, 5xx and the macOS and Windows connection resets (errno 54 and 10054) itself. It lets the Linux reset (104), DNS failures, refused connections, server disconnects and timeouts through. The limiter caught some of those only because their text contained "connect". Waited-on Discord deliveries never had any retry for them. ## How - `fire_and_forget` runs the task once through `enqueue` and logs a failure with its dedup key and exception type. Exception text is logged only when error details are enabled, same as before. - `DiscordMessenger` gets a `_with_retry` that drives the shared `delivery_failures.decide()`, like Telegram's. `aiohttp.ClientConnectionError`, `aiohttp.ClientPayloadError` (a response cut off midway) and `TimeoutError` count as network failures and share the 3-call budget with 1s and 2s backoff. Everything else, including `DiscordServerError` after discord.py's own tries and certificate verification failures, raises at once, so the two layers do not nest. Send, fetch plus edit, and fetch plus delete are each retried as one operation. The existing `NotFound` and `Forbidden` handling is unchanged. - Each send carries one nonce, reused on every attempt. discord.py sends it with `enforce_nonce`, so Discord returns the existing message instead of posting a duplicate when a retried send had already landed. - Accepted overlap: a macOS or Windows reset that outlasts discord.py's 5 tries gets up to 2 more calls from us. - Accepted tradeoff: Discord only remembers a nonce for a few minutes. If a send lands but its response is lost, and discord.py then waits out a multi-minute 429 inside the retry, the retry can post a second message. Discord's send rate limits reset within seconds, so this needs a rate limit real traffic should not hit. Bounding it would mean timing discord.py's internal waits or changing its rate-limit handling for every request. Tests: - `test_fire_and_forget_runs_failed_task_once` fails on main with 3 runs. - Discord: an edit after a Linux reset is delivered, a retried send reuses its nonce, a rejected edit is not retried, persistent network failures stop after 3 calls, an edit after a truncated response is delivered, and a certificate failure is not retried. Five of these fail before the change that fixes them. - `test_fire_and_forget_failure_logged` makes `enqueue` itself fail, so only the wrapper can produce the log. Checked that it fails with that log removed. #2327 is closed separately. Everything it describes was fixed by #2428. Local checks: `scripts/ci.ps1 -Skip playwright,macos-desktop` passed on the Discord retry commit (11516 passed, 17 skipped). After the last commit, ruff, ty and the messaging suite passed (531 passed, 1 skipped). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge; no actionable new issue was found.

Summary

 This PR removes background retries from `MessagingRateLimiter` and puts Discord delivery retries in `DiscordMessenger`. - Background message tasks are enqueued once instead of being replayed after failures. - Discord deliveries retry selected network failures without duplicating sends.

Diagram

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Queued background delivery] --> B[Limiter runs operation once] B --> C[Discord operation] C --> D{Result} D -->|Success| E[Return result] D -->|Network or truncated response| F{Attempts below three?} F -->|Yes| G[Wait, then retry same operation] G --> C F -->|No| H[Raise and log failure] D -->|Certificate failure or other rejection| H ```

[19.04] feat(ros2-bridge): let a YAML action server's handler accept or reject goals (#4248)

* [19.04] feat(dora-message, dora-core): ros2 `accept: auto | handler` for action servers

A new optional `ros2:` field for a YAML action server: `auto` (the
default) accepts each goal on arrival, `handler` lets the handler accept
or reject it on a `goal_response` input. The field is appended last, so
the wire-format gate sees an addition; `ros2:` is outside the 1.x
guarantee. validate_ros2_accept checks that `accept` is only set on an
action server and that `accept: handler` has a `goal_response` input; it
runs on the resolution path too, so `dora start` enforces it.

Refs #4234

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [19.04] feat(ros2-bridge): let the handler accept or reject action goals

With `accept: handler`, the YAML action server forwards each new goal on
`goal` and answers the ROS 2 client once the handler answers on
`goal_response` (`goal_id` metadata, a one-element boolean array). Goals
waiting for the handler count toward the 8-goal limit; one without an
answer within 10 s is rejected, as are those still waiting when the
dataflow stops. With a `cancel` output, the handler is told about a goal
that timed out or failed to start after it accepted it.

On DDS the main loop accepts (accept_goal + start_executing_goal, shared
with auto mode as accept_and_start) or rejects the goal, so acceptance and
cancels stay serialized there. On Zenoh the SendGoal request is answered
then. A ticker thread (try_send, so it never blocks goal or cancel events)
drives the timeout for both transports.

Refs #4234

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [19.04] feat(examples), ci(ros2-dds): an accepting handler, and accept/reject cells

dataflow-accept.yml runs the Fibonacci server with `accept: handler`; the
example handler answers `goal_response` when it declares that output and
rejects orders above 46, whose last value overflows i32. The DDS interop
matrix gains yaml-action-server-accept and yaml-action-server-reject;
action_peer.py gets --order and --expect-reject.

Refs #4234

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [19.04] docs: accepting action goals in the YAML bridge; changelog

Refs #4234

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [19.04] refactor(ros2-bridge): infer handler-decided goals from a goal_response input

Drop the `accept: auto | handler` key. Adding a public field to
`Ros2BridgeConfig` is a breaking change for cargo-semver-checks: the
struct can be built with a literal, so the Breaking changes gate fails
against v1.1.0. The bridge now waits for the handler's decision when
the node declares a `goal_response` input, the same way it handles
cancels when the node declares a `cancel` output. The YAML schema and
the `dora-message` API are unchanged.

fix(daemon): keep node IPC listeners and zenoh plans off other dataflows' planned ports (#4247)

* fix(daemon): keep node IPC listeners off other dataflows' planned Zenoh ports

#4184 kept a node's IPC listener off the Zenoh ports planned by its own
dataflow. A port planned by another dataflow on the same daemon is only
probed free, not held, until that dataflow's node binds it, so a node of
a concurrently started dataflow could still take it.

Snapshot the listen endpoints of every running dataflow when a Spawner is
built (it is used within one daemon event, so no other dataflow can be
planned before its listeners bind) and have `spawn_node` avoid them along
with the dataflow's own plan.

Fixes #4242

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017Yk5WHyy7gQ3uzF2Nbftcw

* fix(daemon): keep zenoh listener plans off other dataflows' planned ports

The planning side had the same cross-dataflow gap as the IPC listener:
`reserve_node_listeners` probes and releases a port without checking what
other dataflows on the daemon have planned but not yet bound, and a
dynamic node's reservation checked only its own dataflow.

Add `reserve_unplanned`, which retries a probe that returns a planned
endpoint (and gives up after 16 attempts, so the planner falls back to
gossip for that node), and use it for both, fed from
`planned_zenoh_endpoints` over every running dataflow.

fix(tensor-pool): unlink only the recorded mirror on cross-machine free (#4246)

Both explicit free paths (the `PeerMessage::Free` handler and
`NodeRequest::Free` via `release_cross_pool`) re-derived the mirror name
from this daemon's machine id and unlinked it unconditionally. On the
origin daemon that derived `dora_pool_{machine}_{df}_{node}_{n}` name is
the sender node's own live, auto-named local segment, and the peer
handler unlinked it even when no cross-pool entry existed at all.

Add `release_cross_pool_entry`, which removes the entry and unlinks only
its `mirror_shmem_name` (as `cleanup_cross_pools` already does), and use
it on both paths. The publish half of `release_cross_pool` is now
`publish_cross_pool_free`; `unlink_cross_pool_segment` had no other user
and is removed.

Fixes #4241

fix(ros2-bridge): answer over-cap and unknown-goal GetResult with STATUS_UNKNOWN, not an error (#4245)

* fix(ros2-bridge): answer an over-cap GetResult with STATUS_UNKNOWN, not an error

When a goal already has MAX_RESULT_WAITERS_PER_GOAL waiters, each from a
different client, the zenoh action server turned the next get_result away
with a service error. rmw_zenoh_cpp drops error replies unread, so that
rclcpp/rclpy client's call never resolved.

Answer it with a normal STATUS_UNKNOWN reply instead, as the Replaced arm
already does for a displaced request, and log a warning so the cap is still
visible on the server side.

Fixes #4244

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017Yk5WHyy7gQ3uzF2Nbftcw

* fix(ros2-bridge-node): answer an unknown-goal GetResult with STATUS_UNKNOWN

The YAML bridge's Zenoh action server rejected a GetResult for a goal it
doesn't know with an error reply. rmw_zenoh_cpp drops error replies unread,
so that rclcpp/rclpy client's call hung, the same failure as #4244.

Answer it with STATUS_UNKNOWN and a default result instead, as the typed
server and rclcpp do. The payload is encoded once per server.

Refs #4244

fix(core): don't resolve a hub node's entrypoint to a directory (#4237)

#4185 made `resolve_path` skip a folder named like the executable, since
it cannot be spawned. `resolve_path_confined`, the resolver for `hub:`
nodes, still accepted it with `exists()`, so a Python package's source
folder named like its console script resolved and the node then failed
at spawn with `Permission denied`, instead of the resolver's "could not

error.

Move the rule into an `is_spawnable` helper (a file, or a folder with a
`__main__.py` that `--uv` runs as `uv run <folder>`) and use it in both
resolvers.

(the grammar its YAML twin accepts) quietly undid the tuning it exists

commits.message:
feat(python)!: make job data access method-only (#5095)

Make all Python `Job` and `AsyncJob` data access method-only. Cached
property accessors are private and underscore-prefixed; public reads use
`id()`, `state()`, `job_type()`, `creation_ms()`, `spec()`, `result()`
and `failure()`. `checkout_latest()` refreshes the complete cached
registry record in place and returns `None`.

```python
job.checkout_latest()
print(job.state(), job.result(), job.failure())
print(job.id(), job.job_type(), job.creation_ms(), job.spec())
```

Cached read methods are synchronous on both handle types. Async handles
use `await job.checkout_latest()` for the live refresh; event history
remains a separate request through `events()`. Update Python SDK
callers, tests and guides to use method calls, including
progress/timeout handling and bounded repr. Cover method-only visibility
and holistic snapshot freshness through both sync and async clients.

BREAKING CHANGE: Python job data access now requires method calls, such
as `job.state()` instead of `job.state`. No property compatibility
aliases remain.

Fixes
https://linear.app/lancedb/issue/ENT-3902/sdk-make-cached-versus-live-job-accessors-unambiguous

docs: use function instead of deprecated udf in examples (#5027)

`lancedb.udf` is a deprecated alias of `lancedb.function` and emits a
`DeprecationWarning`. This switches the quickstart and the curation
examples to `function`, so readers who copy them no longer see the
warning. The quickstart snippet is regenerated from its test.

feat(nodejs): add tag-based branch creation and default tag versions (#5145)

Node.js did not provide parity with the Python tag fixes in #5136.
`tags.create()` required an explicit version, and `branches.create()`
could not fork from a tag without resolving a numeric version that loses
the tag's branch identity.

This adds Node.js parity:

- `tags.create(tag, version?)` defaults an omitted version to the
version visible to the table handle, including checked-out and
time-travel handles. Explicit versions are unchanged.
- `branches.create(name, { fromTag })` forks through `Ref::Tag`,
preserving the tag's branch and version. Existing `create(name,
fromRef?, fromVersion?)` calls are unchanged. Mixing `fromTag` with
another source is rejected before `main` normalization.
- A missing Embedded branch keeps its original error and now includes
the actual `branches.create(..., { fromTag: ... })` call as guidance.
Enterprise 404s keep their original error without guessing from the
message.
- Enterprise uses the existing tag resolution and branch-create wire
contract; no wire changes.

The released web guide remains on the published package examples. The
new API is documented in the TypeScript API reference and source, with
Node regression coverage.

feat: add table.delta for version-to-version row changes (#5135)

Adds native `Table::delta(from_version, to_version=None)` and Python
sync/async `table.delta(...)` for version-to-version row changes.
`TableDelta` exposes streaming `inserted_rows()`, `updated_rows()`,
`upserted_rows()`, `deleted_row_ids()`, and `list_transactions()`.

Endpoints are resolved once on independent dataset handles.
`to_version=None` uses the table handle's visible snapshot, and the
handle's checkout is not changed. Only versions `>= 1` and tags on the
current branch are accepted; cross-branch tags, reversed ranges, version
0, and missing endpoints are rejected. Equal valid endpoints return
empty readers with the same schemas.

Row-level readers require stable row ids at both endpoints and report
the `storage_options={"new_table_enable_stable_row_ids": "true"}`
creation guidance when they are absent. `list_transactions()` does not
require stable row ids.

Row-level readers also fail closed when the range contains a `Restore`,
or when transaction history cannot prove the range is restore-free,
because restored rows can retain older row-version metadata that the
delta readers omit. The error directs consumers to a full rescan and
reinitializing the checkpoint at the range end version.
`list_transactions()` remains available for readable history. The
Versioning guide includes Python and Rust checkpoint-delta examples with
stable-row-ID setup and this Embedded limitation.

Embedded `branches.diff()` remains a separate API.

Refs OSS-2860

feat: add cleanup jobs and previews across SDKs (#5107)

LanceDB SDK users connected to Enterprise had no explicit API to submit
durable cleanup or preview its work; Python's existing cleanup helper
remained a warning-only no-op. This PR adds the SDK support for
[ENT-2687](https://linear.app/lancedb/issue/ENT-2687) through public SQL
and Job APIs. It requires a compatible Enterprise release supporting
`VACUUM`, JSON preview and result format version 1. Existing
cleanup/optimize helpers retain their behavior; the new APIs reject
Embedded and historical-version handles.

This was accomplished with the following changes:

- Add `cleanup_async()` / `cleanupAsync()` and `explain_cleanup()` /
`explainCleanup()` in Python sync/async, TypeScript and Rust.
- Preserve the handle's namespace/branch and resolve retention as
invocation → table/branch TTL → deployment default. Omission inherits,
zero is explicit, and malformed options fail rather than being
discarded.
- Require one nonempty durable SQL receipt, preserving diagnostics
without REST fallback, query-ID substitution or automatic resubmission
after ambiguous acceptance.
- Add versioned `CleanupPlan` estimates and `CleanupResult`
measurements. Preview creates no cleanup job or reservation; results
preserve known zero, unknown retry/recovery totals and nonfatal failed
deletes, excluding auxiliary sweeps.
- Retain typed results on reopening and reuse shared
status/progress/events/wait/cancel APIs. Timeout leaves work running;
cancellation cannot undo deletion or prove storage I/O stopped.
- Document Ownership/parent Usage and required coordination at every
retention value: disable/drain automatic cleanup and prevent competing
cleanup, tag creation/update, branch creation and restore across all
clients until completion. The server does not enforce exclusion;
concurrent restore can leave the current table unreadable.
- Update Python's legacy no-op warning and the maintenance, Python, Rust
and generated TypeScript references.

| Interface | Submit with seven-day retention |
| --- | --- |
| SQL | `VACUUM events WITH (min_age_seconds = 604800);` |
| CLI | `lancedb admin table cleanup --table events --min-age-seconds
604800 --wait` |
| Python | `job = table.cleanup_async(min_age_seconds=604800)` (use
`await` with AsyncTable) |
| TypeScript | `const job = await table.cleanupAsync({ minAgeSeconds:
604800 });` |
| Rust | `let job =
table.cleanup_async(CleanupOptions::new().min_age_seconds(604800)).await?;`
|

### Testing

Added submission/preview, validation, typed-result and reopening tests,
and updated the legacy no-op warning assertion. Focused Python
cleanup/Job and compaction/prewarm regressions passed, alongside **34
TypeScript** and **46 Rust** tests. **31 end-to-end scenarios** passed

perf(python): stream plain sync batches on demand (#5143)

## Problem

Synchronous local `table.search().to_batches()` creates one Python
future per batch through the background event loop. At the default
1024-row cap, a large scan pays that Python round trip thousands of
times even though the Rust stream can produce the next batch
immediately.

## Change

Use a pull-driven synchronous reader for native, non-namespace, ordinary
lazy plain scans. The query is executed once with the same
`QueryExecutionOptions` as the async path: `None` keeps the 1024-row
cap, `0` leaves sizing to the engine, and a positive value caps each
returned batch. Each `__next__` releases the GIL, waits for exactly one
batch from the same Rust stream through the reviewed
`block_on_interruptible`, and stores the stream back on success.

- No background producer and no Python `LOOP.run` per batch.
- A read error, interrupt, EOF, or the last owner drops the stream. A
normal early `break` can resume the same reader.
- The public `pa.RecordBatchReader` still comes from `from_batches`, so
the schema, Arrow capsule, and exception types stay unchanged. Existing
PyArrow `close()` behavior is unchanged; the known PyArrow close issue
is separately scoped.
- Routing is limited to native, non-namespace, lazy plain scans. Vector,
take, FTS/hybrid, remote, namespace, `to_arrow` direct eager routes, and
Blob `bytes`/`descriptions` keep their existing paths. Take ordering
from #5140 remains on the take path.
- Forward explicit `scan_in_order` through the pull launch; base-only
ordered `to_batches` results and the incompatible `order_by`/fragment
behavior are included in the scan-order suite.
- Adds a public RTE `to_batches` regression: the default LSM route sees
pending memtable writes, while `use_rte(False)` remains base-only.

## Validation

`test_sync_query_direct.py`: 53 passed.

feat!: add explicit scan order contract for local queries (#5138)

BREAKING CHANGE: `QueryRequest` now has a public `scan_in_order:
Option<bool>` field. Existing code that constructs `QueryRequest` with
an exhaustive struct literal must add `scan_in_order: None` to retain
the previous backend default, or use `..Default::default()` where
appropriate. Python defaults are unchanged: leaving `scan_in_order()`
uncalled keeps `None`.

## Problem

Plain Embedded LanceDB scans already use Lance's ordered scan on a fixed
snapshot, but the storage-order contract was undocumented and callers
had no way to require it. Explicit `order_by` sorts the whole result.
Ranked, Enterprise, RTE/LSM, legacy scalar-index and namespace-pushdown
paths cannot always preserve base manifest order.

## Behavior

- `scan_in_order(true)` requires manifest order without adding a sort:
fragments in manifest order, then rows in fragment order.
- `true` disables scalar-index filter planning. Legacy scalar-index
plans can materialize index rows in a different sequence, so filters are
evaluated over the manifest-ordered scan instead. Filter semantics are
unchanged, but the scan can read more data. Default filtered scans can
still use those plans and may not preserve manifest order.
- `scan_in_order(false)` permits the backend to scan unordered. It does
**not** guarantee a different order; an explicit nonempty `order_by`
still sorts.
- Leaving the option unset preserves the backend default. The documented
manifest-order default applies to an unfiltered base-only scan of a
pinned Embedded table version. RTE tables scan the LSM by default and
need `use_rte(false)` for the base-only guarantee. Enterprise and
namespace-pushed scans have no order guarantee.
- `true` conflicts with nonempty `order_by`, take queries,
vector/full-text/hybrid/reranked queries, RTE/LSM reads, and Enterprise
tables. These fail explicitly instead of silently dropping the
requirement. Take conflict validation happens at the shared
take-preparation boundary before offset or row-id selectors are
stripped.
- `with_fragments()` is rejected with `scan_in_order(true)` because
fragment objects cannot be validated against the pinned dataset version.
Use `fragment_ids()`, which resolves fragment ids from the manifest and
preserves manifest order. Both sync and async pandas scanner paths share
this rule.
- Namespace `QueryTable` pushdown executes `true` against Embedded
storage instead of dropping the order. The existing path preserves
projection, filtering, limits, version/branch selection, and RTE
routing; if Embedded storage cannot be read, the query fails.

Supported entry points are plain Rust `Table::query()`, Python sync
`table.search()` and async `table.query()`. The Python pandas scanner
fast path forwards the option and disables scalar-index planning for
explicit order. Existing takes and `with_fragments()` calls with `None`
or `false` are unchanged.

## Validation

- Rust: 6 `scan_in_order` tests, 32 take tests, 25 query-route tests.
- Python: `test_query.py` and `test_namespace.py` 352 passed, 1 skipped
against a matching extension.
- Scoped `pytest --doctest-modules python/lancedb/query.py -k
scan_in_order`: 2 passed. The Rust/Python examples create their own
tables and are executable.
- Regressions cover legacy 0.1 and stable BTREE tables with update and a
filter admitting every row, across pinned versions before and after

and fixed-version multi-fragment reads with deletions, one-row batches,
and limit/offset. No `SortExec` is added.

--check`; Ruff format/check; `git diff --check`.

perf(python): add direct sync query execution (#5141)

## Summary

Route ordinary local `table.search(...).to_arrow()` queries through
private synchronous schema and eager-collection bindings instead of the
Python background event loop. Plain scans, vector searches (including
default vector-column inference), and native FTS in lazy Blob mode now
complete with zero `LOOP.run` submissions.

The synchronous path reuses the existing query lowering, core query
execution, eager collector, Arrow ownership, projection validation,
fragments, row ids, Blob finalization, reranking, and snapshot handling.

releases the GIL while waiting, checks CPython signals on the caller
thread at a bounded interval, and aborts and drops collected state when
a handler raises. Multi-threaded Tokio callback re-entry uses

routing are unchanged. No public API is added.

feat(python)!: preserve input order for take offsets (#5140)

## Summary

Add an opt-in `preserve_order` flag to sync and async `take_offsets`. It
exposes the existing Rust `TakeRestoreExec` ordering path and carries
the flag through `QueryRequest`, `PyQueryRequest`, and the Python
`Query` model.

## Behavior

- Default `preserve_order=False` keeps the existing incremental,
unspecified-order behavior.
- `preserve_order=True` returns found rows in input order, including
repeated offsets.
- Missing non-negative offsets keep filter semantics and are omitted;
negative offsets remain rejected by the existing `u64` contract.
- Rust take queries apply `limit`/`offset` after order and repetition
are restored. Python take builders and Query conversion do not expose
pagination.
- An explicit `order_by` conflicts with offset `preserve_order` and
raises clearly. `take_row_ids` keeps its existing implicit ordering and
explicit-sort behavior.
- `__getitems__` is unchanged: it keeps its Python re-alignment and
strict missing-offset (`ArrowIndexError`) behavior.

## Remote lookup

The remote lookup sends only the deduplicated `_rowoffset IN (...)`
filter and restores order/repetition client-side; there is no new wire
field or backend extension. Namespace take queries stay on local
execution, and RTE/LSM rejects the `_rowoffset` lookup loudly.

## Testing

- Old reviewed head reproduced the serialization regression:
`test_query_serialization_sync/async` failed because the Query model
exposed `False` for an unset field.
- Fixed by using `Optional[bool] = None` and mapping Rust `false` to
absent in `PyQueryRequest`; explicit `True` still survives the actual
round trip.

- Remote ordered Blob bytes, remote permutation, and Blob mode focused
cases: 3 passed.

--check` passed.

## Migration

`lancedb::query::QueryRequest` is a public non-`#[non_exhaustive]`
struct. Downstream code that constructs it with an exhaustive struct
literal must add `preserve_order: false` or use `..Default::default()`.
The field is client-side metadata and is not sent over the remote
protocol.

feat(python)!: support vector columns in permutation torch formats (#5131)

BREAKING CHANGE: `Permutation.with_format("torch_row")` now uses PyTorch
dtype promotion instead of NumPy promotion. Mixed numeric columns can
change dtype, for example int64 and float32 now produce float32 instead
of float64. Cast columns before formatting when the old dtype matters.
Nullable scalar integer and floating columns still produce NaN; nulls in
nested fixed-size-list or tensor columns, and in bfloat16 columns, are
rejected.

## Problem

`Permutation.with_format("torch")`, `"torch_col"`, and `"torch_row"`
fail when the selected columns include a vector (`FixedSizeList`)
column, which is the column training workloads need. The conversion also
has to preserve Arrow slice offsets, logical `FixedShapeTensor` axes,
and visible nested nulls instead of flattening over them.

## Behavior

- Add `with_format("torch_dict")`: a dict of per-column `(B, *S)`
tensors, usable directly with a `DataLoader` identity collate. Tensors
share Arrow storage where the layout allows.
- Extend `torch` per-row dicts to nested `FixedSizeList` and
`FixedShapeTensor`; PyTorch's default collate stacks them back into `(B,
*S)` tensors.
- Preserve `torch_col` as `(C, B, *S)`, including a zero-copy
`unsqueeze(0)` view for one column.
- Preserve `torch_row` as per-row `(C, *S)` tensors, including `(1,)`
for one scalar column, with `torch.promote_types` for mixed numeric
dtypes. Nullable scalar integer and floating columns keep their previous
NaN behavior; nested fixed-size-list and tensor nulls are rejected.
- `torch_col` and `torch_row` reject heterogeneous sample shapes with
the field names, shapes, and guidance to `torch_dict`.
- Support nested fixed-size lists, `FixedShapeTensor` logical axis
permutations, boolean/integer/floating leaves, empty batches, and
nonzero slice offsets. `torch_dict`, `torch`, and `torch_col` reject
visible nulls.
- NumPy still returns one ndarray. Its pandas conversion may copy, may
promote mixed numeric columns to a common numeric dtype (for example
int64 and float32 to float64), and produces an object array for nested
or incompatible columns.
- `lance.bfloat16` is accepted only for a `FixedSizeBinary(2)` leaf
carrying the `ARROW:extension:name` metadata; offsets/length and byte
order are handled before viewing as `torch.bfloat16`. Unmarked binary
columns are rejected.

This is Python-only and does not change persistence, pickling, or public
method signatures.

fix(python): write enum members as their values in table.update (#5061)

`table.update(values=...)` fails for a member of an int- or float-valued
Enum. `value_to_sql` dispatches it to the `int` or `float` handler, and
`str()` returns the member name, so the SQL reads `priority =

`NotImplementedError`. #3232 stores a `(int, Enum)` field as int64 and

disagrees.

The int and float handlers now convert with `int()` and `float()` first,
and an `Enum` handler writes `value.value`. Str-valued members already
worked, because `str.replace` returns a plain `str`. No issue is open

perf(python): deduplicate sync query preparation (#5130)

## Summary

Sync query execution rebuilt schema-derived state several times inside
one call: for vector-column inference, blob projection validation,
row-id preparation, async handoff, and result finalization. A plain
point lookup paid five schema reads and five background-loop submissions
per `to_arrow()`.

This change prepares the schema and projected blob sources once per
execution and reuses them through scan setup, result finalization, and
the async handoff. Sync-prepared queries tell the async layer that blob
row ids are already resolved; nothing is cached between executions, so a
reused builder still observes schema changes. Plain scans and explicit
vector columns no longer read the schema just to infer a vector column,
and the dead vector conversion in `LanceVectorQueryBuilder.to_batches()`
is removed.

Non-lazy vector `to_arrow()` stays on its lazy materialization path, so
reranking and snapshot merging run once before the aggregate blob
conversion. Async behavior, namespace routing, fragments, timeouts, and
public APIs are unchanged. A direct synchronous Rust terminal remains
follow-up work.

`vector`; 50 warmups + 500 calls per run; p50 of three runs. Baseline
and candidate Python packages ran against the same `release-no-lto`

single host.

fix(python): preserve blob query snapshots and row-id guidance (#5129)

## Summary

- Preserve the query snapshot carried by a remote query result when
`fetch_blobs` or `fetch_blob_files` receives that result table, instead
of reading row IDs from the table's current snapshot.
- Send the expected `x-lancedb-query-snapshot` on the descriptor take
used by `fetch_blob_files` and verify the response echo before decoding
any descriptor. NULL and empty descriptors cannot escape unverified.
- Point missing `_rowid` and missing row-id errors at
`take_offsets(offsets, with_row_id=True)` for callers that have row
positions, while keeping the existing missing/deleted row-id details.
- Keep `fetch_blobs` row-ID based. Positional access and seekable
video/DataLoader handle design remain separate work aligned with
ENT-4059; this PR does not add `offsets=` or change that contract.
- Document the behavior and keep empty row-id requests at zero I/O.

## Compatibility

Server 0.5.0 is the basic remote Blob API floor. Snapshot-bound
descriptor reads need the actual query identity echo from the serving

verified, `fetch_blob_files` fails explicitly instead of accepting
descriptors. Metadata-free row-id input keeps the existing
current-snapshot behavior. This does not claim production rollout or
real server testing.

## Summary

`create_table` / `create_empty_table` now accept registered storage
bases and the embedded opt-in for blob URIs outside them. A create with
data registers `initial_bases` in the same commit, so external Blob v2
references no longer need an empty create followed by `add`.

`allow_external_blob_outside_bases`, with `BasePath` re-exported.

dicts, and duck-typed `lance.DatasetBasePath`; `id=None` lets Lance
assign an ID and explicit `0` or duplicate explicit IDs are rejected.

without pylance and keeps field metadata such as
`lancedb:logical_type=mp4`.

opt-in before normalization, input iteration, or HTTP; empty/false
defaults remain an ordinary create.
- Native namespace create merges namespace and connection storage
options into the caller's store parameters instead of replacing them.
This is reconciled with #5114's refresh layering, so caller-scoped
options survive create, refresh, and reopen while namespace-vended
values keep their precedence.
- The outside-base opt-in applies to one write: setting it on create
does not carry over to a later `add()`.

## Validation

--tests --examples`, `cargo clippy --quiet --features remote --tests
--examples`.

/ 87 skipped), matching the CI no-pylance suite. The lightweight and

assertions there; only the pylance-only manifest introspection moved

- Rust and sync Python two-base probes assert that base 1's scoped

- `test_namespace_refresh_layers_caller_scoped_options` covers the
