- Updated `main` through #5127 (including #5114) is merged;
`rust/lancedb/src/database/namespace.rs` and `rust/lancedb/src/table.rs`
match `main`, and no #5114 code was stacked before it merged.

## Dependency note

The Lance dependency stays pinned at the `v15.0.0-beta.25` release on
`main`. With that pin, mixing an automatic base ID (`id=0`) and an
explicit non-zero ID may still collide; the approved upstream fix is
https://github.com/lance-format/lance/pull/11307. Use distinct explicit
non-zero IDs for multi-base creates, or automatic IDs for every base,
until a Lance release containing that fix is pinned. A failed mixed
create can leave the table name listed but unopenable; retrying with
distinct explicit IDs succeeds. Multi-base validation here uses explicit
IDs and bootstrap uses a single automatic ID, so the mixed-ID case is
not claimed as verified until a Lance release containing that fix is
pinned.

fix: add dataset path hint and sync open_table location (#5128)

## Summary

- Expose `location=` on sync `LanceDBConnection.open_table()`, matching
the existing async entry point while leaving remote and namespace APIs
unchanged.
- When a `ListingDatabase` connection URI ends in `.lance`, append a
parent-directory and table-stem hint to the derived-URI `TableNotFound`
error. The error classification and source chain are preserved, and no
extra storage probes are made.

Context: OSS-2858 remains canceled. This is only the narrow embedded DX
follow-up; it does not add a top-level `lancedb.open_table(uri)` API.

## Verification

- Rust targeted listing tests for the `.lance` hint and the
explicit-location path.
- Python sync `open_table` tests for `location=` and the `.lance` hint.
- Pickle round-trip of a sync `location=` table after #5114.
- `cargo check --features remote --tests --examples`, `cargo fmt
--check`, Ruff format/check.

perf(python): add native eager collection for to_arrow (#5127)

## Summary

`to_arrow()` currently collects results one Python future per batch:
both sync and async paths call `to_batches()`, which crosses the
Python/Rust bridge for every default 1024-row batch. Vector queries also
materialize the whole native stream even when no reranker is configured.

This adds a shared Rust eager collector. `execute_to_reader` collects
the batches in Rust, asks the core to skip the default 1024-row output
slicing, and exposes the result through the Arrow C Stream interface, so
Python builds the Table without a Python future per batch. Sync and
async `to_arrow`, including FTS, vector and hybrid eager paths, use it.
`AsyncVectorQuery.to_batches` no longer materializes results when there
is no reranker and now honors `max_batch_length`.

Schema, empty results, timeout, cancellation, and error behavior are
preserved. The existing fragment guard is enforced on the new fast path,
and namespace-pushdown routing keeps its existing Python/Rust split.

## Benchmark

Development-profile editable build, full scans on one revision, 1 warmup
+ 5 measured runs. Absolute values are not release-profile numbers;
compare before/after on the same build.

| Workload | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 5M rows x 3 columns, async | 3.054 s | 0.087 s (35.1x) |
| 5M rows x 3 columns, sync | 3.462 s | 0.090 s (38.3x) |
| 200k rows x 129 columns, async | 0.354 s | 0.082 s (4.3x) |
| 200k rows x 129 columns, sync | 0.387 s | 0.085 s (4.5x) |

The narrow scan returned 4,883 batches capped at 1,024 rows before and
611 batches up to 8,192 rows after.

feat(python): default StreamingDataLoader workers to forkserver (#5112)

## Problem

`StreamingDataLoader` left PyTorch's platform default in place for
worker processes, which is `fork` on Linux. Forked workers inherit the
parent process's native runtime and connections, which is the failure
mode behind the fork-isolation work.

## Behavior

When `num_workers > 0` and `multiprocessing_context` is omitted or
`None`, workers now use `forkserver` when the platform provides it,
otherwise `spawn`. Explicit start-method names and context objects are
unchanged. With `num_workers == 0`, no context is selected, preserving
PyTorch's single-process handling. Callbacks and worker state must be
picklable under the selected start method, following PyTorch's
DataLoader rules.

Existing `StreamingDataset` serialization is sufficient for the default
worker path. This does not change the explicit fork opt-in or the native
client reopen path in #3851.

fix(python): isolate tokio runtime shutdown across fork generations (#5113)

## Problem

A Python process that forks while LanceDB work is in flight inherits the
parent's tokio runtime and its outstanding-call count, but the worker
threads that would release that count do not survive the fork. A child
that exits without using LanceDB can wait for parent work and try to
shut down the inherited runtime; a child that creates its own runtime
can have stale guards decrement its fresh counter.

## Behavior

In-flight calls are now counted per fork generation. An inherited guard
only updates the counter it was created with, and `shutdown` waits only
for the current generation. A runtime tagged with an older generation is
removed and leaked in the child instead of being shut down or joined.
The at-fork child handler still only increments the generation counter.

The fork hook is installed at the start of the first top-level call,
before generation accounting, closing the window where a fork between
accounting and runtime initialization could leave the child sharing the
parent counter.

## Validation

- New fork regressions cover parent work held across fork, child exit
without and with its own runtime, and an inherited guard. Each passes
when run alone in a fresh process.
- `cargo test --quiet --features remote -p lancedb-python --lib
runtime::tests` passes 8 tests in both default parallel and serial
modes.
- `cargo clippy --quiet --features remote -p lancedb-python --tests
--examples` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` pass.
- Rebuilt the PyO3 extension; `test_remote_connection_after_fork` and
`test_inherited_remote_table_reopens_after_fork` pass.

fix: reject unsupported layout options in remote add (#5118)

## Summary

`RemoteTable::add` only transmits the write mode to the remote insert
endpoint, so non-default layout options in `lance_write_params` were
silently ignored. This rejects them before schema lookup and before
either single-request or multipart transmission.

Guarded fields:

- `max_rows_per_file`
- `max_rows_per_group`
- `max_bytes_per_file`

Default `WriteParams` and `mode = Overwrite` keep their existing
behavior. Other write parameters remain untouched.

## Tests

- Focused remote-table regressions cover each guarded field on both
single-request and multipart paths, and verify default, `Create`,
`Append`, and `Overwrite` behavior.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --quiet --features remote -p lancedb --tests`
- Targeted `cargo test --features remote -p lancedb --lib
remote::table::tests::...`

Refs OSS-2882. This is the P0 hotfix; the table-level persistent layout
design remains tracked separately in OSS-2882 and is not closed by this
PR.

fix: keep nonempty order_by out of namespace query pushdown (#5122)

## Problem

With namespace `QueryTable` pushdown enabled, a query with a nonempty
`order_by` was sent to the namespace server even though the request
schema has no `order_by` field. With `limit(1)` this returned the wrong
top row instead of the requested ordering.

## Fix

Treat a nonempty `order_by` as requiring local execution in both the
Python and Rust namespace pushdown gates. `None` or an empty ordering
still uses pushdown. Local execution preserves branch, version and RTE
semantics; if local storage cannot be read, the query fails explicitly
rather than silently dropping the ordering.

## Validation

- Public Python sync `search().order_by(...).limit(1).to_arrow()` and
async `query().order_by(...).limit(1).to_arrow()` against a namespace
mock: returned id 1 with zero pushdown calls.
- `python/tests/test_namespace.py`: 83 passed.
- Rust namespace pushdown tests: 5 passed; `table::query::tests`: 21
passed.
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy`, and Ruff clean.

Fixes
[OSS-3126](https://linear.app/lancedb/issue/OSS-3126/bug-namespace-querytable-pushdown-silently-drops-order-by).

fix: pin native permutation builds to one snapshot (#5126)

## Problem

`PermutationBuilder` pinned backends that returned a snapshot handle,
but `NativeTable` returned `None`. A namespace-backed latest handle
could count and record the local table version while its row-id scan was
pushed to a server that returned newer rows. A native handle with read
refresh enabled could also advance between the version read, count, and
scan. The result was a permutation whose recorded version, row count,
and row ids did not describe one snapshot.

## Fix

- Return an independent pinned native handle from
`NativeTable::snapshot_at_current_version()`, so one build's version,
count, and scan share a dataset.
- Report `scan_order_is_deterministic()` false when a main/latest native
handle may push queries to a namespace server, whose `QueryTable`
request carries no order. Local scans remain deterministic at a fixed
version.

Refs OSS-3109

The query `scan_in_order` API and Python dispatch remain a separate
slice.

fix(python): reject Expr inputs on unregistered Function definitions (#5125)

`FunctionDefinition.__call__` ran the decorated Python callable with any
value it was given, so `my_function(value=col("value"))` executed user
code against an `Expr` or silently returned one, with errors such as
`float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'Expr'`. A
column reference is not a local value: it binds only on a registered
`FunctionVersion`.

An unregistered definition now rejects `Expr` positional and keyword
arguments with `TypeError` before the callable runs, and names the
supported path: `create_function`/`create_function_async`, then
`col(...)` on the returned version. Plain Python and Arrow arguments,
and the class `__init__`/`__call__` lifecycle, are unchanged.

The Function authoring guide's batch example did not register either: a
`pyarrow.Array` annotation carries no element types, so `score_batch`
raised `TypeError` for missing `input_schema` and `output_schema`, and
the page claimed one `pa.RecordBatch` parameter could read several
columns. The example now passes both schemas, shows one `pa.Array`
parameter per input column for multi-column functions, and states that
`input_schema` matches parameters one to one, so a `RecordBatch`
parameter binds one input column. The GPU class example on the same page
had the same missing-schema defect and is fixed too.

Compatibility: code that passed `col(...)` to an unregistered definition
now gets `TypeError` instead of running user code against an `Expr`.
That call was never a supported binding and produced no usable result;
no supported call changes.

chore(python): clarify package summary and search keywords (#5124)

Replace the placeholder `lancedb` PyPI summary with factual wording
covering vector, full-text, and hybrid search on Lance tables. Narrow
the keywords to `lance`, `vector-search`, `full-text-search`, `dataset`,
and `versioning`.

Metadata-only change; runtime behavior is unchanged.

Refs OSS-2883

fix(python): keep Permutation builder copies shallow (#5121)

## Summary

`Permutation`'s `with_*` builders use `copy.copy`, but `Permutation` had
no `__copy__`. Python therefore fell back to
`__getstate__`/`__setstate__`, which calls
`permutation_table.to_arrow()` (unsupported for remote tables) and
rebuilds the base table and reader on every builder call.

Add a targeted `__copy__` that shallow-copies the instance state. The
copy keeps the existing table handles and reader and can change its own
attributes without affecting the original. Pickle serialization and
persist semantics are unchanged.

Refs OSS-2857. The persist feature remains open.

fix(python): accept column names in order_by and validate early (#5119)

## Summary

- Accept column names, `(column_name, "asc"|"desc")` tuples,
`ColumnOrdering`, and `{"column_name": ...}` dicts in both sync and
async `order_by`, including mixed lists.
- Distinguish a bare direction tuple from a list of column names by
container type; `None` and `[]` clear ordering.
- Validate at setter time with actionable errors for unknown dict keys
and invalid directions.
- Export `ColumnOrdering` from `lancedb` and document the accepted forms
with examples.
- Reject non-empty ordering on sync hybrid queries explicitly instead of
silently ignoring it.

Fixes OSS-3108. Namespace pushdown (OSS-3126) is intentionally out of
scope.

## Tests

- `python/tests/test_query.py` (214 passed, 1 skipped)
- `python/tests/test_query.py -k order_by` (7 passed)
- `python/tests/test_fts.py -k order_by` (2 passed)
- `python/tests/test_remote_db.py::test_query_sync_maximal`
- `pytest --doctest-modules python/lancedb/query.py` (21 passed)
- `ruff format` / `ruff check`

fix(python): start background event loop lazily (#5111)

## Summary

Importing `lancedb` currently starts a daemon thread running a private
asyncio loop, even when the process never performs a synchronous
database operation.

Start that loop on the first actual coroutine submission instead.
Concurrent first callers share one initialization, and a forked child
resets the singleton to the unstarted state without touching the
inherited thread or lock, then starts fresh work lazily on first use.

The Rust-side runtime and the existing fork/reopen contracts are
unchanged.

## Validation

- New import, first-use, concurrent first-use, and fork parent/child
coverage passes.
- Existing import, debugger-inspection, cancellation, and remote fork
tests pass.
- `ruff format --check .` and `ruff check .` pass.

fix(python): reject unsupported fragment constraints (#5120)

`with_fragments()` / `fragment_ids()` were only honored by the embedded
plain-scan blob Pandas path. Every other sync, async, and remote
terminal could silently ignore the selection and scan the full table,
and async query conversions plus FTS `count_rows()` could drop the
constraint before execution.

This change makes unsupported paths fail with `NotImplementedError`
before I/O, preserves fragment state across async
Standard/Vector/FTS/Hybrid conversions, and keeps the supported embedded
blob `to_pandas()` behavior unchanged. The FTS `count_rows()` sync and
async entry points now reject fragment constraints explicitly.

Refs OSS-2859

feat(python): make native tables and connections picklable (#5114)

## Summary

Adds `__getstate__`/`__setstate__` to native `LanceTable` and
`LanceDBConnection` so a PyTorch `Dataset` that keeps both can cross
`spawn` and `forkserver` worker boundaries. `Permutation` and
`StreamingDataset` now delegate to the same table state representation
while retaining compatibility with older pickle payloads.

## Pickle contract

- Reconnects from the serialized connection and preserves the table
name, namespace path, explicit storage overrides, location, index-cache
setting, managed versioning and pushdown routing.
- Standard mode reopens at latest; `checkout(version)` remains pinned to
the resolved branch/version; branch handles preserve their branch.
Cross-branch tag checkout records the actual live branch.
- `read_consistency_interval=timedelta(0)` remains distinct from `None`.
- `memory://` tables keep the existing Arrow snapshot export/rebuild
behavior.
- `Session` and unreconstructable custom namespace clients fail at
`pickle.dumps` with an explicit `TypeError`; declared namespace
configurations reconstruct, including an omitted properties map.
- Namespace storage options keep caller-only overrides layered over the
live provider, with vended values winning conflicts. Caller options
survive refresh, refreshed credentials replace old vended values, an
explicit provider remains selected on open, and an empty provider
response stays empty rather than restoring an expired seed.
- Declared Python namespace connections reopen through their connection
provider instead of turning the reconstructed client into an explicit
table provider.

## Verification

- Fresh binding build with `uv run --extra tests --extra dev maturin
develop --extras tests,dev`.
- End-to-end `DataLoader` holding `self._db` and `self._table`: spawn
and forkserver passed.
- `test_namespace.py`: 90 passed; `test_table.py` + `test_db.py` +
`test_permutation.py`: 700 passed, 17 skipped.
- Focused namespace provider/pickle regressions: passed, including
caller-only and vended keys after a declared-namespace refresh.
- Rust `test_namespace_connection_with_storage_options` and
`test_manifest_enabled_vend_input_storage_options`: passed.
- `cargo clippy -p lancedb --features remote --tests --examples`, `cargo
fmt --check`, exact CI Pyright (0 errors/0 warnings), and Ruff passed.
- DataLoader Workers documentation updated; Vale reports 0 findings.

## Scope

Does not change the fork hard-error policy, #3851, or direct
`LanceNamespaceDBConnection` pickling. It does not claim changes to the
existing namespace dir `index_cache_size` behavior. This supersedes the
earlier draft #3486, which only moved the table-state portion.

fix(python): accept optional discard_weight in split_hash (#5116)

### Problem

`PermutationBuilder.split_hash()` raises `TypeError` when
`discard_weight` is omitted because the Python wrapper forwards `None`
while the PyO3 binding requires `u64`. The `_lancedb.pyi` stub also
disagrees with the native signature: it omits `split_names` and types
`discard_weight` as non-optional.

### Behavior

The native binding accepts an optional `discard_weight` and treats
omitted/`None` as `0`, so `split_hash(..., split_names=[...])` works
without passing a discard weight. The stub now matches the binding. A
regression test verifies that omitting `discard_weight` assigns every
row exactly like explicit `0`.

Fixes OSS-2856.

commits.message:
feat(oq): quantize Inkling 2 Mini

oQ now accepts the inkling2_loop model type. The sanitizer maps the loop controllers and message queries, and calibration walks the layer visits in run order, so a looped layer sees all three passes. Its sensitivity is the worst of its passes. The runtime loader now casts each loop part before the final stack so oQ can replay it, with the same values.
chore(cuda-helper): bump the helper to 0.1.7
chore: bump version to 0.8.1

feat(inkling2): support Inkling 2 Mini (#5468)

* feat(inkling2): run looped checkpoints

Inkling 2 checkpoints with a loop_config run a block-aligned core of layers several times per token. Each later pass restarts from the prelude output and reads the blocks of the previous pass through messages, which low-rank controllers mix into the q, k, v and MLP inputs.

The loader maps the per-layer controllers and the cross-pass message queries onto the core layers. Every layer visit owns its cache entry, and the DSpark draft taps count visits, so the bundled draft reads the same states as the reference.

The controller down projection runs as a batched FP32 matmul over its two input halves. A single [rows, 2H] x [2H, r] matmul gets a row-count dependent kernel in MLX, which made prefill chunking change the logits.

* fix(inkling2): size the prefill helper cache by its kept layers

The loop support sized the cache by the layer schedule. The prefill helper drops the later layers of a plain model, so its cache had entries for layers it never ran.

* feat(inkling2): load the inkling2_loop model type

The looped checkpoint now sets model_type to inkling2_loop. It runs the same Inkling 2 model, so the loader, the VLM engine, DSpark, the MTP checks and model discovery accept both types.

The prefill helper and oQ keep only inkling2 because neither supports loops.

---------

Co-authored-by: jundot <jundot@users.noreply.github.com>

feat(hy4): add Hy4 and Hy4-flash with DFly2 MTP, oQ and oQh (#5463)

Tencent Hy4 (hy_v4_vl) and Hy4-flash (hy_v4_flash) load as native VLMs with image input. The FP8 releases load directly, and oQ and oQh convert both models one layer at a time. DFly2 drafts through Lightning MTP, including for concurrent requests. Decode-exact verify is implemented but off by default.

Custom kernels cover the hyper-connections, attention sinks in sparse MLA and block-mask attention, and indexer scoring and top-k, with NAX paths on M5. Row-exact verify now covers 2 and 3 bits.

On an M3 Ultra with Hy4-flash FP8, prefill at 32k goes from 467 to 720 tok/s, and decode reaches 38-39 tok/s with MTP depth 5.

Co-authored-by: Andreas Petersson <andreas@capacity.at>

fix(inkling2): load releases with a ModelOpt quantization_config

The public Inkling 2 checkpoints now have a ModelOpt quantization_config. mlx-lm then fails to load them, and oQ and oQe fail too. Drop that config when loading, and let oQ accept these sources.

fix(mtp): per-row rollback of affine/turboquant batch caches in batched verify (#5253)

* fix(mtp): per-row rollback of affine/turboquant batch caches in batched verify

Batched Lightning MTP and batched DFlash verify on quantized batch caches
(affine8, affine4, turboquant KV) took the scalar rollback path:
copy.deepcopy of the whole batch cache per distinct accepted count, then a
row extract and merge. Qwen3.8-27B with affine8 KV and DFlash2, 2 sessions
at ~128K tokens under a 48 GB ceiling: usage goes from 41 GB to 55 GB when
both sessions start decoding and the enforcer aborts both requests.

- BatchTurboQuantKVCache.trim_rows drops a different count per row without
  moving packed state: rows keep host-side write ends (_row_ends), appends
  go to each row's own end and make_mask hides the dropped columns. filter
  keeps the row ends; extend and finalize realign the rows first.
- fused_batch treats these caches as vector-rollback capable: each row is
  trimmed before the model's rollback, and the caches read as speculating
  while it runs, so mlx-vlm's append-cache trim leaves them alone.
- The native affine kernel stops each row at its own written end, so a
  decode step without a mask (Qwen3.5 left-padded decode) never reads a
  shorter row's dropped tokens.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: skip the ragged-row kernel tests where TensorOps do not launch

The new tests guarded on Metal being available. On a system where the
TensorOps attention kernel does not build (the CI runner), the native
attention returns None and the tests failed on their own precondition.
Use the launch probe test_affine4.py already has.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(mtp): vector rollback for batches that mix quantized and plain KV

turboquant_skip_last is on by default, so the last attention layer stays a
plain BatchKVCache and every quantized batch is a mixed batch. Those fell
back to the scalar rollback, which deep-copies the whole batch cache for
each distinct accepted count. They now take the vector rollback: the
quantized layers drop per row in place, the model's rollback trims the
plain layer, and then every layer is realigned so each row ends at the same
column again (the quantized rows rolled one layer at a time, a deferred
plain tail realigned). The model's one attention mask fits all layers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(affine4): bound each row at its own end on the non-native attention routes

After trim_rows, a decode or verify step with mask=None or "causal" reached
the native kernels with per-row ends, but when they declined (a cache under
256 tokens, no TensorOps, or an unsupported shape) the fused and portable
routes got the plain mask and a shorter row read its dropped draft columns.
The batch mask now carries the row ends whenever a row ends before the last
column.

Reported with a repro and the fix by masterfasa.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(turboquant): realign ragged rows in place, moving only the short rows

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(mtp): realign a mixed batch only when its layers disagree on the row ends

After a per-row rollback the quantized layers keep each row at its own end
and the plain layer keeps the same ends as a deferred tail, so the one mask
the model builds fits both. Rows move only when the plain layer realigns
(its tail grew past the bound, or a filter, extend or outside read realigned
it). The common part of the plain tail is dropped so the bank stays as wide
as the quantized layers, and a single-token decode of a ragged batch takes
the per-row seam even without left padding.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(mtp): trim ragged rollback comments and fold tests into existing files

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: jundot <jundot@users.noreply.github.com>

perf(cache): join quantized caches layer by layer with room to grow (#5321)

* perf(cache): join quantized caches layer by layer into buffers with room to grow

Two requests that restore a long quantized prefix and start decoding together
needed about twice their KV on top of the batch:

- generate._merge_caches kept every request's whole cache alive next to the
  batch it was copied into until the last layer was merged. The merge now runs
  one layer at a time and lets go of each donor layer, as the join of a
  running batch already does. That join also drops the singleton layer it
  copied into a batch layer, and both loops index the layers: zip and
  enumerate keep their last tuple, which held a donor layer for longer.
- A restored, merged or joined quantized state was exactly as long as its
  tokens, so the first token appended to it copied the whole packed state and
  left the old buffer in the MLX pool, and every 256 tokens did it again.
  Restore, merge and join now write the states into one zero buffer with
  spare columns, long caches grow by 1/64 of their length instead of 256
  tokens, and a filter keeps the spare columns.

Synthetic affine8 caches at Qwen3.8-27B geometry (4 KV heads, dim 256),
65,536 tokens x 4 layers per request, peak above the two requests and pool
afterwards, in units of one request's KV (one layer is 0.25):

  merge of two pending requests        2.25 / 2.25  ->  0.51 / 0
  a request joins one running alone    1.50 / 2.00  ->  0.51 / 0
  first token on the 2-row batch       0.51 / 1.98  ->  0    / 0
  first tokens on a restored cache     0.26 / 1.00  ->  0    / 0

Written states are unchanged: a differential run of merge, extend, filter,
extract, trim and append scenarios on affine8, affine4 and TurboQuant caches
gives identical arrays on main and here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(cache): keep at least 64 spare tokens instead of up to two growth steps

A built state reserved two growth steps past its tokens, so short and mid
contexts carried up to a full 256-token step more per row and layer than
they need (+50% resident KV at 256 tokens, +20% at 1K, measured by
masterfasa). It now reserves up to the next step boundary past
tokens + 64: a decode step, a verify block or a short suffix chunk still
fits without a growth copy.

* refactor(cache): trim comments and fold join tests into existing files

The streamed refinement walk passed the causal attention mask to every

from layer 0 on the refinement saw other layer inputs than the resident
walk and wrote other codes, in oQe and oQh builds. The streamed imatrix
walk already skips the mask for recurrent layers; the refinement walk
now does the same.

Adds a streamed-vs-resident output test for enhanced builds (oQe, and

A lookup of up to 64 rows advises every page of the weight, scale and bias tensors before copying any from the mapping, instead of reading each tensor through the I/O pool in turn.

feat(cluster): run DeepSeek V4.1 tensor-parallel on Macs with different memory (#5272)

Each DeepSeek V4.1 tensor-parallel rank can hold its own number of output groups and expert blocks, sized to its memory when an equal split does not fit. Expert blocks follow the checkpoint's w2 groups and oQh rotation blocks. JACCL tensor-parallel ranks default to Metal fast sync.

feat(dsv41): release expert bank slots for a prefill that needs them (#5406)

* feat(dsv41): release expert bank slots for a prefill that needs them

A long prefill that runs short of memory currently has two options: shrink
the chunk, or collapse every layer's expert bank to the routing floor. The
banks are the only large resident block that can give memory back without a
model reload, so give them the same sized release/restore the generic
ExpertCache has (#4842): shrink each bank by the coarse step that covers the
shortfall, keeping the hottest experts, and grow it back to the plan's
capacity at the next decode step, where misses refill the empty slots.

_ExpertSlots gains a runtime capacity beside the shared plan's loaded
capacity, plus release_slots/restore_slots/_resize. _resize keeps slot_of in
least-to-most-recently-used order so _victim keeps its tie-break, rebuilds
the writable host views, and materializes every replacement array before
publishing the new capacity, so a failed allocation leaves the bank unchanged.
A bank whose slots are already a contiguous prefix is copied in place instead
of gathered, so a restore's transient stays at old + new slots.

loading.py records the banks on the model and engine/vlm.py wires them into
the existing moe_offload_release/restore/releasable hooks, on the union of the
generic caches and the banks, so the scheduler, the pool's admission ladder
and the unload settle all use the same paths as every other offloaded MoE
model. No new setting, env var or hardware gate.

feat(oq): refine DeepSeek V4.1 routed expert codes below oQ4

The oQe code refinement from #5292 never ran on DeepSeek V4.1, whose own exporter writes the build. Below oQ4 that exporter re-rounds the FP4 routed experts to affine codes, which is where the refinement helps most.

After the export, the routed experts now get their codes re-picked against per-expert calibration Grams, with the dequantized FP4 source as the target. The Grams come from the staged source forward the oQh experts already use, now shared by both passes. Scales, biases and sizes stay the same, so the build format does not change.

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 oQ3e, KL against the source over 30 windows of 2048 tokens drops 5.4% (95% CI -7.4% to -3.0%). Korean drops 9.1% and Japanese 6.4%, English text and mixed code stay within noise, and Python code rises 2.3%. The pass adds about 1h45m on an M3 Ultra.

perf(gemma4): fused MoE router and combine for decode and verify rows (#5315)

* perf(gemma4): fused MoE router and combine for decode and verify rows

Gemma 4's MoE layers route with argpartition, take_along_axis, a softmax over
the kept logits, a gather and a multiply by per_expert_scale, then combine the
experts with (w * y).sum(-2): about six launches in the router and two in the
combine per MoE layer per step (30 layers on 26B-A4B).

For up to 16 token rows (one-token decode, a speculative verify block, a small
decode batch) the router is now one launch and the combine one launch. Both
reproduce the stock arithmetic bit for bit: argpartition at these widths is a
stable ascending sort, so the kept experts come out ascending in (logit, index)
and logits tied at the k-th place keep the highest index; the softmax rounds
exp, the two four-wide partial sums and the reciprocal in the activation dtype;
the k-sum rounds after each add. The router also stops recomputing
scale * root_size on every call. Prefill chunks, other dtypes and top_k > 8 keep
the stock ops.

perf(messages): start oversized completed tool histories collapsed (#24547)

### What this PR does

Before this PR: agent message lists always pass `expandToolSteps: true`,
so every completed process group mounts its full tool history on first
paint. In a long agent turn this reached ~12k–16k DOM nodes per group
(one group held 211,844 characters of tool output), even though most of
it sits far off-screen.

After this PR: ordinary turns keep the current auto-expanded behavior. A
completed history with more than 80 entries or more than 100 KiB of tool
payload text starts collapsed and can be expanded with the existing
process trigger. An explicit user toggle still wins through the message
disclosure cache.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Runtime captures of the main renderer showed the largest expanded groups
at 11,939 and 16,256 DOM nodes (one group: 211,844 characters, 26 tool
blocks), while the visible message list only held ~2.4k nodes. The
top-level history is auto-expanded in agent sessions because
`agentMessageListAdapter` sets `expandToolSteps: true`, independent of
the thinking auto-collapse preference.

The fix is a render-budget guard in the existing `defaultExpanded`
decision:

- cap by entry count (cheap) and by a bounded payload-length estimate
(never materialises a JSON string, early-exits at the budget,
depth-limited);
- keep explicit disclosure state authoritative;
- leave the `collapseCompletedToolHistory: false` inline path unchanged.

Alternatives considered: unmounting expanded history for keep-alive
background tabs (React 19 `<Activity>`) would cut more DOM, but it
changes tab-switch cost and inner state, so it is out of scope here.

### Breaking changes

None. Behavior changes only for histories above the thresholds, which
start collapsed instead of expanded.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The two thresholds are empirical (80 entries / 100 KiB). The largest
observed expanded group was 211,844 characters; a normal turn in the
same session stayed around 39k characters. Explicit user expansion is
never overridden.

### Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run --project renderer
src/renderer/components/chat/messages`: 115 files / 1,232 tests passed,
including two new cases (81 entries and a 120 KB tool output start
collapsed, and still expand on click).
- `pnpm typecheck:web` passed.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint --deny-warnings`, and `eslint` on the changed files
passed.

```release-note
Start very large completed tool histories collapsed so long agent turns no longer mount tens of thousands of DOM nodes on open.
```

---------

Signed-off-by: NatsUIJM <NatsUIJM@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: NatsUIJM <NatsUIJM@users.noreply.github.com>

Test the Windows signing caller check and document activation limits

Run the packaging worker input check under PowerShell for allowed and refused callers. Document that the tag check before draft creation is not atomic and needs tag protection, and that production signing must not be enabled before the production token moves to a protected release-signing environment. Remove obsolete signed RC dispatch rows.

Release RC drafts from version tags, build branch rc read-only

release_rc.yml now runs only for the push that creates a version tag equal to version.inc and pointing at the pushed commit; release.py never creates a tag and checks it again right before creating the draft. Offline tests run with PyYAML in a job without write access. Each platform has its own publisher job after its build; the macOS/Linux workers only stage release files (stage_release) and no longer publish.

ci_rc.yml builds the five targets on branch rc with read-only access, no tag, no draft and no signing. ccpp_win_rc.yml becomes an unsigned standalone diagnostic. windows_package.yml refuses production signing outside release_rc.yml on a tag, and test signing outside a manual nightly.

Fix the Windows packaging job on the runner image

windows-2022 ships the Chocolatey package wixtoolset 3.14.1.20250415, so pinning the package 3.14.1 was a refused downgrade. Use the installed WiX, install that package revision only when WiX is missing, and require WiX 3 at least 3.14.1 (the template is WiX 3; 3.14.1 completes its security fix) instead of an exact version.

Also name the job after its signing mode: Package (unsigned), Sign (test) and package or Sign (production) and package.

Check the RC release files before any final upload

Review follow-up: the staged MSI must be the checked installer and the portable ZIP is checked before the three final uploads; every ZIP path segment must be a plain Windows name; binaries under hidden paths are refused because the portable artifact would drop them; the package is walked top-down so a junction is refused before it is listed.

Build the Windows nightly with the shared workers

ccpp_win.yml now uses windows_build.yml and windows_package.yml in nightly mode. Triggers, the manual sign=true test signing, dated identity and artifact names are unchanged; unsigned packaging never receives the SignPath token. Documents the shared jobs and the installer contents check.

Verify Windows installer contents before upload

Test-InstallerPayload.ps1 extracts the MSI administratively, without installing it, and requires the EXE/DLL files of the package byte for byte and the expected ProductVersion; for RC release files it also checks the portable ZIP. Nothing is uploaded before this check.

Review hardening of the build/package split: separate SignPath policy per mode without fallback, RC MSI version read from SLIC3R_RC_VERSION_DOTS, links and junctions refused in the transferred artifact, ProductVersion checked inside Prepare-Binaries.ps1, hidden files kept in the transfer, fixed test identity.

Split the Windows RC build from signing and packaging

windows_build.yml compiles one commit and uploads the unsigned package with a manifest. windows_package.yml downloads that exact artifact, verifies it against the same checkout, renders the WiX source from the repository template, signs when requested and stages release files. Triggers, artifact names and signing rules are unchanged.
add missing SuperSlicer_logo icon

Use the shared MSVC pipeline for Windows Debug

Remove Strawberry Perl and legacy cache actions, restore the same clean dependency cache as the nightly and RC, and keep Debug symbols without copying the debug CRT into the artifact.

Preserve the numeric version of Windows nightly MSIs

Keep the four-part ProductVersion from version.inc. Capture the build date once for the binary version strings and MSI filename, and use that filename through linking, signing and upload.

Keep Windows builds on bundled MSVC GMP and MPFR

Isolate CMake and its dependency builds from Strawberry Perl and GNU toolchain paths, and explicitly select the bundled GMP and MPFR import libraries. Invalidate the old shared Windows cache.

commits.message:
Merge pull request #1578 from r-vasquez/sr-guid-schema-locator

sr: support schema GUIDs in ConfluentHeader

Merge pull request #1579 from twmb/sr-decodeindex-length

sr: reject an index count longer than the record

sr: support schema GUIDs in ConfluentHeader

Confluent has a second schema ID encoding that identifies the schema by
its GUID: magic byte 1, then the 16 bytes of the GUID, then the protobuf
index. Confluent's serializers do not write it in front of the message;
they write it as the value of the __key_schema_id or __value_schema_id
record header. Their deserializers accept either encoding in either
place. This adds three functions to ConfluentHeader for it:

  - AppendEncodeGUID is the GUID twin of AppendEncode.
  - DecodeGUID is the GUID twin of DecodeID. It is strict and returns
    ErrBadHeader for anything that is not a GUID header.
  - DecodeIDOrGUID accepts both forms, for a consumer that does not
    know which one the producer wrote.

The functions only encode and decode bytes; reading or writing the
record header is up to the caller.

The GUID is a string in the text form that the registry returns, the
same as SubjectSchema.GUID and Client.SchemaByGUID. The SerdeHeader
interface, the existing functions, and Serde do not change.

The ErrBadHeader message no longer names the 5 byte header and the 0
magic byte, because the error now also covers the GUID form.

sr: reject an index count longer than the record

DecodeIndex now returns io.EOF when a record claims more message indexes
than it has bytes left. Previously, with maxLength 0, DecodeIndex
allocated a slice of the claimed length before reading any index, so a
9-byte corrupt record could allocate 512 MiB, and a 15-byte one panicked
with "makeslice: len out of range". Each index takes at least one byte,
so a longer count can never be read; io.EOF is what a short read already
returns.

fix(coding-agent): run shutdown cleanup when the Windows console closes (#11889)

## Problem

pi listens for SIGHUP only on POSIX (`process.platform !== "win32"` in
interactive, print and RPC mode). The check came with the first SIGHUP
handler (5d440b055, #3212), and neither the commit nor the issue
mentions Windows.

On Windows, Node never emits SIGTERM (`TerminateProcess` cannot be
caught), but libuv does emit SIGHUP when the console window or terminal
tab is closed (`CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT`). Windows then ends the process about
5 s later (measured 4.8-5.1 s). With no SIGHUP listener, closing the
window ran no `session_shutdown` and killed no process trees:

```
pi in a conhost window, bash tool running `bash -c "sleep 300"`, close the window
before: pi exits at once, no session_shutdown, ping/sleep.exe + bash.exe keep running
```

Libuv's job object kills the bash process Node spawned, but not what
bash started.

Enabling SIGHUP alone was not enough. On Windows,
`killTrackedDetachedChildren()` started an asynchronous `taskkill /F /T`
per pid, and the shutdown paths call `process.exit` right after it. pi's
exit kills the shell (libuv's job), and `taskkill /T` walks parent pids,
so it no longer finds the shell's descendants. Killing a shell and
exiting at once left `sleep.exe` + bash 6 out of 6 times.

## Solution

- Interactive, print and RPC mode listen for SIGHUP on all platforms.
- On Windows, `killTrackedDetachedChildren()` runs one `taskkill /F /T
/PID a /PID b ...` and waits for it (`spawnSync`, 2 s timeout, well
below the ~5 s Windows allows after a close). `windowsHide` gives
taskkill its own hidden console, so it does not receive the closing
console's close event. This also fixes the same race on the
dead-terminal and crash exit paths, which already call it.
- Normal quit in interactive mode (Ctrl+D, `/quit`) and RPC `shutdown()`
call `killTrackedDetachedChildren()` after `dispose()`. `dispose()` only
starts the asynchronous kill of a running user `!` command or RPC `bash`
command, which had the same race: quitting while `!ping -n 3000
127.0.0.1` ran left `ping.exe` and two `bash.exe` on Windows (before and
after enabling SIGHUP). Agent bash tool commands were not affected,
since dispose waits for the aborted tool.
- `docs/extensions.md` notes that on Windows `session_shutdown` has
about 5 s after a console close.

## Testing

Windows 11 x64, Git Bash, built pi started in a new `conhost.exe` or
`wt.exe -w new` window by a PowerShell script, with a test extension
whose fake model runs one bash tool call and which logs
`session_shutdown`. The window was closed by posting `WM_CLOSE` to the
console window; Ctrl+D and `/quit` were typed with `WriteConsoleInput`.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| conhost close, print / RPC | exit 1 after ~20 ms, no
`session_shutdown`, ping + 2 bash left | exit 129 after 270-370 ms,
`session_shutdown` runs, nothing left |
| conhost close, interactive | same | exit 0 after 390-600 ms, nothing
left |
| Windows Terminal window close, all 3 modes | same as conhost | same as
conhost |
| `session_shutdown` hook taking 3 s | - | completes, exit at ~3.3 s |
| `session_shutdown` hook taking 8 s | - | Windows kills pi at 5.03 s
(`0xC000013A`); processes already gone, since the kill runs before
`session_shutdown` |
| Ctrl+D / `/quit` while a `!` command runs; RPC stdin EOF while a
`bash` command runs | command left running | nothing left |

- Writes to the closed console do not throw or hang (no EPIPE);
interactive runs reached the normal exit path.
- The waited taskkill takes 190-330 ms, only when a command is running;
otherwise `killTrackedDetachedChildren()` returns at once.
- Linux (WSL), real pi: SIGHUP exits 129, SIGTERM 143, both run
`session_shutdown` and leave nothing; RPC stdin EOF exits 0. Same before
and after.
- New tests: SIGHUP on win32 in `print-mode.test.ts` (fails without the
change), the single waited taskkill and unchanged POSIX behaviour in
`shell-kill-process-tree.test.ts`, kill after dispose on RPC stdin EOF
in `rpc-prompt-response-semantics.test.ts` (fails without the change).
These and `bash-close-hang-windows` pass.
- `npm run check`: clean apart from `check:install-lock:coding-agent`,
which fails on Windows on unmodified `main` too (the generator orders
the `chalk` entry differently); the steps after it pass.

## Notes

- `taskkill /T` still misses processes whose parent already exited, for
example `sleep` in `bash -c "sleep 300; echo x"`, `sleep 300 | cat` or
`sleep 300 &` in Git Bash. This is the gap #11854 closes with a job
object. #11854 touches the same signal handlers and
`killTrackedDetachedChildren()`; whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- Not tested: closing a single tab of a Windows Terminal window with

fix(tui): move repeated prompts to the front of editor history instead of duplicating them (#12370)

Fixes #12279. Alternative to #12280.

**Problem.** Tree navigation re-renders the branch with
`populateHistory: true`, which calls `Editor.addToHistory` for every
prompt on the branch. `addToHistory` only skipped a repeat of the most
recent entry, so each navigation duplicated the branch's prompts. With
prompts p1..p5, going back to p4 turned history `p5 p4 p3 p2 p1` into
`p3 p2 p1 p5 p4 p3 p2 p1`, and the duplicates push older entries out of
the 100-entry cap.

**Fix.** `addToHistory` now moves a prompt that is already in history to
the most recent position instead of adding it again (like zsh
`HIST_IGNORE_ALL_DUPS`).

Why here and not in the callers (#12280 stops tree navigation from
filling history):
- Navigating to a branch from an earlier run that pi did not start on
still adds its prompts to Up-arrow history, once. With #12280 those
prompts never reach history.
- `/fork`, `/clone` and `/resume` back to a session also re-add prompts;
this covers them without changes in coding-agent.

Behavior change: a prompt submitted several times is stored once, at its
latest position. The old test "allows non-consecutive duplicates in
history" was replaced.

**Validation.**
- New editor test for #12279; it and the updated duplicate test fail on
the old code.
- tmux, session with prompts p1..p5, going back with `/tree`: history is
`p3 p2 p1 p5 p4` after going back to p4, then `p2 p1 p3 p5 p4` after
going back to p3. Before: 8, then 10 entries.
- `npm run check` passes.

feat(chord,p2): send the sync protocol version with every Radius request

A later handoff of a session to another server will change the sync rules
for that session. Radius can tell how a body is encoded (v: 2 per line), but
not which rules the writer follows, so an older server waking up after a
handoff could keep writing under the old rules.

Chord exports SYNC_PROTOCOL (1), the version of its sync rules, separate
from the body encoding (LOG_VERSION). p2's Radius adapter sends it as the
pi-sync-protocol header on every request. A 409 protocol_too_old (the
session needs a newer protocol) is terminal: uploads for that store stop
with a message to update Pi instead of retrying forever. RadiusSyncError
now carries Radius's error code.

fix(p2): index forked subagents from their fork point

Search indexed every subagent from its first entry. A subagent forked from
the main conversation (a Discord thread's or a spinoff extension's) reads
the main conversation's entries up to its fork point before its own, and
those keep their own conversation ID:

  entries(fork) = [1:#2, 1:#4, ..., 1:#78, fork:#643, fork:#676]

The worker sent them in the fork's batch, the server refused the batch
("index messages must belong to the batch conversation"), and the worker
retried every second. The fork was never indexed, and neither was any
subagent after it in the registry.

The worker now reads the records of the top-level conversations and the
subagents in one commit and starts each at its fork point (parent.at), as
/tree branches already did. The inherited entries stay indexed once, with
the conversation that stores them; a conversation without a fork point
starts at 0 as before.

Test: search.test.ts forks a subagent through the Discord thread path; its
own messages are found under the fork, the inherited one only under
conversation 1. Without the fix the test times out waiting for the fork's
message.

fix(ai): remove abort listeners after retry backoff (#12348) *Completed retry backoffs now release their abort listeners, preventing caller-owned signals from accumulating stale retry state.* ## Context `retryAssistantCall()` attaches an abort listener while waiting between attempts. The listener uses `{ once: true }`, but that removes it only when the signal aborts. When the timer completes normally, the listener remains attached. As a result, three completed backoffs leave three listeners on the caller’s signal even when the subsequent attempt succeeds. Repeated retries can retain additional listeners and their closures for the lifetime of that signal. ## Implementation The backoff now uses a named abort handler. When the timer completes, it removes that handler before resolving. If the signal aborts first, the existing behavior remains unchanged: the timer is cleared, the listener removes itself after firing, and the retry returns an aborted assistant message. The retry regression exercises three transient failures followed by a successful response and verifies that no abort listeners remain on the caller-owned signal. ## Validation We created a temporary TUI hook ran eleven timer-backed retry waits against one signal and displayed the listener count after every completed backoff and Node’s standard diagnostic was piped to a log file for review. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | On `origin/main`, each completed backoff retained another listener. The final count was 11 and Node emitted a `MaxListenersExceededWarning` whose stack pointed to `sleep()` in `retry.ts`. After this change, the listener count remained zero after every completed backoff. The final count was zero and the redirected warning log remained empty. Closes #10506

fix(chord): close remote sync bodies a pull reads but does not consume

pullSession read a remote body and could then throw before consuming it:
a copy behind an archive slot gets HistoryUnavailableError right after
the read. FileSystemSyncRemote returned the body as an async generator
over an already open file, and a generator that never started does not
run its finally, even on return(). The file was left to garbage
collection: a DEP0137 warning on Node 22 (seen in CI in the chord sync
tests), and on Node 26 an uncaught ERR_INVALID_STATE that ends the
process.

pullSession now passes each body it reads through readBody, which calls
return() on the body's iterator when the read ends, also when it threw
or never started. A FileSystemSyncRemote body is an iterator that closes
its file at its end, on a failed read, or on return(), also before the
first read. getBatch/getSnapshot document the rule: a body may hold a
file or a connection until it is read to the end or return() is called.

return() is the standard way to stop an async iterator, so the remote
interface stays as it is. p2's Radius remote returns its fetch response
body, which return() cancels, so it needs no change.

Tests: two regression tests count opened and closed file readers instead
of waiting for garbage collection.

fix(chord,p2): continue a backup from a full copy after the outbox was turned off

Turning backup off drops the store's outbox; turned on again, the outbox starts
at the store's head, past what the backup holds. uploadSession then failed with
OutboxUnavailableError on every attempt, and the scheduler retried forever.

The upload now puts an archive (the store's whole state) into the slot after
the remote's head whenever the outbox does not reach back to it, so the backup
goes on in the same history. remoteHistory and pullSession restore from the
newest archive slot along the chain; a copy behind it gets
HistoryUnavailableError and restores fresh. foldSession folds every slot the
snapshot covers, also those before an archive slot.

A full copy, because nothing records what changed while the outbox was off:
the store holds only its current state, so it cannot tell which rows changed
after the last sync or which were deleted. Sending only the difference needs a
download of the backup to compare against, or a per-row seq with deletion
markers in the store; a one-off upload after a rare off/on is cheaper than
either for now.

fix(coding-agent): keep tool preview text readable across terminal themes (#12347) *Tool previews now apply Pi’s theme foreground to unscoped highlighted text, keeping code readable when Pi and the terminal use contrasting color themes.* ## Context The shared syntax highlighter assigned colors to recognized tokens such as keywords and numbers, but emitted unscoped text without a foreground color. Identifiers, operators, spaces, and punctuation therefore inherited the terminal’s default foreground instead of Pi’s theme. This made ordinary code text nearly invisible on tool cards when the terminal and Pi used contrasting themes. A dark terminal with Pi’s light theme produced pale text on a pale card, while a light terminal with Pi’s dark theme produced dark text on a dark card. ## Implementation The CLI highlighting theme now uses Pi’s `text` color as its default formatter. fix(ai,coding-agent): make system the default instruction role in openai-completions (#12134)

TLDR:
On chat-completions api, change the default instruction role from
developer to system.

Inspired by: #12101 by @qoli

---
The trigger was #10741: Groq's qwen/qwen3.8-27b failed on the first
message:
`400: minijinja: rendering failed: raise_exception: Unexpected message
role.`

Problem: openai-completions sent the system messages of every reasoning
model with the `developer` role unless the catalog turned it off.
`developer` is OpenAI's role; many other hosts' chat templates reject
it, as Groq's Qwen template does.

Every new OpenAI-compatible provider or reasoning model hit the same bug
until someone added `supportsDeveloperRole: false` to the catalog; about
20 provider files carried that line. Nothing in models.dev says which
role a model accepts, so the catalog could not get this right on its
own.

Solution: detectCompat() now defaults supportsDeveloperRole to true only
for api.openai.com. Every other host gets `system`. This applies to the
initial system prompt and to mid-conversation system messages.

Built-in models whose role changes from developer to system:
- groq: 5 (gpt-oss and Qwen)
- xiaomi, xiaomi-token-plan-*: 9 MiMo models
- openrouter: 89 openai/* and anthropic/* models; 12 of them (newer GPT
models) also support mid-conversation system messages
(supportsMidConvoSystemMessages), which change role too All other
built-in Chat Completions models already sent `system`.

Why the default is only api.openai.com:
- api.openai.com keeps `developer` because OpenAI documents it as the
role for its reasoning models. In practice this rarely matters: the
built-in OpenAI models all use the Responses API, so it only affects
custom models that call OpenAI through openai-completions.
- Azure is excluded. Its built-in OpenAI models also use the Responses
API; its only built-in Chat Completions model is DeepSeek, which needs
`system`.
- OpenRouter is excluded: its Chat Completions reference accepts
`system` ("System message for setting behavior") and `developer` with
the same fields, and gives no reason to prefer `developer` for any model
(https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/chat/create-a-chat-completion).
The openai/* and anthropic/* exception came in with #5309 without a
reported need.
- compat.supportsDeveloperRole still overrides the default.
- The Responses API has its own setting and is unchanged.

The now-redundant `supportsDeveloperRole: false` lines are removed from
the catalog and the llama extension.

How we checked it is safe: live requests to the affected hosts, each
model given the same instruction once as `developer` and once as
`system`:
- Groq qwen/qwen3.8-27b: developer 400, system OK. Groq gpt-oss-20b:
both OK.
- Xiaomi mimo-v2.6-pro and mimo-v2.6-flash: both roles OK.
- OpenRouter openai/gpt-5-mini, openai/gpt-oss-20b,
anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, moonshotai/kimi-k2.6, qwen/qwen3.6-plus,
deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro: both roles OK.
- OpenRouter openai/gpt-5.4-mini and openai/gpt-5.5 with an instruction
added mid-conversation: both roles OK.

Released clients: they fetch new catalogs from pi.dev and still default
supportsDeveloperRole to true, so the removed `false` lines would make
them send `developer` to hosts that reject it. MINIMUM_PI_VERSION is
raised to 1.5.3 so they keep the last catalog published for them.

Fixes high sleep current of BWRY panels (#598)

The BWRY panels exhibit high sleep current (600uA) when light sleep is requested; the current should be around 10uA. This changes the sleep mode to deep sleep which does achieve the very low sleep current.

Fixed the PNG decoder leaking when png_to_epd returns early (#835)

png_to_epd allocated its 49 KB decoder before two early returns and
freed it on neither: the previous-image return on FastEPD panels, and
the -1 on Spectra 6 panels when the frame buffer can't be allocated.
The decoder is now allocated after the first and deleted before the
second. The only caller never asks for the previous image, so the first
can't happen yet.

Fixed a crash when there's no memory for the PNG decoder (#834)

png_to_epd allocated its 49 KB decoder with plain new, which throws
std::bad_alloc when the heap has no block that size and aborts the
device (core dump from a desk OG: operator new(49472) in png_to_epd).
The null check after it never ran. The decoder is now allocated without
throwing, png_to_epd logs the failure and returns -1, and draw_image
stops instead of refreshing with that as the mode. The same -1 already
came back from the Spectra 6 branch when its frame buffer failed, and
was refreshed with too.

test(workflow): add integration tests for in-place child retries

Add end-to-end integration tests for in-place `Workflow` child retries across parallel branches, parallel workers, dynamic children, static agents, and resumable/HITL workflows.

- Add integration tests for sibling checkpoint status during an in-place retry, parallel worker children with and without their own `retry_config`, sibling budget isolation when a child has its own policy, resumable failure recovery and HITL resume after an in-place retry, a child rejecting an awaited `ctx.run_node()` result, and static `BaseAgent` child retries.

Testing Plan:
- Unit and integration tests in `tests/unittests/workflow/test_workflow_failures.py`, `tests/unittests/workflow/test_workflow_hitl.py`, and `tests/unittests/workflow/test_workflow_parallel_worker.py`.

Co-authored-by: Thomas Zettl <zettlt@google.com>
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026182927

fix(workflow): retry a failed workflow child in place

Retrying a `Workflow` from `START` when a static child failed cancelled running siblings, re-ran finished siblings without output, and multiplied a child's `max_attempts` by the workflow's.

- Propagate `Workflow.retry_config` to static children without their own policy on build and `model_copy` (including through parallel workers and nested workflows), retrying failed children in place while siblings keep running. `Workflow.graph` holds copies of inheriting children (cloning agents), leaves `edges` nodes unchanged, and does not re-propagate if `graph` is reassigned directly; `retry_config` is frozen on `Workflow`, and workflows without `retry_config` do not read child policies.
- Stop retrying child failures reported via `ctx.error` in `NodeRunner`. Workflow-level failures such as `timeout` still retry the whole workflow; with both `timeout` and `retry_config`, a child cut short by `timeout` can run up to `max_attempts`² times and end with `NodeTimeoutError`.
- Update docstrings, the RetryConfig and parallel worker guides, and the NodeRunner architecture reference.

Breaking change: Assigning `retry_config` on a `Workflow`, including in a subclass's `model_post_init`, now raises `pydantic.ValidationError` (use `Workflow(..., retry_config=...)` or `node(workflow, retry_config=...)`). A child's own `retry_config` replaces `Workflow.retry_config` for that child rather than falling back to a whole-workflow retry when a failure is outside the child's `exceptions` or exhausts its `max_attempts`. A `timeout` on a parallel worker child (`parallel_worker=True`, other than a `Node` subclass) and failures of detached `asyncio.create_task(ctx.run_node(...))` children without their own `retry_config` are no longer retried by `Workflow.retry_config`.

Testing Plan:
- Unit tests in `tests/unittests/workflow/test_node_runner_failure.py` and `tests/unittests/workflow/test_workflow_failures.py` covering in-place child retries alongside running/finished siblings (flat and nested), per-child budgets and `retry_config` override (`max_attempts` and `exceptions`), loop agent cloning, `model_copy`, frozen `Workflow.retry_config` assignment, spec-constrained mock agents, and detached dynamic children.

Co-authored-by: Thomas Zettl <zettlt@google.com>

commits.message:
Decrease pixel clock frequency to 20MHz (#767)

### Summary
Fixes #763 Issue

Lowers `pixel-clock-hz` from `40000000` (40 MHz) to `20000000` (20 MHz) in `waveshare,s3-touch-amoled-206.dts` while keeping `.psram_dma_direct = 1`.

### Root Cause & Testing on Hardware
Tested on the **Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.06**:
1. **With `psram_dma_direct = 0`:** SD card apps load without freezing, *but* fast UI swiping triggers `spicommon_dma_setup_priv_buffer: Failed to allocate priv TX buffer` and severe screen glitches because internal SRAM is too tight for 64KB DMA bounce buffers.
2. **With `psram_dma_direct = 1` and `pixel-clock-hz = <20000000>`:** Keeping PSRAM direct DMA active eliminates the internal SRAM allocation errors during swiping, while lowering the QSPI pixel clock to 20 MHz prevents `SPI2` (display) + `SPI3` (SDSPI) from saturating PSRAM DMA bandwidth (`DMA TX underflow`) when loading `.elf` apps from the SD card.

Verified on physical hardware: UI swiping is completely glitch-free and SD-installed `.elf` apps launch cleanly with zero errors.
Standby and sleep (#768)

Merge pull request #4587 from hathach/dwc2-host-dma-reqqueue

dwc2/hcd: DMA mode never waits for request-queue space

dwc2/hcd: DMA mode never waits for request-queue space

In buffer DMA mode the core's DMA scheduler writes the request queue
itself (Databook 2.2.3.1): IN tokens, complete-splits, PING, ZLP. An
HS bulk IN the device keeps NAKing holds all of its entries, so
GNPTXSTS.NPTxQSpcAvail read 0 at every sample.

- The SOF replay of a parked control/bulk complete-split (#4265)
  waited for a free entry in DMA mode too, so behind such a bulk IN
  the complete-split never went out: the start-split was ACKed, then
  nothing until the 5 s control timeout. Every FS device behind an HS
  hub failed to enumerate (STM32H7S3 host, CH32V305 HS CDC + ESP32-S3
  and STM32C071 FS on one hub).
- channel_send_in_token() spun on the same condition in DMA mode,
  which stalled each HS control IN while such a bulk IN was pending
  (a descriptor sweep took 2295 ms, 42 ms with this).

Both now wait only in slave mode, as Linux dwc2 does. The split test
covers the DMA replay with a full queue.

pio_usb: see a new device after a detach on a suspended port

A frame does not check a suspended root port for a detach, and looks for a
new connection only on a port that is not connected. A port is suspended from
the connect until the bus reset of its enumeration ends. If the device leaves
in that time, during usbh's 150 ms attach debounce, usbh sees SE0 ("Device
unplugged while debouncing") and ends the enumeration without a bus reset.
The port then stayed connected and suspended for good, and no device attached
later was seen, until a reboot (or now an hcd_deinit()/hcd_init()).

hcd_port_connect_status() now marks such a port disconnected when it reads
SE0, so the next frame detects a new connection. Not during a bus reset,
where the host drives SE0 itself.

Test: Raspberry Pi Pico, PIO-USB host on GP20/21, an STM32C071 cdc_msc device
detached and reattached by its debug probe (reset and halt drops its pull-up).
- Host always running, 50 attaches, every 2nd only 20-300 ms long: before,
  the port was stuck after the first short attach (3 mounts in total); after,
  every long attach mounted (26 mounts), never stuck.
- hcd_deinit()/hcd_init() cycles with 40 random detaches: before, 1 cycle in
  about 69 found no device for 15 s; after, 0 failures in 53 cycles.

Merge pull request #4585 from sage-mode-hunter/fsdev-setup-len-bound

dcd(fsdev): copy at most 8 bytes of a SETUP packet

Merge pull request #4584 from sage-mode-hunter/class-get-direction

msc, ncm, dfu, printer: stall GET requests sent host-to-device

pio_usb: add hcd_deinit(), so tuh_deinit() and tuh_init() work

tuh_deinit() failed its TU_ASSERT(hcd_deinit()) with the Pico-PIO-USB host,
because hcd_pio_usb.c had no hcd_deinit(). An application that stops the host
around a sleep (the core that runs the host is idle, so it misses a detach)
could not restart it.

Pico-PIO-USB cannot be initialized twice: pio_usb_host_init() claims PIO
state machines and program space and starts the SOF timer. Its
pio_usb_host_stop()/pio_usb_host_restart() cannot be used: they wait for
flags that only the host stack removed from Pico-PIO-USB in 2024 cleared, so
they never return. So:
- hcd_deinit() parks every root port: no SOF and no transfers (suspended),
  a bus reset that is under way is ended (its hcd_port_reset_end() will not
  come, and the lines would stay in SE0), endpoints and pending interrupt
  status are cleared, and the IRQ handler drops events until the next
  hcd_init().
- hcd_init() calls pio_usb_host_init() only the first time. After
  hcd_deinit() it marks the ports as disconnected, so the next frame reports
  the device that is attached now as a new connection, and usbh enumerates
  it. Events are enabled before pio_usb_host_init(), so a connect in the
  first frame is not dropped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

dcd(fsdev): copy at most 8 bytes of a SETUP packet

handle_ctr_setup() copied COUNT_RX bytes into its 8-byte stack buffer
and only checked for 8 afterwards. EP0 RX is sized to 8 only at bus
reset and after a missed SETUP; once a control OUT completes,
handle_ctr_rx() sets it to the max packet size, and the SIE stores a
SETUP data packet of up to that size. A host sending a SETUP with a
longer DATA0 packet made the ISR write up to 56 bytes past the buffer.

Copy at most 8 bytes; any other count still goes through the
missed-setup path. Adds a host fixture that drives the real driver on
RAM registers.

msc, ncm, dfu, printer: stall GET requests sent host-to-device

MSC GET_MAX_LUN, NCM GET_NTB_PARAMETERS and GET_NTB_INPUT_SIZE, DFU
GETSTATUS and printer GET_DEVICE_ID are device-to-host, but were answered
whatever the direction bit said. An OUT one armed an OUT data stage into
the reply buffer: a stack local of the already returned handler for
GET_MAX_LUN, GET_NTB_INPUT_SIZE and GETSTATUS, read-only data for
GET_NTB_PARAMETERS and GET_DEVICE_ID. Stall them unless the direction is
IN, as usbd does for GET_STATUS and GET_INTERFACE.

membrowse comment: queue every pending job (concurrency queue: max)

The default single queue lets a pending job replace another: a late older
Build's comment job could cancel the newest pending one, which then never
posts. queue: max keeps them in FIFO order; a superseded one still stops at
is-current.

commits.message:
client-side: run each compile on a current-thread runtime

A client-side invocation built a multi-thread runtime with two workers,
which it then mostly waited on: the compile runs in a child process and
cache I/O goes over IPC. Starting those threads in every invocation made
a cache hit 1.3ms slower (13.6ms to 12.3ms per hit, one at a time, for a
file whose server-mode hit takes 8ms).

Use the current-thread runtime server mode clients already use. Blocking
work still goes to the blocking thread pool.

A library without a kind must stay without one: rustc picks the kind per
target (e.g. static with crt-static), so turning it into dylib changes
the output.

The match's fallback arm only runs when parsing fails, so it was a line of

rustc lists the profile in its dep-info, so its contents already reach the hash key. Listing it as an output made every cache hit write it back, and the new mtime made cargo rebuild every crate that reads it.

`clap_err.exit()` leaves through std::process::exit, which skips the
`__llvm_profile_write_file()` call in our `exit`. The Windows PGO build
finds sccache's profile by running `sccache --version`, which takes
that path, so it got no profile and failed with "the instrumented
binary wrote no profile".

Make `-ftime-trace` hasheable as in pre 0.18

config: reject an invalid SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE instead of ignoring it

A value that parse_size cannot read, such as 20GB or 1.5G, was dropped
without a message and the cache kept its 10G default. Report it like the
other malformed environment variables do.

parse_size also multiplied without an overflow check, so a huge value
such as 16777216T panicked in a debug build. Treat that as invalid too.

rust: exclude CARGO_TARGET_DIR and CARGO_BUILD_* from the hash key

They configure Cargo; what they change for rustc arrives as hashed arguments. Hashing them gave each target directory its own cache.

rust: cache incremental compiles with SCCACHE_ALLOW_INCREMENTAL=cache

Crates compiled with `-C incremental=<dir>` (cargo's default for workspace
members and path dependencies in the dev profile) are never cached, so a
cache shared between checkouts or machines misses on them whenever they
are not built locally yet.

With SCCACHE_ALLOW_INCREMENTAL=cache in the environment of the compile,
they are cached; like `1`, it also allows CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1. The
incremental directory is left out of the cache key and out of the dep-info
and file-names runs of rustc, but the key records that the compile is
incremental, since rustc's outputs differ (e.g. the default
codegen-units). A hit leaves the incremental directory as it was; a miss
compiles incrementally as asked. Such compiles are not distributed. On
Windows the variable's name is matched ignoring case, as env::var does in
the client. Without it, nothing changes, keys included.

commits.message:
feat: turn audio/video transcripts and slide media into tracks (#4752)

* fix(pptx): keep video and audio shapes and record their media file

A video shape (python-pptx Movie) was not a Picture, so the backend
skipped it and the video was absent from the document. An audio shape
came out as a plain picture of its speaker icon, with nothing to say
that it plays a file.

A video shape now becomes a picture of its poster frame, on its slide.
Video and audio pictures record the media file in a docling__video or
docling__audio meta field: the path inside the package for an embedded
file, or the link target for a linked file. The media element in
p:nvPr gives the kind; the p14:media extension or the media element
gives the relationship.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* fix(odf): record the video and audio file of an ODP media frame

The ODP backend skipped the draw:plugin of a media frame. Only its
draw:image preview came out, as a plain picture.

The preview picture now records the media file in the same
docling__video or docling__audio meta field as PPTX. A frame without a
preview gets an empty picture. When LibreOffice declares its generic
media type, the manifest or the file extension gives the kind.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* docs: describe how slide video and audio are recorded

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* feat(pptx,odf): load the media files that a slide plays

A pipeline needs the bytes of a media file to convert it. The new
DeclarativeDocumentBackend.load_media takes the value of a
docling__video or docling__audio field and returns the bytes. The
default returns None.

The PPTX backend reads an embedded file from its package part and the
ODP backend from its archive. A linked file goes through the
ImageResourceLoader rules: a URL needs enable_remote_fetch, and a local
file needs enable_local_fetch, a document read from a Path, and a place
in the folder of the document or below it.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* feat(pipeline): convert slide video and audio with do_media_conversion

The new ConvertPipelineOptions.do_media_conversion (off by default)
makes the simple pipeline convert each recorded media file with the ASR
pipeline (audio) or the video pipeline (video), with the Whisper model
of media_asr_options. The result goes in a group right after the
picture: the transcript with its timestamps and, for a video, the
sampled frames. The items take the provenance and the content layer of
the picture.

A media file that cannot be loaded or converted, also for a missing
ASR extra, keeps its picture, is listed in the conversion errors, and
makes the result a partial success. A linked file that the backend
options do not allow is skipped with a warning.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* docs: describe the conversion of slide video and audio

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* style(odf): restore the blank line lost in the merge with main

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* fix(media): handle legacy containers and media shown on several slides

From the review of Steve-Allison:

- Older decks embed .wmv, .m4v, .mpg, .mpeg, .flv, .asf, .wma or
  .aiff. With LibreOffice's generic media type, the ODP backend did not
  record such a file. media_kind() now knows these containers.
- The video pipeline reads only some containers. A video in another one
  is recorded but not converted, with a warning, so the deck no longer
  becomes a partial success for a file that cannot be converted at all.
- A media part that several slides show is converted once; each slide
  gets its copy of the result.

A video without an audio track already converts to its frames without
an error; a test now covers it.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Nguyen <danielnguyenh07@gmail.com>

* feat(asr): put the transcript in a track and optionally keep the media

Add the transcript items to one TrackItem instead of the body. With the new
keep_media option (--keep-media), reference the input file as the track's audio,
or video for a video file, so that e.g. a DocLang archive stores it. Only file
inputs are supported, and the CLI then keeps them in place.

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

* feat: put video and WebVTT transcripts in a track

Like ASR, add the frames and transcript of a video, and the cues of a WebVTT file,
to one TrackItem. Frames become instants at their timestamp. The video pipeline
also takes keep_media (--keep-media), which references the input file as the
track's video.

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

* feat(cli): keep the source in DCLX archives

With the new --keep-source option, store the input file unchanged in the archive
written by --to dclx, with the file name and media type of the document's origin.
Only file inputs have a source to store. A source that is also the media of a
track (--keep-media) is stored once.

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

* feat(media): turn slide video and audio into tracks

A video or audio object on a PPTX or ODP slide becomes a track, with its poster
frame or icon as the cover and a MediaRef to the media file, in place of a picture
with a docling__video or docling__audio meta field. With do_media_conversion, the
transcript and frames go in that track instead of a group after the picture. The
new keep_media option (also --keep-media) holds the media file in the track, so
that a DocLang archive stores it. Media in a container that a track cannot
reference yet, such as .wmv, stays a picture.

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

* fix(asr): use standard media types for audio inputs

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

* fix(asr): strip the segment text of native Whisper

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

* feat(cli): transcribe slide media with --convert-media

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

* feat(media): keep the media of older decks in tracks

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

* test: follow DocLang 0.10 and the new track media types

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

* fix(deps): require docling-core 2.108.0

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

* test: follow the title detection of docling-core 2.107 in the LaTeX ground truth

Signed-off-by: Panos Vagenas <pva@zurich.ibm.com>

fix(calendar): describe expanded days of monthly and yearly rules as every such day (#5451)

* fix(calendar): describe a day without a position in a monthly or yearly rule as every such day

In a MONTHLY or YEARLY recurrence rule, a BYDAY day without a position,
such as BYDAY=MO, stands for every Monday of the month or of the year
(RFC 5545, 3.3.10). The description read "Monthly on Monday", which
states a rule that repeats once a month. Write "Monthly on every Monday"
instead. A day with a position, and the days of a weekly rule, are
described as before.

Signed-off-by: Gagan baghel <78648366+gagan-baghel@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(calendar): describe month days of a yearly rule without BYMONTH as days of every month

In a YEARLY rule without BYMONTH, BYMONTHDAY=1 stands for the 1st of every
month (RFC 5545, 3.3.10). The description read "Yearly on the 1st", which
states a rule that repeats once a year. Add "of every month".

Signed-off-by: Gagan baghel <78648366+gagan-baghel@users.noreply.github.com>
