commits.message:
[vllm, rollout, perf] refactor: read sampled-token log-probs from flat lists (#8689)

### What does this PR do?

Reads sampled-token log-probs from vLLM's flat lists instead of one
`Logprob` dict per generated token, and makes
the prompt log-prob reader work with flat lists. Outputs are unchanged.
In a standalone AsyncLLM benchmark on one
B300, rollout wall time fell from 6.99 s to 6.29 s (−10%).

Today `rollout.calculate_log_probs=True` without a top-k head sends
`logprobs=0` without `flat_logprobs`, so vLLM
builds a dict for every token and the server walks those dicts to get
one float each. #8010 turned on flat lists
for the top-k path only, because `if sampling_params["logprobs"]:` is
false for `0`.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs:
https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+flat_logprobs. Only
#8010 (merged,
  top-k path) matches, so this does not duplicate an existing PR.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

```bash
# vLLM 0.30, one B300 (model path redacted)
VLLM_TOPK_SUPPORT_MODEL_PATH=<Qwen3-0.6B-sized checkpoint> \
  python3 -m pytest -q -rA tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_topk_support.py

pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main)
# all hooks passed
```

- The new test runs the same prompts, including a one-token prompt, with
sampled and prompt log-probs and
`flat_logprobs` off and on (greedy). Tokens, sampled log-probs and
`extract_prompt_logprobs` output must match
  exactly. `vllm.yml` runs this file.
- On vLLM 0.24, `extract_prompt_logprobs` on main raises `IndexError`
for a one-token prompt with flat lists; with
  this PR it returns the same result as the dict path.

Benchmark: standalone `AsyncLLM` on one B300 (vLLM 0.30, mp executor,
`max_num_seqs=256`,
`logprobs_mode=processed_logprobs`), a Qwen3-0.6B-sized model, 496
requests submitted together with output lengths
fixed to a real rollout's (226K tokens). Two runs per mode, spread ≤
0.14 s.

| Mode | Rollout wall time | Front-end CPU | Front-end GC |
|---|---|---|---|
| `logprobs=0`, dict (main) | 6.99 s | 6.85 s | 3.26 s |
| `logprobs=0`, flat (this PR) | **6.29 s (−10%)** | 6.03 s | 2.67 s |
| `logprobs=None` (reference) | 4.96 s | 1.90 s | 0.00 s |

In this workload the `AsyncLLM` process is CPU-bound once log-probs are
on, and the gain comes from less Python
object and GC work in that process. GPU-bound workloads may gain less.

### API and Usage Example

No API or config change.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py`: request
`flat_logprobs` whenever log-probs are requested
(`logprobs is not None`, previously `> 0`), and read the `logprobs=0`
path with `extract_sampled_logprobs`.
- `verl/workers/rollout/utils.py`: add `extract_sampled_logprobs`, which
takes the first entry of each flat row, the
  sampled token.
- `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/utils.py`:
`extract_prompt_logprobs` reads rows by index from 1 instead of
slicing `[1:]`. With the flag on, prompt log-probs are `FlatLogprobs`
too, and in vLLM < 0.29 an empty slice (a
  one-token prompt) raises `IndexError`.
- `TokenOutput.log_probs` is still a list of floats. Top-k extraction
uses the existing path. Both paths benefit
  from the one-token prompt fix. SGLang and TRT-LLM are unchanged.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute
Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] pre-commit on the changed files, as above. Full-repo pre-commit
was not run.
- [x] Add / Update [the
documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). Not
needed: no user-facing change.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI
workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows):
the new test runs in `vllm.yml`.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request`
channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1).
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, update the

commits.message: Update GoogleTest for Clang 21 compatibility (#2097)

Keep Yoga's min-content pass off committed nodes (#2077)

Summary:

X-link: https://github.com/meta/litho/pull/1096


Fixes https://github.com/react/react-native/issues/59678. With `enableFlexboxAutoMinSizeInStrictMode` on, a Text that holds a View under `<experimental_LayoutConformance mode="strict">` crashes on the JavaScript thread once a later commit lays its container out again while the Text stays as an earlier commit laid it out.

`computeMinContentMainSize` (https://github.com/react/react-native/issues/57057, memoised in https://github.com/react/react-native/issues/58833) walks each flex item's subtree through `getChild(i)` and measures the leaves it reaches, but unlike the rest of the algorithm it never calls `cloneChildrenIfNeeded()`. An item's children are still the committed tree's until the item's own layout clones them, whether its measurement then comes from its cache or its flex basis from its style, so the pass runs measure callbacks on, and writes its memoised results into, nodes the tree being laid out does not own. A committed Paragraph's cached content still points at the View its own `layout()` replaced with a laid-out clone, and React's reference followed that clone, so the View is already destroyed when the pass reads it.

This clones a container's children before the pass descends into them, as `calculateLayoutImpl` does before its writes and `layoutAbsoluteDescendants` does since react/yoga#1675. So that a relayout does not clone every item's subtree, a memoised min-content now holds as long as the node's cached measurements do: the pass reuses it under the condition `calculateLayoutInternal` reuses them, now `isCacheStale`, and `calculateLayoutInternal` drops a memo from an earlier layout where it drops them. A container's memo is keyed on the owner's width only when a percentage margin or padding in the subtree it walked resolves against it, as a cached layout is since react/yoga#2042. A relayout then walks, and clones, only the subtrees that changed.

Because a memo now outlives its layout, `YGNodeSetMinContentWidth` and `YGNodeSetMinContentHeight` mark the node dirty when the value changes, as style setters do, and `YGMinContentMeasureFunc` says its results are kept, as a measure function's are, until the node is marked dirty.

`yogaNodeMeasureCallbackConnector` now calls `ensureUnsealed()` on the node it measures, so a committed node reaching it asserts in debug builds where it happens rather than as a read of freed memory later.

## Changelog:

[GENERAL] [FIXED] - Fix a crash measuring a Text that holds a View under strict layout conformance with automatic minimum sizes

X-link: https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/59688

Test Plan:
- `yarn fantom Text-flexboxAutoMinSize-itest View-flexboxAutoMinSize-itest`: on `main` with only the tests and the assertion, the Text file aborts with `Attempt to mutate a sealed object.` and the View cases pass; with this change all four cases pass, and so does `LayoutConformance-itest` with `enableFlexboxAutoMinSizeInStrictMode` on and off.
- `MinContentTest.cpp`, which I built with gtest against the libraries Fantom's tester links: on `main`, `testWalkClonesChildrenOfAnotherTree` and `testUnchangedItemIsNotMeasuredAgain` fail; with this change all five cases pass.
- react/yoga's tests at react/yoga@0747590, whose `yoga/` matches this base's, and at react/yoga@41118bd pass with this change applied.
- Cost, in callgrind's instructions per commit on a Release build, against `main` at e6da2e5d8: a commit that lays a column of 100 or 1,000 unchanged rows out again runs 18% fewer when a View below them changes, and 21% fewer when the column's width changes ([counts](https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/59688#issuecomment-6531336486)).
- CI: `test_react_common_cxx` and `validate_cxx_api_snapshots` pass in React Native's Android CI image, as do `yarn flow-check`, ESLint over the two tests and the formatters over the changed files. I could not run `test_ios_rntester`; Yoga's sources compile for the iOS simulator with `Yoga.podspec`'s flags.

Reviewed By: javache


Pulled By: adityasharat

Differential Revision: D130641328

Pull Request resolved: https://github.com/react/yoga/pull/2077

commits.message:
docs: rt-tokio: show how to run local tasks on an own runtime

# Summary

The docs of `TokioRuntime` now say that, when tasks need not be
`Send`, an application that builds its own Tokio runtime must run
Openraft inside a `LocalSet` or a `LocalRuntime`, and show how with
`LocalSet::run_until`.

# Details

In single-threaded mode, `TokioRuntime::spawn` calls `spawn_local`,
which panics outside a `LocalSet` or, from tokio 1.51, a
`LocalRuntime`. `TokioRuntime::block_on` sets up a `LocalSet`, but an
application that drove Openraft on a runtime it built itself, such as
a current-thread runtime, panicked at the first spawn, and the docs
did not say why.

The doc example builds a current-thread runtime and spawns a task
inside `LocalSet::run_until`. The same code works whether tasks need
to be `Send` or not, so the doctest runs in every mode. The new test
`test_spawn_non_send_task_on_own_runtime` does the same in
single-threaded mode, with a task that holds an `Rc`.

fix: rt-tokio: follow openraft-rt's single-threaded mode

# Summary

`TokioRuntime` now spawns tasks with `spawn_local` and runs `block_on`
on a `LocalSet` whenever the `single-threaded` feature of `openraft-rt`
is enabled, not only when its own `single-threaded` feature is.

# Details

`OptionalSend` drops its `Send` bound when `openraft-rt` has the
`single-threaded` feature, but `TokioRuntime` chose between
`tokio::spawn` and `spawn_local` by the feature of `openraft-rt-tokio`.
When another crate in the build enabled only
`openraft-rt/single-threaded`, such as the compio or monoio adapter,
`TokioRuntime::spawn` passed a future that need not be `Send` to
`tokio::spawn`, and the crate failed to compile with E0277.

`openraft-rt` now exports the hidden macro `__if_single_threaded!`,
which expands one of two branches by the feature of `openraft-rt` as
resolved for the whole build. `TokioRuntime::spawn` uses it, and so
does the type of the `local` field: a `LocalSet` in single-threaded
mode, otherwise a unit struct whose `block_on` calls the runtime's.
The `single-threaded` feature of `openraft-rt-tokio` still turns this
mode on.

`make test-runtime` and the `rt-tokio` CI job also test the crate with
`--features openraft-rt/single-threaded`. New tests check that
`TokioRuntime::new(2)` starts two workers, and that in single-threaded
mode a spawned task can hold an `Rc`.

docs: rt-monoio: fix the Raft link and list the Tokio MPSC channel

# Summary

The crate docs of `openraft-rt-monoio` now build with broken intra-doc
links denied, and their list of primitives taken from Tokio includes
the MPSC channel.

# Details

The intra-doc link to `openraft::Raft` could not resolve, because this
crate depends on `openraft-rt`, not on `openraft`. It now points to the
`Raft` page on docs.rs.

The list of Tokio primitives named `Watch` and `Mutex`, but
`MonoioMpsc` also wraps `tokio::sync::mpsc`. The list now names `Mpsc`
and why: Monoio has no channel, and the bounded channel of `local_sync`
0.1.1 has no weak sender, which `MpscSender::downgrade` needs. A line
after the list says that `Oneshot` uses the `local_sync` oneshot
channel.

docs: rt-monoio: document that task panics unwind block_on

# Summary

The docs of `MonoioRuntime` and of its `JoinError` now state that a
panic in a spawned task unwinds out of the `block_on` call that drives
the runtime, instead of reaching the task's `JoinHandle`.

# Details

Monoio 0.2.4 polls a task without catching unwinds, so a panic in a
task spawned with `AsyncRuntime::spawn` passes through the executor
before any task that awaits the `JoinHandle` gets a result. That is why
`JoinError` is `Infallible`; the old comment said only that joining
always succeeds. For Openraft, a panic in the core task therefore
cannot be reported as `Fatal::Panicked`: the panic ends `block_on`, and
no caller on the runtime gets an error.

Reporting the panic through the join result would need a `JoinError`
other than `Infallible`, a public API change that this commit leaves
out.

The new test `test_spawned_task_panic_unwinds_out_of_block_on` runs the
runtime on a thread of its own, because the panic ends that thread, and
requires the thread's join to return the child's panic payload. The
parent waits for the child with a 10-second timeout, so a runtime that
caught the panic fails the test instead of hanging it.

fix: rt-compio: report the final watch value before the closure

# Summary

On compio, `WatchReceiver::changed()` now returns `Ok(())` once for a
value sent just before the last sender was dropped, and returns
`RecvError` only after that, as the tokio, monoio and simulated
runtimes do.

# Details

see's `changed()` checks whether the channel is closed before it
compares versions. A receiver that was waiting for a change when the
last sender sent a value and was dropped therefore got `RecvError`,
although `borrow_watched()` then read the new value. `wait_until_ge()`
and `wait_until()` returned the error instead of the value, so a final
update, such as the last flush progress, looked like a shutdown.

When see's `changed()` fails, `SeeReceiver::changed()` now marks the
current value seen with `borrow_and_update()`, and returns `Ok(())` if
that value had not been seen; otherwise it returns `RecvError`. Each
receiver keeps its own version, and a channel closed without a new
value still fails at once.

The new conformance test
`Suite::test_watch_changed_reports_final_value_before_close` checks
three cases:

- A waiting `changed()` and a second receiver each get `Ok(())` and
  read 1, then get `RecvError`.
- A waiting `wait_until_ge(&1)` returns 1.
- A closed receiver that has seen every value gets `RecvError`.

It fails on compio without the fix, and passes on the tokio (default
and `single-threaded`), monoio and simulated runtimes.

Validated with `cargo test` on `rt-compio`, `rt-tokio` in both modes,
`rt-monoio` and `rt-sim`.

refactor: rt-compio: rename FlumeMutex to FuturesMutex

# Summary

The compio adapter's mutex type is now `FuturesMutex`, named after the
`futures::lock::Mutex` it wraps, instead of `FlumeMutex`.

# Details

`FlumeMutex` wraps `futures::lock::Mutex` and returns its guard; flume
only provides the adapter's MPSC channel. The old name sent anyone who
reads the type name, for example in a diagnostic about lock
contention, to the wrong library. `FuturesMutex` follows
`FuturesOneshot`, the adapter's oneshot over
`futures::channel::oneshot`.

The type sits in a private module and is reached only through
`<CompioRuntime as AsyncRuntime>::Mutex<T>`, so no caller can name it.
The associated type, the guard type and the locking behavior do not
change.

Validated with `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D
warnings` on `rt-compio/Cargo.toml`.

fix: rt: take timer deadlines at the call and poll the future first

# Summary

The `AsyncRuntime` docs now state two timer rules that tokio follows:
`sleep(d)` and `timeout(d, f)` take their deadline when called, not
when first polled, and a timeout polls its future before it checks
the deadline. The compio adapter now follows both. The tokio, monoio
and simulated adapters already did.

# Details

The compio adapter broke both rules:

- It built both delays with `compio::time::sleep`, an `async fn` that
  reads the clock on its first poll, so a timer created now and
  polled later waited `d` from that poll.
- `CompioTimeout` checked the delay before the future, so
  `timeout(Duration::ZERO, ready(1))` returned `Err(Elapsed)` where
  tokio returns `Ok(1)`.

`sleep` now computes the deadline as `Instant::now() + d` and waits
through `sleep_until`, and `timeout` uses the same delay. A duration
too large to add to the current time gives a delay that never fires;
compio's `sleep` panicked with "overflow when adding duration to
instant" on the first poll. `CompioTimeout` now polls the future
first and checks the delay only while the future is pending.

The new tests:

- `test_relative_timers_start_at_creation` creates a sleep and a
  timeout, waits past their duration, and checks that both are ready
  on their first poll and that `sleep(Duration::MAX)` stays pending.
- `test_timeout_polls_future_first` checks that `timeout` and
  `timeout_at` return a ready future's output after their deadline.

With the old code, both tests fail.

Validated with `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D
warnings` on `rt-compio/Cargo.toml`, as the Makefile's `test-runtime`
and `clippy` targets run them, plus `make verify` and
`make docs-check`. PR CI does not build rt-compio.

docs: bench: record the #2304 results of idle-groups

# Summary

`benchmarks/idle-groups/results.md` records the measurements of the
changes that #2304 led to, from retiring the ticker (#2378) to
starting the engine queues empty (#2440), next to the 0.10.0 baseline

chore: bench: add measure_change.py to idle-groups

# Summary

`benchmarks/idle-groups/scripts/measure_change.py` measures a change
against the code before it. It builds the benchmark in one checkout
without the change and with it, then runs each `--case` with the two
builds in turns, so that both see the same machine load.

# Details

The measurements of #2304 ran a Bash version of this script from
outside the repository, and the follow-up tasks of #2454 use it. This
version is in Python, like the scripts of `benchmarks/minimal`. It
writes to `--out-dir`, by default under the benchmark's `target/`,
instead of a fixed directory. It also restores files that a change
adds or removes, keeps the saved copies when a restore fails, and
stops when a run fails. It rejects a file name that exists in neither
the checkout nor `--base`, such as a typo, which would leave the change
of the intended file in both builds.

`measure_change_test.py` covers the parsing of a case, the check of
the file names, and the swap of the files of a change, including the
new mtime of a restored file, which makes cargo rebuild it.
`make verify-bench-idle-groups` runs it.

Refs: #2304
Refs: #2454

fix: rt-compio: report a cancelled task as cancelled, not panicked

# Summary

`CompioRuntime::is_panic` now returns `true` only for a task that
panicked, and `CompioJoinError` shows the join error's own message. A
task cancelled by a dropped runtime no longer looks like a panic.

# Details

compio's `JoinError` has two variants, `Panicked` and `Cancelled`. A
task is cancelled when, for example, the runtime that owns it is
dropped before the task finishes. The adapter treated both as a panic:
`is_panic` always returned `true`, and `CompioJoinError` always
displayed "Spawned task panicked". `CoreState::started` uses
`is_panic` to choose the RaftCore result, so a cancelled RaftCore task
was reported as `Fatal::Panicked` instead of `Fatal::Stopped`.

`is_panic` now matches `JoinError::Panicked`, and `CompioJoinError`
displays the wrapped error: "Task has panicked" or "Task was
cancelled". Dropping a `CompioJoinHandle` still detaches the task.

Two unit tests await a task that panics and a pending task whose
runtime was dropped, and check `is_panic` and the message for each.
With the old code, the cancelled case fails on `is_panic` and the
panicked case on the message.

Validated with `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D
warnings` on `rt-compio/Cargo.toml`, as the Makefile's `test-runtime`
and `clippy` targets run them, and `make verify`. PR CI does not
build rt-compio.

fix: macros: only treat known paths as #[since] field markers

# Summary

Inside a `#[since]` struct or enum, a field or variant attribute is
now a marker only when its path is `since`, `openraft_macros::since`,
`openraft::macros::since` or `openraft::openraft_macros::since`. Other
attributes stay on the field for rustc.

# Details

`is_since` matched any attribute whose last path segment is `since`,
in both the expansion and the error cleanup. Another tool's
`#[clippy::since]` on a field therefore made the expansion fail with
"expected attribute arguments in parentheses", and a misspelled
`#[openraft_macro::since(...)]` was rewritten into docs instead of
failing to resolve.

`is_since` now compares the whole path with `MARKER_PATHS`. A marker
written through another alias, or with a leading `::`, is no longer
rewritten, and rustc rejects it. No marker in this repository uses
such a path. The `since` docs list the accepted paths.

- The unit test `test_is_since` covers the four paths and six
  attributes that are not markers.
- The expansion fixture `since/expand/marker_paths.rs` uses each path
  on a field and keeps `#[clippy::since]` next to a real marker.

With the old `is_since`, both new tests fail, and a container with a
misspelled marker compiles. With the new one, that container fails
with E0433.

Validated with `cargo test --manifest-path macros/Cargo.toml --lib
--test test_since` on nightly and on stable, with the latest
cargo-expand and `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"`, and `make fmt_check`.

Make vote_progress_api accept either the candidate vote or the

# Details

test: macros: pin #[since] errors for a missing or repeated argument

# Summary

New trybuild cases check the exact error and span when `#[since]`
lacks `version`, repeats `version`, or repeats `date`.

# Details

The compile-fail cases covered malformed versions and dates, an
invalid field version and an unknown key, but none of the argument
rules in `Since::from_tokens`, `set_version` and `set_date`. A

published in the API docs while every fixture still passed.

- `missing_version.rs`: `#[since(date = "...")]` on a function, and a

docs: openraft: show how to expose Raft to clients

# Summary

Add `docs::components::application_api`, which shows how an
application translates Openraft's metrics and errors into types it
owns, how a client retries each write rejection, and which read policy
keeps the 0.9 read behavior.

# Details

Metrics and errors are generic over the type config, so an application
with several Raft groups has one type per group, and serializing them
for clients ties its API to Openraft's releases. The page's compiled
example projects `RaftMetrics` and `ClientWriteError` of two type
configs into versioned application types with one generic function
each.

The retry table separates the cases a single "forward to leader"
helper merges: `NotLeader` redirects or needs leader discovery,
`LeadershipTransfer` points at a node that may not lead yet,
`LeaseExpired` carries no leader and is retried on the same node, and
`LogEntryDiscarded` may still commit, so it is retried only with
deduplication.

`ReadPolicy::ReadIndex` keeps the 0.9 behavior, `LeaseRead` relies on
bounded clock drift, and both wait for the read log id to be applied.

The upgrade guide's errors section links to the page. Hiqlite's 0.10
port added per-group error variants, a placeholder type config for its
wire types, and a leader lookup that loses the forward reason.

feat: openraft: read back the runtime switches

# Summary

`RuntimeConfigHandle` gains `is_tick_enabled()`,
`is_heartbeat_enabled()`, `is_elect_enabled()` and
`is_pre_vote_enabled()`, and a new cluster-control page explains how
to keep a voter from campaigning, how to tell whether a leadership
transfer landed, and how membership changes interact with the leader.

# Details

The handle could only set the switches, so an admin API that reports
whether a node campaigns had to mirror the value itself, and the
mirror drifts from what Raft reads. Each getter starts from its
`Config` field and follows the setter.

The new `docs::cluster_control::leadership` page covers:

- a voter with `enable_elect` off still votes, counts toward quorums
  and takes over on a leadership transfer; automatic failover needs a
  voter that may campaign and can reach a quorum; `Trigger::elect()`
  and `Trigger::transfer_leader()` work regardless of the switch;
- `Trigger::transfer_leader()` returns once queued, so the page shows a
  bounded metrics wait that tells the target taking over from another
  node taking over and from a timeout;
- a leader that removes itself commits the change first and hands over
  after `removed_leader_step_down`, two events an operator observes
  separately; `InProgress` and `UncommittedLeaderLog` are retried on the
  same leader; changes across several Raft groups are not atomic.

`Trigger::transfer_leader()` and `RuntimeConfigHandle::elect()` link
to the page.

Hiqlite's 0.10 port mirrored `enable_elect` in its own atomic, and its
shutdown handover inferred success from the old node no longer
leading.

docs: openraft: make the storage suites a 0.10 migration step

# Summary

The 0.9 to 0.10 upgrade guide now runs the storage test suites as a
step of its own, shows where `apply()` may send a response, and says
what the suites cover and what they leave to the application.

# Details

- The porting steps add "run the storage test suites against the
  ported stores" right after updating the stores.
- In 0.10 a client gets its answer when the responder sends it, not
  when `apply()` returns. The state machine section shows a persistent
  state machine that holds the responses until its transaction commits
  durably, and describes a state machine kept in memory: it makes each
  entry visible before responding, and relies on the last persisted
  snapshot plus the logs up to the persisted committed log id after a
  restart, so the log store keeps those logs and implements
  `save_committed()`. Blank and membership entries are included.
- The test suite section names the boundaries the log suite checks
  (inclusive `purge()`, `truncate_after()` keeping its argument, the
  last log id once every entry is purged), introduces
  `ApplicationSuite` from 0.10.1, and states that neither suite tests
  restart, crash recovery or snapshot transport.

Hiqlite's WAL port had to fix exactly these boundaries, and its new
log suite test was the first to check them.

test: macros: fail when a #[since] fixture has no snapshot

# Summary

The `#[since]` snapshot test now fails when a positive input has no
`*.expanded.rs` file, instead of writing one and passing. Fixture
authors still generate snapshots with `MACROTEST=overwrite`, as in the
`expand!` driver.

# Details

`pass` called `macrotest::expand`, which writes the current expansion
to a missing `*.expanded.rs` file and counts the case as refreshed,
not failed. A fixture committed without its snapshot therefore passed
in CI with no reviewed expected docs.

`pass` now calls `macrotest::expand_without_refresh`, which fails on
a missing snapshot and writes nothing. With `MACROTEST=overwrite` it
calls `macrotest::expand`, which writes missing snapshots and replaces
changed ones. This is the same change #2439 made to `test_expand.rs`.

Checked with `valid_semver.expanded.rs` removed: the old driver
recreated the file and passed. The new one fails with "expected but
not found" and leaves the file absent. With `MACROTEST=overwrite` it
writes the file back, identical to the checked-in one. A changed
`with_date.expanded.rs` still fails.

Validated with `cargo test --manifest-path macros/Cargo.toml --test
test_since` on nightly with the latest cargo-expand and
`RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"`, and `make fmt_check`.

docs: openraft: show what a RaftNetworkV2 transport must carry

# Summary

Document the transport mistakes that compile but silently disable a
feature, and test that the HTTP example carries Pre-Vote.

# Details

- getting-started lists `pre_vote()` and `transfer_leader()` with their
  targets and what their defaults do: the default `pre_vote()` grants
  without contacting the peer, so Pre-Vote no longer protects the term,
  and the default `transfer_leader()` reports the target unreachable,
  also when a removed leader hands over. The production checklist
  points there.
- `examples/network-v2-http/tests/pre_vote.rs` sends a pre-vote from a
  candidate whose log is behind to a leader and expects a refusal. With
  the client's `pre_vote()` override removed, the default grant fails
  the test.
- `AppendEntriesResponse::into_append_result()` gains a doctest for an
  empty heartbeat with and without a previous log and for a partial
  send, and points new wire formats at carrying `AppendResult` with its
  conflict hint.
- `RaftNetworkV2::full_snapshot()` no longer claims a default chunking
  implementation; there is none. The upgrade guide gains a section on
  sending a snapshot: a staging file per transfer, bounded chunks,
  cancellation, validation before `Raft::install_full_snapshot()`, and
  the tests to run, with the raft-kv-rocksdb example as reference.
- `RaftNetworkV2::pre_vote()` now says that `Trigger::elect(true)` also
  sends a pre-vote, and the upgrade guide says a port can keep the
  sequential `stream_append()` default and pipeline later.

Hiqlite's 0.10 port called `elect(true)` without implementing
`pre_vote()`, and chunked its own snapshots through a fixed scratch
file.

docs: openraft: choose a rollout before porting to 0.10

# Summary

The 0.9 to 0.10 upgrade guide now opens with a rollout decision: what
Openraft guarantees and what the application must check for porting
the source, reopening 0.9 data, running mixed versions, and rolling
back. It lists the minimum checks for a rolling upgrade and falls back
to a cold restart.

# Details

Hiqlite's 0.10 migration kept its data but needed a cold restart: its
bincode transport cannot carry a `VoteRequest` between versions. The
guide covered stored data and snapshot messages but did not say which
other RPCs keep their 0.9 encoding.

The data and wire compatibility section now lists the RPCs whose
layout is unchanged, explains that a positional codec cannot carry
`VoteRequest` or `ForwardToLeader` across versions in either
direction, notes that 0.9 has no Pre-Vote or TransferLeader RPC, and
states that `openraft-legacy` keeps only the v1 network and its
snapshot messages.

A startup guard that checks reachable peers cannot prove that an
unreachable peer stopped, so the guide recommends an explicit protocol
version in the transport handshake.

docs: dir-transfer: say who cleans up after a failed receive

# Summary

The crate docs now say that the receiver owns the target directory:
each attempt needs its own empty directory, and after a failure or
cancellation the receiver discards the partial one.

# Details

The transport contract said only that a failed or cancelled session
is discarded. Dropping a `DirWriter` leaves the files it has already
created, and `DirWriter::new` requires an empty directory, so a retry
into the same directory fails with `AlreadyExists` at the first
leftover file.

The new paragraph tells the receiver to give each attempt an existing,
empty directory, to keep the handle that owns it alive until
`recv_dir` returns, and to discard it after a failure or cancellation.
It links to `DirWriter::new` and `recv_dir`. No code changes.

Validated with `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --manifest-path
examples/dir-transfer/Cargo.toml --no-deps` and the example's rustfmt
check.

# Summary

The `Setup | System RocksDB` step of the Jepsen `check` job now
installs `librocksdb-dev` through the same apt sources as the node

`http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/` for any file it fails to serve.

# Details

The step replaced every source with the Azure mirror alone, so an

fix: macros: reject an expand! template without variables

# Summary

`expand!` now reports "Expected at least one template variable" for a
template with an empty variable list, in both `KEYED` and `!KEYED`
modes, as its docs require.

# Details

`Expand::parse` accepted `()` as the variable list. Without argument
tuples, `expand!(KEYED, () => { ... },)` compiled and emitted nothing.
With a tuple, it failed with "Expected the same number of
arguments(``) as template variables(`[]`)", which does not name the
problem.

The parser now rejects an empty variable list before it reads the
template body and the tuples, and points the error at the `()`. Only
invocations without variables break, and the docs already forbid
them.

The new trybuild case `expand/fail/no_variable.rs` covers both modes
without tuples, and `KEYED` with a tuple. The old parser accepts the
first two and gives the arity message for the third. The new positive
fixture `expand/expand/single_variable.rs` covers the smallest valid
template, `(K,)`, with argument tuples written with and without a
trailing comma.

Validated with `cargo test --manifest-path macros/Cargo.toml` on
nightly and on stable, with the latest cargo-expand and
`RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"`, and `make verify`.

test: jepsen: fall back to Ubuntu's archive for node images

# Summary

When `UBUNTU_APT_MIRROR` is set, the node image now reads its sources
through APT's mirror method: the CI mirror first, then
`http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/` for any file the CI mirror fails
to serve.

# Details

Run 44661852653 failed its `liveness` and `packet-flaky` jobs in the
image build: azure.archive.ubuntu.com timed out for about ten minutes,
and all three apt-get attempts fell inside that outage. Each attempt
used the same host, so an outage of one mirror longer than the retry
loop still failed the build. The other seven jobs of that run built
their images.

The mirror setup also sets `Acquire::Retries::Delay "false"`. With
the default delay, apt 2.8.3 hung after the InRelease fallback: the
Packages index retries it delayed never restarted. Without the delay,
a build whose CI mirror refused connections finished `apt-get update`
in 22 s and installed every package from the fallback.

The fallback serves every pocket the stock sources use, including
noble-security. Local builds, which leave `UBUNTU_APT_MIRROR` empty,
keep Ubuntu's stock sources and apt defaults.

Failed run: https://github.com/databendlabs/openraft/actions/runs/44661852653/job/136041710061

perf: openraft: start the engine and responder queues empty

# Summary

Every Raft node reserved 64 slots in each of six queues: the engine's
command queue, its four pending-respond queues, and RaftCore's client
responder queue. That is about 41 KiB per node, held whether or not
the node has anything to queue. The queues now start without a
buffer, allocate on their first push, and keep the capacity they grow
to, as before.

# Details

With 1,000 idle leaders (benchmarks/idle-groups, stub followers), the
heap still allocated drops from 214 to 174 MiB, and the footprint, the
median of three runs, from 215 to 197 MiB. With 1,000 idle
three-member groups, the footprint drops from 548 to 473 MiB, and with
5,000 leaders, from 931 to 837 MiB, one run each.

A queue that reaches 64 entries now reallocates about five times on
the way, once, since it keeps its capacity.

cad plugin install: the plugin's install moves into cad, the install command gets a current cad and hands over, and installs are counted (#898)

## Why

The hosted install command did two jobs: it installed cad, and it
installed the plugin into every agent app, from a 2,600-line script
served by the website that cad also ran unattended. That script could
not be versioned or tested against one release, nothing counted how
installs went, and a slow or failed install was invisible to us.

This change amends a law on purpose (`docs/contributing/decisions.md`,
"Two layers, one direction of knowledge"). Before: cad knows nothing of
skills or agent apps. Now: cad names agent apps, skills and the plugin
in exactly one place, `cad_server/plugin/`, reached only by `cad
plugin`. Everything else in cad stays as it was, and the policy tests
hold the new line.

## What changes

**In cad (`packages/cad`)**
- `cad_server/plugin/`: the table of apps, each app's install and
cleanup, and the terminal extras (the CAD logo, the live line, the
marks), moved from `scripts/install/install.py` function for function.
Standard library only, imported up front.
- `cad plugin install` (new): the plugin in every agent app found, then
`cad plugin update auto` on. Exit 0, 1 (every app found failed), 2
(usage), 75 (another run holds the lock and a server began this one).
- `cad plugin update`: runs that same code in process, with the
bookkeeping of the server's background run around it. It no longer
downloads the hosted script.
- One run at a time: a lock in the state folder for the whole run. A
server's run that finds it held answers 75 after trying for two seconds;
a person's run waits.
- cad's own update holds while a run is going (automatic: not due; typed
`cad update`: refused in one line), so the environment is never replaced
under a running install.
- A server-began run has a hard stop a minute past its 15-minute
deadline.
- Only a global install keeps its release as the one the plugin is up to
date for.

**The hosted install command (`scripts/install/`)**: `install.py` goes
from 2,607 lines to under 1,000 and knows no app.
- It makes sure uv is there, installs or repairs cad, and, where a
person ran it, brings an existing cad up to date with that cad's own
`cad update` (inside its major; never where cad started the script).
- It hands over to `<cad> plugin install`. Where that cad has no such
command (0.11.12, 0.11.13) it runs the newest release's: `uv tool run
... cad@latest plugin install`.
- It still writes the report released cads read, last and whole; a
plugin step that ended badly is a `"failed"` entry there, so a bridge
attempt is retried.

**Telemetry**: everything goes through `api.texttocad.dev` to the one
PostHog project; nothing posts to PostHog itself. No list of the agent
apps on a computer is ever sent.
- cad (schema 12, `POST /v1/events`): `install`, one per run (who began
it, how it ended, what the terminal showed, seconds, and how many apps
were found and how many failed, as counts), and `install_failure`, one
per app whose install failed (cad's key for the app, a failure word,
seconds). An app that went well is never named. Under every existing
rule (told first, the environment's and the person's no, never in CI or
a development build). A person's run gives the notice; a server's run
and a run cad started in the background do not. A crash in the command
is reported by the existing `exception` reporting.
- The hosted script (`POST /v1/install`, new): one anonymous report only
where it failed and no working cad could count it: the stage, an exit
status, the system, uv's version, and for a crash the error's type and
the install script's function names and line numbers. On a run cad
started it says nothing and reports only where the person had been told.
- The receiver (`apps/api`): reads schema 12, and takes that report as a
person-less `install_failed` event in the same project, 30 per 10
minutes per client address. It deploys when this merges (`Deploy API`),
so it is live before any release sends to it.

**Release safety**
- `scripts/release/newest_cad.py`, called by `Deploy Docs`: a production
deploy of the site (and with it the hosted script) is refused until
PyPI's newest cad has `cad plugin install`. Until the release that
carries this is out, do not deploy the docs site from `main`.
- `check-wheel-contents.sh` requires `cad_server/plugin/`.

**Docs**: `decisions.md`, `docs/install.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `AGENTS.md`,
`CONTRIBUTING.md`, the testing guide, `scripts/README.md`, the privacy
policy.

## What it costs

- A correction to an app's row now needs a release of cad, and reaches a
computer when its cad updates. A cad that does not update keeps its
table, and its list of skill names, while `latest` carries the newest
plugin.
- Released 0.11.12 and 0.11.13, and the bridge from 0.10.0 to 0.11.11,
still run the hosted script unattended.
- A person's run of the install command now updates a working cad,
without waiting for the feed's hour.
- CI: the update rehearsal gains one route on shard 1/2 (about 6 seconds
measured on Linux, plus fetching 0.11.13 from PyPI); `Deploy Docs` gains
a check of about 9 seconds.

## Tested

- Every job of `Test` on this branch, among them `install.ps1` on
Windows PowerShell 5.1, the real installs with the real Claude Code,
Codex and Gemini CLI on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu, the update rehearsals
on all three (the new route from real 0.11.13 with them), and the
package suites on Linux, Windows and the Python 3.11 floor.
- An independent review of the code found no blocker; its seven findings
are fixed here.

## Not yet run anywhere

- A person's own computer: apps already set up, earlier copies of the
plugin, Windows packaged apps.
- The logo and the live line in a real terminal (CI has none).
- The `Deploy Docs` wiring of the new guard (the script it calls is unit
tested).
- The new telemetry end to end: that takes the deployed receiver and a
released cad.

Feature lengths go to Fusion in mm, inputs are read by their value, and the snapshot tests build every case in inches

commits.message:
Merge pull request #2221 from doronz88/docs/webinspector-blank-frame-cause

webinspector: Describe why a large message stalls

webinspector: Describe why a large message stalls

webinspectord's read handler does a single SSLRead per socket event and
never drains what TLS has buffered, so the 8192 bytes measured in #2219
are the host's socket buffer rather than a limit of the device.
MobileDevice.framework stalls the same way once a message spans two
TLS records, so there is no host framing to copy; the blank frame
stays.

Merge pull request #2220 from doronz88/fix/webinspector-large-message-stall

webinspector: Follow every message with a blank frame

webinspector: Follow every message with a blank frame

Over the lockdown service webinspectord takes a message in 8192 bytes
at a time and picks up the rest of a larger one only once more data
arrives. A message past that size - a Runtime.evaluate carrying a long
script - was therefore never answered until something else was sent.

Send a blank frame of its own after every message, as appium-ios-device
does. webinspectord ignores its content, and the RSD shim, which does
not stall, accepts it too.

Fixes #2219

[Core] Refresh the RBAC policy in every API server worker in the background (#11450)

A role change only reached the worker that made it. The RBAC middleware
reads each worker's in-memory casbin model and never reloads it, so a
demoted admin kept admin endpoints on other workers for minutes.

its model when the version moved. Rebuilds happen off the enforcer's lock,

commits.message:
fix(dual): fmod derivs ignored divisor; safe_log2/log10 name lookup (#2205)

All along (and I'm pretty sure my mistake in not reasoning it though
properly), our implementation of fmod(a,b) with derivs failed to to
take b's rate of change into consideration. Basically, we assumed
b was constant. (Which I bet it usually is in practice, so we never
noticed this.)

More detailed in-the-weeds explanation from Claude:

fmod(a,b) = a - N*b where N = trunc(a/b) is piecewise constant, so its
derivative is a' - N*b'. All implementations only passed through a's
derivs and dropped the -N*b' term (and if only b had derivs, the result
got zero derivs). This was the case in the Dual safe_fmod in dual.h
(used by the cpp backend and the no-bitcode fallback) and in the
llvm_gen_modulus code generators for both the scalar and batched LLVM
backends. Fix all three. The extra computation only happens when b has
derivs, so the common fmod(x, constant) case is unchanged. For b == 0,
N is taken to be 0, preserving the old pass-through of a's derivs.

Also, the Dual safe_log2 and safe_log10 in dual.h called unqualified
safe_log2/safe_log10 on the float value, which only resolves if a float
version happens to be visible in the OSL namespace (dual.h alone did not
compile when they were instantiated). Qualify them as OIIO:: like
safe_log already does. These are only used when USE_FAST_MATH=OFF.

Add an fmod-with-varying-divisor case to testsuite/derivs.

Assisted-by: Claude Code / Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>

fix: Reject .oso %structfields hints on non-struct symbols (#2224)

Found by fuzzing. When loading an .oso, a `%structfields{...}` hint
was applied to the most recent symbol without checking that the symbol
is a struct. For a non-struct symbol, TypeSpec::structspec() returns
nullptr, which was then dereferenced (a null pointer/out-of-bounds
read, depending on platform).

Assisted-by: Claude Code / Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>

fix: Don't under-align the 4D simplex noise gradient table (#2222)

Found by fuzzing / UBSan.  fast_grad4::lut_wide in sfm_simplex.h is a
Block<Vec4,32>, a type that is declared 128-byte aligned, but the
variable was declared alignas(64).

Assisted-by: Claude Code / Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>

fix: Avoid int overflow adjusting read/write ranges in insert_code (#2225)

Found by fuzzing. RuntimeOptimizer::insert_code() shifts every
symbol's first/last read/write op index that falls at or after the
insertion point. But Symbol::mark_always_used() sets the last
read/write to INT_MAX as an "always used" sentinel, and incrementing
it is signed overflow.

Fix: leave the INT_MAX sentinel alone when shifting.

Assisted-by: Claude Code / Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>

admin: switch release-announcements to linuxfoundation action (#2218)

The release announcement Slack posting action has transitioned from
John Mertic's personal account to linuxfoundation.

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>

fix: Reject out-of-range jump targets when loading .oso files (#2223)

Found by fuzzing. The .oso loader accepted any integer as an op's jump
target.

Fix: after the whole file is parsed (jumps point forward, so they
can't be checked as each op is read), verify every jump target lies
after its op and no further than one past the last op, and reject the
shader with an error otherwise.

A new oso-bad-jumps test loads hand-written .oso files with a jump
past the end of the code, a backward jump, and a jump to the op
itself, plus a shader with legal jumps that must still load.

Assisted-by: Claude Code / Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>

test: Update ref output for icx (#2219)

PR #2203 failed to update one reference image. We didn't know because
that ref image only matches on icx, and only on some GH
runners. Specifically, only on Intel CPUs. The AMD EPYC runners match
the other (previously fixed) reference output. Most of the runners
seem to be AMD, so this only intermittendly failed and usually
succeeded if rerun, so I didn't try too hard to track it down until
now.

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>

fix(oslc): avoid invalid downcast in one_default_literal (#2221)

We cast to a `ASTliteral*` unconditionally, but only used it if it
really was a literal. That's harmless in practice, but UB, and it was
caught by the sanitizer.

Assign null if it's not a valid cast. We still only use the pointer
if it really was the right type.

Assisted-by: Claude Code / Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>

fix(android): keep Play Billing's first answer so a second one can't crash the app

Play Billing 8.3.0 answers a request twice when it doesn't finish in 28.5 s:
its main-thread timeout cancels the request (interrupting the worker's
reconnect wait) and answers "Timeout communicating with service", and the
interrupted worker answers SERVICE_DISCONNECTED to the same listener.
PlayBilling resumed its continuation on each answer, so the second threw
IllegalStateException: Already resumed (store build 167 crash in
PlayBilling.monthly's onProductDetailsResponse).

only the first answer via an AtomicBoolean.

Replace CABALOPTS hack with cabal.project

Cross-compile linux.armv6hf instead of emulating it

Build GHC 9.14.1 as a cross compiler with clang/lld 20 targeting the
ARM1176, using Raspbian trixie's libraries as a sysroot (Ubuntu's armhf
toolchain and libraries are ARMv7). This replaces the full userspace
emulation with QEMU and a Raspbian chroot.

Compared with the emulated trixie builder, the stripped binary drops from
44.1MB to 21.0MB (35.6MB in the v0.11.0 release), and building ShellCheck
takes about 5 minutes instead of 46.

Most of the size reduction comes from running llc without the integrated
assembler. Otherwise, LLVM 13+ marks GHC's closures with SHF_GNU_RETAIN and
--gc-sections can't remove anything. Split sections in GHC's own boot
libraries also help.

commits.message:
Merge branch 'contrib/jameslavrenz/pie-batch-fc' into 'master'

perf(fc/pie): weight-stationary batched FC for P4 and S31 (GH #63)

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!99

Merge branch 'perf/pie_conv_1x1_transpose' into 'master'

perf(conv): transpose the 16-pixel 1x1 batch with PIE on P4 and S31

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!97

test(conv): cases for the PIE 1x1 batch transpose

- in_ch 24 and 40: whole 16-channel blocks plus an overlapping last
  block. Two output rows, so the dual-core row split does not run and
  one core takes the 16-pixel batch.
- in_ch 48 with the input 3 bytes off a 16-byte boundary.
- 4x4 with in_ch 264 and 256 outputs: the filter-major path, split
  across both cores.
- 6x5 with in_ch 24 and 32 outputs: the caller's half keeps its batch,
  so the row split runs.

perf(conv): transpose the 16-pixel 1x1 batch with PIE on P4 and S31

- The position-batched 1x1 path transposes 16 pixels to channel-major
  once per batch. Every output-channel panel then reads the same staging.
- Each 16-channel block is two passes of 8 pixels. Each pass is eight
  loads one pixel apart, a 3-stage zip network (8, 16, 32 bit) and
  sixteen 8-byte stores, so the staging is written once.
- When in_ch is not a multiple of 16, the last block covers the last 16
  channels and overlaps the block before it.
- The transpose is out of line, so the rest of esp_nn_conv_s8_1x1 keeps
  its smaller stack frame.
- qacc16_run_channels starts with a compiler memory barrier. Its MAC asm
  reads the staging through pointers, so every staging store lands first.
- The dual-core row split of the 1x1 conv is skipped when the worker's
  half would lose the 16-pixel batch. It still runs where two cores win:
  - more than 32 outputs and in_ch a multiple of 16;
  - 16 pixels with a filter of 64 KB or more, where the filter-major path
    does not batch;
  - the caller's half keeps every 16-pixel batch, as for 6x5 or 4x7.
- docs/performance.md: the ESP32-P4 and ESP32-S31 convolution rows come
  from one bench_app run, with the chip revision, clock and ESP-IDF
  version.

Add a weight-stationary PIE batch FC for P4 and S31.

Sum each filter row once and reuse it across the batch. On P4 and S31 the 1x1 floor is the rev v3.2 sweep: a row shorter than 8 stays off, a row of 8 needs a batch of 8, a longer row needs a batch of 2, and outputs need to be at least 4.
